## Canada Elections Act {#canada-elections-act .Title-of-Act}

[S.C.]{.abbr title="Statutes of Canada"} 2000, c. 9
:::

Assented to 2000-05-31

An Act respecting the election of members to the House of Commons,
repealing other Acts relating to elections and making consequential
amendments to other Acts
::::

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::: section
::: Enacts
Her Majesty, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate and House
of Commons of Canada, enacts as follows:
:::

## [Short Title]{.HTitleText1} {#h-203471 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Short title

**[[1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1 .sectionLabel}** This Act may be cited as
the [Canada Elections Act](/eng/acts/E-2.01).

## [Interpretation]{.HTitleText1} {#h-203474 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-2 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  definitions in this subsection apply in this Act.

  [[advance poll]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[advance poll]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a vote held under Part
      10. ([vote par anticipation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[advance polling station]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[advance polling station]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a polling
      station established under subsection 168(3). ([bureau de vote par
      anticipation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[broadcaster]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[broadcaster]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who is licensed
      by the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission
      under the [Broadcasting Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01) to carry on a
      programming undertaking. ([radiodiffuseur]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[broadcasting]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[broadcasting]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means broadcasting, as
      defined in subsection 2(1) of the [Broadcasting
      Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01), that is regulated and supervised by the
      Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission
      pursuant to section 5 of that
      Act. ([radiodiffusion]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[Broadcasting Arbitrator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[Broadcasting Arbitrator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the person
      appointed as Broadcasting Arbitrator under subsection
      332(1). ([arbitre]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[by-election]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[by-election]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an election other than a
      general election. ([élection partielle]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[candidate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[candidate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person whose nomination
      as a candidate at an election has been confirmed under subsection
      71(1) and who, or whose official agent, has not yet complied with
      sections 477.59 to 477.72 and 477.8 to 477.84 in respect of that
      election. ([candidat]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[capital asset]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[capital asset]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any property with a
      commercial value of more than \$200 that

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a registered party, an electoral
        district association or a candidate, is normally used outside an
        election period other than for the purposes of an election;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a nomination contestant, is
        normally used outside a nomination contest other than for the
        purposes of a nomination contest; and

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a leadership contestant, is
        normally used outside a leadership contest other than for the
        purposes of a leadership contest. ([bien
        immobilisé]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[chief agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[chief agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the chief agent named in
      the application of a political party to become a registered party
      as required under paragraph 385(2)(h) or a chief agent's
      replacement appointed under subsection 400(1). ([agent
      principal]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[close of nominations]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[close of nominations]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the deadline
      for the receipt of nominations set out in subsection
      70(2). ([clôture des candidatures]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[closing day for nominations]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[closing day for nominations]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the day
      referred to in section 69. ([jour de clôture]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[commercial value]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[commercial value]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to property
      or a service, means the lowest amount charged at the time that it
      was provided for the same kind and quantity of property or service
      or for the same usage of property or money, by

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person who provided it, if the person is in
        the business of providing that property or service; or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} another person who provides that property or
        service on a commercial basis in the area where it was provided,
        if the person who provided the property or service is not in
        that business. ([valeur commerciale]{.DefinedTermLink
        lang="fr"})

  [[Commissioner]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[Commissioner]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the Commissioner of
      Canada Elections appointed under subsection
      509(1). ([commissaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[common-law partner]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[common-law partner]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to an
      individual, means a person who is cohabiting with the individual
      in a conjugal relationship, having so cohabited for a period of at
      least one year. ([conjoint de fait]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a monetary contribution
      or a non-monetary contribution. ([contribution]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[election]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[election]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an election of a member to
      serve in the House of Commons. ([élection]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[election advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[election advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      transmission to the public by any means during an election period
      of an advertising message that promotes or opposes a registered
      party or the election of a candidate, including by taking a
      position on an issue with which a registered party or candidate is
      associated. For greater certainty, it does not include

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the transmission to the public of an editorial,
        a debate, a speech, an interview, a column, a letter, a
        commentary or news;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distribution of a book, or the promotion of
        the sale of a book, for no less than its commercial value, if
        the book was planned to be made available to the public
        regardless of whether there was to be an election;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of a document directly by a
        person or a group to their members, employees or shareholders,
        as the case may be;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the transmission by an individual, on a
        non-commercial basis on the Internet, of his or her personal
        political views; or

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the making of telephone calls to electors only
        to encourage them to vote. ([publicité
        électorale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[election advertising expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[election advertising expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
      expense incurred in relation to

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the production of an election advertising
        message; and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of an election advertising
        message to the public. ([dépenses de publicité
        électorale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[election documents]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[election documents]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the following
      documents:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the writ with the return of the election
        endorsed on it;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the nomination papers and other documents filed
        by the candidates or filed on their behalf under section 67;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the reserve supply of undistributed blank
        ballot papers;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} documents relating to the revision of the lists
        of electors;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the statements of the vote from which the
        validation of results was made;

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the other documents sent to the Chief Electoral
        Officer from the various polling stations, the various advance
        polling stations or the returning officer's office, including

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} stubs and unused ballot papers,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} ballot papers cast for the various
          candidates,

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} spoiled ballot papers,

        - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} rejected ballot papers,

        - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the list of electors used at the polling
          station, advance polling station or returning officer's
          office,

        - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} written authorizations of candidates'
          representatives,

        - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} used transfer certificates, if any, and

        - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} registration certificates; and

      - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed forms referred to in section 162
        --- other than those referred to in paragraph 162(i.1) --- and
        any other prescribed form to be used at a polling station,
        advance polling station or returning officer's office that
        contains personal information relating to an
        elector. ([documents électoraux]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[election officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[election officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person referred
      to in subsection 22(1) or appointed under section
      32. ([fonctionnaire électoral]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[election period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[election period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the period beginning
      with the issue of the writ and ending on polling day or, if the
      writ is withdrawn under subsection 59(1) or is deemed to be
      withdrawn under subsection 31(3) of the [Parliament of Canada
      Act](/eng/acts/P-1), on the day that the writ is withdrawn or
      deemed to be withdrawn. ([période électorale]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[election survey]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[election survey]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a survey respecting
      whether persons intend to vote at an election or who they voted
      for or will vote for at an election or respecting an issue with
      which a registered party or candidate is associated. ([sondage
      électoral]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[elector]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[elector]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who is qualified as
      an elector under section 3. ([électeur]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[electoral district]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[electoral district]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a place or
      territorial area that is represented by a member in the House of
      Commons. ([circonscription]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[electoral district agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[electoral district agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person
      appointed under subsection 456(1), and includes the financial
      agent of a registered association. ([agent de
      circonscription]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[electoral district association]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[electoral district association]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
      association of members of a political party in an electoral
      district. ([association de circonscription]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[eligible party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[eligible party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a political party
      that satisfies the criteria for registration set out in section
      387. ([parti admissible]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[future elector]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[future elector]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a Canadian citizen
      who is 14 years of age or older but under 18 years of age. ([futur
      électeur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[judge]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[judge]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, when used to define the judicial
      officer on whom is conferred specific powers, means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the Province of Ontario, a judge
        of the Superior Court of Justice;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the Province of Quebec, a judge
        of the Superior Court of Quebec;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the Provinces of Nova Scotia,
        British Columbia and Prince Edward Island, a judge of the
        Supreme Court of the Province;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the Provinces of New Brunswick,
        Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta, a judge of the Court of
        Queen's Bench of the Province;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the Province of Newfoundland and
        Labrador, a judge of the Trial Division of the Supreme Court of
        Newfoundland and Labrador;

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the electoral district of Yukon,
        a judge of the Supreme Court of Yukon;

      - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the electoral district of the
        Northwest Territories, a judge of the Supreme Court of the
        Northwest Territories;

      - [(h)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the electoral district of
        Nunavut, a judge of the Nunavut Court of Justice; and

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in relation to any place or territory in
        Canada,

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if a vacancy exists or arises in the office
          of any such judge or if such a judge is unable to act by
          reason of illness or absence from their judicial district, the
          judge exercising the jurisdiction of that judge,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if there is more than one judge exercising
          that jurisdiction, the senior of them, and

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} if no judge is exercising that
          jurisdiction, a judge designated for the purpose by the
          Minister of Justice. ([juge]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[leadership campaign agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[leadership campaign agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person
      appointed under subsection 478.5(1), and includes the financial
      agent of a leadership contestant. ([agent de campagne à la
      direction]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[leadership campaign expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[leadership campaign expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      2018, c. 20, s. 1\]]{.Repealed}

  [[leadership contest]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[leadership contest]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a competition for
      the selection of the leader of a registered party. ([course à la
      direction]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[leadership contestant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[leadership contestant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who
      has been registered in the registry of leadership contestants
      referred to in section 478.4 in respect of a leadership contest
      and who, or whose financial agent, has not yet complied with
      sections 478.8 to 478.97 in respect of that leadership
      contest. ([candidat à la direction]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the list showing
      the surname, given names, civic address and mailing address of
      every elector in a polling division and the identifier that is
      assigned to the elector by the Chief Electoral Officer.  ([liste
      électorale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a member of the House of
      Commons. ([député]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[Minister]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[Minister]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the member of the Queen's
      Privy Council for Canada designated by the Governor in Council for
      the purposes of this Act. ([ministre]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[monetary contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[monetary contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an amount of
      money provided that is not repayable. ([contribution
      monétaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[National Capital Region]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[National Capital Region]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the National
      Capital Region as described in the schedule to the [National
      Capital Act](/eng/acts/N-4). ([région de la capitale
      nationale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[nomination campaign expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[nomination campaign expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      2018, c. 20, s. 1\]]{.Repealed}

  [[nomination contest]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[nomination contest]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a competition for
      the selection of a person to be proposed to a registered party for
      its endorsement as its candidate in an electoral
      district. ([course à l'investiture]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[nomination contestant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[nomination contestant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who
      is named as a nomination contestant under paragraph 476.1(1)(c) in
      a report filed in accordance with subsection 476.1(1) in respect
      of a nomination contest and who, or whose financial agent, has not
      yet complied with sections 476.75 to 476.94 in respect of that
      nomination contest. ([candidat à l'investiture]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[non-monetary contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[non-monetary contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      commercial value of a service, other than volunteer labour, or of
      property or of the use of property or money to the extent that
      they are provided without charge or at less than their commercial
      value. ([contribution non monétaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[oath]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[oath]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes a solemn affirmation and a
      statutory declaration. ([serment]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[official agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[official agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person appointed
      under subsection 477.1(1) or an official agent's replacement
      appointed under section 477.42. ([agent officiel]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[official list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[official list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the list
      of electors prepared by the returning officer under section
      106. ([liste électorale officielle]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[partisan advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[partisan advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      transmission to the public by any means during a pre-election
      period of an advertising message that promotes or opposes a
      registered party or eligible party or the election of a potential
      candidate, nomination contestant or leader of a registered party
      or eligible party, otherwise than by taking a position on an issue
      with which any such party or person is associated. For greater
      certainty, it does not include

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the transmission to the public of an editorial,
        a debate, a speech, an interview, a column, a letter, a
        commentary or news;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distribution of a book, or the promotion of
        the sale of a book, for no less than its commercial value, if
        the book was planned to be made available to the public
        regardless of whether there was to be an election;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of a document by a Senator or
        a member the expense of which is paid by the Senate or House of
        Commons;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of a document directly by a
        person or a group to their members, employees or shareholders,
        as the case may be;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the transmission by an individual, on a
        non-commercial basis on the Internet, of his or her personal
        political views; or

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the making of telephone calls to electors only
        to encourage them to vote. ([publicité
        partisane]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[partisan advertising expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[partisan advertising expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
      expense incurred in relation to

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the production of a partisan advertising
        message; and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of a partisan advertising
        message to the public. ([dépenses de publicité
        partisane]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[periodical publication]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[periodical publication]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a paper,
      magazine or periodical that is published periodically or in parts
      or numbers and that contains public news, intelligence or reports
      of events, or advertisements. ([publication
      périodique]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[personal information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[personal information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means personal
      information as defined in section 3 of the [Privacy
      Act](/eng/acts/P-21). ([renseignements
      personnels]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[political affiliation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[political affiliation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a
      candidate, means the name of the political party that has endorsed
      him or her or the word "independent", as the case may be, included
      in the nomination paper in accordance with subparagraph
      66(1)(a)(v). ([appartenance politique]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[political party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[political party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an organization one
      of whose fundamental purposes is to participate in public affairs
      by endorsing one or more of its members as candidates and
      supporting their election. ([parti politique]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[polling day]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[polling day]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to an election,
      means the date fixed for voting at the election under paragraph
      57(1.2)(c) or subsection 59(4) or 77(2). ([jour du
      scrutin]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[polling division]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[polling division]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a polling division
      referred to in section 538. ([section de vote]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[polling station]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[polling station]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a place established
      under section 120, 122, 125, 205, 206, 207, 253 or 255 for
      electors to cast their votes. ([bureau de
      scrutin]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[potential candidate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[potential candidate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person whose
      nomination as a candidate at an election has not been confirmed
      under subsection 71(1) but who

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is selected in a nomination contest;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is deemed to be a candidate under section 477;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is a member or, if Parliament is dissolved, was
        a member on the day before the dissolution; or

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} has the support of a political party to be a
        candidate of that party. ([candidat potentiel]{.DefinedTermLink
        lang="fr"})

  [[pre-election period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[pre-election period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the period
      beginning on the June 30 before the day set in accordance with
      subsection 56.1(2) for the holding of a general election and
      ending on the day before the earlier of

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the first day of an election period for a
        general election, and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the 37th day before the Monday referred to in
        subsection 56.1(2) or, if the Governor in Council makes an order
        under subsection 56.2(3), the 37th day before the alternate day
        referred to in that order. ([période
        préélectorale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[preliminary list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[preliminary list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      list of electors prepared by the Chief Electoral Officer under
      subsection 93(1). ([liste électorale
      préliminaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[prescribed]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[prescribed]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to a form or a
      solemn declaration, means one that is authorized by the Chief
      Electoral Officer. ([prescrit]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[recount]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[recount]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a recount of votes by a
      judge under Part 14. ([dépouillement judiciaire]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[registered agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[registered agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person appointed
      under subsection 396(1), and includes the chief agent of a
      registered party. ([agent enregistré]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[registered association]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[registered association]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an electoral
      district association that is registered in the registry of
      electoral district associations referred to in section
      455. ([association enregistrée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[registered party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[registered party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a political party
      that is registered in the registry of political parties referred
      to in section 394 as a registered party. ([parti
      enregistré]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[Register of Electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[Register of Electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the Register of
      Electors established under paragraph 44(1)(a). ([Registre des
      électeurs]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[Register of Future Electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[Register of Future Electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      Register of Future Electors established under paragraph
      44(1)(b). ([Registre des futurs électeurs]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[revised list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[revised list of electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the list of
      electors prepared by the returning officer under section
      105. ([liste électorale révisée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[spoiled]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[spoiled]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to a ballot or a
      special ballot as defined in section 177, means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one that has not been deposited in the ballot
        box but has been found by an election officer or a [[unit
        election officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in section
        177 to be soiled or improperly printed; or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} one that is dealt with under subsection 152(1),
        including in relation to advance polls by virtue of subsection
        171(1), or subsection 213(4), 242(1) or
        258(3). ([annulé]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[volunteer labour]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[volunteer labour]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any service
      provided free of charge by a person outside their working hours,
      but does not include such a service provided by a person who is
      self-employed if the service is one that is normally charged for
      by that person. ([travail bénévole]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[writ]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[writ]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a writ of
      election. ([bref]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Commercial value of capital assets

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Act, the commercial value
  of any capital asset that is used during a nomination contest, an
  election period or a leadership contest, as the case may be, is the
  lower of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the commercial value of the rental of the same kind
    of asset during the period during which the capital asset was used,
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the commercial value of the same kind of asset if
    one were purchased.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No commercial value

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Act, other than section
  477.9, the commercial value of property or a service is deemed to be
  nil if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the property or service is provided by a Canadian
    citizen, or a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of
    the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), who
    is not in the business of providing that property or service; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the commercial value of the property or service is
    \$200 or less.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Satisfactory proof of identity and
  residence

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Act, satisfactory proof of
  identity and satisfactory proof of residence are established in the
  manner determined by the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A reference to a time of day in this Act is a
  reference to local time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Descriptive cross-references

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If, in any provision of this Act, a reference to
  another provision of this Act or a provision of any other Act is
  followed by words in parentheses that are or purport to be descriptive
  of the subject-matter of the provision referred to, those words form
  no part of the provision in which they occur but are inserted for
  convenience of reference only.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[polling
  day]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a writ for an election is withdrawn under
  subsection 59(1) or is deemed to be withdrawn under subsection 31(3)
  of the [Parliament of Canada Act](/eng/acts/P-1), then, in Parts 16.1
  and 17 and Divisions 1, 2, 4 and 5 of Part 18, [[polling
  day]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the day that the writ is withdrawn or
  deemed to be withdrawn.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions of [[election
  advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} and [[partisan
  advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of the definitions [[election
  advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} and [[partisan
  advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, promoting or opposing includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in relation to a registered party or eligible
    party,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} naming it,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} identifying it, including by its logo, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} providing a link to an Internet page that does
      anything referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the election of a potential
    candidate, a nomination contestant, a candidate or a leader of a
    registered party or eligible party,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} naming him or her,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} showing a photograph, cartoon or drawing of him
      or her,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} identifying him or her, including by political
      affiliation or by any logo that he or she has, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} providing a link to an Internet page that does
      anything referred to in subparagraphs (i) to (iii).

## [PART 1]{.HLabel1}[Electoral Rights]{.HTitleText1} {#h-203583 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Persons qualified as electors

**[[3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-3 .sectionLabel}** Every person who is a
Canadian citizen and who on polling day is 18 years of age or older is
qualified as an elector.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 3
- [2018, c. 31, s. 3](#1041245-1131125){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041245-1131125.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-3-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 3"){.PITLink}

s. 3\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-4-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 4"){.PITLink}

**[[5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-5 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31,
s. 3\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-5-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 5"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Persons entitled to vote

**[[6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-6 .sectionLabel}** Subject to this Act, every
person who is qualified as an elector is entitled to have his or her
name included in the list of electors for the polling division in which
he or she is ordinarily resident and to vote at the polling station for
that polling division.

**[[7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-7 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31,
s. 4\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-7-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 7"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place of ordinary residence

- **[[8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-8 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  place of ordinary residence of a person is the place that has always
  been, or that has been adopted as, his or her dwelling place, and to
  which the person intends to return when away from it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}One place of residence only

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person can have only one place of ordinary
  residence and it cannot be lost until another is gained.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person residing outside Canada

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The place of ordinary residence of a person who
  resides outside Canada is their last place of ordinary residence in
  Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary absence

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Temporary absence from a place of ordinary residence
  does not cause a loss or change of place of ordinary residence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place of employment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a person usually sleeps in one place and has their
  meals or is employed in another place, their place of ordinary
  residence is where they sleep.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary residence

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Temporary residential quarters are considered to be a
  person's place of ordinary residence only if the person has no other
  place that they consider to be their residence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary residential quarters

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A shelter, hostel or similar institution that
  provides food, lodging or other social services to a person who has no
  dwelling place is that person's place of ordinary residence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 8
- [2018, c. 31, s. 5](#1041248-1130837){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041248-1130837.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-8-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 8"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interpretation of ordinary residence

**[[9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-9 .sectionLabel}** If the rules set out in
section 8 are not sufficient to determine the place of ordinary
residence, it shall be determined by the appropriate election officer by
reference to all the facts of the case.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Former member candidates and electors
living with them

- **[[10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-10 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  candidate at a general election who, on the day before the dissolution
  of Parliament immediately before the election, was a member, and any
  elector living with the candidate on that day who would move, or has
  moved, with the candidate to continue to live with the candidate, is
  entitled to have his or her name entered on the list of electors for,
  and to vote at the polling station to which is assigned, the polling
  division in which is located

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the place of ordinary residence of the former
    member; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 6\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the office of the returning officer for the
    electoral district in which the former member is a candidate.

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 6\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Former member candidates and electors
  living with them --- notice to returning officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a candidate or elector referred to in
  subsection (1) provides notice to the returning officer, at least two
  days before polling day, of his or her intention to vote at the
  polling station, the candidate or elector is entitled to have his or
  her name entered on the list of electors for, and to vote at the
  polling station to which is assigned, any polling division in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the electoral district in which the former member
    is a candidate; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the electoral district in the National Capital
    Region where the former member resides for the purpose of carrying
    out parliamentary duties.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 10
- [2018, c. 31, s. 6](#1041256-1131147){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041256-1131147.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-10-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 10"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-11 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31,
s. 7\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-11-20050401.html "Link to previous version of section 11"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Residence at by-election

- **[[12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-12 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  elector is entitled to vote at a by-election unless his or her place
  of ordinary residence on polling day is situated in the same electoral
  district that includes the polling division in which was situated the
  elector's place of ordinary residence at the beginning of the revision
  period established by section 96.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Address change within electoral
  district

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of a by-election only and despite
  anything in this Act, an elector who, during the period between the
  beginning of the revision period and ending on polling day, has
  changed his or her place of ordinary residence from one polling
  division to another polling division in the same electoral district
  may register his or her name on the list of electors in the new
  polling division.

## [PART 2]{.HLabel1}[Chief Electoral Officer and Staff]{.HTitleText1} {#h-203635 .Part}

### [Chief Electoral Officer]{.HTitleText2} {#h-203636 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment and term of office

- **[[13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-13 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} There
  shall be a Chief Electoral Officer who shall be appointed by
  resolution of the House of Commons to hold office during good
  behaviour for a term of 10 years. He or she may be removed for cause
  by the Governor General on address of the Senate and House of Commons.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No re-appointment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who has served as Chief Electoral Officer is
  not eligible for re-appointment to that office.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 13
- 2014, c. 12, s. 3
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-13-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 13"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of substitute

- **[[14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-14 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  case of the death, incapacity or negligence of the Chief Electoral
  Officer while Parliament is not sitting, a substitute Chief Electoral
  Officer shall, on the application of the Minister, be appointed by
  order of the Chief Justice of Canada or, in the absence of the Chief
  Justice of Canada, by the senior judge of the Supreme Court of Canada
  then present in Ottawa.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tenure of office of substitute

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A substitute Chief Electoral Officer shall act as
  Chief Electoral Officer until 15 days after the beginning of the next
  session of Parliament unless the Chief Justice of Canada or the judge
  who made the order to appoint the substitute Chief Electoral Officer
  sooner directs that the order be revoked.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Absence of Chief Justice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the absence of both the Chief Justice of Canada
  and of the judge who made the order to appoint the substitute Chief
  Electoral Officer, the order may be revoked by any other judge of the
  Supreme Court of Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remuneration of substitute

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The substitute Chief Electoral Officer is entitled to
  be paid the remuneration fixed by the Governor in Council.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rank, powers and duties

- **[[15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections 509.1(2) and
  (3), the Chief Electoral Officer shall rank as and have all the powers
  of a deputy head of a department, shall perform the duties of the
  office on a full-time basis and shall not hold any other office under
  Her Majesty or engage in any other employment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Salary and expenses of Chief Electoral
  Officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall be paid a salary
  equal to the salary of a judge of the Federal Court, other than the
  Chief Justice of that Court, and is entitled to be paid reasonable
  travel and living expenses while absent from his or her ordinary place
  of residence in the course of his or her duties.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superannuation and compensation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer is deemed to be employed
  in the public service for the purposes of the [Public Service
  Superannuation Act](/eng/acts/P-36) and to be employed in the federal
  public administration for the purposes of the [Government Employees
  Compensation Act](/eng/acts/G-5) and any regulations made under
  section 9 of the [Aeronautics Act](/eng/acts/A-2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Communication with Governor in Council

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall communicate with
  the Governor in Council through the Minister for the purposes of this
  Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 15
- 2002, c. 8, s. 116
- 2003, c. 22, s. 101(E)
- [2018, c. 31, s. 8](#1041265-1111196){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041265-1111196.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-15-20050401.html "Link to previous version of section 15"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers and duties of Chief Electoral
Officer

**[[16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} exercise general direction and supervision over the
  conduct of elections;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that all election officers act with fairness
  and impartiality and in compliance with this Act;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} issue to election officers the instructions that the
  Chief Electoral Officer considers necessary for the administration of
  this Act; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} exercise the powers and perform the duties and
  functions that are necessary for the administration of this Act, other
  than Division 1.1 of Part 16.1.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 16
- 2014, c. 12, s. 4
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-16-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 16"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Guidelines and interpretation notes

- **[[16.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall,
  in accordance with this section, issue guidelines and interpretation
  notes on the application of this Act --- other than Division 1.1 of
  Part 16.1 --- to registered parties, registered associations,
  nomination contestants, candidates and leadership contestants.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, in accordance with
  this section, on application by the chief agent of a registered party,
  issue a guideline or interpretation note on the application of a
  provision of this Act --- other than a provision of Division 1.1 of
  Part 16.1 --- to registered parties, registered associations,
  nomination contestants, candidates and leadership contestants.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consultations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Before issuing a guideline or interpretation note,
  the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide a copy of the proposed
  guideline or interpretation note to the Commissioner and to the
  members of the Advisory Committee of Political Parties established by
  subsection 21.1(1). The Commissioner and those members may provide
  their written comments to the Chief Electoral Officer within 45 days
  after the day on which the copy is sent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Comments

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, in preparing the
  guideline or interpretation note, take into consideration any comments
  received under subsection (3).

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 9\]]{.Repealed}

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 9\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issuance

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall issue the guideline
  or interpretation note by registering it in the registry referred to
  in section 16.4 as soon as possible after preparing it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nature of guidelines and interpretation
  notes

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The guidelines and interpretation notes are issued
  for information purposes only. They are not binding on registered
  parties, registered associations, nomination contestants, candidates
  or leadership contestants.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 5, 153
- [2018, c. 31, s. 9](#1041276-1111203){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041276-1111203.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-16.1-20150802.html "Link to previous version of section 16.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for written opinion

- **[[16.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall,
  in accordance with this section, on application by the chief agent of
  a registered party, issue a written opinion on the application of any
  provision of this Act --- other than a provision of Division 1.1 of
  Part 16.1 --- to an activity or practice that the registered party or
  a registered association, nomination contestant, candidate or
  leadership contestant of the registered party proposes to engage in.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consultations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before issuing an opinion, the Chief Electoral
  Officer shall provide a copy of the proposed opinion to the
  Commissioner and to the members of the Advisory Committee of Political
  Parties established by subsection 21.1(1). The Commissioner and those
  members may provide their written comments to the Chief Electoral
  Officer within 30 days after the day on which the copy is sent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Comments

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, in preparing the
  opinion, take into consideration any comments received under
  subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Pre-publication

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Within 90 days after the day on which the application
  is made, the Chief Electoral Officer shall publish on his or her
  Internet site for a period of 30 days the opinion as well as a notice
  stating that the opinion will be issued at the expiry of that period.
  However, if the 90-day period coincides or overlaps with the election
  period of a general election, the opinion and the notice shall be
  published no later than 90 days after polling day for that election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issuance

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} On the expiry of the 30-day period referred to in
  subsection (4), the Chief Electoral Officer shall issue the opinion by
  registering it in the registry referred to in section 16.4.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opinion binding

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If all the material facts have been submitted by an
  applicant for an opinion and they are accurate, the opinion issued by
  the Chief Electoral Officer under this section is binding on the Chief
  Electoral Officer and the Commissioner with respect to the activity or
  practice of the registered party, registered association, nomination
  contestant, candidate or leadership contestant in question. It remains
  binding for as long as the material facts on which it was based remain
  substantially unchanged and the activity or practice is carried out
  substantially as proposed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Precedential value

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} An opinion issued by the Chief Electoral Officer
  under this section has precedential value for the Chief Electoral
  Officer and the Commissioner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contrary interpretation

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The opinion remains binding in accordance with
  subsection (6), and has the precedential value referred to in
  subsection (7), for as long as a contrary interpretation has not been
  subsequently issued by means of a guideline or interpretation note
  issued under section 16.1 or an opinion issued under this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 5, 153

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New interpretation

**[[16.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.3 .sectionLabel}** If an opinion that is
published under subsection 16.2(4) interprets a provision of the Act in
a way that contradicts an interpretation of that provision provided in a
previously issued opinion, the new interpretation does not replace the
former interpretation until the date that the new opinion is issued
under section 16.2.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registry

**[[16.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-16.4 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall establish and maintain a registry on his or her Internet
site that contains every guideline and interpretation note that is
issued under section 16.1, every opinion that is issued under section
16.2 and all comments of the Commissioner that are provided under
subsection 16.1(3) or 16.2(2).

  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s.
  12\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to disclose documents and

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the request of the Commissioner, the Chief
  Electoral Officer shall disclose to the Commissioner any document or
  information that the Chief Electoral Officer obtained under this Act
  and that the Commissioner considers necessary to the exercise or
  performance of his or her powers, duties and functions under this Act.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to adapt Act

- **[[17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-17 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} During
  an election period or within 30 days after it, if an emergency, an
  unusual or unforeseen circumstance or an error makes it necessary, the
  Chief Electoral Officer may, for the sole purpose of enabling electors
  to exercise their right to vote or enabling the counting of votes,
  adapt any provision of this Act and, in particular, may extend the
  time for doing any act, subject to subsection (2), or may increase the
  number of election officers or polling stations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation --- power to adapt

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall not extend the
  voting hours at an advance polling station or, subject to subsection
  (3), the voting hours on polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Emergency --- extending voting hours

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If voting at a polling station is interrupted on
  polling day by an emergency and the Chief Electoral Officer is
  satisfied that, if the voting hours at the polling station are not
  extended, a substantial number of electors will not be able to vote,
  the Chief Electoral Officer shall extend the voting hours at the
  polling station for the period the Chief Electoral Officer considers
  necessary to give those electors a reasonable opportunity to vote, as
  long as the polling station does not in any case

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} close later than midnight on polling day; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} remain open during polling day for a total of more
    than 12 hours.

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Public education and information programs

- **[[18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-18 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer may implement public education and information
  programs to make the electoral process better known to the public,
  particularly to those persons and groups most likely to experience
  difficulties in exercising their democratic rights.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Communication with public

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may, using any media or
  other means that he or she considers appropriate, provide the public,
  both inside and outside Canada, with information relating to Canada's
  electoral process and the democratic rights to vote and to be a
  candidate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information outside Canada

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may establish programs
  to disseminate information outside Canada concerning how to vote under
  Part 11.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Communication with electors with a
  disability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall ensure that any
  information on the following that is provided under subsections (1) to
  (1.2) in an advertising message is accessible to electors with a
  disability:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} how to become a candidate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} how an elector may have their name added to a list
    of electors and may have corrections made to information respecting
    them on the list;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} how an elector may vote under section 127 and the
    times, dates and locations for voting;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} how an elector may prove their identity and
    residence in order to vote, including the pieces of identification
    that they may use to that end; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the measures for assisting electors with a
    disability to access a polling station or advance polling station or
    to mark a ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Communication with future electors with
  a disability

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} If the Chief Electoral Officer provides, in an
  advertising message, any information under subsections (1) and (1.1)
  on how a future elector may have their name added to the Register of
  Future Electors and may have corrections made to information
  respecting them in that register, the Chief Electoral Officer shall
  ensure that the information is accessible to future electors with a
  disability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unsolicited calls

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall not provide
  information under this section by the use of calls, as defined in
  section 348.01, that are unsolicited.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 18
- 2014, c. 12, s. 7
- [2018, c. 31, s. 14](#1041313-1111161){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041313-1111161.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}International cooperation

**[[18.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-18.01 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may provide assistance and cooperation in electoral matters to
electoral agencies in other countries or to international organizations.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 8
- [2018, c. 31, s. 15](#1041317-1111164){.wb-lbx

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting studies

- **[[18.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-18.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may
  carry out studies on voting, including studies respecting alternative
  voting means.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Alternative voting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may devise and test an
  alternative voting process for future use in an election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting technology --- electors with a
  disability

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall develop, obtain or
  adapt voting technology for use by electors with a disability, and may
  test the technology for future use in an election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prior approval

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Neither an alternative voting process nor voting
  technology tested under subsection (2) or (3) may be used in an
  election without the prior approval of the committees of the Senate
  and of the House of Commons that normally consider electoral matters.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 18.1

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to enter into contracts, etc.

- **[[18.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-18.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may
  enter into contracts, memoranda of understanding or other arrangements
  in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada or in the Chief
  Electoral Officer's name in the exercise or performance of his or her
  powers, duties and functions under this Act or any other Act of
  Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Leases

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may authorize a returning
  officer to enter into a lease in the Chief Electoral Officer's name,
  subject to any terms and conditions that the Chief Electoral Officer
  specifies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contracts, etc., binding on Her Majesty

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every contract, memorandum of understanding and
  arrangement entered into in the Chief Electoral Officer's name is
  binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada to the same extent as it is
  binding on the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Goods and services

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 9 of the [Department of Public Works
  and Government Services Act](/eng/acts/P-38.2), the Chief Electoral
  Officer may procure goods and services from outside the federal public
  administration.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 8

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Signature

**[[18.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-18.3 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under a
provision of this Act for a signature may be satisfied in any manner
that the Chief Electoral Officer authorizes.

::: HistoricalNote

:::

### [Staff]{.HTitleText2} {#h-203779 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Staff

**[[19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-19 .sectionLabel}** The staff of the Chief
Electoral Officer consists of employees appointed in accordance with the
[Public Service Employment Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Technical assistance

- **[[20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-20 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer may engage on a temporary basis the services
  of persons having technical or specialized knowledge of any matter
  relating to the Chief Electoral Officer's work to advise and assist
  him or her in the exercise or performance of his or her powers, duties
  and functions under this or any other Act of Parliament and, with the
  Treasury Board's approval, may fix and pay those persons' remuneration
  and expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Casual and temporary staff

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any additional employees that the Chief Electoral
  Officer considers necessary for the exercise or performance of his or
  her powers, duties and functions under this Act that are related to
  the preparation for, and the conduct of, an election may be employed
  on a casual or temporary basis in accordance with the [Public Service
  Employment Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation

**[[21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-21 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may delegate to any member of his or her staff, subject to any
limitations that he or she may specify, any of his or her powers, duties
and functions under this or any other Act of Parliament, except the
power to delegate.

### [Advisory Committee of Political Parties]{.HTitleText2} {#h-203796 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Establishment

- **[[21.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-21.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  committee is established, to be known as the Advisory Committee of
  Political Parties, consisting of the Chief Electoral Officer and two
  representatives of each registered party appointed by the party's
  leader.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Purpose

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The purpose of the committee is to provide the Chief
  Electoral Officer with advice and recommendations relating to
  elections and political financing.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advice and recommendations not binding

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The committee's advice and recommendations are not
  binding on the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meetings

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The committee shall meet at least once a year and its
  meetings shall be presided over by the Chief Electoral Officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 11
:::

## [PART 3]{.HLabel1}[Election Officers]{.HTitleText1} {#h-203808 .Part}

### [General]{.HTitleText2} {#h-203809 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election officers

- **[[22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-22 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  following persons are election officers:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} field liaison officers appointed under section
    23.2;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} returning officers appointed under subsection
    24(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} assistant returning officers appointed under
    subsection 26(1) or 28(5) and additional assistant returning
    officers appointed under subsection 30(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} persons authorized by a returning officer under
    section 27 to exercise powers or perform duties under this Act;

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} persons designated pursuant to subsection
    28(3.1);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(g.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the special voting rules administrator appointed
    under section 181;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} special ballot officers appointed under subsection
    183(1) or section 184; and

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} liaison officers for correctional institutions
    appointed under subsection 248(1).

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 20\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election officers --- exclusions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, a representative of a
  candidate who is present at a polling station is not an election
  officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Who shall not be appointed election
  officers

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The following persons shall not be appointed as an
  election officer:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a minister of the Crown or a member of the
    executive council of a province;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a member of the Senate or the House of Commons;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a member of the legislative assembly of a province;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a judge or deputy judge of any superior court or
    any bankruptcy or insolvency court and, in Yukon and the Northwest
    Territories, a judge of the Supreme Court;

  - [(d.1)]{.lawlabel} a person who was a candidate at the last general
    election or at a by-election held since the last general election;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a person who has served in Parliament in the
    session immediately before the election or in the session in
    progress at the time of the election; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who, within seven years before the
    proposed appointment, has been found guilty of any offence under
    this Act or the [Referendum Act](/eng/acts/R-4.7), or a regulation
    made under the [Referendum Act](/eng/acts/R-4.7), or under an Act of
    the legislature of a province, or a regulation made under an Act of
    the legislature of a province, relating to provincial, municipal or
    school board elections.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Qualifications

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An election officer must be qualified as an elector,
  and an election officer referred to in paragraph (1)(a.1) or (b) must
  reside in the electoral district in which he or she is to exercise
  powers or perform duties under this Act or in an adjacent electoral
  district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election officers younger than 18

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (4), an election officer appointed
  under section 32 may be under 18 years of age but must be at least 16
  years of age.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- acting as election
  officer

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} No person shall act as an election officer knowing
  that they do not meet the requirements for an election officer set out
  in this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 22
- 2002, c. 7, s. 91
- 2006, c. 9, s. 173
- 2014, c. 2, s. 48, c. 12, s. 12
- [2018, c. 31, s. 20](#1041335-1111206){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041335-1111206.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-22-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 22"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solemn declaration

- **[[23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-23 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before
  assuming duties, an election officer shall make, in writing, a solemn
  declaration, in the prescribed form, that he or she will exercise the
  powers and perform the duties of the office in an impartial manner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No election officer shall communicate information, or
  use personal information, that is obtained in the course of exercising
  his or her powers or performing his or her duties under this Act,
  other than for a purpose related to the exercise of those powers or
  the performance of those duties.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sending of solemn declarations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall send his or her solemn
  declaration and that of the assistant returning officer without delay
  to the Chief Electoral Officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 23
- [2018, c. 31, s. 21](#1041357-1131173){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041357-1131173.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-23-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 23"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unsolicited calls

**[[23.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-23.1 .sectionLabel}** An election officer
shall not communicate with the public by the use of calls, as defined in
section 348.01, that are unsolicited.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 13
:::

### [Field Liaison Officers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-203863 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of field liaison officers

- **[[23.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-23.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may
  appoint a field liaison officer in respect of a given geographical
  area in accordance with the process established under subsection (2)
  and may remove him or her only in accordance with the procedure
  established under that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Qualifications

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall prescribe the
  qualifications for the appointment of persons as field liaison
  officers and shall establish for field liaison officers an external
  appointment process as defined in subsection 2(1) of the [Public
  Service Employment Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01) on the basis of merit and a
  fair procedure for their removal on the grounds set out in subsection
  (9).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meaning of merit

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The appointment of a person as a field liaison
  officer is made on the basis of merit if the Chief Electoral Officer
  is satisfied that the person meets the essential qualifications for
  the work to be performed and has regard to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any additional qualifications that the Chief
    Electoral Officer considers to be an asset for the work to be
    performed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any current or future operational requirements.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Period of appointment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A field liaison officer shall be appointed for the
  period determined by the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Re-appointment

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may re-appoint any field
  liaison officer who has performed the functions of a field liaison
  officer in a satisfactory manner, regardless of whether or not other
  persons are considered for the appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuation in office

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A field liaison officer may, with the Chief Electoral
  Officer's approval, continue in office after the expiry of the period
  referred to in subsection (4) until the field liaison officer is
  re-appointed or another person is appointed to the office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Responsibilities

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A field liaison officer is responsible, under the
  Chief Electoral Officer's general direction, in respect of the
  geographical area to which they are assigned, for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} providing support to returning officers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} acting as an intermediary between the returning
    officers and the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} on the Chief Electoral Officer's request, providing
    support in relation to the appointment of returning officers.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No partisan conduct

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} No field liaison officer shall knowingly engage in
  politically partisan conduct and in particular shall not make a
  contribution to a nomination contestant, a candidate or a leadership
  contestant or belong to or make a contribution to, be an employee of
  or hold a position in, a registered party, an eligible party or an
  electoral district association.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal from office

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may remove from office
  any field liaison officer who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is incapable, by reason of illness, disability or
    otherwise, of satisfactorily exercising their powers or performing
    their duties under this Act;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fails to competently exercise a field liaison
    officer's powers or competently perform a field liaison officer's
    duties under this Act or to comply with an instruction of the Chief
    Electoral Officer issued under paragraph 16(c); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} contravenes subsection (8), whether or not the
    contravention occurs in the exercise of their powers or the
    performance of their duties under this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 13
- [2018, c. 31, s. 22](#1041368-1111210){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041368-1111210.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-23.2-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 23.2"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-203893 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of returning officers

- **[[24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-24 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall appoint a returning officer for each
  electoral district in accordance with the process established under
  subsection (1.1) and may only remove him or her in accordance with the
  procedure established under that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Qualifications

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall prescribe the
  qualifications for the appointment of persons as returning officers,
  and shall establish for returning officers an external appointment
  process within the meaning of subsection 2(1) of the [Public Service
  Employment Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01) on the basis of merit and a fair
  procedure for their removal on the grounds set out in subsection (7).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meaning of merit

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} The appointment of a person as a returning officer
  is made on the basis of merit if the Chief Electoral Officer is
  satisfied that the person meets the essential qualifications for the
  work to be performed and has regard to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any additional qualifications that the Chief
    Electoral Officer considers to be an asset for the work to be
    performed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any current or future operational requirements.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of office

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer shall be appointed for a term
  of ten years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New term

  [(1.4)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may, after consultation
  with the leader of every recognized political party in the House of
  Commons, appoint for a new term any returning officer who has
  performed the functions of a returning officer in a satisfactory
  manner, whether or not other persons are considered for the
  appointment, if the office of returning officer is vacant by reason of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the expiry of the returning officer's term of
    office; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the revision of the boundaries of the electoral
    district as a result of a representation order made under section 25
    of the [Electoral Boundaries Readjustment Act](/eng/acts/E-3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuation in office

  [(1.5)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer may, with the approval of the
  Chief Electoral Officer, continue in office after his or her term
  expires until he or she is reappointed or until another person is
  appointed to the office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Responsibility of returning officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer is responsible, under the general
  direction of the Chief Electoral Officer, for the preparation for and
  conduct of an election in his or her electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to act to enable elections
  to be held

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every returning officer to whom a writ is directed
  shall, on its receipt, or on notification by the Chief Electoral
  Officer of its issue, cause to be promptly taken any of the
  proceedings directed by this Act that are necessary in order that the
  election may be regularly held.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vacancy

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The office of returning officer does not become
  vacant unless the returning officer dies, resigns, is removed from
  office, reaches the end of his or her term of office or ceases to
  reside in the electoral district, or unless the boundaries of the
  electoral district are revised as a result of a representation order
  made under section 25 of the [Electoral Boundaries Readjustment
  Act](/eng/acts/E-3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resignation

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer who intends to resign shall give
  written notice to that effect to the Chief Electoral Officer and the
  resignation is effective only when it is accepted by the Chief
  Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No partisan conduct

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} No returning officer shall, while in office,
  knowingly engage in politically partisan conduct and in particular
  shall not make a contribution to a nomination contestant, a candidate
  or a leadership contestant or belong to or make a contribution to, be
  an employee of or hold a position in, a registered party, an eligible
  party or an electoral district association.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal from office

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may remove from office
  any returning officer who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is incapable, by reason of illness, disability or
    otherwise, of satisfactorily exercising his or her powers or
    performing his or her duties under this Act;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fails to competently exercise a returning officer's
    power or competently perform a returning officer's duty under this
    Act or to comply with an instruction of the Chief Electoral Officer
    described in paragraph 16(c);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} fails to complete the revision of the boundaries of
    the polling divisions in their electoral district as instructed by
    the Chief Electoral Officer under subsection 538(3); or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} contravenes subsection (6), whether or not the
    contravention occurs in the exercise of his or her powers or the
    performance of his or her duties under this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary suspension

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may temporarily suspend
  from office a returning officer for any grounds set out in subsection
  (7).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duration of suspension

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The period of suspension expires at the end of the
  period that the Chief Electoral Officer considers appropriate.
  However, if a procedure is commenced --- either before or during the
  period of suspension --- that could lead to the returning officer's
  removal, the period of suspension expires on the day on which the
  Chief Electoral Officer makes his or her final decision in that
  regard.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List in [Canada
Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)

**[[25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-25 .sectionLabel}** Between the 1st and 20th
days of January in each year, the Chief Electoral Officer shall publish
a list in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) of the name,
address and occupation of the returning officer for each electoral
district in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 25
- 2006, c. 9, s. 175
:::
