[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assistant returning officer

- **[[26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-26
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Without delay after being appointed,
  a returning officer shall, with the Chief Electoral Officer's prior
  approval of the individual proposed to be appointed, appoint an
  assistant returning officer, who shall hold office at pleasure.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on appointment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer shall not appoint his or her
  spouse, common-law partner, child, mother, father, brother, sister,
  the child of his or her spouse or common-law partner, or a person who
  lives with him or her as an assistant returning officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 26, c. 12, s. 40
- [2018, c. 31, s. 24](#1041395-1131175){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041395-1131175.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-26-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 26"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation

- **[[27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-27 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer for an electoral district may, with the Chief
  Electoral Officer's prior approval, authorize any person acting under
  his or her direction to exercise any of the powers or perform any of
  the duties of a returning officer under this Act, except those
  described in subsection 24(3), sections 62 and 63, subsection 71(1),
  sections 71.1, 74, 77, 130, 293 to 298 and 300, subsection 301(6) and
  sections 313 to 316.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorization in writing

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An authorization under subsection (1) shall be signed
  and dated by the returning officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 27
- 2014, c. 12, s. 15
- [2018, c. 31, s. 25](#1041397-1131177){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041397-1131177.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-27-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 27"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification if returning officer
incapacitated

- **[[28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-28 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} It is
  the duty of a returning officer or an assistant returning officer to
  notify the Chief Electoral Officer without delay if the returning
  officer at any time becomes unable to act.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2006, c. 9, s. 176\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assistant returning officer to act

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 24(1.5), if a returning officer
  is absent or unable to act or if a returning officer's office is
  vacant, the assistant returning officer shall act in place of the
  returning officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designated person to act --- suspension
  of returning officer

  [(3.01)]{.lawlabel} If a returning officer is under suspension during
  the six months before the day set in accordance with subsection
  56.1(2) for the holding of a general election or during any election
  period that falls in whole or in part outside that six-month period,
  the Chief Electoral Officer may designate a person to act in the
  returning officer's place, and that person may, during and after that
  period, exercise the powers and perform the duties of a returning
  officer in relation to that election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designated person to act --- absence of
  returning and assistant returning officers

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} If, during the six months before the day set in
  accordance with subsection 56.1(2) for the holding of a general
  election or during any election period that falls in whole or in part
  outside that six-month period, a returning officer is absent or unable
  to act or a returning officer's office is vacant and, at the same
  time, the assistant returning officer is absent or unable to act or
  the assistant returning officer's office is vacant, the Chief
  Electoral Officer shall designate a person to act in place of the
  returning officer, and that person may, during and after that period,
  exercise the powers and perform the duties of a returning officer in
  relation to that election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment within limited period

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} When the office of a returning officer becomes
  vacant, the Chief Electoral Officer shall appoint a new returning
  officer without delay.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of assistant returning
  officer

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Every assistant returning officer who is required to
  act as a returning officer under subsection (3) shall appoint an
  assistant returning officer without delay.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 28
- 2006, c. 9, s. 176
- 2014, c. 12, s. 16
- [2018, c. 31, s. 26](#1041401-1111223){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041401-1111223.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-28-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 28"){.PITLink}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of returning officer

- **[[29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-29 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  returning officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} without delay after removing an assistant returning
    officer from office, notify the assistant returning officer in
    writing of the removal and send a copy of the notice to the Chief
    Electoral Officer; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} without delay after the death or resignation of an
    assistant returning officer, notify the Chief Electoral Officer in
    writing of the death or resignation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of substitute

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an assistant returning officer dies, resigns,
  becomes disqualified or incapable of acting or refuses to act, or is
  removed from office for any other reason, the returning officer shall
  without delay appoint a substitute with the Chief Electoral Officer's
  prior approval.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tenure of office of assistant returning
  officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} When a returning officer ceases to hold office, the
  assistant returning officer appointed by him or her remains in office
  until the returning officer's successor appoints a new assistant
  returning officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resignation by assistant returning
  officer

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An assistant returning officer who intends to resign
  shall give written notice to the returning officer or, if the office
  of returning officer is vacant, to the Chief Electoral Officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 29
- [2018, c. 31, s. 27](#1041410-1131184){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041410-1131184.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-29-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 29"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional assistant returning officer

- **[[30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-30 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  request by a returning officer, the Chief Electoral Officer may
  designate areas in the returning officer's electoral district and
  authorize, in writing, the appointment of an assistant returning
  officer, in addition to the assistant returning officer appointed
  under subsection 26(1), for each of those areas.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer shall appoint an additional
  assistant returning officer and establish an office in each area
  designated by the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation limited

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An assistant returning officer appointed under
  subsection (2) may perform the functions of an assistant returning
  officer only in respect of the area for which they are appointed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Further limitation

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An assistant returning officer appointed under
  subsection (2) is not an assistant returning officer for the purposes
  of subsections 28(1), 60(2), 70(1) and 293(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 30
- [2018, c. 31, s. 28](#1041415-1111228){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041415-1111228.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-30-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 30"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- acting in another
capacity

**[[31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-31 .sectionLabel}** No returning officer or
assistant returning officer appointed under subsection 26(1) shall act
in any other capacity under this Act.

### [Election Officers Appointed by Returning Officer]{.HTitleText2} {#h-203989 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election officers

- **[[32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-32
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3)
  and 33(2) and (3), a returning officer shall, after the issue of the
  writ, appoint in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's
  instructions the election officers that the returning officer
  considers necessary for exercising election officers' powers and
  performing election officers' duties under this Act in the returning
  officer's electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment before issue of writ

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer may, in accordance with the Chief
  Electoral Officer's instructions, appoint election officers before the
  issue of the writ if the returning officer considers that it is
  desirable to do so for the purpose of training and preparing them to
  exercise their powers and perform their duties under this Act after
  the issue of the writ.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum number of election officers
  appointed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Before the eighth day after the issue of the writ, a
  returning officer shall not appoint more than half the number of
  election officers referred to in subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 32
- 2001, c. 21, s. 3(E)
- [2018, c. 31, s. 29](#1041417-1131193){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041417-1131193.html"}
:::

Version](section-32-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 32"){.PITLink}
:::

31, s. 29\]]{.Repealed}

[Previous

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solicitation of names

- **[[33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-33 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} As
  soon as possible after the issue of the writ, a returning officer
  shall solicit names of persons suitable to be election officers from
  the candidates of registered parties that endorsed candidates in the
  last election in the electoral district or from the registered
  associations of those registered parties --- or, if such a registered
  party has no registered association in that electoral district, from
  that registered party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Persons whose names are provided to be
  appointed

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the number of names provided under subsection (1)
  within seven days after the issue of the writ is less than, or equal
  to, the number of election officers remaining to be appointed under
  subsection 32(1) after the returning officer has appointed election
  officers under section 32, the returning officer shall, subject to
  subsection 37(1), appoint the persons named as election officers.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proportional distribution

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the number of names provided under subsection (1)
  within seven days after the issue of the writ is more than the number
  of election officers remaining to be appointed under subsection 32(1)
  after the returning officer has appointed election officers under
  section 32, the returning officer shall, subject to subsection 37(1),
  appoint from those names the election officers remaining to be
  appointed as far as possible in the proportion of the votes received
  in the last election in the electoral district by the candidates of
  the registered parties whose candidates or registered associations
  provided names under subsection (1), or that themselves provided names
  under that subsection, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal or replacement

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a returning officer removes or replaces an
  election officer, the former election officer shall return all
  election documents and election materials in his or her possession to
  the returning officer or to an authorized person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists of election officers

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Each returning officer shall make available to each
  candidate, on completion of the list, a list of the election officers
  for the electoral district who will be responsible for assisting the
  returning officer or assistant returning officer in the revision of
  lists of electors under Part 7.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Identification

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Each election officer shall, while exercising his or
  her powers or performing his or her duties, wear or carry the
  identification that is supplied by the Chief Electoral Officer and
  shall show it on request.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 33
- [2018, c. 31, s. 29](#1041417-1131211){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041417-1131211.html"}
:::

Version](section-33-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 33"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Refusal to appoint

- **[[37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-37 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  returning officer may, on reasonable grounds, refuse to appoint as an
  election officer a person recommended by a candidate or by a
  registered association or registered party and shall immediately
  advise the candidate, association or party of the refusal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recommendation of another person

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If as a result of the refusal a position is not
  filled and there are no more persons whose names were provided by the
  candidate, registered association or registered party under subsection
  33(1) who may be appointed under subsection 33(2) or (3), the
  candidate, association or party may recommend another person within 24
  hours after being advised of the refusal.

::: HistoricalNote

:::

Version](section-37-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 37"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Record of election officers' powers and
duties

**[[38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-38 .sectionLabel}** A returning officer shall
keep a record of the powers and duties that he or she has assigned to
each election officer, and of the time at which or during which each
election officer is to exercise a power or perform a duty assigned to
him or her.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 38

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election officers

**[[39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-39 .sectionLabel}** An election officer shall
exercise or perform, in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's
instructions, any power or duty assigned to him or her by a returning
officer.

### [Equality of Votes]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204063 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List of names to be provided

**[[40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-40 .sectionLabel}** The registered parties
that have the right to provide the returning officer with lists of names
of suitable persons to be appointed as election officers for the
purposes of a by-election under subsection 29(1.1) of the [Parliament of
Canada Act](/eng/acts/P-1) because of an equality of votes are the same
registered parties as those who had that right for the purposes of the
election that resulted in the equality of votes.

### [New Electoral Districts]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204066 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Results transposed

- **[[41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-41 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When a
  new electoral district is established, the Chief Electoral Officer
  shall transpose the results from the previous general election to the
  polling divisions that are in the new electoral district in order to
  determine which registered parties' candidates, registered
  associations or registered parties have the right to provide the
  returning officer for that electoral district with lists of persons to
  be appointed as election officers.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 30\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 30\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} When the Chief Electoral Officer has determined which
  candidates, registered associations or registered parties have the
  right to provide lists of names under subsection (1), he or she shall
  notify those registered parties without delay of that right.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 41
- 2014, c. 12, s. 22
- [2018, c. 31, s. 30](#1041421-1111233){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041421-1111233.html"}
:::

Version](section-41-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 41"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Merger of Registered Parties]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204078 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attribution of votes for appointments

**[[42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-42 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes of
subsection 33(3) and section 41, in a case in which a registered party
that endorsed a candidate in the last election merges with one or more
parties that were registered parties at the last election,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the merged party is deemed to have endorsed a
  candidate in the last election in the electoral district; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} that candidate is deemed to have received the same
  number of votes as the candidate who, among the candidates of the
  merging parties, received the largest number of votes at that
  election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 42
- [2018, c. 31, s. 31](#1041425-1131237){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041425-1131237.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-42-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 42"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Prohibitions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204081 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibitions

**[[43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-43 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} knowingly obstruct an election officer in the
  exercise of his or her powers or the performance of his or her duties;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} without authority, use identification simulating that
  used by an election officer or intended to replace that prescribed by
  the Chief Electoral Officer for that purpose; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} having been removed or replaced as an election
  officer, fail to return any election documents or election materials
  in his or her possession to the returning officer or to an authorized
  person.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 43
- [2018, c. 31, s. 32](#1041427-1111239){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041427-1111239.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-43-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 43"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right of access

- **[[43.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-43.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person who is in control of an apartment building, condominium
  building or other multiple-residence building or a gated community
  shall prevent an election officer or a member of the staff of a
  returning officer from obtaining access to the building or gated
  community, as the case may be, between 9:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m., to
  exercise his or her powers or perform his or her duties under this
  Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a person
  who is in control of a multiple-residence building whose residents'
  physical or emotional well-being may be harmed as a result of
  permitting the activities referred to in that subsection.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 21, s. 3
- [2018, c. 31, s. 33(E)](#1041429-1111241){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041429-1111241.html"}
:::

Version](section-43.1-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 43.1"){.PITLink}
:::

## [PART 4]{.HLabel1}[Register of Electors and Register of Future Electors]{.HTitleText1} {#h-204094 .Part}

### [Maintenance and Communication]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204095 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maintenance of Registers

- **[[44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-44 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall maintain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a register of persons who are qualified as
    electors, to be known as the Register of Electors; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a register of persons who are qualified as future
    electors, to be known as the Register of Future Electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of Registers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Register of Electors and the Register of Future
  Electors shall contain, for each elector or future elector who is
  included in it, as the case may be, his or her surname, given names,
  gender, date of birth, civic address, mailing address and any other
  information that is provided under subsections 49(2), 211.2(4),
  223(2), 233(2) and 251(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Identifier

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Register of Electors and the Register of Future
  Electors shall also contain, for each elector or future elector, as
  the case may be, a unique, randomly generated identifier that is
  assigned by the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Future electors becoming electors

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), the Register of Future
  Electors may continue to contain information about a former future
  elector after he or she becomes an elector until he or she is included
  in the Register of Electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inclusion optional

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Inclusion in the Register of Electors and the
  Register of Future Electors is optional.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Parental consent not necessary

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A future elector's inclusion in the Register of
  Future Electors does not require the consent of the future elector's
  parents or guardian or tutor.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 44
- 2001, c. 21, s. 4
- 2007, c. 21, s. 4
- [2018, c. 31, s. 36](#1041437-1120912){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041437-1120912.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-44-20080301.html "Link to previous version of section 44"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists to members and registered parties

- **[[45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-45 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} By
  November 15 in each year, the Chief Electoral Officer shall make
  available to the member for each electoral district and, on request,
  to each registered party that endorsed a candidate in the electoral
  district in the last election, a copy --- taken from the Register of
  Electors --- in electronic form, or in formats that include electronic
  form, of the lists of electors for the electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of lists of electors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The lists of electors shall set out each elector's
  surname, given names, civic address and mailing address, and the
  identifier that is assigned to the elector by the Chief Electoral
  Officer and shall be arranged in the form established by the Chief
  Electoral Officer according to the civic addresses of the electors or,
  if that is not appropriate, in alphabetical order by their surnames.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply if November 15 falls
  during an election period or if the vote at a general election was
  held during the six months before that date.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Merger of parties

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), a registered party
  that is the result of a merger of two or more registered parties is
  deemed to have endorsed a candidate in the last election if one of the
  merging parties so endorsed a candidate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 45
- 2007, c. 21, s. 5
- [2018, c. 31, s. 37](#1041441-1131240){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041441-1131240.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-45-20080301.html "Link to previous version of section 45"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Updates]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204118 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sources of information

- **[[46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-46 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Register of Electors and the Register of Future Electors shall be
  updated from

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} information

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} that electors or future electors, as the case may
      be, have given the Chief Electoral Officer, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} that is held by a federal department or body and
      that electors or future electors, as the case may be, have
      expressly authorized to be given to the Chief Electoral Officer;
      and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} information that the Chief Electoral Officer
    considers reliable and necessary for updating the surname, given
    names, gender, date of birth, civic address and mailing address of
    electors and future electors included in the Register of Electors or
    Register of Future Electors, as the case may be, and that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is held under an Act of the legislature of a
      province mentioned in Schedule 2, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} comes from any other source mentioned in
      Schedule 2.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Source of information: Register of
  Future Electors

  [(1.01)]{.lawlabel} The Register of Electors shall be updated from
  information that the Chief Electoral Officer holds in the Register of
  Future Electors about future electors who become electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Retention of certain information

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may retain information
  collected under paragraph (1)(b), but not included in the Register of
  Electors or Register of Future Electors, for the purpose of
  correlating information subsequently collected with information
  already contained in the relevant register.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amendments to Schedule 2

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may at any time amend
  Schedule 2 by adding, changing or deleting the name of an Act of the
  legislature of a province or of any other source of information, but
  no such amendment comes into force until notice of it is published in
  the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 46
- 2007, c. 21, s. 6
- [2018, c. 31, s. 39](#1041447-1120923){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041447-1120923.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-46-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 46"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information from Minister of Citizenship
and Immigration

**[[46.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-46.01 .sectionLabel}** Despite
subparagraph 46(1)(a)(ii), for the purpose of assisting the Chief
Electoral Officer in updating the Register of Electors, including by
deleting the name of a person who is not an elector, the Minister of
Citizenship and Immigration may, at the request of the Chief Electoral
Officer in writing, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with any of the
following information, in relation to a person, that is contained in
databases maintained by the Department of Citizenship and Immigration
that relate to [[permanent residents]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} and
[[foreign nationals]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as those terms are defined
in subsection 2(1) of the [Immigration and Refugee Protection
Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5) and with the date when the information referred to
in paragraph (d) was included or updated in those databases:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} his or her surname and given names;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} his or her gender;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} his or her date of birth;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} his or her addresses; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} any unique identifier that that Minister has assigned
  to him or her under that Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 40](#1041461-1111250){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041461-1111250.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Citizenship information

**[[46.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-46.1 .sectionLabel}** For the purpose of
assisting the Chief Electoral Officer in updating the Register of
Electors or Register of Future Electors, the Minister of National
Revenue may, on a return of income referred to in subsection 150(1) of
the [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3), request that an individual who is
filing a return of income under paragraph 150(1)(d) of that Act indicate
in the return whether he or she is a Canadian citizen.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 21, s. 7
- [2018, c. 31, s. 40](#1041461-1120926){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041461-1120926.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-46.1-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 46.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information in respect of deceased
individuals

**[[46.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-46.2 .sectionLabel}** For the purpose of
updating the Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors, the
Minister of National Revenue shall, at the request of the Chief
Electoral Officer, provide the name, date of birth and address of any
individual to whom paragraph 150(1)(b) of the [Income Tax
Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3) applies if that individual has, in his or her last
return of income filed under paragraph 150(1)(d) of that Act, authorized
that Minister to provide his or her name, date of birth and address to
the Chief Electoral Officer for the relevant register.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 21, s. 7
- [2018, c. 31, s. 40](#1041461-1120929){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041461-1120929.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-46.2-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 46.2"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of returning officer

**[[47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-47 .sectionLabel}** During the election
period, each returning officer shall update the Register of Electors
from the information that he or she obtains under this Act, other than
information in relation to an elector with respect to whom an
application has been granted under subsection 233(1.1).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other duties

**[[47.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-47.1 .sectionLabel}** Between election
periods, a returning officer shall perform any duties related to the
updating of the Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors that
are requested by the Chief Electoral Officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 21, s. 8
- [2018, c. 31, s. 41](#1041465-1120932){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041465-1120932.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-47.1-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 47.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adding electors and future electors

- **[[48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-48 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall, before including an elector in the
  Register of Electors or a future elector in the Register of Future
  Electors, send him or her the Chief Electoral Officer's information
  relating to him or her and ask if he or she wishes to be included in
  the relevant register.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation of elector or future elector

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector or future elector who wishes to be
  included in the relevant register shall confirm, correct or complete
  the information, in writing, and give it to the Chief Electoral
  Officer along with a signed certification that he or she is qualified
  as an elector or as a future elector, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of the
  inclusion of an elector or future elector that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} done at his or her request;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} done using information from lists of electors or
    future electors established under provincial law that contain
    information that the Chief Electoral Officer considers sufficient
    for the elector's or future elector's inclusion; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} done using information to update the Register of
    Electors under subsection 46(1.01).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 48
- [2018, c. 31, s. 41](#1041465-1120945){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041465-1120945.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-48-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 48"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Listing requests

- **[[49]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-49 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  person may at any time request the Chief Electoral Officer to include
  him or her in the Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors,
  by providing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a signed certification that he or she is qualified
    as an elector or as a future elector, as the case may be;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} his or her surname, given names, gender, date of
    birth, civic address and mailing address; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} satisfactory proof of identity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Optional information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the information referred to in
  subsection (1), the Chief Electoral Officer may invite the elector or
  future elector to give any other information that the Chief Electoral
  Officer considers necessary to implement any agreements entered into
  under section 55, but the elector or future elector is not required to
  do so.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 49
- [2018, c. 31, s. 41](#1041465-1120956){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041465-1120956.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-49-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 49"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corrections

**[[50]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-50 .sectionLabel}** An elector or future
elector may inform the Chief Electoral Officer of changes to the
information in the Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors,
as the case may be, relating to him or her, and the Chief Electoral
Officer shall make the necessary corrections to the relevant register.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 50
- [2018, c. 31, s. 41](#1041465-1120961){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041465-1120961.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-50-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 50"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Verification

**[[51]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-51 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} contact an elector or future elector to verify the
  Chief Electoral Officer's information relating to him or her; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} request the elector or future elector to confirm,
  correct or complete the information within 60 days after receiving the
  request.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 51
- [2018, c. 31, s. 41](#1041465-1120968){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041465-1120968.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-51-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 51"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deletion of names

- **[[52]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-52 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall delete from the Register of Electors or
  Register of Future Electors the name of any person who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is dead;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is not an elector or future elector, as the case
    may be, subject to subsection 44(4);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} requests in writing to have his or her name
    deleted;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} is, by reason of mental incapacity, under a
    court-ordered protective regime, including guardianship, tutorship
    or curatorship, and whose authorized representative under the regime
    requests in writing that the person's name be deleted; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} is a future elector with a mental incapacity whose
    parent requests in writing that the future elector's name be
    deleted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A person's name may be deleted under paragraph
  (1)(d) only if the authorized representative has provided the Chief
  Electoral Officer with a copy of the court order and satisfactory
  proof of that representative's identity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deletion of name --- discretionary

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may delete from the
  Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors the name of any
  person who fails to comply with a request referred to in paragraph
  51(b) within the 60 days.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 52
- 2014, c. 12, s. 23
- [2018, c. 31, s. 42](#1041480-1120975){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041480-1120975.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-52-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 52"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restrictions

- **[[53]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-53 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If an
  elector so requests the Chief Electoral Officer in writing,
  information in the Register of Electors relating to that elector shall
  be used only for federal electoral or referendum purposes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction --- Register of Future
  Electors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a future elector so requests the Chief Electoral
  Officer in writing, information in the Register of Future Electors
  relating to the future elector shall be used only for the purposes of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} updating the Register of Electors; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of information in the course of
    public education and information programs implemented under
    subsection 18(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 53
- [2018, c. 31, s. 43](#1041491-1120985){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041491-1120985.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-53-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 53"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to personal information

**[[54]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-54 .sectionLabel}** At the written request of
an elector or future elector, the Chief Electoral Officer shall send him
or her all the information in the Chief Electoral Officer's possession
relating to him or her.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 54

### [Agreements on Giving Information]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204188 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provincial bodies

- **[[55]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-55 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer may enter into an agreement with any body
  responsible under provincial law for establishing a list of electors
  or future electors, governing the giving of information contained in
  the Register of Electors or Register of Future Electors, or the giving
  of information referred to in subsection 44(2) or (3) that the Chief
  Electoral Officer intends to include in either register, if that
  information is needed for establishing such a list.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the Chief Electoral Officer
  shall not enter into an agreement governing the giving of information
  contained in the Register of Future Electors, or the giving of
  information referred to in subsection 44(2) or (3) in relation to
  future electors, with any body that is required under provincial law
  to give or to make available to political parties, entities associated
  with a political party or members of a legislature information
  relating to future electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall include in the
  agreement conditions regarding the use and protection of personal
  information given under the agreement.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 21, s. 9\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Valuable consideration

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An agreement mentioned in subsection (1) may require
  valuable consideration to be provided in exchange for the information
  given.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 55
- 2007, c. 21, s. 9
- [2018, c. 31, s. 45](#1041495-1120994){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041495-1120994.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-55-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 55"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Prohibitions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204199 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibitions

**[[56]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-56 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} knowingly make a false or misleading statement,
  orally or in writing, relating to their qualification as an elector or
  as a future elector or relating to any other information referred to
  in section 49;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} knowingly make a false or misleading statement,
  orally or in writing, relating to another person's qualification as an
  elector or as a future elector, to that other person's surname, given
  names, gender, civic address or mailing address, or to the identifier
  assigned to that other person by the Chief Electoral Officer, for the
  purpose of having that other person's name deleted from the Register
  of Electors or Register of Future Electors, as the case may be;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} request the listing in the Register of Electors or
  Register of Future Electors of the name of a person who is not
  qualified as an elector or as a future elector, as the case may be,
  knowing that the person is not so qualified;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} knowingly apply to have included in the Register of
  Electors or Register of Future Electors the name of an animal or
  thing;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} knowingly use personal information that is obtained
  from the Register of Electors except as follows:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to enable registered parties, members or candidates
    to communicate with electors in accordance with section 110,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of the administration and
    enforcement of this Act or the [Referendum Act](/eng/acts/R-4.7), or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with the conditions included in an
    agreement made under section 55, in the case of information that is
    transmitted in accordance with the agreement,

- [(e.1)]{.lawlabel} knowingly use personal information that is obtained
  from the Register of Future Electors except as follows:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of updating the Register of
    Electors,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of the transmission of
    information in the course of public education and information
    programs implemented under subsection 18(1),

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of the administration and
    enforcement of this Act or the [Referendum Act](/eng/acts/R-4.7), or

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with the conditions included in an
    agreement made under section 55, in the case of information that is
    transmitted in accordance with the agreement; or

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} knowingly use other personal information that is
  transmitted in accordance with an agreement made under section 55
  except in accordance with the conditions included in the agreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 56
- 2007, c. 21, s. 10
- [2018, c. 31, s. 46](#1041510-1121006){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041510-1121006.html"}
:::

## [PART 5]{.HLabel1}[Conduct of an Election]{.HTitleText1} {#h-204213 .Part}

### [Date of General Election]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204214 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of Governor General preserved

- **[[56.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-56.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this section affects the
  powers of the Governor General, including the power to dissolve
  Parliament at the Governor General's discretion.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election dates

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (1), each general election must
  be held on the third Monday of October in the fourth calendar year
  following polling day for the last general election, with the first
  general election after this section comes into force being held on
  Monday, October 19, 2009.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 10, s. 1
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Alternate day

- **[[56.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-56.2 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Chief Electoral Officer is of the opinion that a Monday that would
  otherwise be polling day under subsection 56.1(2) is not suitable for
  that purpose, including by reason of its being in conflict with a day
  of cultural or religious significance or a provincial or municipal
  election, the Chief Electoral Officer may choose another day in
  accordance with subsection (4) and shall recommend to the Governor in
  Council that polling day be that other day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of recommendation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Chief Electoral Officer recommends an
  alternate day for a general election in accordance with subsection
  (1), he or she shall without delay publish in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) notice of the day recommended.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Making and publication of order

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Governor in Council accepts the
  recommendation, the Governor in Council shall make an order to that
  effect. The order must be published without delay in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The alternate day must be either the Tuesday
  immediately following the Monday that would otherwise be polling day
  or the Monday of the following week.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Timing of proclamation

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} An order under subsection (3) shall not be made after
  August 1 in the year in which the general election is to be held.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 10, s. 1
:::

### [Writs of Election]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204235 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}General election --- proclamation

- **[[57]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-57 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Governor in Council shall issue a proclamation in order for a general
  election to be held.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-election --- order

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council shall make an order in
  order for a by-election to be held.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} The proclamation or order shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} direct the Chief Electoral Officer to issue a writ
    to the returning officer for each electoral district to which the
    proclamation or order applies;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fix the date of issue of the writ; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} fix the date for voting at the election, which date
    must be no earlier than the 36th day and no later than the 50th day
    after the day on which the writ was issued.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}General election

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a general election,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the writ shall be the same for
    all electoral districts;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} polling day shall be the same for all electoral
    districts; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the proclamation shall fix a date for the return of
    the writ to the Chief Electoral Officer, which date shall be the
    same for all of the writs.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election held on a Monday

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4) and section 56.2, polling
  day shall be on a Monday.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a general election that is not held on
  a day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2, if,
  in the week in which the election is to be held, the Monday is a
  holiday, polling day shall be held on the Tuesday of that week.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Times when polling day is a Tuesday

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the day fixed for the vote is a Tuesday because of
  subsection (4) or section 56.2, any time period specified under this
  Act before or after polling day is to be calculated as if polling day
  were the Monday.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 57
- 2001, c. 21, s. 5
- 2007, c. 10, s. 2
- [2018, c. 31, s. 47](#1041521-1111252){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041521-1111252.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-57-20070503.html "Link to previous version of section 57"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Writs forwarded to returning officer

**[[58]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-58 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall issue a writ in Form 1 of Schedule 1 to the returning
officer for the electoral district in which the election is to be held
without delay after the proclamation is issued or the order is made
under section 57.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 58
- 2001, c. 21, s. 6
- 2007, c. 10, s. 3
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-58-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 58"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Withdrawal of writ

- **[[59]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-59 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Governor in Council may order the withdrawal of a writ for any
  electoral district for which the Chief Electoral Officer certifies
  that by reason of a flood, fire or other disaster it is impracticable
  to carry out the provisions of this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of Chief Electoral Officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Governor in Council orders the withdrawal of a
  writ, the Chief Electoral Officer shall publish a notice of the
  withdrawal in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and, on
  being ordered by the Governor in Council to do so, shall, within three
  months after the date of publication of the notice, issue a new writ
  ordering an election to be held.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Polling day

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The day named in the new writ for polling day is
  determined by the Governor in Council, but may be no later than the
  50th day after the day on which the new writ was issued.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Postponement of election and new
  polling day

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Chief Electoral Officer certifies that by
  reason of a flood, fire or other disaster it is impracticable to carry
  out the provisions of this Act with regard to an electoral district,
  but the Governor in Council is of the opinion that the withdrawal of
  the writ under subsection (1) is not warranted, the Governor in
  Council may, by order, postpone the election by up to seven days for
  that electoral district and, correspondingly, extend the election
  period and fix the date for the new polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Postponement of election --- rules

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the Governor in Council orders the postponement of
  an election for an electoral district under subsection (4), then, in
  respect of that electoral district, the following rules apply in
  respect of any time period before polling day specified under this
  Act:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if this Act authorizes or requires anything to be
    done on a day that is a certain number of days before polling day or
    done within a period that ends before polling day, and the day
    occurs or the period ends before the day on which the postponement
    order is made, then polling day is deemed to still be the day fixed
    under paragraph 57(1.2)(c) and not the day fixed under subsection
    (4);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if this Act authorizes or requires anything to be
    done within a period that ends on or before polling day and the
    period ends on or after the day on which the postponement order is
    made, then

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} anything done as authorized or required on or
      before the day on which the postponement order is made is valid,
      and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in respect of anything not done as authorized or
      required on or before that day, the period during which the thing
      is authorized or required to be done is extended by the number of
      days by which the election is postponed;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if this Act authorizes or requires anything to be
    done on a day that is a certain number of days before polling day
    and that day occurs on the day on which the postponement order is
    made, then

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} anything done as authorized or required on that
      day is valid, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in respect of anything not done as authorized or
      required on that day, the day on which the thing is authorized or
      required to be done is postponed by the number of days by which
      the election is postponed;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if a period is extended under subparagraph (b)(ii)
    or a day is postponed under subparagraph (c)(ii), then any mention
    of a number of days before polling day prevails over any mention of
    a day of the week before polling day; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of this subsection, if the
    original polling day fixed under paragraph 57(1.2)(c) is a Tuesday
    because of section 56.2 or subsection 57(4), it is deemed to be a
    Monday.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 59
- [2018, c. 31, s. 48](#1041525-1111272){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041525-1111272.html"}
:::

Version](section-59-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 59"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Returning officer to open and maintain
office

- **[[60]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-60 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every
  returning officer shall, without delay after receiving the writ or
  notice by the Chief Electoral Officer of the issue of the writ, open
  an office in premises that are accessible to electors with a
  disability in a convenient place in the electoral district and shall
  maintain the office throughout the election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Hours

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may fix the hours that
  the office must be open and the minimum number of hours of compulsory
  attendance at it by the returning officer and the assistant returning
  officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 60
- [2018, c. 31, s. 49](#1041527-1111277){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041527-1111277.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-60-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 60"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of staff

- **[[61]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-61 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer may authorize returning officers to appoint
  the staff that they consider necessary for the purposes of this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Employment of staff

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Staff mentioned in subsection (1) shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be appointed in the prescribed form;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make a solemn declaration in the prescribed form;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} be discharged as soon as their services are no
    longer needed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 61
- [2018, c. 31, s. 50](#1041529-1131244){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041529-1131244.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-61-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 61"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Notice of Election by Returning Officer]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204283 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of election

**[[62]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-62 .sectionLabel}** Within four days after
the issue of the writ, each returning officer shall sign and issue a
Notice of Election in Form 2 of Schedule 1 that indicates

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the deadline for the receipt of nominations;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date for polling day;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date and time, not later than seven days after
  polling day, for the validation of results; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the address of the returning officer's office.

### [Return by Acclamation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204290 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return by acclamation

- **[[63]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-63 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When,
  as of 2:00 p.m. on the 19th day before polling day, the returning
  officer has confirmed a nomination for only one candidate, the
  returning officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} without delay declare the candidate elected by
    endorsing the return of the writ in the prescribed form on the back
    of the writ and returning it to the Chief Electoral Officer; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within 48 hours after the return of the writ, send
    a certified copy of it to the elected candidate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report with return

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the returning officer returns the writ to the
  Chief Electoral Officer, the returning officer shall include with it a
  report of the proceedings during the election period, including any
  nomination proposed and rejected for non-compliance with this Act.

### [Holding of an Election]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204298 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Holding of election

- **[[64]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-64 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the
  nomination of more than one candidate is confirmed in an electoral
  district, an election shall be held.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of grant of a poll

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall, within five days after
  the closing day for nominations, if more than one candidate is
  nominated, post in the returning office a notice of grant of a poll in
  the prescribed form that indicates

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and political affiliation, if any, of each
    candidate, as stated in the nomination papers, in the order in which
    their names are to be placed on the ballots;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the official agent for each candidate,
    as stated in the nomination papers; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name, if any, and the number of each of the
    polling divisions and the addresses of the polling stations in that
    electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to election officers

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall make the notice of grant
  of a poll available to, for each polling station, an election officer
  who is assigned to work in the polling station. The election officer
  shall post the notice in the polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Documents to candidates

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall send to each candidate,
  on the later of the 31st day before polling day and the day on which
  the candidate's nomination is confirmed, up to 10 copies of a document
  that sets out a description of the boundaries of the polling divisions
  in the electoral district.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 64
- 2014, c. 12, s. 24
- [2018, c. 31, s. 51](#1041531-1131247){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041531-1131247.html"}
:::

:::

## [PART 6]{.HLabel1}[Candidates]{.HTitleText1} {#h-204313 .Part}

### [Qualifications]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204314 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligible candidates

**[[65]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-65 .sectionLabel}** The following persons are
not eligible to be a candidate:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person who is not qualified as an elector on the
  date on which his or her nomination paper is filed;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who is disentitled under paragraph 502(3)(a)
  while they are so disentitled;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a member of the legislative assembly of a province;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 52\]]{.Repealed}

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the Chief Electoral Officer;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a judge appointed by the Governor in Council, other
  than a citizenship judge appointed under the [Citizenship
  Act](/eng/acts/C-29);

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} a person who is imprisoned in a correctional
  institution;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} an election officer; and

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a person who was a candidate in a previous election
  and for whom a return, report, document or declaration has not been
  provided under subsection 477.59(1), if the time and any extension for
  providing it have expired.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 65
- 2002, c. 7, s. 92
- 2014, c. 2, s. 49, c. 12, s. 25
- [2018, c. 31, s. 52](#1041533-1131250){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041533-1131250.html"}
:::
