[Previous
Version](section-65-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 65"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Nomination of Candidates]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204328 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Manner of nomination

- **[[66]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-66 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  nomination paper shall be in the prescribed form and include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a solemn declaration, in the prescribed form, made
    by the prospective candidate of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} his or her name, address and occupation,

    - [(i.1)]{.lawlabel} any other name by which he or she is commonly
      known --- other than a name that could be confused with the name
      of a political party --- and that he or she wishes to appear on
      the ballot instead of the name referred to in subparagraph (i),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the address designated by the prospective
      candidate for service of documents under this Act,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the prospective
      candidate's official agent,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the auditor's name, address and occupation, if
      the prospective candidate has appointed an auditor under
      subsection 477.1(2),

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the name of the political party that has endorsed
      the prospective candidate or, if none, the prospective candidate's
      choice to either have the word "independent" or no designation of
      political affiliation under his or her name in election documents,
      and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} if the prospective candidate's statement
      includes the name of a political party that has endorsed him or
      her but the returning officer is unable to verify, under paragraph
      71(2)(c), that the party has done so, the prospective candidate's
      choice of either one of the two options referred to in
      subparagraph (v) or the withdrawal of his or her nomination paper;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a statement signed by the prospective candidate
    consenting to the nomination;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 53\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a statement signed by the official agent consenting
    to act in that capacity;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} for any electoral district except one listed in
    Schedule 3, the names, addresses and signatures, made in the
    presence of a witness, of at least 100 electors resident in the
    electoral district;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} for an electoral district listed in Schedule 3, the
    names, addresses and signatures, made in the presence of a witness,
    of at least 50 electors resident in the electoral district;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and signature of the witness to
    each signature made under paragraph (e) or (f); and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, a signed statement by the
    prospective candidate setting out the name of the person who is
    authorized by the prospective candidate under subsection 67(7).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Particulars of candidates --- name

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subparagraphs (1)(a)(i) and (i.1),
  the name shall not include any title, degree or other prefix or
  suffix.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Particulars of candidates ---
  occupation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subparagraph (1)(a)(i), the
  occupation shall be stated briefly and shall correspond to the
  occupation by which the prospective candidate is known.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Witness ensures signatures are local
  electors'

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A witness to a signature referred to in paragraph
  (1)(e) or (f) shall use due diligence to ensure that the signatures
  that are made in his or her presence are all made by electors resident
  in the electoral district.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 66
- 2001, c. 21, s. 7
- 2014, c. 12, s. 26
- 2018, c. 31, s. 53
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-66-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 66"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing of nomination paper

- **[[67]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-67 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  prospective candidate shall file the nomination paper with the
  returning officer in the electoral district in which the prospective
  candidate is seeking nomination at any time between the date of the
  issue of the Notice of Election and the close of nominations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of identity --- prospective
  candidate

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A prospective candidate who personally files his or
  her nomination paper shall provide the returning officer with the
  following proof of his or her identity:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one piece of identification issued by a Canadian
    government, whether federal, provincial or local, or an agency of
    such a government, that contains a photograph of the prospective
    candidate and his or her name referred to in subparagraph
    66(1)(a)(i); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two pieces of identification of a type authorized
    under subsection (3), each of which establishes that name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorized types of identification

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may authorize types of
  identification for the purposes of subsections (2) and (8). For
  greater certainty, any document may be authorized, regardless of who
  issued it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Name prospective candidate commonly
  known by --- documents

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a prospective candidate wishes a name referred to
  in subparagraph 66(1)(a)(i.1) to appear on the ballot instead of the
  name referred to in subparagraph 66(1)(a)(i), he or she shall file
  with the returning officer documents of a type authorized under
  subsection (5) as proof that he or she is commonly known by that name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorized types of documents

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may authorize types of
  documents for the purposes of subsection (4).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's consent

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a prospective candidate has appointed an auditor,
  the prospective candidate shall file with the returning officer by the
  close of nominations a statement signed by the auditor consenting to
  act in that capacity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorized person

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A prospective candidate may authorize another person
  to carry out, on the prospective candidate's behalf, any of the
  prospective candidate's obligations under subsections (1), (4) and
  (6).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of identity --- authorized person

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} A person authorized under subsection (7) who files a
  nomination paper on behalf of a prospective candidate shall file on
  the prospective candidate's behalf with the returning officer,
  together with the nomination paper, the following proof of the
  prospective candidate's identity:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy, signed by the prospective candidate, of one
    piece of identification issued by a Canadian government, whether
    federal, provincial or local, or an agency of such a government,
    that contains a photograph of the prospective candidate and his or
    her name referred to in subparagraph 66(1)(a)(i); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a copy, signed by the prospective candidate, of
    each of two pieces of identification of a type authorized under
    subsection (3), each of which establishes that name.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 67
- 2001, c. 21, s. 8
- 2014, c. 12, s. 27
- 2015, c. 37, ss. 2, 6
- [2018, c. 31, s. 54](#1041584-1131290){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041584-1131290.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-67-20151027.html "Link to previous version of section 67"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Party may endorse only one candidate per
district

- **[[68]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-68 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  political party may endorse only one prospective candidate in each
  electoral district for a given election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New endorsement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, with respect to a particular electoral district,
  a candidate who has been endorsed by a political party dies before
  2:00 p.m. on the 5th day before the closing day for nominations or
  withdraws in accordance with subsection 74(1), the party may endorse
  another candidate in that electoral district before the close of
  nominations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Names of endorsed candidates

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The chief agent of a political party shall provide
  the Chief Electoral Officer, no later than 24 hours before the close
  of nominations, with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of every prospective candidate who has
    been endorsed by the party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the electoral district in which the prospective
    candidate intends to be a candidate; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person or persons who endorsed the
    prospective candidate on the party's behalf.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to returning officers

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} As soon as feasible after receiving the information
  set out in paragraphs (3)(a) to (c), but no later than the close of
  nominations, the Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the information
  to the returning officer of the electoral district referred to in
  paragraph (3)(b).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 68
- 2001, c. 21, s. 9
- [2018, c. 31, s. 55](#1041588-1131298){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041588-1131298.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-68-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 68"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Closing day for nominations

**[[69]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-69 .sectionLabel}** The closing day for
nominations shall be Monday, the 21st day before polling day.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Hours of attendance

- **[[70]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-70 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer and the assistant returning officer shall attend
  between noon and 2:00 p.m. on the closing day for nominations at the
  office of the returning officer in order that the returning officer
  may receive nominations for prospective candidates who have not yet
  filed their nomination papers.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Close of nominations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No nomination may be received from any person who
  enters the office of the returning officer after 2:00 p.m. on the
  closing day for nominations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designated filing place

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer may authorize a person to
  receive --- or examine, in the case of paragraph (b) --- the following
  in any place designated by the returning officer:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the nomination paper;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the piece or pieces of identification referred to
    in paragraphs 67(2)(a) and (b);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the documents referred to in subsection 67(4);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the statement referred to in subsection 67(6); and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the copy or copies of the piece or pieces of
    identification referred to in paragraphs 67(8)(a) and (b).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 70
- [2018, c. 31, s. 56](#1041590-1131308){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041590-1131308.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-70-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 70"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to candidate of confirmation or
refusal

- **[[71]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-71 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer shall, not later than 48 hours after a nomination
  paper is filed, give the prospective candidate notice, in the
  prescribed form, of the confirmation of the nomination or of the
  refusal to accept the nomination.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Verification of nomination papers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before giving confirmation of a nomination or
  refusing to accept one, the returning officer shall verify, in
  accordance with the instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that the prospective candidate's identity has been
    proven by the piece or pieces of identification provided under
    subsection 67(2) or the copy or copies filed under subsection 67(8),
    as the case may be;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} that the nomination paper is complete, including
    having at least the number of signatures referred to in paragraph
    66(1)(e) or (f), as the case may be;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that the signatures referred to in paragraph
    66(1)(e) or (f) are those of electors who are entitled to vote in
    the electoral district in which the prospective candidate intends to
    seek nomination; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} that the political party named in the nomination
    paper as having endorsed the prospective candidate has done so, as
    evidenced by the information provided under paragraph 68(3)(a) in
    respect of that prospective candidate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Correction or replacement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A nomination paper that a returning officer has
  refused to accept may be replaced by another nomination paper or may
  be corrected if the new or corrected nomination paper is filed with
  the returning officer by the close of nominations.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 71
- [2018, c. 31, s. 57](#1041600-1131315){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041600-1131315.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-71-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 71"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Name prospective candidate commonly known
by --- determination

- **[[71.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-71.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  a nomination paper includes a name referred to in subparagraph
  66(1)(a)(i.1) and documents have been filed under subsection 67(4) in
  respect of the prospective candidate, then the returning officer shall
  determine, in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's
  instructions, whether the documents prove that the prospective
  candidate is commonly known by that name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confusion with name of political party
  --- determination

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the returning officer determines that the
  documents prove that the prospective candidate is commonly known by
  that name, but in the returning officer's opinion the name could be
  confused with the name of a political party, he or she shall notify
  the Chief Electoral Officer, who shall determine whether the name
  could be confused with one and shall inform the returning officer of
  the determination.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Name to appear on ballot

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The name referred to in subparagraph 66(1)(a)(i.1)
  shall be the name that appears on the ballot in respect of the
  prospective candidate unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the returning officer determines under
    subsection (1) that the documents filed under subsection 67(4) do
    not prove that the prospective candidate is commonly known by that
    name; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Chief Electoral Officer determines under
    subsection (2) that the name could be confused with the name of a
    political party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Clarification

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, if the name referred to in
  subparagraph 66(1)(a)(i.1) is not, under subsection (3), the name that
  is to appear on the ballot in respect of the prospective candidate,
  then the name that is to appear on the ballot in respect of the
  prospective candidate shall be the name referred to in subparagraph
  66(1)(a)(i).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of name to appear on ballot

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall, not later than 48 hours
  after the nomination paper is filed, give the prospective candidate
  notice, in the prescribed form, of whether the name referred to in
  subparagraph 66(1)(a)(i.1) is the name that is to appear on the ballot
  in respect of the prospective candidate.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 58](#1041605-1131330){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041605-1131330.html"}
:::

**[[72]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-72 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31,
s. 59\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-72-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 72"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic filing

- **[[73]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-73 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who files a nomination paper or any other document under
  section 67 may do so by electronic means. In order for the nomination
  to be valid, the returning officer must receive the document in
  electronic form by the close of nominations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of identity

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If a prospective candidate files the nomination
  paper under section 67 by electronic means, he or she may, to prove
  his or her identity, file by electronic means the copy or copies
  referred to in paragraph 67(8)(a) or (b). If the prospective candidate
  does so, he or she need not provide proof of his or her identity under
  subsection 67(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cancellation of nomination

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the original documents are not received on time,
  the returning officer shall cancel the nomination unless the person in
  respect of whom the nomination paper was filed satisfies the returning
  officer that all reasonable measures were taken to ensure that the
  original documents were received on time.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 73
- 2014, c. 12, s. 28(F)
- [2018, c. 31, s. 60](#1041608-1131334){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041608-1131334.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-73-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 73"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Withdrawal of candidate

- **[[74]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-74 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  candidate may withdraw at any time before 5:00 p.m. on the closing day
  for nominations by filing, in person, with the returning officer a
  statement in writing to that effect signed by the candidate and
  witnessed by two electors who are entitled to vote in the electoral
  district in which the candidate's nomination was confirmed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consequences of withdrawal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When a candidate withdraws under subsection (1), any
  votes cast for the candidate at the election are void.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minor corrections

**[[75]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-75 .sectionLabel}** A candidate may, before
5:00 p.m. on the closing day for nominations, provide in writing to the
returning officer any change that he or she wishes to be made to his or
her name, address or occupation as set out in the nomination paper.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Votes for persons not properly nominated
to be void

**[[76]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-76 .sectionLabel}** Any votes given for a
person other than a candidate are void.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Postponement of closing day for
nominations on death of candidate

- **[[77]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-77 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  candidate endorsed by a registered party dies after 2:00 p.m. on the
  5th day before the closing day for nominations and before the close of
  polling stations on polling day, the election is postponed and the
  returning officer shall, after communicating with the Chief Electoral
  Officer, fix the 2nd Monday after the death as the closing day for
  nominations in that electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New polling day

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notice of the day fixed under subsection (1) shall be
  given by a further Notice of Election distributed and posted as
  specified by the Chief Electoral Officer, and there shall also be
  named by the Notice of Election a new polling day, which shall be
  Monday, the 21st day after the day fixed under that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists of electors

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The lists of electors to be used at a postponed
  election shall be the lists of electors that were revised before the
  6th day before the new polling day.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Postponement of election

**[[78]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-78 .sectionLabel}** The postponement of an
election under section 77 and the fixing of a new closing day for
nominations does not invalidate the nomination of the other candidates.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballots void

**[[79]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-79 .sectionLabel}** If an election is
postponed under section 77, all ballots that are cast before the
postponement are void and shall be destroyed.

### [Rights of Candidates]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204432 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Leave of absence

**[[80]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-80 .sectionLabel}** Every employer of
employees to whom Part III of the [Canada Labour Code](/eng/acts/L-2)
applies shall, on application, grant any such employee leave of absence,
with or without pay, to seek nomination as a candidate and to be a
candidate for the period during the election period that may be
requested.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Canvassing, etc., in residential areas

- **[[81]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-81 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person who is in control of an apartment building, condominium
  building or other multiple-residence building or a gated community may
  prevent a candidate or his or her representative from

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an apartment building, condominium
    building or gated community, canvassing, between 9:00 a.m. and 9:00
    p.m., at the doors to the apartments, units or houses, as the case
    may be; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a multiple-residence building,
    campaigning, between 9:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m., in a common area in
    the multiple residence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a person
  who is in control of a multiple residence building whose residents'
  physical or emotional well-being may be harmed as a result of
  permitting canvassing or campaigning referred to in that subsection.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 81
- 2007, c. 21, s. 11
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-81-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 81"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Campaigning in public places

- **[[81.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-81.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person who is in control of a building, land, street or any other
  place, any part of which is open without charge to members of the
  public, whether on a continuous, periodic or occasional basis ---
  including any commercial, business, cultural, historical, educational,
  religious, governmental, entertainment or recreational place --- may
  prevent a candidate or his or her representative from campaigning in
  or on that part when it is open without charge to members of the
  public.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a place
  if campaigning in or on it would be incompatible with the function and
  purpose of the place or inconsistent with public safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 21, s. 12
:::

### [Prohibition]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204459 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligible candidate

**[[89]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-89 .sectionLabel}** No person shall sign a
nomination paper consenting to be a candidate knowing that he or she is
not eligible to be a candidate.

**[[90]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-90 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2014, c. 12,
s. 30\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-90-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 90"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publishing false statement to affect
election results

- **[[91]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-91 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person or entity shall, with the intention of affecting the results of
  an election, make or publish, during the election period,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a false statement that a candidate, a prospective
    candidate, the leader of a political party or a public figure
    associated with a political party has committed an offence under an
    Act of Parliament or a regulation made under such an Act --- or
    under an Act of the legislature of a province or a regulation made
    under such an Act --- or has been charged with or is under
    investigation for such an offence; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a false statement about the citizenship, place of
    birth, education, professional qualifications or membership in a
    group or association of a candidate, a prospective candidate, the
    leader of a political party or a public figure associated with a
    political party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Clarification

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) applies regardless of the place where
  the election is held or the place where the false statement is made or
  published.

::: HistoricalNote

:::

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publishing false statement of candidate's
withdrawal

**[[92]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-92 .sectionLabel}** No person or entity shall
publish a false statement that indicates that a candidate has withdrawn.

## [PART 7]{.HLabel1}[Revision of Lists of Electors]{.HTitleText1} {#h-204475 .Part}

### [Preliminary Lists of Electors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204476 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preliminary lists and information to
returning officer

- **[[93]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-93 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} As
  soon as possible after the issue of a writ, the Chief Electoral
  Officer shall prepare a preliminary list of electors for each polling
  division in an electoral district, and shall make it available to the
  returning officer for the electoral district along with all the other
  information in the Register of Electors that relates to the electors
  of that electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preliminary lists to parties

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall make available in
  electronic form or in formats that include electronic form, to each
  registered party or eligible party that requests them, the preliminary
  lists of electors for an electoral district in respect of which a writ
  has been issued.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form of preliminary list of electors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A preliminary list of electors shall contain only the
  name and address of each elector in the electoral district and the
  identifier that is assigned to the elector by the Chief Electoral
  Officer and shall be arranged according to the civic addresses of the
  electors or, if that is not appropriate, in alphabetical order by
  their names.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of preliminary lists

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, not later than the
  31st day before polling day, determine the number of names appearing
  on the preliminary lists of electors for each electoral district and
  cause that information to be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 93
- 2007, c. 21, s. 13
- [2018, c. 31, s. 62](#1041614-1131339){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041614-1131339.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-93-20080301.html "Link to previous version of section 93"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preliminary lists to candidates

**[[94]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-94 .sectionLabel}** Each returning officer to
whom the preliminary lists of electors for his or her electoral district
have been made available shall make them available to each candidate in
the electoral district who requests them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 94
- [2018, c. 31, s. 63](#1041618-1131344){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041618-1131344.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-94-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 94"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Notice of Confirmation of Registration]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204493 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to electors

- **[[95]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-95 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  returning officer shall, as soon as possible after the issue of a writ
  but not later than the 24th day before polling day, send a notice of
  confirmation of registration to every elector whose name appears on
  the preliminary list of electors, except electors who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are [[incarcerated electors]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}
    as defined in section 177;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 64\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} are referred to in section 222.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form of notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The notice of confirmation of registration shall be
  in the form established by the Chief Electoral Officer and shall
  indicate

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the address of the elector's polling station, and
    whether or not it is in premises that are accessible to electors
    with a disability;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the voting hours on polling day;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a telephone number to call for more information;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the dates of advance polls and the voting hours and
    locations of advance polling stations; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the fact that proof of an elector's identity and
    residence will be required before the elector is allowed to vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Particular needs

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The notice of confirmation of registration shall
  invite the elector to contact the returning officer if he or she

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} requires a language or sign language interpreter;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} requires a polling station that is in premises that
    are accessible to electors with a disability, which his or her
    polling station is not; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is unable to attend at a polling station because of
    a disability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Change in polling station address

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If, on or before the 5th day before polling day,
  there is a change in the address of the polling station of an elector
  to whom a notice of confirmation of registration has been sent, the
  returning officer shall send another notice to the elector indicating
  the new address.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 95
- 2007, c. 21, s. 14
- 2014, c. 12, s. 32
- [2018, c. 31, s. 64](#1041627-1131350){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041627-1131350.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-95-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 95"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Revision Process]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204516 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revision of preliminary lists of electors

- **[[96]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-96 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall, as soon as possible after the issue of
  a writ, fix the commencement date for the revision of the preliminary
  lists of electors. The revision period shall terminate at 6:00 p.m. on
  the 6th day before polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cancellation of by-election

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a writ is deemed to have been superseded and
  withdrawn under subsection 31(3) of the [Parliament of Canada
  Act](/eng/acts/P-1), any revisions that are made to the preliminary
  lists of electors before the deemed withdrawal are deemed to have been
  approved by the returning officer or the assistant returning officer
  on the day fixed by the Chief Electoral Officer under subsection (1)
  as the beginning date for the revision of the preliminary lists of
  electors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 96
- 2014, c. 12, s. 33
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-96-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 96"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election officers who are designated to
receive applications

- **[[97]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-97 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer, assistant returning officer and other election
  officers for an electoral district may receive applications for
  additions or corrections to, or deletions from, a preliminary list of
  electors or the Register of Electors for their electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Applications for addition, correction
  or deletion

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} All applications referred to in subsection (1) that
  are received by election officers other than the returning officer or
  assistant returning officer shall, on completion, be presented to the
  returning officer or assistant returning officer for his or her
  approval.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 97
- [2018, c. 31, s. 65](#1041634-1131358){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041634-1131358.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-97-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 97"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revision offices

**[[98]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-98 .sectionLabel}** The returning officer may
open one or more offices for the revision of the preliminary lists of
electors. The office or offices shall be in premises that are accessible
to electors with a disability.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 98
- 2014, c. 12, s. 34
- [2018, c. 31, s. 65](#1041634-1131361){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041634-1131361.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-98-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 98"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revision --- purpose

**[[99]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-99 .sectionLabel}** The returning officer and
assistant returning officer for an electoral district shall revise the
preliminary lists of electors for that electoral district by

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} adding the names of electors who were omitted from
  the lists;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} correcting information respecting electors whose
  names are on the lists; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} deleting the names of persons whose names were
  incorrectly inserted on the lists.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information in Register of Electors

**[[99.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-99.1 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may, for the purpose of section 99, provide to the returning
officer and assistant returning officer information contained in the
Register of Electors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 21, s. 15
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election officers to act in pairs

- **[[100]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-100
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Election officers shall act in pairs
  when they assist the returning officer or assistant returning officer
  in the revision of the preliminary lists of electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disagreement between election officers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In case of disagreement between members of a pair,
  the two election officers shall refer the matter to the returning
  officer or assistant returning officer for a decision and are bound by
  that decision.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 100
- [2018, c. 31, s. 66](#1041638-1131369){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041638-1131369.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-100-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 100"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Relevant elector information

- **[[101]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-101 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer or assistant returning officer may add the name of
  any elector to the preliminary list of electors if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the elector completes the prescribed registration
    form, establishes that he or she should be included on the list and
    provides satisfactory proof of identity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} another elector who lives at the same residence as
    the elector completes the prescribed registration form, establishes
    that the elector should be included on the list and provides
    satisfactory proof of identity in respect of that elector;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} another elector who does not live at the same
    residence as the elector completes the prescribed registration form
    for the elector, establishes that the elector should be included on
    the list and provides

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} written authorization from the elector allowing
      the other elector to complete the form for him or her, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} satisfactory proof of identity in respect of
      both electors; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the elector, or another elector who lives at the
    same residence as the elector, completes the prescribed registration
    form, and makes the solemn declaration in the prescribed form, at
    their residence and in the presence of a pair of election officers
    assisting the returning officer or assistant returning officer in
    the revision of the preliminary lists of electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prescribed registration form

  [(1.01)]{.lawlabel} The prescribed registration form shall include a
  statement, to be signed by the elector who completes the form, that
  the elector whose name is to be added to the preliminary list of
  electors under subsection (1) is qualified as an elector.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Addition of elector's name

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer or assistant returning
  officer may also add to the preliminary list of electors the name of
  any elector whose name is added to the Register of Electors after that
  list has been prepared.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion from Register of Electors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector whose name is added to a preliminary list
  of electors under paragraph (1)(a) may request that his or her name
  not be included in the Register of Electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Change of address

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The previous address of an elector whose name is
  added to a preliminary list of electors under any of paragraphs (1)(a)
  to (d) and who has changed his or her address since being listed in
  the Register of Electors shall be provided and the elector's name
  shall then be deleted from the Register of Electors in relation to the
  previous address.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deletion of name of elector

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer or assistant returning officer
  may delete the name of a person from a preliminary list of electors if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person requests it and provides satisfactory
    proof of identity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is established that the elector is deceased;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is established that the information provided in
    respect of the elector is not valid; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} it is established that the elector no longer
    resides at the address indicated on the list.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corrections

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer or assistant returning officer
  may approve corrections to the information, in respect of an elector,
  on a preliminary list of electors if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the elector has requested the correction under
    subsection 97(1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there is an omission, inaccuracy or error.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Address change within electoral
  district

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An elector who changes his or her address within an
  electoral district may, by telephone or otherwise, on providing
  satisfactory proof of identity and residence to one of the election
  officers mentioned in subsection 97(1), apply to have the relevant
  corrections made to the appropriate preliminary list of electors.
  Another elector who lives at the same residence as the elector in
  question, on providing satisfactory proof of identity and residence in
  respect of the elector in question, may apply to have the relevant
  corrections made to that list in respect of the elector in question.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 101
- 2007, c. 21, s. 16
- 2014, c. 12, s. 35
- [2018, c. 31, s. 67](#1041640-1131371){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041640-1131371.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-101-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 101"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of confirmation of registration

**[[102]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-102 .sectionLabel}** Each returning officer
shall, as early as possible during the revision period but not later
than the 5th day before polling day, send a notice of confirmation of
registration that contains the information described in subsections
95(2) and (3) to every elector whose name has been added to a
preliminary list of electors during the revision period, except electors
referred to in subsection 95(1).

**[[103]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-103 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2018, c.
31, s. 68\]]{.Repealed}

Version](section-103-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 103"){.PITLink}
:::

31, s. 68\]]{.Repealed}

### [Updated Preliminary Lists of Electors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204603 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists to candidates

**[[104.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-104.1 .sectionLabel}** Each returning
officer shall, on the 19th day before polling day, make available the
most current preliminary lists of electors for his or her electoral
district to each candidate in the electoral district who requests them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 21, s. 17
- [2018, c. 31, s. 69](#1041645-1131374){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041645-1131374.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-104.1-20080301.html "Link to previous version of section 104.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists to registered parties

**[[104.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-104.2 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall, on the 19th day before polling day, make available in
electronic form or in formats that include electronic form the most
current preliminary lists of electors for each electoral district to
each registered party that has endorsed a candidate in that electoral
district and that requests them.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 69](#1041645-1131378){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041645-1131378.html"}
:::

### [Revised Lists of Electors and Official Lists of Electors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204608 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revised list of electors

- **[[105]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-105 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  returning officer shall, on the 11th day before polling day, prepare a
  revised list of electors for each polling division in the electoral
  district for use at the advance poll.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of revised lists

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, not later than the
  7th day before polling day, determine the number of names appearing on
  the revised lists of electors for each electoral district and cause
  that information to be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Official list of electors

**[[106]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-106 .sectionLabel}** Each returning officer
shall, without delay after the 7th day before polling day but no later
than the 3rd day before polling day, prepare the official list of
electors for each polling station for use on polling day.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 106
- 2014, c. 12, s. 36
- [2018, c. 31, s. 70](#1041649-1131381){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041649-1131381.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-106-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 106"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form of lists

- **[[107]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-107 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  revised list of electors for each polling division and official list
  of electors for each polling station shall be in the form established
  by the Chief Electoral Officer. The official list of electors shall
  indicate each elector's polling division number.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists to election officers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each returning officer shall make available to
  election officers the revised list of electors or official list of
  electors, as the case may be, that the election officers need to
  conduct the vote in the advance polling station or polling station to
  which they are assigned. The list shall indicate each elector's year
  of birth.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists to candidates

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Each returning officer shall make available to each
  candidate a version of the revised lists of electors and the official
  lists of electors that does not indicate an elector's year of birth.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists to registered parties

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall make available in
  electronic form or in formats that include electronic form, for each
  electoral district, a version of the revised lists of electors and the
  official lists of electors that does not indicate an elector's year of
  birth to each registered party that has endorsed a candidate in that
  electoral district.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 107

- 2014, c. 12, s. 37

:::

:::

### [Merger of Polling Divisions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204629 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Merger of polling divisions

- **[[108]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-108
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After the end of the revision
  period, the returning officer may, with the prior approval of the
  Chief Electoral Officer, merge a polling division with an adjacent
  polling division in the same electoral district.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 71\]]{.Repealed}

### [Final Lists of Electors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204635 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Final list of electors

- **[[109]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-109 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall, without delay after polling day,
  prepare final lists of electors for each electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lists to member and parties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall make available in
  electronic form, or in formats that include electronic form, the final
  lists of electors for each electoral district to each registered party
  that has endorsed a candidate in the electoral district and to the
  member who was elected for the electoral district in the last
  election.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 72\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 109

### [Use of Lists of Electors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204645 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered parties

- **[[110]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-110 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  registered party to which lists of electors are made available under
  section 45, subsection 93(1.1), section 104.2, subsection 107(4) or
  section 109 may use the lists for communicating with electors,
  including using them for soliciting contributions and recruiting party
  members.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligible parties

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} An eligible party to which preliminary lists of
  electors are made available under subsection 93(1.1) may use the lists
  for communicating with electors, including using them for soliciting
  contributions and recruiting party members.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Members

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A member to whom lists of electors or final lists of
  electors are made available under section 45 or 109, respectively, may
  use the lists for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} communicating with his or her electors; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the member is a member of a registered party,
    soliciting contributions for the registered party and recruiting
    party members.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Candidates

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A candidate to whom the preliminary lists of electors
  are made available under section 94 or 104.1, or to whom the revised
  lists of electors or the official lists of electors are made available
  under subsection 107(3), may use the lists for communicating with his
  or her electors during the election period, including using them for
  soliciting contributions and campaigning.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 110
- 2007, c. 21, s. 19
- 2014, c. 12, s. 38
- [2018, c. 31, s. 73](#1041658-1131411){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041658-1131411.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-110-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 110"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Prohibitions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204659 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibitions in relation to lists of
electors

**[[111]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-111 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} wilfully apply to be included in a list of electors
  in a name that is not his or her own;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} wilfully apply, except as authorized by this Act, to
  be included in a list of electors for a polling division if he or she
  is already included in a list of electors for another polling
  division, which list was prepared for use at the same election;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} wilfully apply, except as authorized by this Act, to
  be included in a list of electors for a polling division in which the
  person is not ordinarily resident;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} apply to have included in a list of electors for an
  electoral district the name of a person, knowing that the person is
  not qualified as an elector or entitled to vote in the electoral
  district;

- [(d.1)]{.lawlabel} compel, induce or attempt to compel or induce any
  other person to make a false or misleading statement relating to that
  other person's qualification as an elector for the purposes of the
  inclusion of that other person's name in a list of electors;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} wilfully apply to have included in a list of electors
  the name of an animal or thing; or

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} knowingly use personal information that is recorded
  in a list of electors for a purpose other than

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to enable registered parties, eligible parties,
    members or candidates to communicate with electors in accordance
    with section 110, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of the administration and
    enforcement of this Act or the [Referendum Act](/eng/acts/R-4.7).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 111
- 2014, c. 12, s. 39
- [2018, c. 31, s. 74](#1041662-1111296){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041662-1111296.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-111-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 111"){.PITLink}
:::

## [PART 8]{.HLabel1}[Preparation for the Vote]{.HTitleText1} {#h-204673 .Part}

### [List of Election Officers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204674 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List of election officers to candidates

- **[[112]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-112 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  returning officer shall, at least three days before polling day, post
  in his or her office, and make available to each candidate or
  candidate's representative, a list of the names of all the election
  officers appointed to act in the electoral district who are assigned
  to a polling station, along with the polling station to which each
  officer is assigned.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to list

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall permit access to, and
  give full opportunity for the inspection of, the list referred to in
  subsection (1) by interested persons at any reasonable time.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 112
- [2018, c. 31, s. 76](#1041666-1131417){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041666-1131417.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-112-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 112"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Election Materials]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204680 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delivery to returning officers

**[[113]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-113 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer, at any time before the issue of the writ or immediately after
the issue of it, shall deliver to the returning officer sufficient
quantities of election materials and the necessary instructions for the
election officers to exercise their powers and perform their duties.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 113
- [2018, c. 31, s. 77](#1041668-1131422){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041668-1131422.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-113-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 113"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballot boxes

- **[[114]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-114 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall provide the returning officer with the
  necessary ballot boxes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Material of ballot box

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each ballot box shall be of the size and shape and
  made of the material determined by the Chief Electoral Officer and be
  constructed to allow seals for the use of the returning officers and
  other election officers to be affixed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 114
- [2018, c. 31, s. 78](#1041670-1131427){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041670-1131427.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-114-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 114"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballot paper

- **[[115]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-115 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} As
  soon as possible after the issue of the writ, the Chief Electoral
  Officer shall provide the returning officer with the paper on which
  the ballots are to be printed. The weight and opacity of the paper
  shall be determined by the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Printing material

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before the closing day for nominations, the Chief
  Electoral Officer shall deliver to every returning officer the
  printing material prepared for that election for the purpose of
  printing the year and the name of the electoral district on the back
  of the ballot.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballot printed in Form 3

- **[[116]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-116 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer shall, as soon as possible after 2:00 p.m. on the
  19th day before polling day, authorize the printing of a sufficient
  number of ballots in Form 3 of Schedule 1.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form of ballot

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Ballots shall have a counterfoil and a stub, with a
  line of perforations between the ballot and the counterfoil and
  between the counterfoil and the stub.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Numbering of ballots

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The ballots shall be numbered on the back of the stub
  and the counterfoil, and the same number shall be printed on the stub
  as on the counterfoil.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Books of ballots

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Ballots shall be in books containing an appropriate
  number of ballots.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation re: ballots, ballot paper

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Each printer shall return all of the ballots and all
  of the unused paper on which the ballots were to have been printed, to
  the returning officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Printer's name and affidavit

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Ballots shall bear the name of the printer who, on
  delivering them to the returning officer, shall include an affidavit
  in the prescribed form that sets out a description of the ballots, the
  number of ballots delivered to the returning officer and the fact that
  all ballots were provided, and all paper returned, as required by
  subsection (5).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 116
- [2018, c. 31, s. 79(F)](#1041672-1111299){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041672-1111299.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-116-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 116"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information on the ballot

- **[[117]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-117
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Ballots shall contain the names of
  candidates referred to in subparagraph 66(1)(a)(i) or (i.1), as the
  case may be, and taken from their nomination papers, arranged
  alphabetically.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Name of party

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The name, in the form referred to in paragraph
  385(2)(b), of the political party that has endorsed the candidate
  shall be listed on the ballot under the name of the candidate if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the candidate's nomination paper includes it;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in subsection 68(3) was
    provided in respect of the candidate in accordance with that
    subsection; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} no later than 48 hours after the close of
    nominations, the party is a registered party.

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2004, c. 24, s. 2\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation of candidate as independent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The word "independent" shall be listed on the ballot
  under the name of the candidate who has requested it in accordance
  with subparagraph 66(1)(a)(v) and may not be so listed in any other
  case.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2001, c. 21, s. 12\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Address or occupation on ballot

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The ballot shall list under the candidate's name the
  address or occupation of a candidate who makes a written request to
  that effect to the returning officer before 5:00 p.m. on the closing
  day for nominations, if the candidate and another candidate on the
  ballot have the same name and both candidates have chosen under
  subparagraph 66(1)(a)(v) to either have the word "independent" or no
  designation of political affiliation under their names in election
  documents.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 117
- 2001, c. 21, s. 12
- 2004, c. 24, s. 2
- 2007, c. 21, s. 20
- 2014, c. 12, s. 40
- 2018, c. 31, s. 80
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-117-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 117"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Property of Her Majesty

**[[118]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-118 .sectionLabel}** Ballot boxes, ballots,
envelopes and marking instruments procured for an election are the
property of Her Majesty.

### [Provision of Election Materials to Election Officers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204724 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Materials to be provided to election
officers

- **[[119]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-119
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before voting begins, each returning
  officer shall provide, in accordance with the Chief Electoral
  Officer's instructions, the election officers who are assigned to a
  polling station in the returning officer's electoral district with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} enough ballots for at least the number of electors
    on the official list of electors for the polling station;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a statement showing the number of ballots that are
    provided, with their serial numbers;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the necessary materials for electors to mark their
    ballots;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an adequate number of templates, provided by the
    Chief Electoral Officer, to enable electors who are visually
    impaired to mark their ballots without assistance;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the instructions of the Chief Electoral
    Officer referred to in section 113;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the official list of electors for use at the
    polling station, enclosing it when possible in the ballot box with
    the ballots and other supplies;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a ballot box for polling day and a separate ballot
    box for each day of advance polling;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the text of the oaths to be administered to
    electors; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the necessary envelopes, forms and other supplies
    that may be authorized or provided by the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Safekeeping of election materials

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Until the opening of the poll, the election officers
  are responsible for all election materials in their possession and
  shall take every precaution to ensure the safekeeping of those
  materials and to prevent any person from having unlawful access to
  them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 119
- 2014, c. 12, s. 41
- [2018, c. 31, s. 82](#1041709-1131438){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041709-1131438.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-119-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 119"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Polling Stations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204741 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Establishment of polling stations

**[[120]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-120 .sectionLabel}** Each returning officer
shall, for polling day, establish polling stations and assign each
polling division to a polling station.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 120
- [2018, c. 31, s. 83](#1041716-1131444){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041716-1131444.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-120-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 120"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Accessibility

- **[[121]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-121 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  polling station shall be in premises that are accessible to electors
  with a disability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a returning officer is unable to secure suitable
  premises for a polling station that are accessible to electors with a
  disability, the returning officer may, with the prior approval of the
  Chief Electoral Officer, establish the polling station in premises
  that are not accessible to such electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting compartments

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Each polling station shall contain a sufficient
  number of voting compartments arranged so that each elector is
  screened from observation and may, without interference or
  interruption, mark their ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Table or desk

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Each voting compartment shall be placed on a hard and
  smooth surface and shall have in it a suitable black lead pencil for
  the use of electors in marking their ballots.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 121
- [2018, c. 31, s. 84](#1041718-1131453){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041718-1131453.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-121-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 121"){.PITLink}
:::

- **[[122]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-122
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s.
  85\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Polling station in school or other
  public building

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Whenever possible, a returning officer shall
  establish a polling station in a school or other suitable public
  building.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Polling station in federal buildings

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer may require the officer in charge
  of a building owned or occupied by the Government of Canada to make
  premises in that building available for use as a polling station, and
  the officer to whom the requirement is directed shall make every
  reasonable effort to comply with the requirement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 122
- [2018, c. 31, s. 85](#1041720-1131461){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041720-1131461.html"}
:::

31, s. 86\]]{.Repealed}

31, s. 86\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-124-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 124"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mobile polling station

- **[[125]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-125 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When
  a polling division consisting of two or more institutions is
  constituted under subsection 538(5), the returning officer may
  establish a mobile polling station to be located in each of those
  institutions successively.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting hours for mobile polling station

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall set the times during
  which a mobile polling station will be located in the institutions
  referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall give notice to the
  candidates of the itinerary of the mobile polling station in
  accordance with the instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provisions applicable to mobile polls

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the instructions of the Chief Electoral
  Officer, the provisions of this Act that relate to ordinary polls
  shall, in so far as they are applicable, apply to mobile polling
  stations.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information --- location of polling
stations

- **[[125.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-125.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer for an
  electoral district and the Chief Electoral Officer shall make the
  addresses of all of the polling stations in the electoral district
  available to, respectively, each candidate in the electoral district
  and each political party that has endorsed a candidate in the
  electoral district. That information shall be made available on the
  later of the 24th day before polling day and the day on which the
  candidate's nomination is confirmed, along with maps of the electoral
  district indicating the boundaries of each polling division and the
  location of each polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of change --- on or before
  5th day before polling day

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, on or before the 5th day before polling day,
  there is a change in the address of any polling station in the
  electoral district, the returning officer and the Chief Electoral
  Officer shall without delay make that information available to the
  candidates and the political parties respectively, along with maps of
  the electoral district indicating the new location of the polling
  station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electoral district maps --- electronic
  format

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The maps that the Chief Electoral Officer is to
  make available to political parties under subsections (1) and (2)
  shall be made available in electronic form or in formats that include
  electronic form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of change --- after 5th
  day before polling day

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, after the 5th day before polling day, there is a
  change in the address of any polling station in the electoral
  district, the returning officer and the Chief Electoral Officer shall
  without delay make that information available to the candidates and
  the political parties respectively.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 43
- [2018, c. 31, s. 87](#1041725-1131473){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041725-1131473.html"}
:::
