### [Prohibitions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204801 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibitions re ballots, etc.

**[[126]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-126 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} forge a ballot;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} without authority under this Act, print a ballot or
  what purports to be or is capable of being used as a ballot at an
  election;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} being authorized under this Act to print a ballot,
  knowingly print more ballot papers than the person is authorized to
  print;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} print a ballot or what purports to be or is capable
  of being used as a ballot at an election with the intention of causing
  the reception of a vote that should not have been cast or the
  non-reception of a vote that should have been cast; or

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} manufacture, import into Canada, have in possession,
  supply to an election officer, or use for the purpose of an election,
  or cause to be manufactured, imported into Canada, provided to an
  election officer, or used for the purposes of an election, a ballot
  box that contains a compartment into which a ballot may be secretly
  placed or a device by which a ballot may be secretly altered.

## [PART 9]{.HLabel1}[Voting]{.HTitleText1} {#h-204809 .Part}

### [Voting Opportunities]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204810 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Manner of voting

**[[127]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-127 .sectionLabel}** An elector may vote

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in person at a polling station on polling day;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in person at an advance polling station during the
  period provided for the advance poll; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} by means of a special ballot issued in accordance
  with Part 11.

### [Polling Day]{.HTitleText2} {#h-204816 .Subheading}

#### [Hours]{.HTitleText3} {#h-204817 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Hours of voting

- **[[128]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-128 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  voting hours on polling day are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} from 8:30 a.m. to 8:30 p.m., if the electoral
    district is in the Newfoundland, Atlantic or Central time zone;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} from 9:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., if the electoral
    district is in the Eastern time zone;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., if the electoral
    district is in the Mountain time zone; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., if the electoral
    district is in the Pacific time zone.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- Saskatchewan

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), if polling day is during a
  time of the year when the rest of the country is observing daylight
  saving time, the voting hours in Saskatchewan are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an electoral district in the Central
    time zone, from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an electoral district in the
    Mountain time zone, from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Daylight-saving time

**[[129]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-129 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may, if he or she considers it necessary, set the voting hours
for the electoral district so that the opening and closing of its polls
coincide with the opening and closing of the polls in other electoral
districts in the same time zone.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When polls lie in two time zones

**[[130]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-130 .sectionLabel}** When more than one
local time is observed in an electoral district, the returning officer
shall, with the prior approval of the Chief Electoral Officer, determine
one local time to be observed for every operation prescribed by this
Act, and shall publish the hours in the Notice of Election referred to
in section 62.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-elections

**[[131]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-131 .sectionLabel}** If only one by-election
is held or if more than one by-election is held on the same day and all
of them are in the same time zone, the hours of voting are from 8:30
a.m. to 8:30 p.m.

#### [Time to Employees for Voting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-204835 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consecutive hours for voting

- **[[132]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-132
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every employee who is an elector is
  entitled, during voting hours on polling day, to have three
  consecutive hours for the purpose of casting his or her vote and, if
  his or her hours of work do not allow for those three consecutive
  hours, his or her employer shall allow the time for voting that is
  necessary to provide those three consecutive hours.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time at convenience of employer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The time that the employer shall allow for voting
  under subsection (1) is at the convenience of the employer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transportation companies

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section and section 133 do not apply to an
  employee of a company that transports goods or passengers by land, air
  or water who is employed outside his or her polling division in the
  operation of a means of transportation, if the additional time
  referred to in subsection (1) cannot be allowed without interfering
  with the transportation service.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No penalty for absence from work to vote

- **[[133]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-133 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  employer may make a deduction from the pay of an employee, or impose a
  penalty, for the time that the employer shall allow for voting under
  subsection 132(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Hourly, piece-work or other basis of
  employment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An employer who pays an employee less than the amount
  that the employee would have earned on polling day, had the employee
  continued to work during the time referred to in subsection 132(2)
  that the employer allowed for voting, is deemed to have made a
  deduction from the pay of the employee, regardless of the basis on
  which the employee is paid.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

**[[134]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-134 .sectionLabel}** No employer shall, by
intimidation, undue influence or by any other means, interfere with the
granting to an elector in their employ of the three consecutive hours
for voting, as provided for in section 132.

#### [Proceedings at the Poll]{.HTitleText3} {#h-204850 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Who may be present at polling station

- **[[135]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-135 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  only persons who may be present at a polling station on polling day
  are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any field liaison officer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the returning officer, his or her representatives
    and any member of his or her staff whom he or she authorizes to be
    present;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} any election officer whom the returning officer
    authorizes to be present;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the candidates;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} two representatives of each candidate or, in their
    absence, two electors to represent each candidate;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an elector and a friend or relative who is helping
    him or her by virtue of subsection 155(1), only for the period
    necessary to enable the elector to vote;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} any observer or member of the Chief Electoral
    Officer's staff whom he or she authorizes to be present;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 88\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} if a polling division of an electoral district in
    which a registered party's leader is a candidate is assigned to the
    polling station, any media representative who --- subject to any
    conditions that the Chief Electoral Officer considers necessary to
    protect the integ­rity of the vote and the privacy of any person
    present at the polling station --- is authorized in writing by the
    Chief Electoral Officer to be present and take any photograph or
    make any audio or video recording of the candidates as they cast
    their votes; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the auditor referred to in section 164.1.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delivery of representative's
  authorization

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When a representative of a candidate is admitted to a
  polling station, the representative shall deliver his or her written
  authorization from the candidate or the candidate's official agent in
  the prescribed form, or a copy of it, to an election officer who is
  assigned to the polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representative authorized in writing

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A representative bearing a written authorization
  referred to in subsection (2), or a copy of one, is a representative
  of the candidate for the purposes of this Act and is entitled to
  represent the candidate to the exclusion of any elector who might
  otherwise claim the right to represent the candidate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solemn declaration

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Each representative of a candidate or each elector
  described in paragraph (1)(d), on being admitted to the polling
  station, shall make a solemn declaration in the prescribed form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solemn declaration

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A candidate's representative who is appointed to more
  than one polling station shall, before being admitted to the first
  polling station, make a solemn declaration in the prescribed form
  before an election officer who is assigned to that polling station.
  The representative is not required to make another solemn declaration
  on being admitted to any other polling station in the same electoral
  district if he or she presents a document, in the prescribed form,
  proving that he or she has already made the solemn declaration.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 135
- 2014, c. 12, s. 44
- [2018, c. 31, s. 88](#1041740-1131488){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041740-1131488.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-135-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 135"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Presence of representatives

- **[[136]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-136 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  candidate or the candidate's official agent may authorize any number
  of representatives of the candidate to be present at a polling
  station, but only two of each candidate's representatives may be
  present at any time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representatives may absent themselves
  from poll

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A representative of a candidate, or an elector
  described in paragraph 135(1)(d), may leave a polling station at any
  time and return at any time before the counting of the votes begins
  and is not required to produce a new written authorization from the
  candidate or official agent, or a copy of one, or to make another
  solemn declaration.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Moving between polling stations

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), a candidate's
  representative may, either before or after the counting of the votes
  begins, go from one polling station to another if those polling
  stations are in the same polling place. However, once the
  representative leaves the polling place, he or she is not permitted to
  return after the counting of the votes begins.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of list of electors and
  conveying information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A representative of a candidate may, during voting
  hours,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} examine the list of electors, provided that the
    representative does not delay an elector in casting his or her vote;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} convey any information obtained by the examination
    referred to in paragraph (a) to a representative of the candidate
    who is on duty outside the polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Photographs, recordings and
  communications devices

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A candidate's representative

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall not take any photograph or make any audio or
    video recording at a polling station; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall not, if he or she uses a communications
    device at a polling station, impede any elector from exercising
    their right to vote or violate the secrecy of the vote.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 136
- 2014, c. 12, s. 45
- [2018, c. 31, s. 89](#1041751-1131491){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041751-1131491.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-136-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 136"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Candidate may act as representative

- **[[137]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-137 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  candidate may perform the duties of a representative of the candidate,
  or may assist the representative in the performance of those duties,
  and may be present at any place that the representative is authorized
  to attend under this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-attendance of representatives

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The non-attendance of a representative of a candidate
  at any time or place authorized by this Act does not in any way
  invalidate any act or thing done during the absence of the
  representative if the act or thing is otherwise duly done.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Initialling ballots

- **[[138]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-138
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before a polling station opens on
  polling day, and in full view of the candidates or their
  representatives who are present at the polling station, an election
  officer who is assigned to the polling station shall initial the back
  of every ballot in the space indicated in Form 3 of Schedule 1,
  entirely in ink or entirely in black pencil so that when the ballot is
  folded the initials can be seen. The initials shall be as similar as
  possible on each ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballots not to be detached

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of initialling, the ballots shall not
  be detached from the books in which they are contained.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vote not to be delayed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The opening of a polling station shall not be delayed
  for the purpose of initialling the ballots. Ballots that are not
  initialled when the polling station opens shall be initialled as soon
  as possible and in all cases before being handed to electors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 138
- [2018, c. 31, s. 90](#1041753-1131495){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041753-1131495.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-138-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 138"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Counting of ballots before opening of
poll

**[[139]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-139 .sectionLabel}** Candidates or their
representatives who are in attendance at least 15 minutes before a
polling station opens are entitled to have the ballots intended to be
used at the polling station carefully counted in their presence and to
inspect the ballots and all other documents relating to the vote.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examining and sealing ballot box

**[[140]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-140 .sectionLabel}** When the polling
station opens, an election officer who is assigned to the polling
station shall, in full view of the candidates or their representatives
who are present, open the ballot box and ascertain that it is empty, and
shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} seal the ballot box with the seals provided by the
  Chief Electoral Officer; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} place the ballot box on a table in full view of all
  present and ensure that the box remains there until the polling
  station closes.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 140
- [2018, c. 31, s. 91](#1041758-1131502){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041758-1131502.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-140-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 140"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Admitting Voters]{.HTitleText3} {#h-204907 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calling electors

**[[141]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-141 .sectionLabel}** Immediately after the
ballot box is sealed, an election officer who is assigned to the polling
station shall call on the electors to vote.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 141
- [2018, c. 31, s. 92](#1041760-1131507){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041760-1131507.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-141-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 141"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electors not to be impeded

**[[142]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-142 .sectionLabel}** An election officer who
is assigned to the polling station shall ensure that every elector is
admitted into the polling station and that the electors are not
disturbed when they are in or near the polling station.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 142
- [2018, c. 31, s. 92](#1041760-1131512){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041760-1131512.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-142-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 142"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Elector to give name and address

- **[[143]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-143 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  elector, in order to receive a ballot, shall give his or her name and
  address to an election officer who is assigned to the polling station,
  and, on request, to a candidate or a candidate's representative.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of identity and residence

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the election officer determines that the elector's
  name and address appear on the list of electors or that the elector is
  allowed to vote under section 146, 147, 148 or 149, then, subject to
  subsection (3), the elector shall provide the election officer with
  the following proof of his or her identity and residence:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one piece of identification issued by a Canadian
    government, whether federal, provincial or local, or an agency of
    such a government, that contains a photograph of the elector and his
    or her name and address; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two pieces of identification of a type authorized
    under subsection (2.1), each of which establishes the elector's name
    and at least one of which establishes the elector's address.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorized types of identification

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may authorize types of
  identification for the purposes of paragraph (2)(b). For greater
  certainty, any document may be authorized, regardless of who issued
  it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person registered as an Indian

  [(2.2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraph (2)(b), a document
  issued by the Government of Canada that certifies that a person is
  registered as an Indian under the [Indian Act](/eng/acts/I-5)
  constitutes an authorized piece of identification.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solemn declaration

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An elector may instead prove his or her identity and
  residence by making the solemn declaration referred to in subsection
  549.1(1) in writing if he or she is accompanied by another elector
  whose name appears on the list of electors for the same polling
  station and who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provides the election officer referred to in
    subsection (1) with the piece or pieces of identification referred
    to in paragraph (2)(a) or (b), respectively; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} vouches for the elector by making the solemn
    declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(2) in writing.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vouching for electors in long-term care
  institution

  [(3.01)]{.lawlabel} If an elector who resides in an institution for
  seniors or persons with a disability wishes to prove his or her
  identity and residence under subsection (3), the other elector
  referred to in that subsection who accompanies him or her may be an
  employee of the institution who resides --- despite that subsection
  --- in any polling division in the elector's electoral district or an
  adjacent electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of
  [[employee]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(3.02)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (3.01),
  [[employee]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes an owner of the institution
  and any person who occupies a management position at the institution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of residence

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} If the address contained in the piece or pieces of
  identification provided under subsection (2) or paragraph (3)(a) does
  not prove the elector's residence but is consistent with information
  related to the elector that appears on the list of electors, the
  elector's residence is deemed to have been proven.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Request to make solemn declaration

  [(3.2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (3.1), if the election officer
  referred to in subsection (1), a candidate or a candidate's
  representative has reasonable doubts concerning the residence of an
  elector referred to in subsection (3.1), the officer, candidate or
  representative may request that the elector make the solemn
  declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing, in which
  case the elector's residence is deemed to have been proven only if he
  or she makes that solemn declaration.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of identification documents

  [(3.3)]{.lawlabel} A candidate or their representative may examine but
  not handle any piece of identification presented under this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the election officer is satisfied that an
  elector's identity and residence have been proven in accordance with
  subsection (2), (3), (3.1) or (3.2), the elector's name shall be
  crossed off the list and, subject to section 144, the elector shall be
  immediately allowed to vote.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 93\]]{.Repealed}

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 93\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall publish each year,
  and within three days after the issue of a writ, in a manner that he
  or she considers appropriate, a notice setting out the types of
  identification that are authorized for the purpose of paragraph
  (2)(b). The first annual notice shall be published no later than six
  months after the coming into force of this subsection.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 143
- 2007, c. 21, s. 21, c. 37, s. 1
- 2014, c. 12, s. 46
- 2018, c. 31, s. 93
:::

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement before making solemn
declaration --- elector

- **[[143.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-143.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a person decides to prove his or
  her identity and residence by making the solemn declaration referred
  to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing, an election officer shall,
  before the person makes the solemn declaration, advise him or her in
  writing of the qualifications for electors and the penalty that may be
  imposed under this Act on a person who is found guilty of voting or
  attempting to vote at an election knowing that he or she is not
  qualified as an elector or who contravenes subsection 549(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement before making solemn
  declaration --- vouching for elector

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person decides to vouch for an elector by making
  the solemn declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(2) in writing,
  an election officer shall, before the person makes the solemn
  declaration, advise him or her in writing of the penalty that may be
  imposed under this Act on a person who contravenes any of subsections
  282.1(1) to (3) or 549(3).

::: HistoricalNote

**[[144]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-144 .sectionLabel}** If the election officer
referred to in subsection 143(1), a candidate or a candidate's
representative has reasonable doubts concerning whether a person
intending to vote is qualified as an elector, the officer, candidate or
representative may request that the person make the solemn declaration
referred to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing, in which case the person
shall not be allowed to vote unless he or she makes that solemn
declaration.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of identity, etc., or oath not
required

**[[144.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-144.1 .sectionLabel}** Once an elector has
been given a ballot, no person shall require the elector to prove his or
her identity and residence in accordance with subsection 143(2) or (3).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Name and address corresponding closely to
another

**[[146]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-146 .sectionLabel}** If the name and address
of a person who asks for a ballot do not appear in the list of electors
but a different name and address in that list correspond so closely as
to suggest that they are intended to refer to that person, the person
shall not be allowed to vote unless he or she makes a solemn declaration
in the prescribed form.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person in whose name another has voted

- **[[147]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-147 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  person asks for a ballot at a polling station after someone else has
  voted under that person's name, the person shall not be allowed to
  vote unless he or she makes the solemn declaration referred to in
  subsection 549.1(1) in writing.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement before making solemn
  declaration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An election officer shall, before the person makes
  the solemn declaration, advise the person in writing of the penalty
  that may be imposed under this Act on a person who is found guilty of
  voting or attempting to vote more than once contrary to section 281.5
  or of requesting or applying for a ballot or special ballot in a name
  that is not his or her own contrary to paragraph 281.7(1)(a).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Name crossed off list in error

**[[148]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-148 .sectionLabel}** If an elector claims
that his or her name has been crossed off in error from an official list
of electors under subsection 176(2) or (3), the elector shall not be
allowed to vote unless the returning officer verifies that the elector's
name was crossed off in error or the elector makes the solemn
declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to prove identity or residence

- **[[148.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-148.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An elector who fails to prove his or
  her identity and residence in accordance with section 143 or to make a
  solemn declaration otherwise required by this Act shall not receive a
  ballot or be allowed to vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When elector refuses to make solemn
  declaration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an elector refuses to make a solemn declaration on
  the ground that he or she is not required to do so under this Act, the
  elector may appeal to the returning officer. If, after consultation
  with the election officer in whose opinion the elector is required to
  make the solemn declaration, the returning officer decides that the
  elector is not required to make it, and if the elector is entitled to
  vote in the polling division, the returning officer shall direct that
  he or she be allowed to do so.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Elector not allowed to vote

**[[149]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-149 .sectionLabel}** An elector whose name
does not appear on the official list of electors in his or her polling
station shall not be allowed to vote unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the elector gives the election officer referred to in
  subsection 143(1) a transfer certificate described in section 158 or
  159 and, for a certificate described in subsection 158(2), fulfils the
  conditions described in subsection 158(3); or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the elector gives the election officer a registration
  certificate described in subsection 161(4).

#### [Voting Procedure]{.HTitleText3} {#h-204993 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delivery of ballot to elector

- **[[150]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-150
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every elector who is admitted to
  vote shall be given a ballot by the election officer referred to in
  subsection 143(1), after that election officer has placed on the back
  of the ballot, in the space indicated in Form 3 of Schedule 1, the
  number of the elector's polling division.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Instructions to elector on receiving
  ballot

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The election officer shall explain to each elector
  how to indicate his or her choice and fold the ballot so that its
  serial number and the initials of the election officer who initialed
  the ballot are visible and shall direct the elector to return the
  marked and folded ballot.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 150
- [2018, c. 31, s. 97](#1041832-1131571){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041832-1131571.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-150-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 150"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Manner of voting

- **[[151]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-151 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  elector shall, after receiving a ballot,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} proceed directly to the voting compartment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} mark the ballot with a cross or other mark in the
    circular space opposite the name of the candidate of his or her
    choice;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} fold the ballot as instructed by the election
    officer; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} return the ballot to the election officer who
    provided it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return of ballot

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The election officer shall, on receiving the ballot
  from the elector,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} without unfolding the ballot, verify that it is the
    same one that was handed to the elector by examining its serial
    number and the initials on it;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} remove and destroy the counterfoil in full view of
    the elector and all other persons present; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} return the ballot to the elector to deposit in the
    ballot box or, at the elector's request, deposit it in the ballot
    box.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 151
- [2018, c. 31, s. 98](#1041841-1131577){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041841-1131577.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-151-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 151"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Spoiled ballot

- **[[152]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-152 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the ballot is incapable of being used, the elector shall return it to
  the election officer referred to in subsection 143(1), who shall mark
  it as a spoiled ballot, place it in the envelope supplied for the
  purpose and give the elector another ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector shall not be given more than one ballot
  under subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 152
- [2018, c. 31, s. 99](#1041848-1131581){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041848-1131581.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-152-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 152"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No delay in voting

- **[[153]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-153
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every elector shall vote without
  delay and leave the polling station as soon as his or her ballot has
  been put into the ballot box.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electors present at close of voting
  hours allowed to vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector who is entitled to vote at a polling
  station and who is in the polling station or in line at the door at
  the close of voting hours shall be allowed to vote.

#### [Special Voting Procedures]{.HTitleText3} {#h-205021 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assistance by election officer

- **[[154]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-154 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  request by an elector who is unable to read or because of a disability
  is unable to vote in the manner described by this Act, an election
  officer who is assigned to the polling station shall assist the
  elector in the presence of another election officer who is assigned to
  the polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Template

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An election officer who is assigned to the polling
  station shall, on request, provide a template to an elector who has a
  visual impairment to assist him or her in marking his or her ballot.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 154
- [2018, c. 31, s. 100](#1041850-1131589){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041850-1131589.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-154-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 154"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assistance by friend or related person

- **[[155]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-155 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an elector requires assistance to vote, one of the following persons
  may accompany the elector into the voting compartment and assist the
  elector to mark his or her ballot:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a friend of the elector;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the elector's spouse or common-law partner; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a relative of the elector or of the elector's
    spouse or common-law partner.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 101\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solemn declaration

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person described in subsection (1) who wishes to
  assist an elector in marking a ballot shall first make a solemn
  declaration, in the prescribed form, that he or she

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} will mark the ballot paper in the manner directed
    by the elector;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} will not disclose the name of the candidate for
    whom the elector voted;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} will not try to influence the elector in choosing a
    candidate; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} has not, during the current election, assisted
    another person, as a friend, to mark a ballot.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 101\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 155, c. 12, s. 40
- 2018, c. 31, s. 101
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-155-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 155"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use of interpreter

**[[156]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-156 .sectionLabel}** An election officer who
is assigned to a polling station may appoint a language or sign language
interpreter to assist election officers at the polling station in
communicating to an elector any information that is necessary to enable
him or her to vote.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 156
- [2018, c. 31, s. 102](#1041886-1131599){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041886-1131599.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-156-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 156"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Elector who is confined to bed

- **[[157]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-157 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} At a
  polling station that has been established in an institution for
  seniors or persons with a disability, when an election officer who is
  assigned to the polling station considers it necessary, the election
  officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} suspend temporarily the voting in the polling
    station; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with the approval of the person in charge of the
    institution, carry the ballot box, ballots and other necessary
    election documents from room to room in the institution to take the
    votes of electors who are confined to bed and ordinarily resident in
    the polling division in which the institution is situated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure for taking the votes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the vote of an elector who is confined to bed is
  taken, an election officer assigned to the polling station shall give
  the elector the assistance necessary to enable the elector to vote,
  and not more than one representative of each candidate may be present.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 157
- [2018, c. 31, s. 103](#1041895-1131605){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041895-1131605.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-157-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 157"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Transfer Certificates]{.HTitleText3} {#h-205051 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for candidate

- **[[158]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-158 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  candidate whose name appears on the list of electors for a polling
  station is entitled on request to receive a transfer certificate to
  vote at another polling station in the same electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for election
  officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An election officer who is assigned to a polling
  station shall issue a transfer certificate to any person --- other
  than himself or herself --- whose name appears on the official list of
  electors for the polling station and who has been appointed to act as
  an election officer for another polling station in the same electoral
  district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Condition

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A transfer certificate issued under subsection (2)
  authorizes the person to vote at the polling station named in it only
  if, on polling day, the person exercises the power or performs the
  duty specified in the certificate at the place mentioned in the
  certificate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for elector whose
  polling station has moved

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If an elector's polling station moves to another
  location after the notice of confirmation of registration has been
  sent, an elector who attends at the polling station set out in the
  notice is entitled on request to receive a transfer certificate to
  vote at that polling station.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 158
- 2007, c. 21, s. 24
- [2018, c. 31, s. 104](#1041902-1131610){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041902-1131610.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-158-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 158"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for elector with
disability

- **[[159]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-159 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  elector who has a disability and is therefore unable to vote without
  difficulty in his or her polling station may apply for a transfer
  certificate to vote at another polling station in the same electoral
  district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall be made in accordance with the
  Chief Electoral Officer's instructions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issue of transfer certificate to
  elector with disability

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An election officer shall issue a transfer
  certificate in the prescribed form, and provide the certificate to the
  person who submitted the application to the officer, if the officer is
  satisfied that the elector's name appears on a list of electors for
  the electoral district.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 159, c. 12, s. 40
- 2007, c. 21, s. 25
- [2018, c. 31, s. 105](#1041904-1131618){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041904-1131618.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-159-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 159"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Signing, numbering and recording transfer
certificate

**[[160]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-160 .sectionLabel}** The election officer
who issues a transfer certificate shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} fill in and sign the certificate and mention on it
  the date of its issue;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} consecutively number the certificate in the order of
  its issue;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of the certificate in the order of its
  issue on the prescribed form;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} not issue the certificate in blank; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} if possible, send a copy of the certificate to an
  election officer who is assigned to the polling station on whose list
  of electors appears the name of the person to whom the certificate has
  been issued.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 160
- [2018, c. 31, s. 106](#1041913-1131623){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041913-1131623.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-160-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 160"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Polling Day Registration]{.HTitleText3} {#h-205081 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration in person

- **[[161]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-161 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  elector whose name is not on the list of electors may register in
  person on polling day before an election officer if the elector

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provides as proof of his or her identity and
    residence the piece or pieces of identification referred to in
    paragraph 143(2)(a) or (b), respectively, the piece or one of those
    pieces containing an address that proves his or her residence; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} proves his or her identity and residence by making
    the solemn declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing
    and is accompanied by another elector whose name appears on the list
    of electors for the same polling station and who

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} provides the piece or pieces of identification
      referred to in paragraph 143(2)(a) or (b), respectively, the piece
      or one of those pieces containing either an address that proves
      that other elector's residence or an address that is consistent
      with information related to that other elector that appears on the
      list of electors, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} vouches for the elector by making the solemn
      declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(2) in writing.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vouching for electors in long-term care
  institution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an elector who resides in an institution for
  seniors or persons with a disability wishes to prove his or her
  identity and residence under subsection (1), the other elector
  referred to in paragraph (1)(b) who accompanies him or her may be an
  employee of the institution who resides --- despite that paragraph ---
  in any polling division in the elector's electoral district or an
  adjacent electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of
  [[employee]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (2), [[employee]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
  includes an owner of the institution and any person who occupies a
  management position at the institution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representative of each candidate

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The election officer shall permit each candidate, or
  one representative of each candidate, in the electoral district to be
  present when an elector is being registered.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of identification documents

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} The representative of a candidate may examine but
  not handle any piece of identification provided by the elector.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration certificate

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the elector satisfies the requirements of
  subsection (1), the election officer shall complete a registration
  certificate in the prescribed form authorizing the elector to vote and
  the elector shall sign it. The registration certificate shall include
  a solemn declaration made by the elector that he or she is qualified
  as an elector under section 3.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List deemed to be modified

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} When a registration certificate is given under
  subsection (4), the list of electors is deemed, for the purposes of
  this Act, to have been modified in accordance with the certificate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- registration on polling
  day

  [(5.1)]{.lawlabel} It is prohibited for any person to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} knowingly apply to be registered on polling day in
    a name that is not their own;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} knowingly apply, except as authorized by this Act,
    to be registered on polling day to vote in a polling division in
    which they are not ordinarily resident;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} apply to be registered on polling day to vote in an
    electoral district knowing that they are not qualified as an elector
    or entitled to vote in the electoral district; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} compel, induce or attempt to compel or induce any
    other person to make a false or misleading statement relating to
    that other person's qualification as an elector for the purposes of
    the registration of that other person on polling day.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 107\]]{.Repealed}

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 107\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement before making solemn
declaration --- elector

- **[[161.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-161.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a person decides to prove his or
  her identity and residence by making the solemn declaration referred
  to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing, an election officer shall,
  before the person makes the solemn declaration, advise him or her in
  writing of the qualifications for electors and the penalty that may be
  imposed under this Act on a person who contravenes subsection 161(5.1)
  or 549(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement before making solemn
  declaration --- vouching for elector

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person decides to vouch for an elector by making
  the solemn declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(2) in writing,
  an election officer shall, before the person makes the solemn
  declaration, advise him or her in writing of the penalty that may be
  imposed under this Act on a person who contravenes any of subsections
  282.1(1) to (3) or 549(3).

::: HistoricalNote

#### [Duties of Election Officers Assigned to Polling Station]{.HTitleText3} {#h-205125 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties

**[[162]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-162 .sectionLabel}** An election officer
assigned to a polling station --- and not necessarily the same election
officer for all of the following --- shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} make, on the prescribed form, the entries required
  under this Act;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} as soon as the elector's ballot has been deposited in
  the ballot box, indicate, beside the name of the elector on the list
  of electors, that the elector has voted;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} indicate, if applicable, on the prescribed form that
  the elector has voted under a transfer certificate issued under
  section 158 or 159 and give the number of the certificate;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 110\]]{.Repealed}

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} indicate, if applicable, on the prescribed form that
  the elector has voted under section 146;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} indicate, if applicable, on the prescribed form that
  the elector has made a solemn declaration and the type of solemn
  declaration;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} indicate, if applicable, on the prescribed form that
  the elector refused to comply with a legal requirement to provide the
  piece or pieces of identification referred to in paragraph 143(2)(a)
  or (b), respectively, or to make a solemn declaration;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} indicate, if applicable, on the prescribed form that
  the elector has been allowed to vote under subsection 148.1(2);

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} indicate, if applicable, on the prescribed form that
  an elector has voted in the circumstances described in section 147,
  that the solemn declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(1) has
  been made or that any other solemn declaration that was required to be
  made was made, note any objection that was made on behalf of any of
  the candidates and indicate the candidate's name;

- [(i.1)]{.lawlabel} prepare, at intervals of no less than 30 minutes,
  using the prescribed form and as directed by the Chief Electoral
  Officer, a document permitting the identification of every elector who
  during that interval has exercised his or her right to vote on polling
  day --- excluding electors who registered on that day --- and, on
  request, provide it to a candidate's representative;

- [(i.2)]{.lawlabel} prepare, each day after the close of the advance
  polling station, using the prescribed form and as directed by the
  Chief Electoral Officer, a document permitting the identification of
  every elector who has exercised his or her right to vote on that day
  --- excluding electors who registered on that day --- and, on request,
  provide it to a candidate's representative; and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} indicate, if applicable, on the prescribed form, that
  an elector has voted under a registration certificate issued under
  subsection 161(4).

::: HistoricalNote

#### [Secrecy]{.HTitleText3} {#h-205142 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Secret vote

**[[163]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-163 .sectionLabel}** The vote is secret.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure in case of contravention of
secrecy

- **[[164]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-164 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} It
  is the duty of the election officers who are present at the polling
  station to draw the attention of any elector to an offence that the
  elector commits in contravening any of paragraphs 281.6(3)(a) to (c)
  and to the punishment to which the elector is liable, but the elector
  shall be allowed to vote in the usual way if he or she has not already
  done so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Clarification

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, if one election officer
  performs his or her duty under subsection (1) with regard to an
  elector, no other election officer need do so with regard to that
  elector.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 164
- [2018, c. 31, s. 111](#1041992-1131661){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1041992-1131661.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-164-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 164"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Audit]{.HTitleText3} {#h-205155 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Engagement of auditor

**[[164.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-164.1 .sectionLabel}** For each general
election and by-election, the Chief Electoral Officer shall engage an
auditor that he or she considers to have technical or specialized
knowledge --- other than a member of his or her staff or an election
officer --- to perform an audit and report on whether election officers
have properly exercised any of the powers conferred on them under this
Act, or properly performed any of the duties imposed on them under this
Act, that are specified by the Chief Electoral Officer.

- 2014, c. 12, s. 53

:::

### [Prohibitions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-205160 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- use of loudspeakers on
polling day

**[[165]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-165 .sectionLabel}** No person shall use a
loudspeaking device within hearing distance of a polling station on
polling day for the purpose of promoting or opposing a political party
that is listed on the ballot under the name of a candidate or the
election of a candidate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 165
- 2001, c. 21, s. 13
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibitions --- emblems, etc., in
polling station

- **[[166]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-166 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} post or display in, or on the exterior surface of,
    a polling place any campaign literature or other material that could
    be taken as an indication of support for or opposition to a
    political party that is listed on the ballot under the name of a
    candidate or the election of a candidate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} while in a polling station, wear any emblem, flag,
    banner or other thing that indicates that the person supports or
    opposes any candidate or political party that is listed on the
    ballot under the name of a candidate, or the political or other
    opinions entertained, or supposed to be entertained, by the
    candidate or party.

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 113\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph (1)(b), a representative of a
  candidate in a polling station may, in the manner authorized by the
  Chief Electoral Officer, wear a badge identifying his or her function
  and the name of the political party that is listed on the ballot under
  the name of the candidate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 166
- 2001, c. 21, s. 14

  ajax-after="1041998-1131668.html"}

## [PART 10]{.HLabel1}[Advance Polling]{.HTitleText1} {#h-205192 .Part}

### [Establishment of Advance Polling Stations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-205193 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Establishment of advance polling
districts

- **[[168]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-168 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  returning officer shall, as directed by the Chief Electoral Officer,
  establish in his or her electoral district advance polling districts
  that consist of one or more polling divisions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Description of districts

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall give the Chief Electoral
  Officer a description of each advance polling district that is
  established.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Establishment of advance polling
  station

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An advance polling station shall be established in
  each advance polling district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Combining advance polling districts

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} When a request is made to a returning officer not
  later than four days after the issue of the writ, the returning
  officer may, with the prior approval of the Chief Electoral Officer,
  combine two advance polling districts into one district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Request to move an advance polling
  station

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} When a request is made to a returning officer not
  later than four days after the issue of the writ to change the
  location of an advance polling station, the returning officer, with
  the prior approval of the Chief Electoral Officer, may do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Accessibility

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An advance polling station shall be in premises that
  are accessible to electors with a disability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If a returning officer is unable to secure suitable
  premises for an advance polling station that are accessible to
  electors with a disability, the returning officer may, with the prior
  approval of the Chief Electoral Officer, establish the advance polling
  station in premises that are not accessible to such electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advance polling station in more than
  one premises

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} If the returning officer is of the opinion that an
  advance polling district consists of or includes remote, isolated or
  low-density communities, the returning officer may, with the prior
  approval of the Chief Electoral Officer and in accordance with the
  Chief Electoral Officer's instructions, establish the advance polling
  station for that district in premises in more than one such community,
  and have the election officers who are assigned to the advance polling
  station --- along with the ballot box, ballots and other necessary
  election documents --- be at given ones of those premises on different
  days of advance polling to take electors' votes. For greater
  certainty, subsections (5) to (7) apply to the advance polling
  station.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 168
- 2007, c. 21, s. 29
- [2018, c. 31, s. 115](#1042007-1111315){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042007-1111315.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-168-20070726.html "Link to previous version of section 168"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Transfer Certificates]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1131670 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for candidate

- **[[168.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-168.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A candidate whose name appears on
  the revised list of electors for an advance polling station is
  entitled on request to receive a transfer certificate to vote at
  another advance polling station in the same electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for election
  officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An election officer who is assigned to an advance
  polling station shall issue a transfer certificate to any person ---
  other than himself or herself --- whose name appears on the revised
  list of electors for the advance polling station and who has been
  appointed to act as an election officer for another advance polling
  station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Condition

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A transfer certificate issued under subsection (2)
  authorizes the person to vote at the advance polling station named in
  it only if, on one of the days of advance polling, the person performs
  the duty specified in the certificate at the place mentioned in the
  certificate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for elector whose
  advance polling station has moved

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If an elector's advance polling station moves to
  another location after the notice of confirmation of registration has
  been sent, an elector who attends at the advance polling station set
  out in the notice is entitled on request to receive a transfer
  certificate to vote at that advance polling station.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 116](#1042014-1131710){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042014-1131710.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer certificate for elector with
disability

- **[[168.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-168.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An elector who has a disability and
  is therefore unable to vote without difficulty in his or her advance
  polling station may apply for a transfer certificate to vote at
  another advance polling station in the same electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application requirements

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall be made in accordance with the
  Chief Electoral Officer's instructions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issue of transfer certificate to
  elector with disability

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An election officer shall issue a transfer
  certificate in the prescribed form, and provide the certificate to the
  person who submitted the application to the officer, if the officer is
  satisfied that the elector's name appears on the revised list of
  electors for the electoral district.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 116](#1042014-1131719){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042014-1131719.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Signing, numbering and recording transfer
certificate

**[[168.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-168.3 .sectionLabel}** The election
officer who issues a transfer certificate shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} fill in and sign the certificate and mention on it
  the date of its issue;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} consecutively number the certificate in the order of
  its issue;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of the certificate in the order of its
  issue on the prescribed form;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} not issue the certificate in blank; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} if possible, send a copy of the certificate to an
  election officer who is assigned to the advance polling station on
  whose list of electors appears the name of the person to whom the
  certificate has been issued.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 116](#1042014-1131728){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042014-1131728.html"}
:::

### [Registration]{.HTitleText2} {#h-205211 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration at advance polling station

- **[[169]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-169
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every elector whose name is not on
  the revised list of electors may register in person, at the advance
  polling station where the elector is entitled to vote, before an
  election officer who is assigned to that advance polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector shall not be registered unless he or she

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provides as proof of his or her identity and
    residence the piece or pieces of identification referred to in
    paragraph 143(2)(a) or (b), respectively, the piece or one of those
    pieces containing an address that proves his or her residence; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} proves his or her identity and residence by making
    the solemn declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing
    and is accompanied by another elector whose name appears on the list
    of electors for the same polling station and who

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} provides the piece or pieces of identification
      referred to in paragraph 143(2)(a) or (b), respectively, the piece
      or one of those pieces containing either an address that proves
      that other elector's residence or an address that is consistent
      with information related to that other elector that appears on the
      list of electors, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} vouches for the elector by making the solemn
      declaration referred to in subsection 549.1(2) in writing.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vouching for electors in long-term care
  institution

  [(2.01)]{.lawlabel} If an elector who resides in an institution for
  seniors or persons with a disability wishes to prove his or her
  identity and residence under subsection (2), the other elector
  referred to in paragraph (2)(b) who accompanies him or her may be an
  employee of the institution who resides --- despite that paragraph ---
  in any polling division in the elector's electoral district or an
  adjacent electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of
  [[employee]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(2.02)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (2.01),
  [[employee]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes an owner of the institution
  and any person who occupies a management position at the institution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of identification documents

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The representative of a candidate may examine but
  not handle any piece of identification provided by the elector.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration certificate

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the elector satisfies the requirements of
  subsection (2), an election officer who is assigned to the advance
  polling station shall complete a registration certificate in the
  prescribed form authorizing the elector to vote and the elector shall
  sign it. The registration certificate shall include a solemn
  declaration made by the elector that he or she is qualified as an
  elector under section 3.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entry

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An election officer who is assigned to the advance
  polling station shall indicate on the prescribed form the names of the
  electors who are permitted to vote under this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- registration at advance
  polling station

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} It is prohibited for any person to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} knowingly apply to be registered at an advance
    polling station in a name that is not their own;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} knowingly apply, except as authorized by this Act,
    to be registered at an advance polling station to vote in an advance
    polling district in which they are not ordinarily resident;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} apply to be registered at an advance polling
    station to vote in an electoral district knowing that they are not
    qualified as an elector or entitled to vote in the electoral
    district; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} compel, induce or attempt to compel or induce any
    other person to make a false or misleading statement relating to
    that other person's qualification as an elector for the purposes of
    the registration of that other person at an advance polling station.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 117\]]{.Repealed}

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 117\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote

- 2007, c. 21, s. 30, c. 37, s. 3
- 2014, c. 12, s. 54

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement before making solemn
declaration --- elector

- **[[169.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-169.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a person decides to prove his or
  her identity and residence by making the solemn declaration referred
  to in subsection 549.1(1) in writing, an election officer shall,

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person decides to vouch for an elector by making

  declaration, advise him or her in writing of the penalty that may be

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List deemed to be modified

**[[170]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-170 .sectionLabel}** When a registration
certificate is completed and signed in accordance with subsection
169(3), the list of electors is deemed to have been modified in
accordance with the certificate.

### [Voting Procedure]{.HTitleText2} {#h-205253 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conduct of advance polls

- **[[171]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-171
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in this Part, an
  advance poll shall be conducted in the same manner as the manner in
  which the vote at a polling station on polling day is conducted and
  shall be regarded as such for all purposes of this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When advance polling stations to be
  open

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An advance polling station shall be open from
  9:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Friday, Saturday, Sunday and Monday, the
  10th, 9th, 8th and 7th days, respectively, before polling day, and
  shall not be open at any other time.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 171
- 2014, c. 12, s. 56
- [2018, c. 31, s. 119](#1042060-1131752){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042060-1131752.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-171-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 171"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of advance poll

- **[[172]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-172 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  returning officer shall, not later than Saturday, the 16th day before
  polling day,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} give a notice, in the prescribed form, in the
    electoral district of the advance poll, that sets out the following
    information:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the numbers of the polling divisions in every
      advance polling district established by the returning officer,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the location of each advance polling station,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the place where, for each advance polling
      station, an election officer who is assigned to the advance
      polling station shall count the number of votes cast at the
      advance polling station, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} that the counting of the votes cast shall begin
      on polling day as soon after the close of the polling stations as
      possible or, with the Chief Electoral Officer's prior approval,
      one hour before the close of the polling stations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} send two copies of the notice to each candidate and
    to the Chief Electoral Officer; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make available to each candidate in the electoral
    district a map of the electoral district indicating the boundaries
    of each advance polling district and the location of each advance
    polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maps made available to registered
  parties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, not later than
  Saturday, the 16th day before polling day, make available to each
  registered party maps of each electoral district --- in electronic
  form or in formats that include electronic form --- indicating the
  boundaries of each advance polling district within the electoral
  district and the location of each advance polling station.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 172
- [2018, c. 31, s. 120](#1042071-1131769){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042071-1131769.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-172-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 172"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Who may vote at advance polls

- **[[173]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-173 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  elector whose name is on the revised list of electors for a polling
  division in an advance polling district may vote at the advance
  polling station established for the advance polling district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Elector not on the revised list

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector whose name is not on the revised list of
  electors may not vote at an advance polling station unless the elector
  has obtained a transfer certificate under section 168.1 or 168.2 or a
  registration certificate under subsection 169(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure by election officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an elector whose name does not appear on the
  revised list of electors has voted, an election officer who is
  assigned to the advance polling station shall indicate on the
  prescribed form that the elector has voted in accordance with
  subsection (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 173
- 2007, c. 21, s. 32
- [2018, c. 31, s. 121](#1042078-1131774){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042078-1131774.html"}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of election officer

- **[[174]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-174 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an elector whose name is on the list of electors makes a request to
  vote at an advance polling station that is established for his or her
  polling division, an election officer who is assigned to the advance
  polling station shall permit the elector to vote unless the elector
  fails to prove his or her identity and residence in accordance with
  section 143 or to make a solemn declaration otherwise required by this
  Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Number of advance polling district

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} An election officer who gives an elector a ballot
  at an advance polling station shall, before providing the ballot,
  place on the back of the ballot, in the space indicated in Form 3 of
  Schedule 1 for the polling division number, the number of the
  elector's advance polling district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Record of votes cast

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An election officer who is assigned to the advance
  polling station shall keep a record in duplicate at the advance
  polling station, in the prescribed form, of the names of all persons
  who vote at the advance polling station, in the order in which they
  vote, and shall mark on the record the notations that an election
  officer who is assigned to a polling station is required by this Act
  to make opposite an elector's name at the polling station on polling
  day.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 174
- 2007, c. 21, s. 33
- 2014, c. 12, s. 57
- [2018, c. 31, s. 122](#1042082-1131782){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042082-1131782.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-174-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 174"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opening of advance polling station

- **[[175]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-175 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} At
  the opening of an advance polling station at 9:00 a.m., an election
  officer who is assigned to the advance polling station shall, in full
  view of the candidates or their representatives who are present,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on the 1st day of advance polling,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} open the ballot box and ascertain that it is
      empty,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} seal the ballot box with the seals provided by
      the Chief Electoral Officer, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} place the ballot box on a table in full view of
      all present and keep it there until the close of the advance
      polling station on that day; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on the 2nd, 3rd and 4th days of advance polling,
    place the ballot box on a table in full view of all present and keep
    it there until the close of the advance polling station on that day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Close of advance polling station

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} At the close of an advance polling station at 9:00
  p.m. on each of the four days of advance polling, an election officer
  who is assigned to the advance polling station shall, in full view of
  the candidates or their representatives who are present, and in
  accordance with instructions that the Chief Electoral Officer
  considers necessary to ensure the integrity of the vote, take the
  measures set out in those instructions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other ballot boxes

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an election officer who is assigned to the advance
  polling station determines, in accordance with the Chief Electoral
  Officer's instructions, that another ballot box is needed at the
  advance polling station, then an election officer who is assigned to
  the advance polling station shall, in full view of the candidates or
  their representatives who are present and in accordance with those
  instructions,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} take the steps set out in subparagraphs (1)(a)(i)
    to (iii) with regard to that other ballot box; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} take the steps set out in paragraph (1)(b) and in
    subsection (2) with regard to the ballot boxes in the circumstances
    set out in those instructions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Candidates may check seals

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The candidates or their representatives may take note
  of the serial numbers of the seals on the following ballot boxes at
  the times indicated:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for any ballot box that was used on a day of
    advance polling, note may be taken when an advance polling station
    closes on each of the four days of advance polling;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for a ballot box that is placed on the table in
    accordance with subsection (1) or (3), note may be taken when it is
    placed there; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for each of the ballot boxes that were used for
    advance polling, note may be taken when the votes are counted on
    polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Custody of ballot boxes

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Until the counting of the ballots on polling day, an
  election officer shall keep the sealed ballot box or boxes in his or
  her custody in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's
  instructions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery of ballot box

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (5), the returning officer may
  recover any ballot box that another election officer is required under
  that subsection to have in his or her custody if the returning officer
  considers that such action is necessary to ensure the integrity of the
  vote. The returning officer shall inform the Chief Electoral Officer
  of the matter as soon as possible.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery of ballot box --- dwelling
  place or vehicle

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If a ballot box to be recovered is in a dwelling
  place or a vehicle, the returning officer may enter the dwelling place
  or vehicle without the occupant's or owner's consent only if the
  returning officer is accompanying a peace officer who enters the
  dwelling place or vehicle under the authority of a warrant issued
  under subsection (8).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authority to issue warrant

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} On ex parte application by the returning officer, a
  justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing a peace officer
  to enter a dwelling place or a vehicle, accompanied by the returning
  officer, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a ballot box is in the dwelling place or vehicle;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} entry to the dwelling place or vehicle is necessary
    to recover the ballot-box; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} entry was refused by the occupant or owner or there
    are reasonable grounds to believe that entry will be refused by, or
    that consent to entry cannot be obtained from, the occupant or
    owner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Means of telecommunication

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} An application for a warrant under subsection (8) may
  be submitted, and the warrant may be issued, by a means of
  telecommunication and section 487.1 of the [Criminal
  Code](/eng/acts/C-46) applies for those purposes with any necessary
  modifications.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Collecting the record of votes cast at an
advance polling station

- **[[176]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-176 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} As
  soon as possible after the close of advance polling stations on
  Monday, the 7th day before polling day, the returning officer shall
  have the original copy of the record of votes cast collected from the
  advance polling stations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Crossing off names of voters at advance
  polls from lists

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without delay after the returning officer collects
  the records of votes cast at advance polling stations, he or she shall
  cross off the lists of electors the names of all electors who voted at
  the advance polling stations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When lists already distributed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an official list of electors is sent to a polling
  station containing the names of electors that appear in the record of
  votes cast at an advance polling station as having already voted, the
  returning officer shall instruct an election officer who is assigned
  to the polling station to cross their names off the list, and the
  election officer shall do so without delay.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 176
- [2018, c. 31, s. 123](#1042086-1131820){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042086-1131820.html"}
:::
