[Previous
Version](section-237.1-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 237.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting by special ballot

**[[238]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-238 .sectionLabel}** An elector who has been
provided with a special ballot may vote only by following the procedure
set out in subsections 227(2) and (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 238
- [2018, c. 31, s. 162](#1042315-1132101){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042315-1132101.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-238-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 238"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Receipt of special ballot --- application
made outside electoral district

- **[[239]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-239 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  order to have their special ballot counted, an elector whose
  application for registration and special ballot was accepted by the
  special voting rules administrator or by a returning officer outside
  the elector's electoral district shall ensure that the special ballot
  is received by the special voting rules administrator in the National
  Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day. The special
  ballot shall be transmitted by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} sending the sealed outer envelope to the special
    voting rules administrator by mail or any other means; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} delivering it to a Canadian Embassy, High
    Commission or Consular Office, to a Canadian Forces base outside
    Canada or to any other place that the Chief Electoral Officer
    designates.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Receipt of special ballot ---
  application made in electoral district

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In order to have their special ballot counted, an
  elector whose application for registration and special ballot was
  accepted by the returning officer in the elector's electoral district
  shall ensure that the ballot is received at the office of that
  returning officer before the close of the polling stations on polling
  day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vote counted

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), a special ballot referred to
  in that subsection that is received by the special voting rules
  administrator in the National Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m.
  on polling day shall be counted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 239
- [2018, c. 31, s. 162](#1042315-1132113){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042315-1132113.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-239-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 239"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Responsibilities of elector

**[[240]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-240 .sectionLabel}** For the purpose of this
Division, an elector has the sole responsibility to ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} his or her application for registration and special
  ballot is made within the period specified; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} his or her special ballot is received within the
  period specified to be counted as a vote.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Elector to be given regular ballot

**[[241]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-241 .sectionLabel}** An elector who applies
to vote in person at the office of the returning officer for his or her
electoral district after ballots for the electoral district have been
printed shall be given a ballot that is not a special ballot and shall
immediately vote in the manner described in paragraphs 151(1)(a) and (b)
and 227(2)(b) to (d) and return the outer envelope to the election
officer.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No marking

**[[241.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-241.1 .sectionLabel}** If, under section
241, an elector is given a ballot that is not a special ballot, no
marking shall be placed on the back of the ballot in the space otherwise
indicated in Form 3 of Schedule 1 for a polling division number.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 162.1](#1042317-1132117){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042317-1132117.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Spoiled ballot

- **[[242]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-242 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the ballot or special ballot is incapable of being used, the elector
  shall return it to the election officer, who shall mark it as a
  spoiled ballot and give the elector another ballot or special ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector shall not be given more than one ballot or
  special ballot, as the case may be, under subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 242
- [2018, c. 31, s. 163](#1042324-1132123){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042324-1132123.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-242-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 242"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assistance

- **[[243]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-243 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When
  an elector personally goes to the office of the returning officer and
  is unable to read or because of a disability is unable to vote in the
  manner described in this Division, the designated election officer
  shall assist the elector by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} completing the declaration referred to in paragraph
    227(2)(c) and writing the elector's name where the elector's
    signature is to be written; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} marking the ballot as directed by the elector in
    the elector's presence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Note on declaration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An election officer who assists an elector under
  subsection (1) shall indicate, by signing the note on the declaration,
  that the elector was assisted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 243
- [2018, c. 31, s. 164](#1042336-1111337){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042336-1111337.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-243-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 243"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assistance by friend or related person

- **[[243.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-243.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If an elector requires assistance to
  vote, one of the following persons may accompany the elector into the
  voting compartment at the office of the returning officer and assist
  the elector to mark his or her ballot:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a friend of the elector;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the elector's spouse or common-law partner; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a relative of the elector or of the elector's
    spouse or common-law partner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solemn declaration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person described in subsection (1) who wishes to
  assist an elector in marking a ballot shall first make a solemn
  declaration in the prescribed form that he or she

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} will mark the ballot paper in the manner directed
    by the elector;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} will not disclose the name of the candidate for
    whom the elector voted;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} will not try to influence the elector in choosing a
    candidate; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} has not, during the current election, assisted
    another person, as a friend, to mark a ballot.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 165](#1042343-1132140){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042343-1132140.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting at home

- **[[243.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-243.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On application of an elector who is
  unable to read --- or who is unable to vote in the manner described in
  this Division because of a disability --- and who is unable to
  personally go to the office of the returning officer because of a
  disability, an election officer shall go to the elector's dwelling
  place and, in the presence of a witness who is chosen by the elector,
  assist the elector by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} completing the declaration referred to in paragraph
    227(2)(c) and writing the elector's name where the elector's
    signature is to be written; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} marking the ballot as directed by the elector in
    the elector's presence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Note on declaration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The election officer and the witness who assist an
  elector under subsection (1) shall indicate, by signing the note on
  the declaration, that the elector was assisted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 243.1
- [2018, c. 31, s. 166](#1042345-1111343){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042345-1111343.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-243.1-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 243.1"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION 5]{.HLabel2}[Incarcerated Electors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-205779 .Subheading}

Definition of [[elector]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[244]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-244 .sectionLabel}** For the purpose of this
Division, [[elector]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an incarcerated elector.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

**[[244.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-244.1 .sectionLabel}** This Division does
not apply to an elector who is incarcerated in a place designated under
subsection 205(1) of the [National Defence Act](/eng/acts/N-5).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 167](#1042355-1132146){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042355-1132146.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entitlement to vote

- **[[245]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-245
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every elector is entitled to vote
  under this Division on the 12th day before polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exercise of right to vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An elector is not entitled to vote under this
  Division unless he or she has signed an application for registration
  and special ballot under section 251 and a declaration described in
  section 257.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vote to be in electoral district

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An elector is entitled to vote under this Division
  only for a candidate in the electoral district in which his or her
  place of ordinary residence is situated as shown on the application
  for registration and special ballot made by the elector under section
  251.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 245
- [2018, c. 31, s. 168](#1042357-1132150){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042357-1132150.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-245-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 245"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation of coordinating officers

**[[246]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-246 .sectionLabel}** The federal and
provincial ministers responsible for correctional institutions shall
each designate a person as a coordinating officer to work, during and
between elections, with the Chief Electoral Officer to carry out the
purposes and provisions of this Division.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 246
- [2018, c. 31, s. 169](#1042359-1132155){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042359-1132155.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-246-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 246"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of issue of the writs

- **[[247]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-247
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Without delay after the issue of the
  writs, the Chief Electoral Officer shall inform the federal and
  provincial ministers responsible for correctional institutions of
  their issue.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligations of ministers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On being informed of the issue of the writs, each
  minister referred to in subsection (1) shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} inform their respective designated coordinating
    officer of their issue;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} designate one or more persons to act as liaison
    officers in connection with the taking of the votes of electors; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} inform the Chief Electoral Officer and their
    respective designated coordinating officer of the name and address
    of each liaison officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 247
- [2018, c. 31, s. 170](#1042368-1132163){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042368-1132163.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-247-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 247"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liaison officers

- **[[248]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-248 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall appoint persons designated under
  paragraph 247(2)(b) in the prescribed form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to cooperate

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} During the election period, a liaison officer shall
  cooperate with the Chief Electoral Officer in the administration of
  the registration and the taking of the votes of electors, including by
  informing the Chief Electoral Officer of the identity of the electors
  who received a special ballot.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 248
- [2018, c. 31, s. 171](#1042375-1132168){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042375-1132168.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-248-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 248"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of coordinating officer

**[[249]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-249 .sectionLabel}** When a coordinating
officer is informed that a liaison officer has been designated, the
coordinating officer shall give the liaison officer all necessary
information on taking the votes of electors.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of entitlement to vote

- **[[250]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-250 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  liaison officer shall, without delay after being appointed, post a
  notice in the prescribed form in a prominent place in the correctional
  institution that informs electors of the date on which they are
  entitled to vote in accordance with this Division.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting hours

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The polling stations shall be open on the 12th day
  before polling day from 9:00 a.m. and shall be kept open until every
  elector who is registered under subsection 251(1) has voted, but in no
  case shall they be kept open later than 8:00 p.m. on that day.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 250
- [2018, c. 31, s. 172](#1042377-1132173){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042377-1132173.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-250-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 250"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for registration and special
ballot

- **[[251]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-251
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before the 12th day before polling
  day, each liaison officer shall ensure that an application for
  registration and special ballot in the prescribed form is completed
  for every eligible elector of the correctional institution who wishes
  to vote, indicating his or her place of ordinary residence as
  determined under subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Residence of elector

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The place of ordinary residence of an elector is the
  first of the following places for which the elector knows the civic
  and mailing addresses:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} his or her residence before being incarcerated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the residence of the spouse, the common-law
    partner, a relative or a dependant of the elector, a relative of his
    or her spouse or common-law partner or a person with whom the
    elector would live but for his or her incarceration;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the place of his or her arrest; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the last court where the elector was convicted and
    sentenced.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Optional information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In addition to providing his or her place of ordinary
  residence, the Chief Electoral Officer may request that the elector
  provide other information that the Chief Electoral Officer considers
  necessary to implement agreements made under section 55, but the
  elector is not required to provide that information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validation

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The liaison officer shall validate the application
  for registration and special ballot by signing it and indicating on it
  the name of the electoral district that includes the place of ordinary
  residence as determined under subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dispute about electoral district

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a dispute arises as to in which electoral district
  an elector may vote, the elector may refer the matter to the returning
  officer for the electoral district where the correctional institution
  is located, and the returning officer shall make a final determination
  in accordance with the process for revising lists of electors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 251, c. 12, s. 40
- [2018, c. 31, s. 173](#1042379-1132175){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042379-1132175.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-251-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 251"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List of incarcerated electors

**[[252]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-252 .sectionLabel}** Applications for
registration and special ballot are deemed to be the list of electors
who vote under this Division.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Polling stations and election officers

- **[[253]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-253
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before the 18th day before polling
  day, each returning officer shall, for each correctional institution
  in his or her electoral district, in consultation with the liaison
  officer for the institution, establish one or more polling stations
  and assign at least two election officers to each polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of election materials

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A liaison officer shall, on receiving the election
  materials and list of candidates,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide, as necessary, the materials to the
    election officers who are assigned under subsection (1) to a polling
    station for the correctional institution; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} post the list of candidates in one or more
    conspicuous places in the correctional institution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 253
- [2018, c. 31, s. 174](#1042386-1132181){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042386-1132181.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-253-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 253"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of election officer

**[[254]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-254 .sectionLabel}** On the day on which the
electors cast their ballots, at each polling station an election officer
who is assigned to the polling station shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} post two or more copies of the voting instructions,
  in the prescribed form, in conspicuous places; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep readily available for consultation by electors a
  copy of this Part, a set of street indexes, a guide to electoral
  districts and a list of candidates.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 254
- [2018, c. 31, s. 175](#1042391-1132186){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042391-1132186.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-254-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 254"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mobile polling stations

- **[[255]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-255 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  liaison officer shall, when required, establish a mobile polling
  station within a correctional institution to take the votes of the
  electors who are confined to their cells or in an infirmary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Common mobile polling stations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer may, in cooperation with liaison
  officers, create a mobile polling station for correctional
  institutions of fewer than 50 electors that are within the returning
  officer's electoral district and that are within reasonable travelling
  distance of each other.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representative of registered party

**[[256]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-256 .sectionLabel}** With the prior
authorization of correctional authorities, a Canadian citizen may
represent a registered party during the taking of the votes at a
correctional institution if he or she provides an election officer who
is assigned to a polling station at the correctional institution with an
authorization in the prescribed form signed by a candidate for that
party, or a copy of one.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 256
- [2018, c. 31, s. 176](#1042393-1132191){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042393-1132191.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-256-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 256"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration of elector

- **[[257]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-257
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before delivering a special ballot
  to an elector, an election officer who is assigned to a polling
  station at a correctional institution shall require the elector to
  complete an application for registration and special ballot, if the
  elector has not already done so, and to sign the declaration on the
  outer envelope.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Giving special ballot to elector

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} After the elector has signed the declaration on the
  outer envelope, the election officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} sign the outer envelope; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} give the elector a special ballot, an inner
    envelope and the outer envelope.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 257
- [2018, c. 31, s. 177](#1042400-1132196){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042400-1132196.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-257-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 257"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting by special ballot

- **[[258]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-258 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  elector shall vote by writing on the special ballot the name of the
  candidate of his or her choice, folding it and, in the presence of the
  election officer,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} placing the ballot in the inner envelope and
    sealing the envelope; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} placing the inner envelope in the outer envelope
    and sealing the outer envelope.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Writing candidate's name

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The candidate shall be indicated on a special ballot
  by writing the candidate's given name or initials and surname. If two
  or more candidates have the same name, their political affiliations
  shall be indicated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Spoiled special ballot

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the special ballot is incapable of being used, the
  elector shall return it to the election officer, who shall mark it as
  a spoiled ballot and give the elector another special ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An elector shall not be given more than one special
  ballot under subsection (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 258
- [2018, c. 31, s. 178](#1042410-1132202){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042410-1132202.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-258-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 258"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assistance

- **[[259]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-259 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an elector is unable to read or because of a disability is unable to
  vote in the manner described in this Division, an election officer who
  is assigned to the polling station shall assist the elector by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} completing the declaration on the outer envelope
    and writing the elector's name where his or her signature is to be
    written; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} marking the special ballot as directed by the
    elector in his or her presence and in the presence of another
    election officer who is assigned to the polling station.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Note on outer envelope

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The election officers shall sign a note on the outer
  envelope indicating that the elector was assisted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 259
- [2018, c. 31, s. 179](#1042422-1111350){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042422-1111350.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-259-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 259"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delivery of documents after the vote

**[[260]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-260 .sectionLabel}** Without delay after the
votes have been cast at a correctional institution, an election officer
who is assigned to the polling station shall deliver to the liaison
officer for the institution

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the outer envelopes that contain the marked special
  ballots;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any unused or spoiled outer envelopes;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any unused or spoiled special ballots and unused
  inner envelopes; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the applications for registration and special ballot.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 260
- [2018, c. 31, s. 180](#1042429-1132206){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042429-1132206.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-260-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 260"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline for return of election material

**[[261]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-261 .sectionLabel}** Every liaison officer
shall ensure that the election material referred to in section 260 is
received by the special voting rules administrator in the National
Capital Region no later than 6:00 p.m. on polling day.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 261
- [2018, c. 31, s. 181](#1042431-1132211){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042431-1132211.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-261-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 261"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Integration into final list of electors

**[[262]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-262 .sectionLabel}** The applications for
registration and special ballot shall be integrated into the final list
of electors referred to in section 109.

### [DIVISION 6]{.HLabel2}[Counting of Votes at the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer]{.HTitleText2} {#h-205883 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

**[[263]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-263 .sectionLabel}** This Division applies
to the counting of all special ballots cast in accordance with this
Part, except those referred to in Division 7.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Administration

- **[[264]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-264 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  counting of the special ballots shall be conducted by special ballot
  officers under the supervision of the special voting rules
  administrator.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special ballot officers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Special ballot officers shall work in pairs of
  persons representing different registered parties.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directives

**[[265]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-265 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall prescribe security instructions for the safekeeping of
special ballots, inner envelopes, outer envelopes and all other election
documents, and instructions for the receiving, sorting and counting of
special ballots.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Counting of votes

**[[266]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-266 .sectionLabel}** The counting of votes
shall commence on a date to be fixed by the Chief Electoral Officer or,
if no date is fixed, on Wednesday, the 5th day before polling day.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Setting aside of inner envelope

- **[[267]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-267 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  special ballot officers shall set aside an inner envelope unopened if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information concerning the elector, as set out
    in the declaration referred to in paragraph 227(2)(c) or subsection
    257(1), does not correspond with the information on the application
    for registration and special ballot;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a declaration referred to in paragraph (a) or in
    section 212 --- other than one in respect of an elector who has
    voted with assistance under section 216, 243 or 259 --- does not
    bear the elector's signature;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the correct electoral district of the elector whose
    ballot is contained in the inner envelope cannot be ascertained;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the outer envelope has been received by the special
    voting rules administrator in the National Capital Region after 6:00
    p.m. on polling day; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the outer envelope relates to an electoral district
    for which the election was postponed in accordance with section 77.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure when elector votes more than
  once

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, after receiving an elector's outer envelope but
  before counting the inner envelopes, the special ballot officers
  ascertain that the elector has voted more than once, they shall set
  the elector's inner envelope aside unopened.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition of inner envelopes that are
  set aside

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} When an inner envelope is set aside unopened as
  described in subsection (1) or (2),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it shall be endorsed by the special voting rules
    administrator with the reason why it has been set aside;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least two special ballot officers shall initial
    the endorsement; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an inner envelope set aside under
    subsection (1), the ballot contained in it is deemed to be a spoiled
    ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Envelopes and declarations kept
  together

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} When an inner envelope is set aside unopened as
  described in this section, it shall be kept with the outer envelope
  and --- if it did not appear on the outer envelope --- the
  declaration.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dispute

  [(3.2)]{.lawlabel} If a dispute arises regarding the setting aside of
  inner envelopes, it shall be referred to the special voting rules
  administrator, whose decision is final.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special report

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The special voting rules administrator shall prepare
  a report in respect of the number of inner envelopes that are set
  aside under this Division.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 267
- [2018, c. 31, s. 182](#1042448-1111354){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042448-1111354.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-267-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 267"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of special ballot officers

**[[268]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-268 .sectionLabel}** Each pair of special
ballot officers shall count the votes for only one electoral district or
part of an electoral district at a time.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rejection of ballots

- **[[269]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-269 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  pair of special ballot officers shall, on examining a special ballot,
  reject it if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it has not been supplied by the Chief Electoral
    Officer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is not marked;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is marked with a name other than the name of a
    candidate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} it is marked with the names of more than one
    candidate; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} there is any writing or mark on it by which the
    elector could be identified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Elector's intent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No special ballot shall be rejected for the sole
  reason that the elector has incorrectly written the name of a
  candidate, if the ballot clearly indicates the elector's intent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disputed ballots

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a dispute arises as to the validity of a special
  ballot, it shall be referred to the special voting rules
  administrator, whose decision is final.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Note of dispute

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The number of disputed special ballots and the name
  of the electoral district in which they were cast are to be noted by
  the special ballot officers.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statements of the vote

- **[[270]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-270 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  pair of special ballot officers shall prepare a statement of the vote
  in the prescribed form and deliver it to the special voting rules
  administrator.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Safekeeping

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The special voting rules administrator shall keep the
  statements of the vote in safe custody until the day after the
  communication of the results under section 280.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy to special ballot officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On request, after the day that the results are
  communicated, a special ballot officer may be given a copy of the
  statement of the vote that he or she prepared.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief Electoral Officer to be informed of
results of vote

**[[271]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-271 .sectionLabel}** Without delay after the
counting of the votes for every electoral district has been completed,
the special voting rules administrator shall inform the Chief Electoral
Officer of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the number of votes counted for each candidate for
  every electoral district;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the total number of votes counted for each electoral
  district; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number of rejected ballots for each electoral
  district.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sending of material to Chief Electoral
Officer

**[[272]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-272 .sectionLabel}** As soon as practicable
after the counting of the votes for every electoral district has been
completed, the special voting rules administrator shall send to the
Chief Electoral Officer, in separate envelopes,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the lists of electors;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} all other documents and election materials received
  from commanding officers and election officers;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the solemn declarations made under subsection 23(1);
  and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the complete files of correspondence, reports and
  records in his or her possession.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 272
- [2018, c. 31, s. 183](#1042463-1132233){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042463-1132233.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-272-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 272"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION 7]{.HLabel2}[Counting of Votes in the Office of the Returning Officer]{.HTitleText2} {#h-205946 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification to candidates

**[[273]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-273 .sectionLabel}** The returning officer
shall, as soon as possible, notify the candidates of the names of the
election officers who he or she assigns to verify the declarations
referred to in paragraph 227(2)(c) and to count the special ballots
issued to electors in his or her electoral district and received at his
or her office.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 273
- [2018, c. 31, s. 184](#1042465-1132238){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042465-1132238.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-273-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 273"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Candidate present at counting

**[[274]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-274 .sectionLabel}** A candidate or his or
her representative may be present for the verification of the
declarations referred to in paragraph 227(2)(c) and the counting of
ballots received at the returning officer's office.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 274
- [2018, c. 31, s. 184](#1042465-1132243){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042465-1132243.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-274-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 274"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballots to be kept sealed

- **[[275]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-275 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer shall ensure that the ballots received at his or her
  office are kept sealed until they are given to an election officer
  referred to in section 273.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return outer envelopes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} All outer envelopes received after the prescribed
  deadline shall be kept separate and sealed and shall be initialled by
  the returning officer and marked with the date and time of their
  receipt.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 275
- [2018, c. 31, s. 185](#1042467-1132247){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042467-1132247.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-275-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 275"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Verification of declarations

- **[[276]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-276 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  election officers referred to in section 273 shall verify the
  declarations made under paragraph 227(2)(c), at the time fixed by the
  Chief Electoral Officer and in accordance with his or her
  instructions, by determining from the information in the declaration
  whether the elector is entitled to vote in the electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall notify the candidates of
  the time and place of the verification.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of materials to election
  officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} One of the election officers shall be provided with
  the applications for registration and special ballot received before
  the deadline, along with any other materials that may be required.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 276
- [2018, c. 31, s. 186](#1042474-1132254){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042474-1132254.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-276-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 276"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Setting aside of inner envelope

- **[[277]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-277 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  election officer referred to in section 273 shall set aside an
  elector's inner envelope unopened if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information concerning the elector, as set out
    in the elector's declaration made under paragraph 227(2)(c), does
    not correspond with the information on the application for
    registration and special ballot;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the declaration --- other than one in respect of an
    elector who has voted with assistance under section 243 or 243.1 ---
    does not bear the elector's signature;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the elector has voted more than once; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the outer envelope was received after the
    prescribed deadline.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registering objections

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the declarations are verified, an election
  officer referred to in section 273 shall register any objection to an
  elector's right to vote in the electoral district in the prescribed
  form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Noting of reasons for setting aside

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} When an elector's inner envelope is set aside
  unopened as described in subsection (1), the election officer who set
  it aside shall note on it the reasons for the setting aside. The
  election officer and another election officer referred to in section
  273 shall both initial the envelope.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Envelopes and declarations kept
  together

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} When an elector's inner envelope is set aside
  unopened as described in this section, it shall be kept with the outer
  envelope and --- if it did not appear on the outer envelope --- the
  declaration.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 277
- 2018, c. 31, s. 187
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-277-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 277"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Counting of inner envelopes

- **[[278]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-278 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  election officers referred to in section 273 shall count all inner
  envelopes that have not been set aside.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inner envelopes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} They shall put all the inner envelopes that have not
  been set aside in a ballot box provided by the returning officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Counting the votes

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} After the close of the polling stations, one of the
  election officers shall open the ballot box and, together with another
  of the election officers, shall open the inner envelopes and count the
  votes.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 278
- [2018, c. 31, s. 188](#1042493-1132276){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042493-1132276.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-278-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 278"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rejection of ballots

- **[[279]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-279 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  election officer shall, in counting the ballots, reject a ballot if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it has not been supplied for the election;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is not marked;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is marked with a name other than the name of a
    candidate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} it is marked for more than one candidate; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} there is any writing or mark on it by which the
    elector could be identified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Elector's intent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An election officer shall not reject a special ballot
  for the sole reason that the elector has incorrectly written the name
  of a candidate, if the ballot clearly indicates the elector's intent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Political affiliation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An election officer shall not reject a special ballot
  for the sole reason that the elector has written, in addition to the
  name of a candidate, the candidate's political affiliation, if the
  ballot clearly indicates the elector's intent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 279
- 2001, c. 21, s. 15
- [2018, c. 31, s. 189](#1042502-1132282){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042502-1132282.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-279-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 279"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION 8]{.HLabel2}[Communication of the Results of the Vote]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206002 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Communication of results

- **[[280]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-280 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall, without delay after the closing of the
  polling stations at an election, inform each returning officer of the
  results of the count under Division 6 for the returning officer's
  electoral district, giving the number of votes cast for each candidate
  and the number of rejected ballots.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Release of information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the returning officer receives information from
  the Chief Electoral Officer respecting the results of the count under
  Division 6, the returning officer shall add those results to the
  results of the count under Division 7 and release all of them as being
  the results of the vote under the Special Voting Rules.

## [PART 11.1]{.HLabel1}[Prohibitions in Relation to Voting]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206008 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

**[[281]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281 .sectionLabel}** The provisions of this
Part apply inside and outside Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 281
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132288){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132288.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-281-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 281"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief Electoral Officer

**[[281.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.1 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall not vote at an election.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132292){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132292.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inducing Chief Electoral Officer to vote

**[[281.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.2 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
induce or attempt to induce the Chief Electoral Officer to vote at an
election knowing that it is the Chief Electoral Officer whom he or she
is inducing or attempting to induce to vote and that the Chief Electoral
Officer is prohibited from voting.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132296){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132296.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Not qualified as elector

**[[281.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.3 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} vote or attempt to vote at an election knowing that
  he or she

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is not a Canadian citizen when he or she votes, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is not 18 years of age or older --- or will not be
    18 years of age or older --- on polling day; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} induce or attempt to induce another person to vote at
  an election knowing that the other person

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is not a Canadian citizen --- or will not be a
    Canadian citizen --- when he or she votes, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is not 18 years of age or older --- or will not be
    18 years of age or older --- on polling day.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132306){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132306.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Not ordinarily resident in electoral
district

**[[281.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.4 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} vote or attempt to vote at an election in a
  particular electoral district knowing that his or her place of
  ordinary residence is not in that electoral district; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} induce or attempt to induce another person to vote at
  an election in a particular electoral district knowing that the other
  person's place of ordinary residence is not in that electoral
  district.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132312){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132312.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting more than once --- general
election

- **[[281.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.5
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person who has voted in a general
  election shall vote again, or attempt to vote again, in that general
  election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting more than once --- by-election

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person who has voted in a by-election shall vote
  again, or attempt to vote again, at that by-election or at any other
  by-election that is held on the same day.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132319){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132319.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Secrecy of the vote

- **[[281.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.6
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person present at a polling
  station or at the counting of the votes shall maintain the secrecy of
  the vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attempting to obtain information about
  elector's vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided by this Act, no person shall, in a
  polling station, attempt to obtain any information as to the candidate
  for whom any elector is about to vote or has voted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Secrecy at the poll

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided by this Act, no person shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on entering the polling station and before
    receiving a ballot or special ballot, openly declare for whom he or
    she intends to vote;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} while in the polling station, show his or her
    ballot or special ballot, when marked, so as to allow the name of
    the candidate for whom he or she has voted to be seen; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} before leaving the polling station, openly declare
    for whom he or she has voted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Secrecy --- marked ballot

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person who has seen a ballot or special ballot
  that has been marked by an elector shall disclose information as to
  how it was marked unless he or she is the elector who marked it or he
  or she has been authorized to make the disclosure by the elector who
  marked it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Secrecy --- counting of the votes

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person shall, at the counting of the votes,
  attempt to obtain information or communicate information obtained at
  the counting as to the candidate for whom a vote is given in a
  particular ballot or special ballot.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132335){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132335.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballots

- **[[281.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.7
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} request or apply for a ballot or special ballot in
    a name that is not his or her own;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} vote using a forged ballot or forged special
    ballot;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} request or apply for a ballot or special ballot to
    which he or she is not entitled;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} provide a ballot or special ballot to any person
    when not authorized under this Act to do so;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} have a ballot or special ballot in his or her
    possession when not authorized under this Act to do so;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} alter, deface or destroy a ballot, the initials of
    the election officer that are signed on a ballot or the number of
    the polling division or advance polling district that is marked on a
    ballot;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} put or cause to be put into a ballot box a ballot,
    special ballot or other paper otherwise than as provided by this Act
    or by instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} take a ballot out of the polling station or the
    office of the returning officer otherwise than as provided by this
    Act or by instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer; or

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} destroy, take, open or otherwise interfere with a
    ballot box or book or packet of ballots or special ballots otherwise
    than as provided by this Act or by instructions of the Chief
    Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballots --- election officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No election officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with the intent of causing the reception of a vote
    that should not have been cast or the non-reception of a vote that
    should have been cast, put his or her initials on the back of any
    paper purporting to be or capable of being used as a ballot at an
    election; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} place on a ballot or special ballot any writing,
    number or mark with intent that the elector to whom the ballot or
    special ballot is to be given, or has been given, can be identified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special ballots --- unit election
  officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No unit election officer shall place on a special
  ballot any writing, number or mark with intent that the elector to
  whom the special ballot is to be given, or has been given, can be
  identified.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132355){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132355.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Photograph, video or copy of marked
ballot

- **[[281.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.8
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} take a photograph or make a video recording of a
    ballot or special ballot that has been marked, at an election, by an
    elector;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make a copy, in any manner, of any ballot or
    special ballot that has been marked, at an election, by an elector;
    or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} distribute or show, in any manner, to one or more
    persons, a photograph, video recording or copy of a ballot or
    special ballot that has been marked, at an election, by an elector.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- persons with visual
  impairment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to any person with a
  visual impairment who takes a photograph or makes a video recording or
  copy of a ballot or special ballot that he or she has marked for the
  purpose of verifying the accuracy of their marking.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- legal proceedings

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who does
  anything referred to in that subsection for the purpose of a recount
  under Part 14 or for the purpose of any other legal proceeding.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132367){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132367.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}False statement

**[[281.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-281.9 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} make a false statement in an application for
  registration and special ballot; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} make a false statement in a declaration signed by him
  or her before an election officer or unit election officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132373){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132373.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person who assists elector --- limit

- **[[282]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} At
  an election, no person shall, as a friend, assist under section 155 or
  243.01, more than one elector for the purpose of marking a ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person who assists elector --- secrecy

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person who assists an elector under section 155 or
  243.01 shall, directly or indirectly, disclose the name of the
  candidate for whom the elector voted or that candidate's political
  affiliation.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 282
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132381){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132381.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-282-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 282"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vouching for more than one person

- **[[282.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall vouch for more than
  one person at an election, except in the cases referred to in
  subsections 143(3.01), 161(2) and 169(2.01).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voucher not qualified as elector, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall vouch for another person if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person who vouches is not qualified as an
    elector;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person who vouches does not personally know the
    other person; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person who vouches does not reside in a polling
    division assigned to the same polling station as the polling
    division in which the other person resides or, in the cases referred
    to in subsections 143(3.01), 161(2) and 169(2.01), in a polling
    division in the other person's electoral district or an adjacent
    electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vouchee acting as voucher

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person who has been vouched for at an election
  shall vouch for another person at that election.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132393){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132393.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Influencing electors

**[[282.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.2 .sectionLabel}** No person shall, in
a polling station or in any place where voting at an election is taking
place, influence or attempt to influence electors to vote or refrain
from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular
candidate or registered party, at the election.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132397){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132397.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Influencing electors --- election
officers and staff of returning officers

**[[282.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.3 .sectionLabel}** Subject to section
141, no election officer, unit election officer or member of the staff
of a returning officer shall, while exercising their powers or
performing their duties, influence or attempt to influence an elector to
vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a
particular candidate or registered party, at an election.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132401){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132401.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Undue influence by foreigners

- **[[282.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity referred to in
  any of paragraphs (a) to (e) shall, during an election period, unduly
  influence an elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or
  refrain from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at
  the election:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an individual who is not a Canadian citizen or a
    [[permanent resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in
    subsection 2(1) of the [Immigration and Refugee Protection
    Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5) and who does not reside in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a corporation or entity incorporated, formed or
    otherwise organized outside Canada that does not carry on business
    in Canada or whose primary purpose in Canada during an election
    period is to influence electors during that period to vote or
    refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a
    particular candidate or registered party, at the election;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a trade union that does not hold bargaining rights
    for employees in Canada;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a foreign political party; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a foreign government or an agent or mandatary of a
    foreign government.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meaning of unduly influencing

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), a person or
  entity unduly influences an elector to vote or refrain from voting, or
  to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate or
  registered party, at an election if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} they knowingly incur any expense to directly
    promote or oppose a candidate in that election, a registered party
    that has endorsed a candidate in that election or the leader of such
    a registered party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} one of the things done by them to influence the
    elector is an offence under an Act of Parliament or a regulation
    made under any such Act, or under an Act of the legislature of a
    province or a regulation made under any such Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, subsection (1) does not apply
  if the only thing done by the person or entity to influence the
  elector to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from
  voting for the particular candidate or registered party, consists of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an expression of their opinion about the outcome or
    desired outcome of the election;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a statement by them that encourages the elector to
    vote or refrain from voting for any candidate or registered party in
    the election; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the transmission to the public through
    broadcasting, or through electronic or print media, of an editorial,
    a debate, a speech, an interview, a column, a letter, a commentary
    or news, regardless of the expense incurred in doing so, if no
    contravention of subsection 330(1) or (2) is involved in the
    transmission.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Collusion

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity shall act in collusion with a
  person or entity to whom subsection (1) applies for the purpose of
  contravening that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Selling advertising space

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity shall sell any advertising space
  to a person or entity to whom subsection (1) applies for the purpose
  of enabling that person or entity to transmit an election advertising
  message or to cause an election advertising message to be transmitted.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132424){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132424.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interfering with marking of ballot

**[[282.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.5 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
interfere with, or attempt to interfere with, an elector who is marking
a ballot or special ballot.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132428){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132428.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preventing elector from voting

**[[282.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.6 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
prevent or attempt to prevent an elector from voting at an election.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132432){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132432.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offering bribe

- **[[282.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.7
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall, during an election
  period, directly or indirectly, offer a bribe to influence an elector
  to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for
  a particular candidate or registered party, at the election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Accepting bribe

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall, during an election period, accept or
  agree to accept a bribe that is offered to them to vote or refrain
  from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular
  candidate or registered party, at the election.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132439){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132439.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Intimidation, etc.

**[[282.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-282.8 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} by intimidation or duress, compel or attempt to
  compel a person to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain
  from voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an
  election; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} by any pretence or contrivance, including by
  representing that the ballot or special ballot or the manner of voting
  at an election is not secret, influence or attempt to influence a
  person to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from
  voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at an election.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 190](#1042509-1132445){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042509-1132445.html"}
:::

## [PART 12]{.HLabel1}[Counting Votes]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206023 .Part}

### [Polling Stations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206024 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Counting the votes

- **[[283]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-283
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Immediately after the close of a
  polling station, an election officer who is assigned to the polling
  station shall count the votes in the presence of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} another election officer who is assigned to the
    polling station; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any candidates or their representatives who are
    present or, if no candidates or representatives are present, at
    least two electors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tally sheets

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} One of those election officers shall supply all the
  persons referred to in paragraph (1)(b) who are present and who
  request one with a tally sheet to keep their own score of the voting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Steps to follow

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The election officer who counts the votes shall, in
  the following order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} count the number of electors who voted, count the
    number of those to whom a certificate was given under subsection
    161(4), make an entry at the end of the list of electors that states
    "The number of electors who voted at this election is (*stating the
    number*). Of these, the number of electors to whom a certificate was
    given under subsection 161(4) is (*stating the number*).", sign the
    list and place the list in the envelope supplied for that purpose;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} count the spoiled ballots, place them in the
    envelope supplied for the purpose, indicate on the envelope the
    number of spoiled ballots, and seal it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} count the unused ballots that are not detached from
    the books of ballots, place them with the stubs of the used ballots
    in the envelope supplied for the purpose, indicate on the envelope
    the number of unused ballots, and seal it;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} total the number of electors indicated under
    paragraph (a) who voted and the numbers arrived at in paragraphs (b)
    and (c) in order to ascertain that all ballots that were provided by
    the returning officer are accounted for;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} open the ballot box and empty its contents onto a
    table; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} examine each ballot, show the ballot to each person
    who is present, and ask the election officer referred to in
    paragraph (1)(a) to make a note on the tally sheet beside the name
    of the candidate for whom the vote was cast for the purpose of
    arriving at the total number of votes cast for each candidate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 283
- 2014, c. 12, s. 61
- [2018, c. 31, s. 191](#1042526-1132455){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042526-1132455.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-283-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 283"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rejection of ballots

- **[[284]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-284 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  examining the ballots, the election officer who counts the votes shall
  reject one

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that has not been supplied by him or her;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that has not been marked in a circle at the right
    of the candidates' names;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} that is void by virtue of section 76;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} that has been marked in more than one circle at the
    right of the candidates' names; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} on which there is any writing or mark by which the
    elector could be identified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No ballot shall be rejected by reason only that an
  election officer placed on it any writing, number or mark, or failed
  to remove the counterfoil or to write the elector's polling division
  number on the back of the ballot.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Counterfoils remaining attached

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a ballot is found with the counterfoil attached,
  the election officer who counts the votes shall, while concealing the
  number on it from all persons present and without examining it, remove
  and destroy the counterfoil.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 284
- [2018, c. 31, s. 192](#1042546-1132463){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042546-1132463.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-284-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 284"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballots not initialled by election
officer

**[[285]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-285 .sectionLabel}** If the election officer
who counts the votes determines that a ballot has not been initialed by
an election officer, he or she shall, in the presence of the election
officer referred to in paragraph 283(1)(a) and witnesses, initial and
count the ballot if satisfied that all ballots that were provided by the
returning officer have been accounted for, as described in paragraph
283(3)(d).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 285
- [2018, c. 31, s. 193](#1042551-1132468){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042551-1132468.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-285-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 285"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Objections to ballots

- **[[286]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-286 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} One
  of the election officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall make a
  record, in the prescribed form, of every objection to a ballot made by
  a candidate or candidate's representative, give a number to the
  objection, write that number on the ballot and initial it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Decision of election officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every question that is raised by the objection shall
  be decided by the election officer who counts the votes, and the
  decision is subject to reversal only on a recount or on application
  under subsection 524(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 286
- [2018, c. 31, s. 193](#1042551-1132476){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042551-1132476.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-286-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 286"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of vote

- **[[287]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-287 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  election officer who counts the votes shall prepare a statement of the
  vote, in the prescribed form, that sets out the number of votes in
  favour of each candidate and the number of rejected ballots and shall
  place the original statement and a copy of it in the separate
  envelopes supplied for the purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies of statement of vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The election officer shall give a copy of the
  statement of the vote to each of the candidates' representatives
  present at the count.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 287
- [2018, c. 31, s. 194](#1042558-1132483){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042558-1132483.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-287-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 287"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Marked ballots

- **[[288]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-288 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} One
  of the election officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall place
  the ballots for each candidate into separate envelopes, write on each
  envelope the name of the candidate and the number of votes he or she
  received, and seal it. The election officers shall sign the seal on
  each envelope, and the witnesses may also sign them.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rejected ballots

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} One of the election officers shall place into
  separate envelopes the rejected ballots, the registration certificates
  and the list of electors, and shall seal the envelopes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Documents enclosed in large envelope

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} One of the election officers shall seal in a large
  envelope supplied for the purpose

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the envelopes that contain the marked ballots for
    the candidates, any spoiled ballots, unused ballots or rejected
    ballots, and the official list of electors; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any other election documents, except for the
    envelopes that contain the statements of the vote and the
    registration certificates.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Documents to be placed in the ballot
  box

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The large envelope described in subsection (3) and
  the envelope that contains the copy of the statement of the vote shall
  be placed in the ballot box.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sealing ballot box

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The ballot box shall be sealed with the seals
  provided by the Chief Electoral Officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 288
- [2018, c. 31, s. 195](#1042570-1132493){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042570-1132493.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-288-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 288"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solemn declarations

**[[288.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-288.01 .sectionLabel}** One of the
election officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall place the form
for each solemn declaration made under subsection 143(3) or paragraph
161(1)(b) or 169(2)(b) in an envelope supplied for the purpose.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 62
- [2018, c. 31, s. 196](#1042577-1132496){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042577-1132496.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-288.01-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 288.01"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Periodic statements of electors who voted

**[[288.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-288.1 .sectionLabel}** One of the election
officers referred to in subsection 283(1) shall place a copy of each
document prepared for the purpose of paragraph 162(i.1) in an envelope
supplied for the purpose.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 62
- [2018, c. 31, s. 196](#1042577-1132499){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042577-1132499.html"}
:::

### [Advance Polls]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206087 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Counting of votes on polling day

- **[[289]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-289 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} At
  least two election officers who are assigned to an advance polling
  station and who are specified in accordance with the Chief Electoral
  Officer's instructions shall, at the close of the polling stations on
  polling day, attend at the place mentioned in the notice of advance
  poll in subparagraph 172(a)(iii) to count the votes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of rules for counting votes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsections 283(1) and (2), paragraphs 283(3)(e)
  and (f) and sections 284 to 288 apply with any necessary modifications
  to the counting of the votes of an advance poll except that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for the application of paragraph 283(3)(e), the two
    or more election officers who are specified in accordance with the
    Chief Electoral Officer's instructions shall open the ballot boxes
    and empty their contents onto a table; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for the application of subsection 288(4), the large
    envelope and the envelope that contains the copy of the statement of
    the vote shall be placed in the ballot box used on the last day of
    advance polling.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no person shall make a
  count of the votes cast at an advance poll before the close of voting
  hours on polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The two or more election officers who are specified
  in accordance with the Chief Electoral Officer's instructions may
  begin counting the votes cast at an advance poll one hour before the
  close of voting hours on polling day if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the returning officer who is responsible for the
    advance polling station has obtained the Chief Electoral Officer's
    prior approval for the counting to begin;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the counting is done in accordance with the Chief
    Electoral Officer's instructions;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the counting is done in a manner that ensures the
    integrity of the vote; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the counting is done in the presence of any
    candidates or their representatives who are present or, if no
    candidates or representatives are present, at least two electors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 289
- 2014, c. 12, s. 63
- [2018, c. 31, s. 197](#1042590-1132510){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042590-1132510.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-289-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 289"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Delivery of Ballot Boxes to Returning Officer]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206099 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sending ballot boxes and envelopes to
returning officer

**[[290]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-290 .sectionLabel}** An election officer who
is assigned to a polling station or an advance polling station shall,
without delay after sealing the ballot box, send to the returning
officer the box, with the envelope that contains the original statement
of the vote, the envelope that contains the registration certificates,
the envelope referred to in section 288.01 and, in the case of an
election officer who is assigned to a polling station, the envelope
referred to in section 288.1.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 290
- 2014, c. 12, s. 64
- [2018, c. 31, s. 198](#1042599-1132513){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042599-1132513.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-290-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 290"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of documents

**[[291]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-291 .sectionLabel}** A returning officer
shall --- on the request of the candidate, his or her representative or
a representative of the candidate's party --- provide him or her, after
polling day, with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} one copy of each statement of the vote in respect of
  the candidate's electoral district; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} one copy of the documents prepared under paragraph
  162(i.1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 291
- 2014, c. 12, s. 65
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-291-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 291"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Safekeeping of ballot boxes

**[[292]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-292 .sectionLabel}** A returning officer, on
the receipt of each ballot box, shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} take every precaution to prevent any other person,
  except the assistant returning officer, from having access to it; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} examine and record the condition of the seals affixed
  to it and, if necessary, affix new seals.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List of persons who made solemn
declaration

**[[292.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-292.1 .sectionLabel}** A returning
officer, on the receipt of each envelope referred to in section 288.01,
shall create a list of the names of all persons who made a solemn
declaration under subsection 143(3) or paragraph 161(1)(b) or 169(2)(b)
and shall include in the list the address of each of those persons.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 66
- [2018, c. 31, s. 199](#1042603-1132516){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042603-1132516.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-292.1-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 292.1"){.PITLink}
