## [PART 13]{.HLabel1}[Validation of Results by the Returning Officer]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206121 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validation of results

- **[[293]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-293
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After a returning officer receives
  all of the ballot boxes, he or she shall, at his or her office, in the
  presence of the assistant returning officer at the time indicated in
  paragraph 62(c), validate the results of the vote from the original
  statements of the vote and the information communicated under section
  280.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjournment if ballot boxes or
  information not received

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, on the day fixed for the validation of the
  results as described in paragraph 62(c), a returning officer has not
  received all the ballot boxes or the information required by section
  280, the returning officer shall adjourn the proceedings for not more
  than seven days.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Further adjournment

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, on the day fixed for the proceedings by virtue of
  an adjournment under subsection (2), the returning officer has not,
  for any reason, received the ballot boxes or information referred to
  in that subsection, the returning officer may make further
  adjournments. The further adjournments may not exceed a total of two
  weeks.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Witnesses at validation

**[[294]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-294 .sectionLabel}** Candidates and their
representatives may attend the validation of the results, but if none of
them is present, the returning officer shall ensure the presence of at
least two electors until the validation is completed.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opening ballot box in certain cases

- **[[295]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-295 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the original statement of the vote is missing, appears to contain an
  error, to be incomplete or to have been altered, or is disputed by a
  candidate or his or her representative, the returning officer may open
  the ballot box and the envelope that contains the copy of the
  statement of the vote or, if that copy is missing, the large envelope.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information on envelopes containing
  ballots

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a copy of the statement of the vote is not found
  or is not useful for the purpose of validating the results, the
  returning officer may use the information that is written on the
  envelopes that contain the ballots for that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall not open an envelope that
  appears to contain ballots.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resealing of loose papers

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the returning officer opens the large envelope, he
  or she shall place its contents into another envelope, seal that
  envelope and initial the seal.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loss or destruction of ballot boxes

- **[[296]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-296 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  ballot box has been destroyed or is missing, the returning officer
  shall ascertain the cause of the destruction or loss and shall
  complete the validation of the results from the original copy of the
  statement of the vote in the same manner as if he or she had received
  the ballot box.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to summon and examine

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the returning officer is unable to obtain either
  the original statement of the vote or the ballot box, he or she

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall ascertain, by any evidence that he or she is
    able to obtain, the total number of votes cast for each candidate at
    the polling stations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for ascertaining the total number of votes under
    paragraph (a), may summon any election officer or other person to
    appear before him or her at a fixed date and time and to bring with
    them all necessary documents; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} may question the election officer or other person
    respecting the matter in question and, if necessary, ask them to
    make a solemn declaration in respect of the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to candidates

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If paragraph (2)(b) applies, the returning officer
  shall give notice to the candidates for that electoral district of the
  date and time fixed for the appearance.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to comply with summons

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Every person to whom a summons is directed under
  paragraph (2)(b) shall obey it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 296
- [2018, c. 31, s. 200](#1042607-1132521){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042607-1132521.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-296-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 296"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate of votes cast

**[[297]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-297 .sectionLabel}** Without delay after the
validation of the results, the returning officer shall prepare a
certificate in the prescribed form that sets out the number of votes
cast for each candidate, and shall deliver the original of the
certificate to the Chief Electoral Officer and a copy of it to each
candidate or his or her representative. In the case described in section
296, the certificate shall indicate the number of votes that have been
ascertained to have been cast for each candidate.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballot boxes

**[[298]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-298 .sectionLabel}** After the close of an
election, each returning officer shall dispose of the ballot boxes as
instructed by the Chief Electoral Officer.

## [PART 14]{.HLabel1}[Judicial Recount]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206156 .Part}

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206157 .Subheading}

Definition of [[judge]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[299]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-299 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this Part, [[judge]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a judge who sits in the
  electoral district where the results are validated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of judge

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A judge who is authorized by sections 300 to 309 to
  act may act, to the extent authorized, within or outside his or her
  judicial district.

### [Recount Procedure]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206163 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Request by returning officer for recount

- **[[300]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-300 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the difference between the number of votes cast for the candidate with
  the most votes and the number cast for any other candidate is less
  than 1/1000 of the votes cast, the returning officer shall make a
  request to a judge for a recount within four days after the results
  are validated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to candidates

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall notify each candidate or
  his or her official agent in writing of the request for a recount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recount automatic

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall fix the date for the recount to be
  conducted within four days after he or she receives the request.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Documents to be supplied

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall attend the recount and
  shall bring all relevant election materials including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the ballot boxes;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the statements of the vote used to validate the
    results; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} all ballots cast and statements of the vote made in
    accordance with Part 11.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for recount

- **[[301]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  elector may, within four days after the day on which a returning
  officer issues a certificate under section 297 and after notifying the
  returning officer in writing, apply to a judge for a recount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to candidates

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The returning officer shall notify each candidate
  or his or her official agent in writing of the application for a
  recount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Grounds for recount

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall fix a date for a recount if it
  appears, on the affidavit of a credible witness, that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an election officer has incorrectly counted or
    rejected any ballots, or has written an incorrect number on the
    statement of the vote for the votes cast for a candidate; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the returning officer has incorrectly added up the
    results set out in the statements of the vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deposit

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The applicant shall deposit with the clerk or
  prothonotary of the court the sum of \$250 as security for the costs
  of the candidate who obtained the largest number of votes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Date for recount and summons

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The date fixed for the recount shall be within four
  days after the judge receives the application. The judge shall summon
  the returning officer to attend and to bring the relevant ballot boxes
  and statements of the vote together with the ballots that were
  counted, and the statements that were completed, under Part 11.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to candidates

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall notify each candidate or his or her
  official agent in writing of the time and place fixed for the recount.
  The judge may decide that service of the notice will be
  substitutional, by mail or posting or in any other manner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Returning officer required to attend

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer to whom a summons is directed
  under subsection (4) shall obey it and shall be present throughout the
  recount.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 301
- 2014, c. 12, s. 67
- [2018, c. 31, s. 201](#1042609-1111360){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042609-1111360.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-301-20190119.html "Link to previous version of section 301"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}More than one application

**[[302]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302 .sectionLabel}** If a judge receives
more than one application for a recount for more than one electoral
district, the recounts shall be conducted in the order in which the
judge receives the applications.

**[[303]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2014, c.
12, s. 68\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-303-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 303"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recount procedure

- **[[304]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-304 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  judge shall conduct the recount by adding the number of votes reported
  in the statements of the vote or by counting the valid ballots or all
  of the ballots returned by election officers or the Chief Electoral
  Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Documents that may be examined

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a recount of all of the ballots returned is
  required, the judge may open the sealed envelopes that contain the
  used and counted, unused, rejected and spoiled ballots. The judge
  shall not open any envelopes that appear to contain other documents or
  refer to any other election documents.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure for certain recounts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a recount conducted by counting the
  valid ballots or all of the ballots returned by election officers or
  the Chief Electoral Officer, the procedure set out in Schedule 4
  applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of judge

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of arriving at the facts with respect
  to a missing ballot box or statement of the vote, the judge has all
  the powers of a returning officer with regard to the attendance and
  examination of witnesses who, in case of non-attendance, are subject
  to the same consequences as in the case of refusal or neglect to
  attend on the summons of a returning officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional powers of judge

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of conducting a recount, a judge has
  the power to summon any election officer as a witness and to require
  him or her to give evidence on oath and, for that purpose, has the
  same power that is vested in any court of record.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Clerical assistants

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the approval of the Chief Electoral
  Officer, a judge may retain the services of support staff to assist in
  the performance of his or her duties under this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 304
- 2014, c. 12, s. 69
- [2018, c. 31, s. 202](#1042632-1132528){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042632-1132528.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-304-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 304"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proceedings to be continuous

**[[305]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305 .sectionLabel}** The judge shall, as far
as practicable, proceed continuously with a recount, except for
necessary breaks and, unless the judge orders otherwise, between 6:00
p.m. and 9:00 a.m.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Security of documents

- **[[306]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-306
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} During a break described in section
  305, the judge or any other person who has possession of ballots and
  other election documents shall keep them sealed in parcels, and the
  seal shall be signed by the judge and may be signed by any other
  person in attendance.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supervision of sealing

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall personally supervise the parcelling
  and sealing of ballots and documents at a recount and take all
  necessary precautions for their security.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Judge may terminate recount

**[[307]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307 .sectionLabel}** Except in a case
referred to in section 300, a judge may at any time terminate a recount
on request in writing by the person who applied for the recount.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure at conclusion of recount

**[[308]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-308 .sectionLabel}** At the conclusion of a
recount, the judge shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} seal the ballots in a separate envelope for each
  polling station and without delay prepare a certificate in the
  prescribed form that sets out the number of votes cast for each
  candidate;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} deliver the original of the certificate to the
  returning officer and a copy of it to each candidate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} return to the returning officer the election
  documents or election materials brought under subsection 300(4) or
  301(4) for the purpose of the recount; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} deliver to the returning officer the reports created
  in the course of the recount.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 308
- 2014, c. 12, s. 70
- [2018, c. 31, s. 203](#1042641-1111364){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042641-1111364.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-308-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 308"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Costs

- **[[309]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-309 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  recount does not alter the result of the vote so as to affect the
  return, the judge shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} order the costs of the candidate for whom the
    largest number of votes have been cast to be paid by the person who
    applied for the recount; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} tax those costs, following as closely as possible
    the tariff of costs allowed with respect to proceedings in the court
    in which the judge ordinarily presides.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposal of deposit and right of action
  for balance

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The money deposited as security for costs shall, as
  far as is necessary, be paid out to the candidate in whose favour
  costs are awarded under subsection (1) and, if the deposit is
  insufficient to cover the costs, the party in whose favour the costs
  are awarded has their action for the balance.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for reimbursement of costs

- **[[310]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-310
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After a recount, a candidate may
  make an application to the Chief Electoral Officer for reimbursement
  of his or her costs in respect of the recount, setting out the amount
  and nature of the costs and whether they were actually and reasonably
  incurred.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief Electoral Officer determines
  costs

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of an application under subsection (1),
  the Chief Electoral Officer shall determine the costs, and shall make
  a request for reimbursement to the Receiver General, up to a maximum
  of \$500 for each day or part of a day during which the judge
  conducted the recount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment from Consolidated Revenue Fund

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Receiver General, on receipt of a request for
  reimbursement from the Chief Electoral Officer, shall pay to the
  candidate the amount requested from the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

### [Failure of Judge to Conduct Recount]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206241 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure of judge to act

- **[[311]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-311 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  judge does not comply with the provisions of sections 300 to 309, an
  aggrieved party may, within eight days after the failure to comply,
  make application for an order under subsection (3)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the Province of Ontario, to a judge of the
    Superior Court of Justice;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the Province of Quebec, New Brunswick or
    Alberta, Yukon, the Northwest Territories or Nunavut, to a judge of
    the Court of Appeal of the Province or Territory;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the Province of Nova Scotia, British Columbia or
    Prince Edward Island, to a judge of the Supreme Court of the
    Province;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the Province of Manitoba or Saskatchewan, to a
    judge of the Court of Queen's Bench for the Province; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador, to a
    judge of the Trial Division of the Supreme Court of Newfoundland and
    Labrador.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application on affidavit

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An application under subsection (1) may be made on
  affidavit, which need not be entitled in any matter or cause, that
  sets out the facts relating to the failure to comply.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order of judge

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The judge to whom an application is made under
  subsection (1) shall, if it appears that there was a failure to
  comply, make an order

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} fixing the time, within the following eight days,
    and place to hear the application;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} directing the attendance of all parties interested
    at that time and place; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} giving directions for the service of the order, and
    of any affidavit on which it was granted, on the judge alleged to
    have failed to comply and on any other interested party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affidavits may be filed in reply

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The judge complained of and any interested party may
  file in the office of the clerk, registrar or prothonotary of the
  court of the judge to whom the application is made affidavits in reply
  to those filed by the applicant and shall provide the applicant with
  copies of them on demand.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 311
- 2002, c. 7, s. 93
- 2014, c. 12, s. 71
- [2018, c. 31, s. 204(F)](#1042645-1111365){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042645-1111365.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-311-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 311"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order of court after hearing

- **[[312]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-312
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After hearing the judge complained
  of and any other parties, the judge to whom the application was made
  or another judge of the same court

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall make an order dismissing the application or
    ordering the judge in default to comply with the requirements of
    this Act in respect of the recount; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may make an order with respect to costs.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Judge to obey order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A judge found to be in default shall without delay
  comply with an order made under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Costs

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Remedies for the recovery of costs awarded under
  paragraph (1)(b) are the same as for costs in ordinary cases in the
  same court.

## [PART 15]{.HLabel1}[Return of the Writ]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206270 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return of elected candidate

- **[[313]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-313 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer, without delay after the sixth day that follows the
  completion of the validation of results or, if there is a recount,
  without delay after receiving the certificate referred to in section
  308, shall declare elected the candidate who obtained the largest
  number of votes by completing the return of the writ in the prescribed
  form on the back of the writ.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Equality of votes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If there is an equality of votes between the
  candidates with the largest number of votes, the returning officer
  shall indicate that on the return of the writ.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sending of documents

- **[[314]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-314 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  completing the return of the writ, the returning officer shall without
  delay send to the Chief Electoral Officer all election documents in
  his or her possession together with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a report of the returning officer's proceedings in
    the prescribed form including his or her comments with respect to
    the state of the election documents received from election officers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a summary, in the prescribed form, of the number of
    votes cast for each candidate at each polling station; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} all other documents that were used at the election,
    including documents prepared under paragraph 162(i.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report re: disappearance of ballot box,
  etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In any case arising under section 296, the returning
  officer shall mention specially in the report the circumstances
  accompanying the disappearance of the ballot boxes or the lack of any
  statement of the vote, and the mode by which the returning officer
  ascertained the number of votes cast for each candidate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 314
- [2018, c. 31, s. 205](#1042655-1132533){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042655-1132533.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-314-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 314"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duplicate of return to each candidate

- **[[315]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-315 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  returning officer shall forward a copy of the return of the writ to
  each candidate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Premature return

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A premature return of the writ is deemed not to have
  reached the Chief Electoral Officer until it should have reached the
  Chief Electoral Officer in due course.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Correction of writ

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, if necessary, send
  back the return of the writ and any or all of the related election
  documents to the returning officer for completion or correction.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where report made before recount

- **[[316]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-316
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where, at the time of the issue of
  an order under section 311 or 312, the returning officer for the
  electoral district in respect of which the order is made has made a
  return of the writ under section 314, the Chief Electoral Officer
  shall, on being provided with a certified copy of the order, send back
  to the returning officer all election documents required for use at
  the recount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of returning officer on recount

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receiving a judge's certificate with respect to
  the result of a recount, the returning officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the result of the recount is that a person other
    than the person named in the original return is to be returned, make
    a substitute return of the writ; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the result of the recount is to confirm the
    return, send the papers back to the Chief Electoral Officer without
    delay and not make a substitute return of the writ.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of substitute return

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A substitute return made under paragraph (2)(a) has
  the effect of cancelling the original return.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure on receipt of return by Chief
Electoral Officer

**[[317]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-317 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer, on receiving each return of the writ, shall, in the order in
which the return is received,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} indicate, in a book kept by the Chief Electoral
  Officer for the purpose, that he or she has received it; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} publish in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) the name of the candidate who was
  declared elected.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Equality of votes

**[[318]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-318 .sectionLabel}** If the return of the
writ indicates an equality of votes between the candidates with the
largest number of votes, the Chief Electoral Officer shall without delay

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} prepare and send to the Speaker of the House of
  Commons or, if none, two members of the House or two candidates who
  have been declared elected, as the case may be, a report stating that
  no candidate was declared elected in the electoral district because of
  the equality of votes; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} publish in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the names of the candidates between whom there was
    an equality of votes, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} notice that, as no candidate was declared elected
    in the electoral district because of the equality of votes, a
    by-election will be conducted under subsection 29(1.1) of the
    [Parliament of Canada Act](/eng/acts/P-1).

## [PART 16]{.HLabel1}[Communications]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206310 .Part}

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206311 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[319]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-319 .sectionLabel}** The definitions in this
section apply in this Part.

[[election advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[election advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2018, c.
    31, s. 206\]]{.Repealed}

[[election survey]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[election survey]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s.
    206\]]{.Repealed}

[[network]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[network]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a network as defined in
    subsection 2(1) of the [Broadcasting Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01), but
    does not include a temporary network operation as defined in that
    subsection. ([réseau]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[network operator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[network operator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person or
    undertaking to which permission has been granted by the Canadian
    Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission to form and
    operate a network. ([exploitant de réseau]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[online platform]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[online platform]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes an Internet site or
    Internet application whose owner or operator, in the course of their
    commercial activities, sells, directly or indirectly, advertising
    space on the site or application to persons or groups. ([plateforme
    en ligne]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[prime time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[prime time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in the case of a radio station,
    means the time between the hours of 6 a.m. and 9 a.m., noon and 2
    p.m. and 4 p.m. and 7 p.m., and, in the case of a television
    station, means the hours between 6 p.m. and midnight. ([heures de
    grande écoute]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 319
- 2014, c. 12, s. 72
- [2018, c. 31, s. 206](#1044071-1132537){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1044071-1132537.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-319-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 319"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Election Advertising]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206326 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Message must be authorized

**[[320]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-320 .sectionLabel}** A candidate or
registered party, or a person acting on their behalf, who causes
election advertising to be conducted shall mention in or on the message
that its transmission was authorized by the official agent of the
candidate or by the registered agent of the party, as the case may be.

**[[321]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-321 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2018, c.
31, s. 207\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-321-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 321"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election advertising posters

- **[[322]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-322 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  landlord or person acting on their behalf may prohibit a tenant from
  displaying election advertising posters on the premises to which the
  lease relates and no condominium corporation or any of its agents may
  prohibit the owner of a condominium unit from displaying election
  advertising posters on the premises of his or her unit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permitted restrictions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a landlord, person,
  condominium corporation or agent referred to in that subsection may
  set reasonable conditions relating to the size or type of election
  advertising posters that may be displayed on the premises and may
  prohibit the display of election advertising posters in common areas
  of the building in which the premises are found.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Blackout period

- **[[323]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-323 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person shall transmit election advertising to the public in an
  electoral district on polling day before the close of all of the
  polling stations in the electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interpretation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The transmission to the public of a notice of an
  event that the leader of a registered party intends to attend or an
  invitation to meet or hear the leader of a registered party is not
  election advertising for the purpose of subsection (1).

- Definition of [[person]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), a person includes
  a registered party and a group within the meaning of Part 17.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 323
- [2018, c. 31, s. 208](#1042661-1111370){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042661-1111370.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-323-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 323"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

**[[324]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-324 .sectionLabel}** Subsection 323(1) does
not apply in respect of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of a message that was transmitted to
  the public on what is commonly known as the Internet before the
  blackout period described in that subsection and that was not changed
  during that period; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distribution during that period of pamphlets or
  the posting of messages on signs, posters or banners.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 324
- 2001, c. 21, s. 16(E)
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- prevention or impairment
of transmission

- **[[325]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-325 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person shall prevent or impair the transmission to the public of an
  election advertising message without the consent of a person with
  authority to authorize its transmission.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply with respect to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the prevention or impairment, by a public
    authority, of an unlawful transmission if reasonable notice has
    first been given to the person who authorized the transmission; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the removal by an employee of a public authority of
    a sign, poster or banner where the posting of it is a hazard to
    public safety.

### [Online Platforms]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1132538 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Online platforms that are subject to
requirements

- **[[325.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-325.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section and section 325.2 apply
  to any online platform that, in the 12 months before the first day of
  the pre-election period, in the case of the publication on the
  platform of a partisan advertising message, or the 12 months before
  the first day of the election period, in the case of the publication
  on the platform of an election advertising message, was visited or
  used by Internet users in Canada an average of at least the following
  numbers of times per month:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 3,000,000 times, if the content of the online
    platform is available mainly in English;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 1,000,000 times, if the content of the online
    platform is available mainly in French; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 100,000 times, if the content of the online
    platform is available mainly in a language other than English or
    French.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registry of partisan advertising
  messages and election advertising messages

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The owner or operator of an online platform that
  sells, directly or indirectly, advertising space to the following
  persons and groups shall publish on the platform a registry of the
  persons' and groups' partisan advertising messages and election
  advertising messages published on the platform during that period:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a registered party or eligible party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a registered association;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a nomination contestant;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a potential candidate or a candidate; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a third party that is required to register under
    subsection 349.6(1) or 353(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be included in registry

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The registry referred to in subsection (2) shall
  include the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an electronic copy of each partisan advertising
    message and each election advertising message published on the
    platform; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for each advertising message referred to in
    paragraph (a), the name of the person who authorized the advertising
    message's publication on the platform, namely

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a registered agent of the registered party or
      eligible party, in the case of an advertising message whose
      publication was requested by a registered party or eligible party,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the financial agent of the registered
      association, in the case of an advertising message whose
      publication was requested by a registered association,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the financial agent of the nomination
      contestant, in the case of an advertising message whose
      publication was requested by a nomination contestant,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the official agent of the potential candidate or
      candidate, in the case of an advertising message whose publication
      was requested by a potential candidate or a candidate, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the financial agent of the registered third
      party, in the case of an advertising message whose publication was
      requested by a registered third party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication period of registry

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The owner or operator of the online platform shall
  publish in the registry referred to in subsection (2) the information
  referred to in subsection (3) for each partisan advertising message
  and each election advertising message during the following periods:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a partisan advertising message,
    during the period that begins on the day on which the online
    platform first publishes the advertising message and ends two years
    after

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the end of the election period of the general
      election immediately following the pre-election period, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the day referred to in paragraph (b) of the
      definition [[pre-election period]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} if there
      is no general election immediately following the pre-election
      period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an election advertising message,
    during the period that begins on the first day on which the online
    platform publishes such an advertising message and ends two years
    after the end of the election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be kept after
  publication period

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The owner or operator of the online platform shall
  keep the information that was included in the registry referred to in
  subsection (2) in respect of each partisan advertising message and
  each election advertising message for five years after the end of the
  applicable publication period referred to in subsection (4).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 208.1](#1042663-1132570){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042663-1132570.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be provided by advertiser

**[[325.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-325.2 .sectionLabel}** A person or group
referred to in any of paragraphs 325.1(2)(a) to (e) that requests the
publication of a partisan advertising message or election advertising
message on an online platform shall provide the owner or operator of the
platform with all the information in the person's or group's control
that the owner or operator needs in order to comply with subsection
325.1(2).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 208.1](#1042663-1132574){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042663-1132574.html"}
:::

### [Election Surveys]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206359 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transmission of election survey results

- **[[326]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-326 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  first person who transmits the results of an election survey --- other
  than a survey that is described in section 327 --- to the public
  during an election period and any person who transmits them to the
  public within 24 hours after they are first transmitted to the public
  must provide the following together with the results:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the sponsor of the survey;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person or organization that
    conducted the survey;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date on which or the period during which the
    survey was conducted;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the population from which the sample of respondents
    was drawn;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the number of people who were contacted to
    participate in the survey;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the margin of error in respect of
    the data obtained; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the address of the Internet site on which a report
    referred to in subsection (3) is published.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional information --- published
  surveys

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the information referred to in
  subsection (1), in the case of a transmission to the public by means
  other than broadcasting, the wording of the survey questions in
  respect of which data is obtained must be provided.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of transmission of survey
  results

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The first person who transmits to the public the
  results of an election survey --- other than a survey that is
  described in section 327 --- shall, if that person is not the sponsor
  of the survey, ensure that the sponsor of the survey has been
  notified, before the transmission, of the date on which the results
  are to be transmitted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report on survey results

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A sponsor of an election survey --- other than a
  survey that is described in section 327 --- shall, during an election
  period, ensure that a report on the results of the survey is published
  and remains for the remainder of that period on an Internet site that
  is available to the public. The sponsor shall do so before
  transmitting the results of the survey, if they are the first person
  to transmit them or, if they are not, as soon as feasible after being
  notified of the date of transmission under subsection (2.1), and the
  report shall include the following, as applicable:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the sponsor of the survey;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the person or organization
    that conducted the survey;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date on which or the period during which the
    survey was conducted;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} information about the method used to collect the
    data from which the survey results are derived, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the sampling method,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the population from which the sample was drawn,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the size of the initial sample,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the number of individuals who were asked to
      participate in the survey and the numbers and respective
      percentages of them who participated in the survey, refused to
      participate in the survey, and were ineligible to participate in
      the survey,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the dates and time of day of the interviews,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the method used to recalculate data to take into
      account in the survey the results of participants who expressed no
      opinion, were undecided or failed to respond to any or all of the
      survey questions, and

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} any weighting factors or normalization
      procedures used in deriving the results of the survey; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the wording of the survey questions and, if
    applicable, the margins of error in respect of the data obtained.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 210\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Broadcast of surveys not based on
recognized statistical methods

**[[327]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-327 .sectionLabel}** The first person who
transmits the results of an election survey that is not based on
recognized statistical methods to the public during an election period
and any person who transmits them within 24 hours after they are first
transmitted to the public must indicate that the survey was not based on
recognized statistical methods.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- causing transmission of
election survey results during blackout period

- **[[328]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-328 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person shall cause to be transmitted to the public, in an electoral
  district on polling day before the close of all of the polling
  stations in that electoral district, the results of an election survey
  that have not previously been transmitted to the public.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- transmission of
  election survey results during blackout period

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall transmit to the public, in an
  electoral district on polling day before the close of all of the
  polling stations in that electoral district, the results of an
  election survey that have not previously been transmitted to the
  public.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of this section, a person includes a
  group within the meaning of Part 17.

### [Broadcasting outside Canada]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206399 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- use of broadcasting
station outside Canada

- **[[330]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-330 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person shall, with intent to influence persons to vote or refrain from
  voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular candidate
  or registered party, at an election, use a broadcasting station
  outside Canada, or aid, abet, counsel or procure the use of a
  broadcasting station outside Canada, during an election period, for
  the broadcasting of any matter having reference to an election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of any
  matter that is broadcast if the broadcasting signals originated in
  Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- broadcasting outside
  Canada

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} During an election period, no person shall broadcast,
  outside Canada, election advertising with respect to an election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 330

:::
