### [Political Broadcasts]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206412 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of Broadcasting Arbitrator

- **[[332]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-332 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  Broadcasting Arbitrator shall be appointed by the Chief Electoral
  Officer without delay after the consultations described in
  section 333. The Broadcasting Arbitrator shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} chosen by a unanimous decision of representatives
    of registered parties; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} named by the Chief Electoral Officer, if the
    consultations do not result in a unanimous decision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of office

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The term of office of the Broadcasting Arbitrator
  shall expire six months after polling day at the general election next
  following his or her appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal for cause

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may remove the
  Broadcasting Arbitrator from office only for cause.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligible for re-appointment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A Broadcasting Arbitrator whose term of office has
  expired is eligible to be re-appointed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Salary

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A Broadcasting Arbitrator shall be paid the salary or
  other remuneration that may be fixed by the Chief Electoral Officer.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Convening of representatives

- **[[333]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-333 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall hold a meeting of two representatives of
  each registered party represented in the House of Commons at that
  time, or if Parliament is dissolved, at the time of dissolution,
  designated in writing by their party leader, for the purpose of
  holding consultations to choose a Broadcasting Arbitrator. The meeting
  shall be held within

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 90 days after polling day at a general election; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 14 days after the day on which the Broadcasting
    Arbitrator dies, becomes incapacitated, resigns or is removed from
    office, if that day is not during the election period of a general
    election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chairperson

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall designate the
  Chairperson at the meeting referred to in subsection (1) and at all
  subsequent consultations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The representatives of the registered parties
  referred to in subsection (1) shall make a report signed by each of
  them to the Chief Electoral Officer of the results of their
  consultations no later than

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} six weeks after a meeting referred to in paragraph
    (1)(a); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} four weeks after a meeting referred to in paragraph
    (1)(b).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vacancy during election period

**[[334]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-334 .sectionLabel}** In the event of the
death, incapacity, resignation or removal of the Broadcasting Arbitrator
during the election period of a general election, the Chief Electoral
Officer shall appoint a new Broadcasting Arbitrator without delay.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Broadcasting time provided to registered
parties

- **[[335]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-335 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  the period beginning on the issue of the writs for a general election
  and ending at midnight on the day before polling day, every
  broadcaster shall, subject to the regulations made under the
  [Broadcasting Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01) and the conditions imposed on it
  under section 9.1 of that Act, make available, for purchase by all
  registered parties for the transmission of political announcements and
  other programming produced by or on behalf of the registered parties,
  six and one-half hours of broadcasting time during prime time on its
  facilities.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When broadcaster affiliated with
  network

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a broadcaster is affiliated with a network, the
  part of the broadcasting time to be made available under
  subsection (1) that may be determined by agreement between the
  broadcaster and the network operator shall be made available by the
  network operator during the portion of the broadcaster's prime time
  broadcasting schedule that has been delegated to the control of the
  network operator.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 335
- 2001, c. 21, s. 17
- [2023, c. 8, s. 43](#1396735-1396890){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1396735-1396890.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-335-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 335"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Request for meeting

- **[[336]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-336 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Broadcasting Arbitrator shall convene a meeting of representatives of
  all registered parties to consult on the allocation of broadcasting
  time made available under section 335 within 30 days after the receipt
  of a written request from the chief agent of a registered party, or
  six months after the Broadcasting Arbitrator takes office, whichever
  is earlier.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of request

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The written request may not be made until the
  Broadcasting Arbitrator has been in office for 60 days.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chairperson

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Broadcasting Arbitrator shall act as Chairperson
  at any meeting referred to in subsection (1).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No allocation

- **[[337]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-337 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  registered party shall not be allocated broadcasting time if, after
  receiving notice of the meeting referred to in subsection 336(1), the
  party

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} indicates in writing to the Broadcasting Arbitrator
    that it does not wish to be allocated broadcasting time; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fails to communicate to the Broadcasting Arbitrator
    its intentions regarding the allocation of the broadcasting time and
    fails to have its representative attend the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Agreement on allocation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Unanimous agreement of the registered parties on the
  allocation of the broadcasting time is binding on all registered
  parties.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Broadcasting Arbitrator decides when no
  agreement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If unanimous agreement is not reached within four
  weeks after the meeting referred to in subsection 336(1), the
  Broadcasting Arbitrator shall allocate the broadcasting time, and that
  allocation is binding on all registered parties.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Factors in allocation

- **[[338]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-338
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) to (5),
  in allocating broadcasting time, the Broadcasting Arbitrator shall
  give equal weight to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the percentage of seats in the House of Commons
    held by each of the registered parties at the previous general
    election; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the percentage of the popular vote at the previous
    general election of each registered party.

  The Broadcasting Arbitrator shall in addition give half the weight
  given to each of the factors referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b) to
  the number of candidates endorsed by each of the registered parties at
  the previous general election, expressed as a percentage of all
  candidates endorsed by all registered parties at that election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Allocation where merger of parties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) to (5), in allocating
  broadcasting time in the case of the merger of two or more registered
  parties, the Broadcasting Arbitrator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in determining the percentage of seats held by a
    merged party at the previous general election for the purpose of
    paragraph (1)(a), include the total number of seats held by the
    merging parties;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in determining the percentage of the popular vote
    of a merged party at the previous general election for the purpose
    of paragraph (1)(b), include the total number of votes obtained by
    the merging parties; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of giving the half-weight under
    subsection (1), assign to the merged party the number of candidates
    endorsed by the merging party that had the greatest number of
    candidates at that election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No allocation in excess of 50%

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In no case shall the Broadcasting Arbitrator allocate
  more than 50% of the total of the broadcasting time to a registered
  party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Allocation of time in excess of 50%

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the calculation under subsection (1) would give
  more than 50% of the total of the broadcasting time to a registered
  party, the Broadcasting Arbitrator shall allocate the excess amount to
  the other registered parties entitled to broadcasting time on a
  proportionate basis.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Discretion re allocation

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the Broadcasting Arbitrator considers that an
  allocation determined in accordance with subsection (1) would be
  unfair to a registered party or contrary to the public interest, the
  allocation may be modified, subject to subsections (3) and (4), in any
  manner that the Broadcasting Arbitrator considers appropriate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of allocation

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Broadcasting Arbitrator shall, as soon as
  possible, give notice in writing of every allocation of broadcasting
  time made by the Broadcasting Arbitrator or by the registered parties
  to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} every registered party; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} every political party that became an eligible party
    either before or after the allocation.

  The notice shall advise an eligible party referred to in paragraph (b)
  that it has 30 days after the receipt of the notice to request that
  broadcasting time be made available to it, for purchase, under section
  339.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New parties entitled to broadcasting time

- **[[339]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-339
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), every
  eligible party referred to in paragraph 338(6)(b) that makes a request
  as described in subsection 338(6) within the time referred to in that
  subsection is entitled to purchase broadcasting time in an amount
  equal to the lesser of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the smallest portion of broadcasting time to be
    made available under section 335 allocated to a registered party
    under sections 337 and 338, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} six minutes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Parties not entitled to time

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An eligible party referred to in paragraph 338(6)(b)
  is not entitled to have any broadcasting time made available to it
  under this section if the party

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} indicates in writing that it does not wish any
    broadcasting time under this section; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fails to make a request as described in subsection
    338(6) within the time referred to in that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Broadcasting time provided to new
  eligible parties

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the broadcasting time to be made
  available under section 335, and within the period referred to in that
  section, every broadcaster shall, subject to the regulations made
  under the [Broadcasting Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01) and to the conditions
  imposed on it under section 9.1 of that Act, make available, for
  purchase by every eligible party entitled to broadcasting time under
  this section, broadcasting time in the amount determined under this
  section for the eligible party for the transmission of political
  announcements and other programming produced by or on behalf of the
  eligible party during prime time on that broadcaster's facilities.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum of 39 minutes

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The maximum amount of broadcasting time available for
  purchase by eligible parties under this section is 39 minutes and,
  once that amount of broadcasting time is reached, all entitlement
  under this section shall be altered or established to be of whatever
  number of minutes or portions of minutes is necessary so that all
  eligible parties requesting time under this section receive the same
  amount of time within the 39-minute limit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 339
- [2023, c. 8, s. 44](#1396739-1396895){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1396739-1396895.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-339-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 339"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reallocation in case of deregistration

- **[[340]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-340 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  registered party to which broadcasting time has been allocated under
  this Part is subsequently deregistered, the Broadcasting Arbitrator,
  within two weeks after publication in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) of the notice of deregistration,
  shall convene the representatives of the remaining registered parties
  and eligible parties to which broadcasting time has been allocated for
  the purpose of reallocating that party's broadcasting time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reallocation in case of loss of
  eligibility

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an eligible party to which broadcasting time
  has been allocated under section 339 subsequently ceases to be an
  eligible party, the Broadcasting Arbitrator, within two weeks after
  the cessation of eligibility, shall convene the representatives of the
  remaining registered parties and eligible parties to whom broadcasting
  time has been allocated for the purpose of reallocating that party's
  broadcasting time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the deregistration or cessation of eligibility
  referred to in subsection (1) or (2), respectively, occurs after the
  issue of the writs for a general election, the broadcasting time that
  was allocated to the deregistered party or to the party that has
  ceased to be eligible shall not be reallocated.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 340
- 2003, c. 19, s. 5
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-340-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 340"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reallocation in case of merger

**[[341]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-341 .sectionLabel}** If two or more
registered parties merge after an allocation of the broadcasting time to
be made available under section 335, the Broadcasting Arbitrator shall
without delay convene the representatives of the registered parties,
including the merged parties, for the purpose of reallocating the
broadcasting time allocated to all registered parties.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Broadcasters to be notified

- **[[342]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-342 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Broadcasting Arbitrator shall notify the Canadian Radio-television and
  Telecommunications Commission of every allocation under sections 337
  and 338 and every entitlement under section 339 as soon as possible
  after it is made or requested and the Commission shall notify every
  broadcaster and every network operator of every such allocation and
  entitlement without delay after it is made and again immediately after
  the issue of the writs for the next general election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to parties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Broadcasting Arbitrator shall, on request,
  provide all registered parties and all eligible parties referred to in
  paragraph 338(6)(b) with the names and addresses of all broadcasters
  and network operators.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Annual review

- **[[343]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-343 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  each of the calendar years after the calendar year in which an
  allocation of broadcasting time has been made under sections 337 and
  338 or an eligible party has requested and has become entitled to
  broadcasting time under section 339, the Broadcasting Arbitrator shall
  convene and chair a meeting of the representatives of all registered
  parties to review the allocation or entitlement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reduction to six and one-half hours

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, at a meeting referred to in subsection (1), it is
  determined that the total broadcasting time allocated or requested
  exceeds six and one-half hours, the Broadcasting Arbitrator shall
  reduce the allocated or requested time to six and one-half hours on a
  proportionate basis and that reduction shall be final and binding on
  all registered parties and eligible parties.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[344]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-344 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  definitions in this subsection apply in subsections (2) and (5).

  [[commercial time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[commercial time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any period of two
      minutes or less during which a broadcaster normally presents
      commercial messages, public service announcements or station or
      network identification. ([temps commercial]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[program time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[program time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any period longer than
      two minutes during which a broadcaster does not normally present
      commercial messages, public service announcements or station or
      network identification. ([durée de l'émission]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of preference by party

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each registered party and each eligible party
  entitled to purchase broadcasting time under this Act shall, not later
  than 10 days after the issue of the writs for a general election, send
  a notice in writing to each broadcaster and each network operator from
  whom it intends to purchase broadcasting time, setting out its
  preference as to the proportion of commercial time and program time to
  be made available to it and the days on which and the hours during
  which that time as so proportioned is to be made available, but at no
  time shall that party obtain broadcasting time before the 5th day
  after the notice is received by the broadcaster or network operator.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consultation to reach agreement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every broadcaster or network operator who receives a
  notice under subsection (2) shall, within two days after its receipt,
  consult with representatives of the registered party or eligible party
  that sent the notice for the purpose of reaching an agreement on the
  requests contained in it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When no agreement

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If no agreement is reached under subsection (3)
  within two days after the commencement of the consultation required by
  that subsection, the matter shall be referred to the Broadcasting
  Arbitrator who shall decide on the requests without delay and give
  notice of his or her decision to the broadcaster or network operator
  and to the representatives of the registered party or eligible party
  that made the requests.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Factors in decision

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} In making a decision under subsection (4), the
  Broadcasting Arbitrator shall take into account the following
  principles:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that each registered party and each eligible party
    should have the freedom and flexibility to determine the proportion
    of commercial time and program time to be made available to it and
    the days on which and the hours during which that time as so
    proportioned should be made available; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that any broadcasting time to be made available to
    a registered party or eligible party should be made available fairly
    throughout prime time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Decision binding

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A decision of the Broadcasting Arbitrator under
  subsection (4) is final and binding on the registered party or
  eligible party, as the case may be, and the broadcaster or network
  operator.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Free broadcasting time

- **[[345]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-345 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  the period beginning on the issue of the writs for a general election
  and ending at midnight on the day before polling day at that election,
  every network operator shall, subject to the regulations made under
  the [Broadcasting Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01) and to the conditions imposed
  on it under section 9.1 of that Act, make available, at no cost, to
  the registered parties and eligible parties referred to in subsection
  (2), for the transmission of political announcements and other
  programming produced by or on behalf of those parties, broadcasting
  time as determined under that subsection if the network formed and
  operated by the network operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} reaches a majority of Canadians whose mother tongue
    is the same as that in which the network broadcasts;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is licensed with respect to more than a particular
    series of programs or type of programming; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} does not involve a distribution undertaking as
    defined in subsection 2(1) of the [Broadcasting
    Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of free broadcasting time

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), the minimum amount
  of broadcasting time that a network operator is to make available
  shall be no less than the amount of free broadcasting time made
  available by it at the last general election and shall be made
  available as follows:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two minutes to every registered party referred to
    in paragraph 337(1)(a) and every eligible party referred to in
    paragraph 339(2)(a); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the remainder to all registered parties that have
    been allocated any of the broadcasting time to be made available
    under section 335 and all eligible parties that have requested
    broadcasting time under section 339 in the proportion that their
    allocated or requested purchasable broadcasting time bears to the
    total broadcasting time allocated or requested under those sections.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Free time not election expense

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The value of free broadcasting time made available to
  a registered party under this section shall not be taken into
  consideration in calculating its election expenses within the meaning
  of section 376.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of population reached

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), a network is
  deemed to reach

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} people resident within the areas served by
    broadcasting stations affiliated to the network that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of A.M. radio stations, are enclosed
      by the night-time interference-free official contour of the
      stations,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of F.M. radio stations, are enclosed
      by the 50 mV per metre official contour of the stations, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of television stations, are
      enclosed by the Grade B official contour of the stations; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} people resident outside the areas described in
    paragraph (a) to whom the signals of broadcasting stations
    affiliated to the network are available via distribution
    undertakings licensed by the Canadian Radio-television and
    Telecommunications Commission.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 345
- 2001, c. 21, s. 18
- 2014, c. 12, s. 74
- [2023, c. 8, s. 45](#1396741-1396897){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1396741-1396897.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-345-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 345"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Broadcasting Arbitrator to prepare
guidelines

**[[346]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-346 .sectionLabel}** The Broadcasting
Arbitrator shall, not later than two days after the issue of the writs
for a general election, prepare and send to the Canadian
Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission a set of guidelines
respecting

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the allocation of or entitlement to broadcasting time
  under this Act;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the procedures for booking broadcasting time by
  registered parties and eligible parties; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any other matters that may be pertinent to the
  conduct of broadcasters and network operators under this Act.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}C.R.T.C. to prepare and send guidelines

**[[347]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-347 .sectionLabel}** The Canadian
Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission shall, not later than
four days after the issue of the writs for a general election, prepare a
set of guidelines respecting the applicability of the [Broadcasting
Act](/eng/acts/B-9.01) and the regulations made under that Act to the
conduct of broadcasters and network operators in relation to a general
election and send them, together with the set of guidelines sent by the
Broadcasting Arbitrator under section 346, to all broadcasters and
network operators.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition relating to rates charged

**[[348]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348 .sectionLabel}** No person shall charge
a registered party, any other political party or a candidate or a person
acting on behalf of any of them,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a rate for broadcasting time made available to the
  party or candidate, in the period beginning on the issue of the writs
  and ending at midnight on the day before polling day, that exceeds the
  lowest rate charged by the person for an equal amount of equivalent
  time on the same facilities made available to any other person at any
  time within that period; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a rate for an advertisement in a periodical
  publication published or distributed and made public in the period
  referred to in paragraph (a) that exceeds the lowest rate charged by
  the person for an equal amount of equivalent advertising space in the
  same issue of the periodical publication or in any other issue of it
  that is published or distributed and made public in that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 348
- 2001, c. 21, s. 19
:::

## [PART 16.1]{.HLabel1}[Voter Contact Calling Services]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206569 .Part}

### [DIVISION 1]{.HLabel2}[Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206570 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[348.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.01 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Part.

[[automatic dialing-announcing device]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[automatic dialing-announcing device]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
    any automatic equipment that has the capability to store or produce
    telephone numbers and that is used alone or in conjunction with
    other equipment to convey a pre-recorded or synthesized voice
    message to those telephone numbers.  ([composeur-messager
    automatique]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[call]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[call]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any of the following types of
    calls that are made to telephone numbers:

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} live voice calls;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} calls made by means of an automatic
      dialing-announcing device;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} calls that consist of a combination of the types
      of calls referred to in paragraphs (a) and
      (b). ([appel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[calling service provider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[calling service provider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person or
    group that carries on a business whose activities include the making
    of calls for or on behalf of another person or group. ([fournisseur
    de services d'appel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[group]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[group]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a registered party, registered
    association, unincorporated trade union, trade association or other
    group of persons acting together by mutual consent for a common
    purpose. ([groupe]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[internal services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[internal services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in relation to a group, the services provided by
      its members or employees, and those provided to it free of charge
      by any individual;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in relation to a candidate, a nomination
      contestant or a third party who is an individual, the services
      provided by them personally or by their employees and those
      provided free of charge to the candidate, contestant or third
      party by any individual; and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in relation to a third party that is a
      corporation, the services provided by its employees and those
      provided to it free of charge by any individual. ([services
      internes]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[official representative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[official representative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a registered party, its chief
      agent;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a registered association, its
      financial agent;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a candidate, their official agent;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a nomination contestant, their
      financial agent;

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a registered third party, its
      financial agent;

    - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an unregistered third party that
      is a corporation, the officer of the corporation who has signing
      authority for it; and

    - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an unregistered third party that
      is a group, a person who is responsible for the
      group. ([représentant officiel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[registered third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[registered third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a third party
    that is registered under section 353. ([tiers
    enregistré]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person or a group, other
    than a registered party, registered association, candidate or
    nomination contestant. ([tiers]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[voter contact calling services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[voter contact calling services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
    services involving the making of calls during an election period for
    any purpose related to an election, including

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} promoting or opposing a registered party, its
      leader, a candidate or a nomination contestant or any position on
      an issue with which such a party or person is associated;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} encouraging electors to vote or to refrain from
      voting;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} providing information about the election,
      including information about voting hours and the location of
      polling stations;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} gathering information about how electors voted in
      past elections or will vote in the election or their views on a
      registered party, its leader, a candidate or a nomination
      contestant or any issue with which such a party or person is
      associated; and

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} raising funds for a registered party, a
      registered association, a candidate or a nomination
      contestant. ([services d'appels aux électeurs]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 75
:::

### [DIVISION 1.1]{.HLabel2}[Provision of Voter Contact Calling Services]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206602 .Subheading}

#### [Agreements Relating to Voter Contact Calling Services]{.HTitleText3} {#h-206603 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- entering into agreement
with calling service provider

**[[348.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.02 .sectionLabel}** A person or group
shall not enter into an agreement with a calling service provider for
voter contact calling services unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person or group is a registered party, a
  registered association, a nomination contestant or a registered third
  party, or an unregistered third party that is a corporation or group,
  and the agreement is entered into on behalf of the person or group by
  the person's or group's official representative;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person is a candidate and the agreement is
  entered into in their own name or on their behalf by their official
  representative or by a person that their official representative has
  so authorized in writing; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person is an unregistered third party who is an
  individual and the agreement is entered into in their own name.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to inform

**[[348.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.03 .sectionLabel}** Before a person
enters into an agreement with a calling service provider for voter
contact calling services, either in their own name or on behalf of
another person or a group, the person shall inform the calling service
provider that the agreement is for voter contact calling services and
shall provide the calling service provider with their name, address and
telephone number and a copy of a piece of identification authorized by
the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission that
contains their name.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to obtain identification
information

- **[[348.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before a calling service provider
  enters into an agreement with a person or group to provide voter
  contact calling services, the calling service provider shall obtain
  from the person who is to enter into the agreement, either in their
  own name or on behalf of the person or a group, their name, address
  and telephone number and a copy of a piece of identification
  authorized by the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications
  Commission that contains their name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to keep identification
  information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The calling service provider shall prepare a record
  of the information obtained and keep that record and the copy of the
  piece of identification for one year after the end of the election
  period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to confirm nature of services

- **[[348.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A calling service provider that
  enters into an agreement to make calls for or on behalf of a person or
  group shall, before the first call is made under the agreement during
  an election period, ask the person or group whether the making of
  calls under the agreement would constitute voter contact calling
  services.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to authorize, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the making of calls under the agreement does
  constitute voter contact calling services, a person who is authorized
  under section 348.02 to enter into an agreement for voter contact
  calling services with respect to the person or group in question
  shall, before the first call is made, authorize the provision of voter
  contact calling services under the agreement and provide the calling
  service provider with their name, address and telephone number and a
  copy of a piece of identification authorized by the Canadian
  Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission that contains their
  name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to obtain identification
  information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the making of calls under the agreement does
  constitute voter contact calling services, the calling service
  provider shall, before the first call is made, obtain from the person
  who provides the authorization in accordance with subsection (2) that
  person's name, address and telephone number and a copy of a piece of
  identification authorized by the Commission that contains that
  person's name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to keep identification
  information

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The calling service provider shall prepare a record
  of the information obtained and keep that record and the copy of the
  piece of identification for one year after the end of the election
  period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

#### [Filing Obligations --- Registration Notices]{.HTitleText3} {#h-206633 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to file registration notice

- **[[348.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A calling service provider that, in
  accordance with an agreement, provides voter contact calling services
  shall file a registration notice with the Canadian Radio-television
  and Telecommunications Commission.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time for filing and contents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For each election period to which the agreement
  applies, the registration notice shall be filed not later than 48
  hours after the first call is made under the agreement and shall set
  out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the calling service provider's name;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person or group that is a party to
    the agreement;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person or group on whose behalf
    calls will be made under the agreement; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the type of calls to be made under the agreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
- [2018, c. 31, s. 214](#1042697-1132592){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042697-1132592.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-348.06-20150802.html "Link to previous version of section 348.06"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to file registration notice
--- agreement

- **[[348.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who enters into an
  agreement with a calling service provider for voter contact calling
  services, either in their own name or on behalf of another person or a
  group, or a person who provides an authorization of the provision of
  voter contact calling services under an agreement in accordance with
  subsection 348.05(2), as the case may be, shall file a registration
  notice with the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications
  Commission.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time for filing and contents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For each election period to which the agreement
  applies, the registration notice shall be filed not later than 48
  hours after the first call is made under the agreement and shall set
  out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the calling service provider's name;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person or group that is a party to
    the agreement;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person or group on whose behalf
    calls will be made under the agreement; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the type of calls to be made under the agreement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to provide copy of
  identification document

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person who files the registration notice shall,
  at the time of filing the registration notice, provide the Commission
  with their name, address and telephone number and a copy of a piece of
  identification authorized by the Commission that contains their name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Except for the purposes of section 348.12, a
  registration notice is deemed not to have been filed if the
  information and the copy of the piece of identification are not
  provided at the time the registration notice is filed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
- [2018, c. 31, s. 215](#1042711-1132595){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042711-1132595.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-348.07-20150802.html "Link to previous version of section 348.07"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to file registration notice
--- live voice calls

- **[[348.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, during an election period, a
  third party that is a corporation or group uses its internal services
  to make live voice calls for any purpose relating to the election,
  including a purpose referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the
  definition [[voter contact calling services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in
  section 348.01, the third party's official representative shall file a
  registration notice with the Canadian Radio-television and
  Telecommunications Commission.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time for filing and contents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The registration notice shall be filed not later than
  48 hours after the first live voice call is made and shall set out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party's name;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and telephone number of the
    official representative; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a statement that the third party is making live
    voice calls.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to provide copy of
  identification document

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The official representative shall, at the time of
  filing the registration notice, provide the Commission with their
  name, address and telephone number and a copy of a piece of
  identification authorized by the Commission that contains their name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Except for the purposes of section 348.12, a
  registration notice is deemed not to have been filed if the
  information and the copy of the piece of identification are not
  provided at the time the registration notice is filed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to file registration notice
--- other calls

- **[[348.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, during an election period, a
  person or group uses their internal services to make calls by means of
  an automatic dialing-announcing device for any purpose relating to the
  election, including a purpose referred to in any of paragraphs (a)
  to (e) of the definition [[voter contact calling
  services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 348.01, the official
  representative of the person or group --- or the person themselves, if
  the person is an unregistered third party who is an individual ---
  shall file a registration notice with the Canadian Radio-television
  and Telecommunications Commission.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time for filing and contents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The registration notice shall be filed not later than
  48 hours after the first call is made and shall set out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person or group;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and telephone number of the
    official representative or individual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a statement that the person or group is making
    calls by means of an automatic dialing-announcing device.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to provide copy of
  identification document

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The official representative or individual shall, at
  the time of filing the registration notice, provide the Commission
  with their name, address and telephone number and a copy of a piece of
  identification authorized by the Commission that contains their name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Except for the purposes of section 348.12, a
  registration notice is deemed not to have been filed if the
  information and the copy of the piece of identification are not
  provided at the time the registration notice is filed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

#### [Role of the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission]{.HTitleText3} {#h-206686 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Administration and enforcement

- **[[348.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Canadian Radio-television and
  Telecommunications Commission is responsible for the administration
  and enforcement of this Division.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}[Telecommunications
  Act](/eng/acts/T-3.4)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The administration and enforcement of this Division
  are to be carried out under Part V of the [Telecommunications
  Act](/eng/acts/T-3.4).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registry

**[[348.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.11 .sectionLabel}** The Canadian
Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission is responsible for
establishing and maintaining a registry, to be known as the Voter
Contact Registry, in which all documents provided to it under sections
348.06 to 348.09 are to be kept.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

- **[[348.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} As soon as feasible but no later
  than 30 days after polling day, the Canadian Radio-television and
  Telecommunications Commission shall, in the manner that it considers
  appropriate, publish the registration notices relating to the election
  that have been filed with it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Clarification

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) precludes the Canadian
  Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission from publishing,
  before polling day, any registration notice filed with it or any
  information related to any incomplete registration notice that is
  filed with it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76
- [2018, c. 31, s. 216](#1042718-1132601){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042718-1132601.html"}
:::

- **[[348.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Canadian Radio-television and
  Telecommunications Commission may, in writing and on any terms it
  specifies, delegate to any person any of the powers, duties and
  functions referred to in sections 348.11 and 348.12.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commission may, in writing, revoke a delegation
  made under subsection (1).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorization of types of identification

**[[348.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.14 .sectionLabel}** The Canadian
Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission may authorize the
types of pieces of identification and of copies of such pieces of
identification for the purposes of sections 348.03 to 348.05 and 348.07
to 348.09.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 76

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure to Commissioner

**[[348.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.15 .sectionLabel}** The Canadian
Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission shall, on the request
of the Commissioner, disclose to the Commissioner any document or
information that it received under this Division that the Commissioner
considers necessary for the purpose of ensuring compliance with and
enforcement of this Act, other than this Division.

### [DIVISION 2]{.HLabel2}[Scripts, Recordings and Lists of Telephone Numbers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206717 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calling service provider --- agreement

**[[348.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.16 .sectionLabel}** Every calling
service provider that, in accordance with an agreement, provides voter
contact calling services shall keep, for three years after the end of
the election period,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of each unique script used in live voice calls
  made under the agreement and a record of every date on which the
  script was used;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a recording of each unique message conveyed by an
  automatic dialing-announcing device that is used to make calls under
  the agreement and a record of every date on which it was so conveyed;
  and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a list of every telephone number called under the
  agreement during the election period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 77
- [2018, c. 31, s. 218](#1042726-1132606){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042726-1132606.html"}
:::

Version](section-348.16-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 348.16"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person or group --- agreement

**[[348.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.17 .sectionLabel}** Every person or
group that enters into an agreement with a calling service provider
under which voter contact calling services are provided shall keep, for
one year after the end of the election period,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of each unique script used in live voice calls
  made under the agreement and a record of every date on which the
  script was used;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a recording of each unique message conveyed by an
  automatic dialing-announcing device that is used to make calls under
  the agreement and a record of every date on which it was so conveyed;
  and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a list of every telephone number called under the
  agreement during the election period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 77
- [2018, c. 31, s. 219](#1042728-1132610){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042728-1132610.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-348.17-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 348.17"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Person or group --- internal services

**[[348.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.18 .sectionLabel}** If, during an
election period, a person or group uses their internal services to make
calls by means of an automatic dialing-announcing device for any purpose
relating to the election, including a purpose referred to in any of
paragraphs (a) to (e) of the definition [[voter contact calling
services]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in section 348.01, the person or group
shall keep, for one year after the end of the election period,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a recording of each unique message conveyed by the
  device and a record of every date on which it was so conveyed; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a list of every telephone number called for that
  purpose during the election period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 77
- [2018, c. 31, s. 220](#1042730-1132615){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042730-1132615.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-348.18-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 348.18"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Third party that is corporation or group
--- internal services

**[[348.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-348.19 .sectionLabel}** If, during an
election period, a third party that is a corporation or group uses its
internal services to make live voice calls for any purpose relating to
the election, including a purpose referred to in any of paragraphs (a)
to (e) of the definition [[voter contact calling
services]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in section 348.01, the third party
shall, if a script is used, keep, for one year after the end of the
election period,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of each unique script used and a record of
  every date on which the script was used; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a list of every telephone number called for that
  purpose during the election period.

## [PART 17]{.HLabel1}[Third Party Advertising, Partisan Activities and Election Surveys]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206738 .Part}

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1132622 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[349]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349 .sectionLabel}** The definitions in this
section apply in this Part.

[[election advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[election advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2018, c.
    31, s. 222\]]{.Repealed}

[[election advertising expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[election advertising expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    2018, c. 31, s. 222\]]{.Repealed}

[[election survey]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[election survey]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an election survey
    that is conducted by, or caused to be conducted by, a third party
    --- a person or group other than a political party that is
    registered under an Act of a province --- during a pre-election
    period or an election period and whose results the person or group
    takes into account

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in deciding whether or not to organize and carry
      out partisan activities or to transmit partisan advertising
      messages or election advertising messages; or

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in their organization and carrying out of those
      activities or their transmission of those messages. ([sondage
      électoral]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[election survey expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[election survey expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an expense
    incurred in respect of the conducting of an election survey

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in Division 1, during a pre-election period;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in Division 2, during an election period; and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in Division 3, during either a pre-election
      period or an election period. ([dépenses de sondage
      électoral]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[expenses]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[expenses]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} amounts paid;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} liabilities incurred;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the commercial value of property and services,
      other than volunteer labour, that are donated or provided; and

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} amounts that represent the difference between an
      amount paid or a liability incurred for property and services,
      other than volunteer labour, and the commercial value of the
      property and services, when they are provided at less than their
      commercial value. ([dépenses]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[group]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[group]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an unincorporated trade union,
    trade association or other group of persons acting together by
    mutual consent for a common purpose. ([groupe]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[partisan activity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[partisan activity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an activity,
    including canvassing door-to-door, making telephone calls to
    electors and organizing rallies, that is carried out by a third
    party --- a person or group other than a political party that is
    registered under an Act of a province --- and that promotes or
    opposes a registered party or eligible party or the election of a
    potential candidate, nomination contestant, candidate or leader of a
    registered party or eligible party, otherwise than by taking a
    position on an issue with which any such party or person is
    associated. It does not include election advertising, partisan
    advertising or a fundraising activity. ([activité
    partisane]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[partisan activity expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[partisan activity expense]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an expense
    incurred in respect of the organization and carrying out of a
    partisan activity. ([dépenses d'activité partisane]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[registered third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[registered third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a third party
    that is registered under section 349.6 or 353. ([tiers
    enregistré]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[third party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in Division 0.1, a person or a group other than

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} during an election period, a candidate, a
        registered party or an electoral district association of a
        registered party, and

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} outside of an election period,

        - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a registered party or eligible party or a
          registered association,

        - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a potential candidate within the meaning of
          paragraph (a), (b) or (d) of the definition [[potential
          candidate]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in subsection 2(1), or

        - [(C)]{.lawlabel} a nomination contestant;

    - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} in Division 1, a person or a group other than

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a registered party or eligible party or a
        registered association,

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a potential candidate within the meaning of
        paragraph (a), (b) or (d) of the definition [[potential
        candidate]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in subsection 2(1), or

      - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a nomination contestant; and

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in Division 2, a person or a group other than a
      candidate, a registered party or an electoral district association
      of a registered party. ([tiers]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 349
- [2018, c. 31, s. 222](#1042742-1132649){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042742-1132649.html"}
:::
