[Previous
Version](section-349-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 349"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION 0.1]{.HLabel2}[Prohibition on Use of Foreign Funds by Third Parties]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1132650 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[349.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following definitions apply in
  this Division.

  [[advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the transmission to the
      public by any means of an advertising message that promotes or
      opposes a registered party or eligible party or the election of a
      potential candidate, nomination contestant, candidate or leader of
      a registered party or eligible party, otherwise than by taking a
      position on an issue with which any such party or person is
      associated. For greater certainty, it does not include

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the transmission to the public of an editorial,
        a debate, a speech, an interview, a column, a letter, a
        commentary or news;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distribution of a book, or the promotion of
        the sale of a book, for no less than its commercial value, if
        the book was planned to be made available to the public
        regardless of whether there was to be an election;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of a document by a Senator or
        a member the expense of which is paid by the Senate or House of
        Commons;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the transmission of a document directly by a
        person or a group to their members, employees or shareholders,
        as the case may be;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the transmission by an individual, on a
        non-commercial basis on the Internet, of his or her personal
        political views; or

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the making of telephone calls to electors only
        to encourage them to vote. ([publicité]{.DefinedTermLink
        lang="fr"})

  [[foreign entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[foreign entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an individual who is not a Canadian citizen or
        a [[permanent resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in
        subsection 2(1) of the [Immigration and Refugee Protection
        Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5);

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a corporation or entity incorporated, formed or
        otherwise organized outside Canada that does not carry on
        business in Canada or whose only activity carried on in Canada
        consists of doing anything to influence electors to vote or
        refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a
        particular candidate or registered party, at an election;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a trade union that does not hold bargaining
        rights for employees in Canada;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a foreign political party; or

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a foreign government or an agent or mandatary
        of one. ([entité étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of
  [[advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of the definition
  [[advertising]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, promoting or opposing includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in relation to a registered party or eligible
    party,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} naming it,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} identifying it, including by its logo, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} providing a link to an Internet page that does
      anything referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in relation to the election of a potential
    candidate, nomination contestant, candidate or leader of a
    registered party or eligible party,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} naming him or her,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} showing a photograph, cartoon or drawing of him
      or her,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} identifying him or her, including by political
      affiliation or by any logo that he or she has, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} providing a link to an Internet page that does
      anything referred to in subparagraphs (i) to (iii).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132679){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132679.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- use of foreign funds

**[[349.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.02 .sectionLabel}** No third party
shall use funds for a partisan activity, for advertising, for election
advertising or for an election survey if the source of the funds is a
foreign entity.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132683){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132683.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- circumventing prohibition
on use of foreign funds

**[[349.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.03 .sectionLabel}** No third party
shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, the prohibition
  under section 349.02; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} act in collusion with another person or entity for
  that purpose.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132689){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132689.html"}
:::

### [DIVISION 1]{.HLabel2}[Partisan Activities, Partisan Advertising and Election Surveys During Pre-election Period]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1132690 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum pre-election period expenses

- **[[349.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 349.4, a third
  party shall not incur the following expenses in an aggregate amount of
  more than \$700,000:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan
    activities that are carried out during a pre-election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} partisan advertising expenses in relation to
    partisan advertising messages that are transmitted during that
    period; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to election
    surveys that are conducted during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum pre-election period expenses
  --- electoral district

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Not more than \$7,000 of the maximum amount referred
  to in subsection (1) shall be incurred to promote or oppose the
  election of one or more potential candidates or nomination contestants
  in a given electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses --- party leader

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The maximum amount set out in subsection (2) only
  applies to an amount incurred with respect to a leader of a registered
  party or eligible party to the extent that it is incurred to promote
  or oppose his or her election in an electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Third party inflation adjustment factor

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The amounts referred to in subsections (1) and (2)
  shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor referred to in
  section 384 that is in effect on the first day of the pre-election
  period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132704){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132704.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- circumventing maximum
amount

**[[349.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.2 .sectionLabel}** A third party shall
not circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, a maximum amount set out in
section 349.1 in any manner, including by splitting itself into two or
more third parties for the purpose of circumventing the maximum amount
or acting in collusion with another third party so that their combined
partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election
survey expenses exceed the maximum amount.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132708){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132708.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- collusion with registered
party

- **[[349.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No third party and no registered
  party shall act in collusion with each other --- including by sharing
  information --- in order to influence the third party in its partisan
  activities that it carries out during a pre-election period, its
  partisan advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or
  causes to be conducted during a pre-election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- collusion with
  potential candidate

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No third party and no potential candidate shall act
  in collusion with each other --- including by sharing information ---
  in order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that
  it carries out during a pre-election period, its partisan advertising
  or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted
  during a pre-election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- collusion with
  associated person

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No third party and no person associated with a
  potential candidate's activities undertaken with a view to the
  potential candidate's eventual election --- including an official
  agent of a potential candidate who is deemed to be a candidate under
  section 477 --- shall act in collusion with each other --- including
  by sharing information --- in order to influence the third party in
  its partisan activities that it carries out during a pre-election
  period, its partisan advertising or its election surveys that it
  conducts or causes to be conducted during a pre-election period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132717){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132717.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- spending by foreign third
parties

- **[[349.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A foreign third party shall not
  incur the following expenses:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to a
    partisan activity that is carried out during a pre-election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} partisan advertising expenses in relation to a
    partisan advertising message that is transmitted during that period;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to an election
    survey that is conducted during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[foreign third
  party]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (1), a [[foreign third
  party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} is a third party in respect of which

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is an individual, the individual

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is not a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is not a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} does not reside in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a corporation or entity,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} it does not carry on business in Canada, or its
      only activity carried on in Canada during a pre-election period
      consists of doing anything to influence electors during that
      period to vote or refrain from voting, or to vote or refrain from
      voting for a particular candidate or registered party, at the
      following election, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} it was incorporated, formed or otherwise
      organized outside Canada; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a group, no person who is
    responsible for the group

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} resides in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132738){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132738.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advertising to name third party

**[[349.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.5 .sectionLabel}** A third party shall
include --- in a manner that is clearly visible or otherwise accessible
--- in any partisan advertising message placed by it its name, its
telephone number, either its civic or its Internet address and an
indication in or on the message that it has authorized its transmission.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132742){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132742.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration requirement for third
parties

- **[[349.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.6
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A third party shall register
  immediately after having incurred the following expenses in an
  aggregate amount of \$500:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan
    activities that are carried out during a pre-election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} partisan advertising expenses in relation to
    partisan advertising messages that are transmitted during that
    period; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to election
    surveys that are conducted during that period.

  However, the third party may not register before the beginning of the
  pre-election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for registration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An application for registration shall be sent to the
  Chief Electoral Officer in the prescribed form and shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is an individual, the
    individual's name, address and telephone number, their signature and
    their declaration that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} they are a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} they are a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} they reside in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a corporation, the name,
    address and telephone number of the corporation and of an officer
    who has signing authority for it, the officer's signature and their
    declaration that the corporation carries on business in Canada;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a group, the name, address
    and telephone number of the group and of a person who is responsible
    for the group, the person's signature and their declaration that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} they are a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} they are a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} they reside in Canada;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the address and telephone number of the third
    party's office where its books and records are kept and of the
    office in Canada to which communications may be addressed and at
    which documents may be served; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and telephone number of the third
    party's financial agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration of financial agent to
  accompany application

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An application under subsection (2) shall be
  accompanied by a declaration signed by the financial agent accepting
  the appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New financial agent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a third party's financial agent is replaced, it
  shall, without delay, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the new
  financial agent's name, address and telephone number and a declaration
  signed by the new financial agent accepting the appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Trade union or corporation

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the third party is a trade union, corporation or
  other entity with a governing body, the application shall include a
  copy of a resolution passed by its governing body authorizing it to
  incur partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses and
  election survey expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of application

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, without delay
  after receiving an application, determine whether the requirements set
  out in subsections (1) to (3) and (5) are met and shall then notify
  the person who signed the application whether the third party is
  registered. In the case of a refusal to register, the Chief Electoral
  Officer shall give reasons for the refusal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application rejected

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A third party may not be registered under a name
  that, in the Chief Electoral Officer's opinion, is likely to be
  confused with the name of a registered party or eligible party, a
  potential candidate, a nomination contestant, a candidate, a
  leadership contestant, a leader of a registered party or eligible
  party or a registered third party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration ends

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 353(1.1), the registration of a
  third party is valid only for the pre-election period during which the
  application is made, but the third party continues to be subject to
  this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132776){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132776.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of financial agent

- **[[349.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.7
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A third party that is required to
  register under subsection 349.6(1) shall appoint a financial agent,
  who may be a person who is authorized to sign an application for
  registration made under that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Financial agent --- ineligible persons

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following persons are not eligible to be a
  financial agent of a third party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an election officer or a member of the staff of a
    returning officer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a potential candidate or --- if the potential
    candidate is deemed to be a candidate under section 477 --- their
    official agent;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the chief agent of a registered party or eligible
    party;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a registered agent of a registered party;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a nomination contestant or their financial agent;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a leadership contestant or their leadership
    campaign agent; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a person who is not a Canadian citizen or a
    [[permanent resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in
    subsection 2(1) of the [Immigration and Refugee Protection
    Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132790){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132790.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement to appoint auditor

- **[[349.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.8
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A third party that is required to
  register under subsection 349.6(1) shall appoint an auditor without
  delay if it incurs the following expenses in an aggregate amount of
  \$10,000 or more:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan
    activities that are carried out during a pre-election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} partisan advertising expenses in relation to
    partisan advertising messages that are transmitted during that
    period; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to election
    surveys that are conducted during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligibility criteria

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following are eligible to be an auditor for a
  third party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person who is a member in good standing of a
    corporation, an association or an institute of professional
    accountants; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a partnership every partner of which is a member in
    good standing of a corporation, an association or an institute of
    professional accountants.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor --- ineligible persons

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The following persons are not eligible to be an
  auditor for a third party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party's financial agent;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who signed the application made under
    subsection 349.6(2);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an election officer or a member of the staff of a
    returning officer;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a potential candidate or --- if the potential
    candidate is deemed to be a candidate under section 477 --- their
    official agent;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the chief agent of a registered party or eligible
    party;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a registered agent of a registered party;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a nomination contestant or their financial agent;
    and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a leadership contestant or their leadership
    campaign agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of appointment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Every third party, without delay after an auditor is
  appointed, shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the
  auditor's name, address, telephone number and occupation and a
  declaration signed by the auditor accepting the appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New auditor

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a third party's auditor is replaced, it shall,
  without delay, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the new
  auditor's name, address, telephone number and occupation and a
  declaration signed by the new auditor accepting the appointment.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132816){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132816.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Responsibilities of financial agent

- **[[349.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.9
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every contribution made during a
  pre-election period to a registered third party for partisan activity,
  partisan advertising or election survey purposes shall be accepted by
  its financial agent, and every partisan activity expense, partisan
  advertising expense or election survey expense incurred during a
  pre-election period on behalf of a registered third party shall be
  authorized by its financial agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A financial agent may authorize a person to accept
  contributions or to authorize the incurring of partisan activity
  expenses, partisan advertising expenses or election survey expenses,
  but that authorization does not limit the financial agent's
  responsibility.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132823){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132823.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interim third-party expenses return

- **[[349.91]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.91
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is required
  to be registered in accordance with subsection 349.6(1) shall file an
  interim third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with the
  Chief Electoral Officer within 5 days after the day on which it became
  required to be registered in accordance with that subsection, if the
  third party

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has incurred expenses referred to in subsection
    349.1(1) in an aggregate amount of \$10,000 or more during the
    period beginning on the day after polling day at the general
    election previous to the pre-election period and ending on the day
    on which it became required to be registered in accordance with
    subsection 349.6(1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has received contributions in an aggregate amount
    of \$10,000 or more for partisan activity, partisan advertising,
    election advertising or election survey purposes during the period
    referred to in paragraph (a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of return

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return shall contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan activity expenses referred to in
    subsection 349.1(2) incurred during the period referred to in
    paragraph (1)(a) and the date and place of the partisan activities
    to which the expenses relate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan advertising expenses referred to
    in subsection 349.1(2) incurred during that period and the date and
    place of the transmission of the partisan advertising messages to
    which the expenses relate;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a list of election survey expenses referred to in
    subsection 349.1(2) incurred during that period and the date of the
    election surveys to which the expenses relate; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a list of all partisan activity expenses, partisan
    advertising expenses and election survey expenses referred to in
    subsection 349.1(1) incurred during that period --- other than those
    referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c) --- and the date and place of
    the partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses
    relate, the date and place of the transmission of the partisan
    advertising messages to which the partisan advertising expenses
    relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election
    survey expenses relate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When no expenses

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a third party has not incurred expenses referred
  to in subsection (2), that fact shall be indicated in its interim
  third-party expenses return.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount, by class of contributor, of
    contributions for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election
    advertising or election survey purposes that were received during
    the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to paragraph (c), for each contributor who
    made contributions of a total amount of more than \$200 for partisan
    activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election
    survey purposes during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a),
    their name, address and class, and the amount and date of each
    contribution;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a numbered company that is a
    contributor referred to in paragraph (b), the name of the chief
    executive officer or president of that company; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the amount, other than an amount of a contribution
    referred to in paragraph (a), that was paid out of the third party's
    own funds during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) for
    partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses, election
    advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return need not
  include any information referred to in subsections (2) and (4) that
  was included in a third-party expenses return that the third party
  previously filed under subsection 359(1) in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a by-election that was held after the general
    election referred to in paragraph (1)(a); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a general election for which the third party
    incurred expenses or received contributions between the day fixed
    under paragraph 57(1.2)(c) for polling day at the general election
    and polling day in an electoral district in which the election was
    postponed under subsection 59(4) or 77(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loans

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (4), a contribution
  includes a loan.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Categories

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraphs (4)(a) and (b), the
  following are the classes of contributor:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} individuals;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} businesses;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} commercial organizations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} governments;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} trade unions;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} corporations without share capital other than trade
    unions; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} unincorporated organizations or associations other
    than trade unions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Names to be provided

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} If the third party is unable to identify which
  contributions were received during the period referred to in paragraph
  (1)(a) for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election
  advertising or election survey purposes, the interim third-party
  expenses return shall include, subject to paragraph (4)(c), the names
  and addresses of every contributor who contributed a total of more
  than \$200 to it during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return shall include
  a declaration that the return is accurate signed by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party's financial agent; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if different from the financial agent, the person
    who signed the application made under subsection 349.6(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supporting documents

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} A third party shall, at the request of the Chief
  Electoral Officer, provide documents evidencing expenses set out in
  the return that are in an amount of more than \$50, including bank
  statements, deposit slips and cancelled cheques.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132867){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132867.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interim third-party expenses return

- **[[349.92]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.92
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is required
  to be registered in accordance with subsection 349.6(1) shall file an
  interim third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with the
  Chief Electoral Officer on September 15, if the third party

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has incurred expenses referred to in subsection
    349.1(1) in an aggregate amount of \$10,000 or more during the
    period beginning on the day after polling day at the general
    election previous to the pre-election period and ending on the
    earlier of September 14 and the last day of the pre-election period;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has received contributions in an aggregate amount
    of \$10,000 or more for partisan activity, partisan advertising,
    election advertising or election survey purposes during the period
    referred to in paragraph (a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Section 349.91 applies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsections 349.91(2) to (10) apply to the return
  under subsection (1), except that a reference to the period referred
  to in paragraph (1)(a) of section 349.91 shall be read as a reference
  to the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) of this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the exceptions set out in subsection
  349.91(5), the interim third-party expenses return need not include
  any information referred to in subsections 349.91(2) and (4) that was
  included in an interim third-party expenses return that the third
  party previously filed under subsection 349.91(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} This section applies only in the case of a general
  election that is held on a day set in accordance with subsection
  56.1(2) or section 56.2.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132880){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132880.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- false, misleading or
incomplete return

**[[349.93]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.93 .sectionLabel}** No third party
shall file under subsection 349.91(1) or 349.92(1) an interim
third-party expenses return that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party knows or ought reasonably to know
  contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} does not substantially set out the information
  required under section 349.91 or 349.92, as the case may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132886){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132886.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- use of certain
contributions

**[[349.94]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-349.94 .sectionLabel}** No third party
shall use a contribution made for partisan activity, partisan
advertising or election survey purposes for the purpose of any of the
following if the third party does not know the name and address of the
contributor or is otherwise unable to determine within which class of
contributor referred to in subsection 349.91(7) the contributor falls:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a partisan activity that is carried out during a
  pre-election period;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a partisan advertising message that is transmitted
  during that period; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an election survey that is conducted during that
  period and whose results the third party takes into account in its
  decisions concerning whether or not to organize and carry out partisan
  activities during that period or to transmit partisan advertising
  messages during that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 223](#1042748-1132893){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042748-1132893.html"}
:::

### [DIVISION 2]{.HLabel2}[Partisan Activities, Election Advertising and Election Surveys During Election Period]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1132894 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum election period expenses

- **[[350]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-350
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 351.1, a third
  party shall not incur the following expenses in an aggregate amount of
  more than \$350,000:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan
    activities that are carried out during the election period of a
    general election;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} election advertising expenses in relation to
    election advertising messages that are transmitted during that
    period; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to election
    surveys that are conducted during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum election period expenses ---
  electoral district

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Not more than \$3,000 of the maximum amount referred
  to in subsection (1) shall be incurred to promote or oppose the
  election of one or more candidates in a given electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses --- party leader

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The maximum amount set out in subsection (2) only
  applies to an amount incurred with respect to a leader of a registered
  party or eligible party to the extent that it is incurred to promote
  or oppose his or her election in an electoral district.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum election period expenses ---
  by-election

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 351.1, a third party shall not
  incur the following expenses in an aggregate amount of more than
  \$3,000 in a given electoral district:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan
    activities that are carried out during the election period of a
    by-election;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} election advertising expenses in relation to
    election advertising messages that are transmitted during that
    period; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to election
    surveys that are conducted during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Uncancellable spending

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a general election that is not held
  on a day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2, or
  of a by-election, a third party is deemed not to have incurred a
  partisan activity expense, an election advertising expense or an
  election survey expense if, on the issue of the writ or writs, it is
  not able to cancel the activity, the transmission of the advertising
  message or the survey, as the case may be, that the expense is in
  relation to.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Third party inflation adjustment factor

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The amounts referred to in subsections (1), (2)
  and (4) shall be multiplied by the inflation adjustment factor
  referred to in section 384 that is in effect on the issue of the writ
  or writs.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 224\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- circumventing maximum
amount

**[[351]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-351 .sectionLabel}** A third party shall not
circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, a maximum amount set out in
section 350 in any manner, including by splitting itself into two or
more third parties for the purpose of circumventing the maximum amount
or acting in collusion with another third party so that their combined
partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election
survey expenses exceed the maximum amount.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 351
- [2018, c. 31, s. 225](#1042774-1132917){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042774-1132917.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-351-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 351"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- collusion with registered
party

- **[[351.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-351.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No third party and no registered
  party shall act in collusion with each other --- including by sharing
  information --- in order to influence the third party in its partisan
  activities that it carries out during an election period, its election
  advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be
  conducted during an election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- collusion with
  candidate

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No third party and no candidate shall act in
  collusion with each other --- including by sharing information --- in
  order to influence the third party in its partisan activities that it
  carries out during an election period, its election advertising or its
  election surveys that it conducts or causes to be conducted during an
  election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- collusion with
  associated person

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No third party and no person associated with a
  candidate's campaign --- including a candidate's official agent ---
  shall act in collusion with each other --- including by sharing
  information --- in order to influence the third party in its partisan
  activities that it carries out during an election period, its election
  advertising or its election surveys that it conducts or causes to be
  conducted during an election period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 225](#1042774-1132926){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042774-1132926.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- spending by foreign third
parties

- **[[351.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-351.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A foreign third party shall not
  incur the following expenses:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to a
    partisan activity that is carried out during an election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} election advertising expenses in relation to an
    election advertising message that is transmitted during that period;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to an election
    survey that is conducted during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[foreign third
  party]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (1), a [[foreign third
  party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} is a third party in respect of which

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is an individual, the individual

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is not a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is not a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} does not reside in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a corporation or entity,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} it does not carry on business in Canada, or its
      primary purpose in Canada during an election period is to
      influence electors during that period to vote or refrain from
      voting, or to vote or refrain from voting for a particular
      candidate or registered party, at the election, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} it was incorporated, formed or otherwise
      organized outside Canada; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a group, no person who is
    responsible for the group

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} resides in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 78.1
- [2018, c. 31, s. 225](#1042774-1132946){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042774-1132946.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advertising to name third party

**[[352]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-352 .sectionLabel}** A third party shall
include --- in a manner that is clearly visible or otherwise accessible
--- in any election advertising message placed by it its name, its
telephone number, either its civic or its Internet address and an
indication in or on the message that it has authorized its transmission.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration requirement for third
parties

- **[[353]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-353 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  third party shall register immediately after having incurred the
  following expenses in an aggregate amount of \$500:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in relation to partisan
    activities that are carried out during an election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} election advertising expenses in relation to
    election advertising messages that are transmitted during that
    period; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to election
    surveys that are conducted during that period.

  However, the third party may not register before the issue of the
  writ.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- deemed registration

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A third party that registered under subsection
  349.6(1) during a pre-election period that ends the day before the day
  of the issue of the writ and that is also required to register under
  subsection (1) is deemed to be registered under that subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for registration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An application for registration shall be sent to the
  Chief Electoral Officer in the prescribed form and shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is an individual, the
    individual's name, address and telephone number, their signature and
    their declaration that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} they are a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} they are a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} they reside in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a corporation, the name,
    address and telephone number of the corporation and of an officer
    who has signing authority for it, the officer's signature and their
    declaration that the corporation carries on business in Canada;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} if the third party is a group, the name, address
    and telephone number of the group and of a person who is responsible
    for the group, the person's signature and their declaration that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} they are a Canadian citizen,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} they are a [[permanent
      resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in subsection 2(1) of
      the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} they reside in Canada;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the address and telephone number of the third
    party's office where its books and records are kept and of the
    office in Canada to which communications may be addressed and at
    which documents may be served; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and telephone number of the third
    party's financial agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration of financial agent to
  accompany application

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An application under subsection (2) must be
  accompanied by a declaration signed by the financial agent accepting
  the appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New financial agent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a third party's financial agent is replaced, it
  shall, without delay, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the new
  financial agent's name, address and telephone number and a declaration
  signed by the new financial agent accepting the appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Trade union or corporation

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the third party is a trade union, corporation or
  other entity with a governing body, the application shall include a
  copy of a resolution passed by its governing body authorizing it to
  incur partisan activity expenses, election advertising expenses and
  election survey expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of application

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, without delay
  after receiving an application, determine whether the requirements set
  out in subsections (1) to (3) and (5) are met and shall then notify
  the person who signed the application whether the third party is
  registered. In the case of a refusal to register, the Chief Electoral
  Officer shall give reasons for the refusal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application rejected

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A third party may not be registered under a name
  that, in the opinion of the Chief Electoral Officer, is likely to be
  confused with the name of a candidate, registered party, registered
  third party or eligible party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration ends

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The registration of a third party is valid only for
  the election period during which the application is made, but the
  third party continues to be subject to the requirement to file a
  third-party expenses return under subsection 359(1).

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of financial agent

- **[[354]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-354 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  third party that is required to register under subsection 353(1) shall
  appoint a financial agent who may be a person who is authorized to
  sign an application for registration made under that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- deemed appointment

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If, at the end of the pre-election period before a
  general election referred to in paragraph 353(1)(a), a third party has
  a financial agent who was appointed under subsection 349.7(1), the
  financial agent is deemed to have been appointed under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Financial agent --- ineligible persons

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following persons are not eligible to be a
  financial agent of a third party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a candidate or an official agent of a candidate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who is the chief agent, or a registered
    agent, of a registered party;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an election officer or a member of the staff of a
    returning officer; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person who is not a Canadian citizen or a
    permanent resident within the meaning of subsection 2(1) of the
    [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 354
- 2001, c. 27, s. 212
- [2018, c. 31, s. 227](#1042811-1132978){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042811-1132978.html"}
:::

Version](section-354-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 354"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement to appoint auditor

- **[[355]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-355 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  third party that is required to register under subsection 353(1) shall
  appoint an auditor without delay if it incurs the following expenses
  in an aggregate amount of \$10,000 or more:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} partisan activity expenses in respect of partisan
    activities that take place during an election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} election advertising expenses in respect of
    election advertising messages that are transmitted during that
    period; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} election survey expenses in relation to that
    period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- deemed appointment

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If, when the obligation under subsection (1) to
  appoint an auditor applies, a third party has an auditor who was
  appointed under subsection 349.8(1), the auditor is deemed to have
  been appointed under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligibility criteria

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following are eligible to be an auditor for a
  third party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person who is a member in good standing of a
    corporation, an association or an institute of professional
    accountants; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a partnership every partner of which is a member in
    good standing of a corporation, an association or an institute of
    professional accountants.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligibility criteria

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The following persons are not eligible to be an
  auditor for a third party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party's financial agent;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who signed the application made under
    subsection 353(2);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an election officer or a member of the staff of a
    returning officer;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a candidate;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the official agent of a candidate;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the chief agent of a registered party or an
    eligible party; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a registered agent of a registered party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of appointment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Every third party, without delay after an auditor is
  appointed, must provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the auditor's
  name, address, telephone number and occupation and a signed
  declaration accepting the appointment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New auditor

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a third party's auditor is replaced, it must,
  without delay, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the new
  auditor's name, address, telephone number and occupation and a signed
  declaration accepting the appointment.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Responsibilities of financial agent

- **[[357]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-357
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every contribution made during an
  election period to a registered third party for partisan activity,
  election advertising or election survey purposes shall be accepted by
  its financial agent, and every partisan activity expense, election
  advertising expense and election survey expense incurred during an
  election period on behalf of a registered third party shall be
  authorized by its financial agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A financial agent may authorize a person to accept
  contributions or to authorize the incurring of partisan activity
  expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses,
  but that authorization does not limit the financial agent's
  responsibility.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 230\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interim third party expenses return

- **[[357.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-357.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is required
  to be registered in accordance with subsection 353(1) shall file an
  interim third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with the
  Chief Electoral Officer on the 21st day before polling day, if the
  third party

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was required to file an interim third-party
    expenses return with the Chief Electoral Officer under subsection
    349.92(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has incurred expenses referred to in subsection
    349.1(1) or 350(1) in an aggregate amount of \$10,000 or more during
    the period beginning on the day after polling day at the previous
    general election and ending on the 23rd day before polling day; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has received contributions in an aggregate amount
    of \$10,000 or more for partisan activity, partisan advertising,
    election advertising or election survey purposes during the period
    referred to in paragraph (b).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of return

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return shall contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a general election that is held on a
    day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan activity expenses referred to
      in subsection 349.1(2) and the date and place of the partisan
      activities to which the expenses relate,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan advertising expenses referred
      to in subsection 349.1(2) and the date and place of the
      transmission of the partisan advertising messages to which the
      expenses relate,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a list of election survey expenses referred to
      in subsection 349.1(2) and the date of the election surveys to
      which the expenses relate, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a list of all partisan activity expenses,
      partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses
      referred to in subsection 349.1(1) --- other than those referred
      to in subparagraphs (i) to (iii) --- and the date and place of the
      partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses
      relate, the date and place of the transmission of the partisan
      advertising messages to which the partisan advertising expenses
      relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election
      survey expenses relate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any general election,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan activity expenses referred to
      in subsection 350(2) and the date and place of the partisan
      activities to which the expenses relate,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of election advertising expenses referred
      to in subsection 350(2) and the date and place of the transmission
      of the election advertising messages to which the expenses relate,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a list of election survey expenses referred to
      in subsection 350(2) and the date of the election surveys to which
      the expenses relate, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a list of all partisan activity expenses,
      election advertising expenses and election survey expenses
      referred to in subsection 350(1) other than those referred to in
      subparagraphs (i) to (iii) and the date and place of the partisan
      activities to which the partisan activity expenses relate, the
      date and place of the transmission of the election advertising
      messages to which the election advertising expenses relate and the
      date of the election surveys to which the election survey expenses
      relate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When no expenses

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a third party has not incurred expenses referred
  to in subsection (2), that fact shall be indicated in its interim
  third-party expenses return.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount, by class of contributor, of
    contributions for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election
    advertising or election survey purposes that were received during
    the period referred to in paragraph (1)(b);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to paragraph (c), for each contributor who
    made contributions of a total amount of more than \$200 for partisan
    activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or election
    survey purposes during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(b),
    their name, address and class, and the amount and date of each
    contribution;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a numbered company that is a
    contributor referred to in paragraph (b), the name of the chief
    executive officer or president of that company; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the amount, other than an amount of a contribution
    referred to in paragraph (a), that was paid out of the third party's
    own funds during the period referred to in paragraph (1)(b) for
    partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising expenses, election
    advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return need not
  include any information referred to in subsections (2) and (4) that
  was included in a third-party expenses return that the third party
  previously filed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} under subsection 359(1) in respect of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a by-election that was held after the general
      election referred to in paragraph (1)(b), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a general election for which the third party
      incurred expenses or received contributions between the day fixed
      under paragraph 57(1.2)(c) for polling day at the general election
      and polling day in an electoral district in which the election was
      postponed under subsection 59(4) or 77(1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under subsection 349.91(1) or 349.92(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loans

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (4), a contribution
  includes a loan.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Categories

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraphs (4)(a) and (b), the
  following are the classes of contributor:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} individuals;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} businesses;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} commercial organizations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} governments;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} trade unions;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} corporations without share capital other than trade
    unions; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} unincorporated organizations or associations other
    than trade unions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Names to be provided

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} If the third party is unable to identify which
  contributions were received during the period referred to in paragraph
  (1)(b) for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election
  advertising or election survey purposes, the interim third-party
  expenses return shall include, subject to paragraph (4)(c), the names
  and addresses of every contributor who contributed a total of more
  than \$200 to it during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The interim third-party expenses return shall include
  a declaration that the return is accurate signed by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party's financial agent; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if different from the financial agent, the person
    who signed the application made under subsection 349.6(2) or 353(2),
    as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supporting documents

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} A third party shall, at the request of the Chief
  Electoral Officer, provide documents evidencing expenses set out in
  the return that are in an amount of more than \$50, including bank
  statements, deposit slips and cancelled cheques.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 231](#1042841-1133050){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042841-1133050.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interim third-party expenses return

- **[[357.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-357.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is required
  to be registered in accordance with subsection 353(1) shall file an
  interim third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with the
  Chief Electoral Officer on the 7th day before polling day, if the
  third party

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was required to file an interim third-party
    expenses return with the Chief Electoral Officer under subsection
    349.92(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has incurred expenses referred to in subsection
    349.1(1) or 350(1) in an aggregate amount of \$10,000 or more during
    the period beginning on the day after polling day at the previous
    general election and ending on the 9th day before polling day; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has received contributions in an aggregate amount
    of \$10,000 or more for partisan activity, partisan advertising,
    election advertising or election survey purposes during the period
    referred to in paragraph (b).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Section 357.01 applies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsections 357.01(2) to (10) apply to the return
  under subsection (1), except that a reference to the period referred
  to in paragraph (1)(b) of section 357.01 shall be read as a reference
  to the period referred to in paragraph (1)(b) of this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the exceptions set out in subsection
  357.01(5), the interim third-party expenses return need not include
  any information referred to in subsections 357.01(2) and (4) that was
  included in an interim third-party expenses return that the third
  party previously filed under subsection 357.01(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 231](#1042841-1133062){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042841-1133062.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- false, misleading or
incomplete return

**[[357.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-357.03 .sectionLabel}** No third party
shall file under subsection 357.01(1) or 357.02(1) an interim
third-party expenses return that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party knows or ought reasonably to know
  contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} does not substantially set out the information
  required under section 357.01 or 357.02, as the case may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 231](#1042841-1133068){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042841-1133068.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- use of certain
contributions

**[[357.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-357.1 .sectionLabel}** No third party
shall use a contribution for the purpose of any of the following if the
third party does not know the name and address of the contributor or is
otherwise unable to determine within which class of contributor referred
to in subsection 359(6) the contributor falls:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a partisan activity that is carried out during an
  election period;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an election advertising message that is transmitted
  during that period; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an election survey that is conducted during that
  period and whose results the third party takes into account in its
  decisions concerning whether or not to organize and carry out partisan
  activities during that period or to transmit election advertising
  messages during that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 231](#1042841-1133075){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042841-1133075.html"}
:::

### [DIVISION 3]{.HLabel2}[Third Parties' Bank Accounts, Registry of Third Parties and Third-Party Expenses Returns]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1133077 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Bank account

- **[[358.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-358.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A third party that is required to
  register under subsection 349.6(1) --- or under subsection 353(1), if
  it was not required to register under subsection 349.6(1) --- shall
  open a separate bank account for the sole purpose of its partisan
  activities that are carried out or to be carried out during a
  pre-election period or an election period, partisan advertising,
  election advertising and election surveys.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Financial institution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The account shall be in a [[Canadian financial
  institution]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in section 2 of the
  [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01), or in an [[authorized foreign
  bank]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in that section that is not
  subject to the restrictions and requirements referred to in subsection
  524(2) of that Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payments and receipts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} All of the third party's financial transactions in
  relation to its partisan activities referred to in subsection (1),
  partisan advertising, election advertising and election surveys that
  involve the payment or receipt of money are to be paid from or
  deposited to the account.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Closure of bank account

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} After polling day, the third party shall close the
  account once all unpaid claims and any outstanding balance have been
  dealt with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Final statement of bank account

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The third party shall, on closing the account,
  provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the final statement of the
  account.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 233](#1042846-1133090){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042846-1133090.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registry of third parties

**[[358.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-358.2 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall maintain, for the period that he or she considers
appropriate, a registry of registered third parties in which is
recorded, in relation to each one, the information referred to in
subsections 349.6(2), 349.8(4) and (5), 353(2) and 355(4) and (5).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 233](#1042846-1133094){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042846-1133094.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Third-party expenses return

- **[[359]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-359
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is required
  to be registered in accordance with subsection 349.6(1) or 353(1)
  shall file a third-party expenses return in the prescribed form with
  the Chief Electoral Officer within four months after polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of return

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The third-party expenses return shall contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a general election that is held on a
    day set in accordance with subsection 56.1(2) or section 56.2,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan activity expenses referred to
      in subsection 349.1(2) and the date and place of the partisan
      activities to which the expenses relate,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan advertising expenses referred
      to in subsection 349.1(2) and the date and place of the
      transmission of the partisan advertising messages to which the
      expenses relate,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a list of election survey expenses referred to
      in subsection 349.1(2) and the date of the election surveys to
      which the expenses relate, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a list of all partisan activity expenses,
      partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses
      referred to in subsection 349.1(1) --- other than those referred
      to in subparagraphs (i) to (iii) --- and the date and place of the
      partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses
      relate, the date and place of the transmission of the partisan
      advertising messages to which the partisan advertising expenses
      relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election
      survey expenses relate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any general election,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a list of partisan activity expenses referred to
      in subsection 350(2) and the date and place of the partisan
      activities to which the expenses relate,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of election advertising expenses referred
      to in subsection 350(2) and the date and place of the transmission
      of the election advertising messages to which the expenses relate,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a list of election survey expenses referred to
      in subsection 350(2) and the date of the election surveys to which
      the expenses relate, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a list of all partisan activity expenses,
      election advertising expenses and election survey expenses
      referred to in subsection 350(1) other than those referred to in
      subparagraphs (i) to (iii) and the date and place of the partisan
      activities to which the partisan activity expenses relate, the
      date and place of the transmission of the election advertising
      messages to which the election advertising expenses relate and the
      date of the election surveys to which the election survey expenses
      relate; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a by-election, a list of partisan
    activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey
    expenses referred to in subsection 350(4) and the date and place of
    the partisan activities to which the partisan activity expenses
    relate, the date and place of the transmission of the election
    advertising messages to which the election advertising expenses
    relate and the date of the election surveys to which the election
    survey expenses relate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When no expenses

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a third party has not incurred expenses referred
  to in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c), that fact shall be indicated in
  its third-party expenses return.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The third-party expenses return shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount, by class of contributor, of
    contributions for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election
    advertising or election survey purposes that were received during
    the period beginning the day after polling day at the general
    election previous to the polling day referred to in subsection (1)
    and ending on that polling day referred to in that subsection;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to paragraph (b.1), for each contributor
    who made contributions of a total amount of more than \$200 for
    partisan activity, partisan advertising, election advertising or
    election survey purposes during the period referred to in paragraph
    (a), their name, address and class, and the amount and date of each
    contribution;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a numbered company that is a
    contributor referred to in paragraph (b), the name of the chief
    executive officer or president of that company; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amount, other than an amount of a contribution
    referred to in paragraph (a), that was paid out of the third party's
    own funds for partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising
    expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} The third-party expenses return need not include
  any information referred to in subsection (4) that was included in a
  third-party expenses return that the third party previously filed
  under subsection (1) in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a by-election that was held after the general
    election referred to in paragraph (4)(a); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a general election for which the third party
    incurred expenses or received contributions between the day fixed
    under paragraph 57(1.2)(c) for polling day at the general election
    and polling day in an electoral district in which the election was
    postponed under subsection 59(4) or 77(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loans

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (4), a contribution
  includes a loan.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Categories

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraphs (4)(a) and (b), the
  following are the classes of contributor:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} individuals;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} businesses;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} commercial organizations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} governments;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} trade unions;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} corporations without share capital other than trade
    unions; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} unincorporated organizations or associations other
    than trade unions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Names to be provided

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If the third party is unable to identify which
  contributions were received during the period referred to in paragraph
  (4)(a) for partisan activity, partisan advertising, election
  advertising or election survey purposes, the third-party expenses
  return shall include, subject to paragraph (4)(b.1), the names and
  addresses of every contributor who contributed a total of more than
  \$200 to it during that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} A third-party expenses return shall include a
  declaration that the return is accurate signed by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party's financial agent; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if different from the financial agent, the person
    who signed the application made under subsection 353(2) or --- if
    subsection 353(1.1) applies --- 349.6(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supporting documents

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} A third party shall, at the request of the Chief
  Electoral Officer, provide documents evidencing expenses set out in
  the return that are in an amount of more than \$50, including bank
  statements, deposit slips and cancelled cheques.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 359
- 2001, c. 21, s. 20

  ajax-after="1042863-1133128.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-359-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 359"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- false, misleading or
incomplete document

**[[359.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-359.1 .sectionLabel}** No third party
shall file under subsection 359(1) a third-party expenses return that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third party knows or ought reasonably to know
  contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} does not substantially set out the information
  required under section 359.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 235](#1042878-1133134){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042878-1133134.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's report

- **[[360]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-360 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  third party incurs partisan activity expenses, partisan advertising
  expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses in
  an aggregate amount of \$10,000 or more, its third-party expenses
  return filed under subsection 359(1) shall include a report made under
  subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's report

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The third party's auditor shall report on the
  third-party expenses return and shall make any examination that will
  enable the auditor to give an opinion in the report as to whether the
  return presents fairly the information contained in the accounting
  records on which it is based.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An auditor shall include in the report any statement
  that the auditor considers necessary, when

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the third-party expenses return that is the subject
    of the report does not present fairly the information contained in
    the accounting records on which it is based;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the auditor has not received from the third party
    all of the required information and explanation; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} based on the auditor's examination, it appears that
    proper accounting records have not been kept by the third party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right of access

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The auditor shall have access at any reasonable time
  to all of the third party's documents that, in the auditor's opinion,
  are necessary to enable the auditor to prepare the report, and may
  require the third party to provide any information or explanation
  that, in the auditor's opinion, is necessary to enable the auditor to
  prepare the report.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 360
- [2018, c. 31, s. 236](#1042887-1133143){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042887-1133143.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-360-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 360"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minor corrections --- Chief Electoral
Officer

- **[[361]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-361 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer may correct a third-party expenses return
  filed under subsection 359(1) if the correction does not materially
  affect its substance.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corrections or revisions at request of
  Chief Electoral Officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may in writing request a
  third party to correct or revise, within a specified period, a
  third-party expenses return filed under subsection 359(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline for correction or revision

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Chief Electoral Officer requests a correction
  or revision, the third party shall provide him or her with the
  corrected or revised version of the return within the specified
  period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 361
