Version](section-361-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 361"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extensions --- Chief Electoral Officer

- **[[361.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-361.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the
  written application of a third party, shall authorize the extension of
  the period referred to in subsection 359(1) unless he or she is
  satisfied that the third party's failure to file the third-party
  expenses return under that subsection was deliberate or was the result
  of the third party's failure to exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application may be made within the period
  referred to in subsection 359(1) or within two weeks after the end of
  that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 237](#1042894-1133160){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042894-1133160.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corrections or revisions --- Chief
Electoral Officer

- **[[361.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-361.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the
  written application of a third party, shall authorize the correction
  or revision of a third-party expenses return filed under subsection
  359(1) if he or she is satisfied by the evidence submitted by the
  third party that the correction or revision is necessary in order for
  the requirements of this Act to be complied with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application made without delay

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall be made immediately after the
  third party becomes aware of the need for correction or revision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline for corrections or revisions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The third party shall provide the Chief Electoral
  Officer with the corrected or revised version of the return within 30
  days after the day on which the correction or revision is authorized
  or within any extension of that period authorized under subsection (4)
  or (5).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New deadline

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written
  application of the third party made within two weeks after the end of
  the 30-day period referred to in subsection (3), shall authorize the
  extension of that period, unless he or she is satisfied that the third
  party's failure to provide the corrected or revised version of the
  return was deliberate or was the result of the third party's failure
  to exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension of new deadline

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written
  application of the third party made within two weeks after the end of
  an extension authorized under subsection (4) or under this subsection,
  shall authorize the further extension of that period, unless he or she
  is satisfied that the third party's failure to provide the corrected
  or revised version of the return was deliberate or was the result of
  the third party's failure to exercise due diligence.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 237](#1042894-1133173){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042894-1133173.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extensions, corrections or revisions ---
judge

- **[[361.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-361.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A third party may apply to a judge
  for an order

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} relieving the third party from the obligation to
    comply with a request referred to in subsection 361(2);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} authorizing an extension referred to in subsection
    361.1(1); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} authorizing a correction or revision referred to in
    subsection 361.2(1).

  The third party shall notify the Chief Electoral Officer that the
  application has been made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application may be made

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (1)(a), within the specified period
    referred to in subsection 361(2) or within the two weeks after the
    end of that period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (1)(b), within two weeks after, as
    the case may be,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if an application for an extension is not made to
      the Chief Electoral Officer within the period referred to in
      subsection 361.1(2), the end of the two-week period referred to in
      that subsection,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the rejection of an application for an extension
      made in accordance with section 361.1, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the end of the extended period referred to in
      subsection 361.1(1); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (1)(c), within two weeks after the
    rejection of an application for a correction or revision made in
    accordance with section 361.2.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Grounds --- extension

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall grant an order authorizing an
  extension unless the judge is satisfied that the third party's failure
  to file the required third-party expenses return was deliberate or was
  the result of the third party's failure to exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Grounds --- corrections or revisions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall grant an order authorizing a
  correction or revision if the judge is satisfied by the evidence
  submitted by the third party that the correction or revision is
  necessary in order for the requirements of this Act to be complied
  with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of order

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The order may require that the third party satisfy
  any condition that the judge considers necessary for carrying out the
  purposes of this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 237](#1042894-1133196){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042894-1133196.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

**[[362]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-362 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall, in the manner he or she considers appropriate,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} publish the names and addresses of registered third
  parties, as they are registered;

- [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} publish, as soon as feasible, returns filed under
  subsection 349.91(1), 349.92(1), 357.01(1) or 357.02(1);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} publish, within one year after the issue of the writ,
  returns filed under subsection 359(1); and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} publish, as soon as feasible, a corrected or revised
  version of a return filed under subsection 359(1) and published under
  paragraph (b).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 362
- [2018, c. 31, s. 238](#1042896-1133203){.wb-lbx

## [PART 18]{.HLabel1}[Financial Administration]{.HTitleText1} {#h-206929 .Part}

### [DIVISION 1]{.HLabel2}[General Financial Provisions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-206930 .Subheading}

#### [Contributions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-206931 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- ineligible contributors

- **[[363]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-363 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person or entity other than an individual who is a Canadian citizen or
  is a permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the
  [Immigration and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5) shall make a
  contribution to a registered party, a registered association, a
  nomination contestant, a candidate or a leadership contestant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return of contributions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a registered party, a registered association, a
  nomination contestant, a candidate or a leadership contestant receives
  a contribution from an ineligible contributor, the chief agent of the
  registered party, the financial agent of the registered association,
  the official agent of the candidate or the financial agent of the
  nomination contestant or leadership contestant, as the case may be,
  shall, within 30 days after becoming aware of the ineligibility,
  return the contribution unused to the contributor or, if that is not
  possible, pay the amount of it --- or, in the case of a non-monetary
  contribution, an amount of money equal to its commercial value --- to
  the Chief Electoral Officer, who shall forward that amount to the
  Receiver General.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provincial divisions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, contributions to and expenses
  of a provincial division of a registered party are contributions to
  and expenses of the party. Similarly, transfers of funds to or by the
  division are transfers to or by the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered agents

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A provincial division of a registered party may
  appoint registered agents, subject to any terms and conditions that
  the appointment specifies. This Act applies to those agents as if they
  were registered agents appointed by the party under subsection 396(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 363
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-363-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 363"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributions --- inclusions and
exclusions

- **[[364]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-364 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  money that is used for a nomination contestant's, a candidate's or a
  leadership contestant's campaign out of their own funds is a
  contribution for the purposes of this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- litigation expenses and
  personal expenses

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Act, any money that is
  used out of a nomination contestant's, candidate's or leadership
  contestant's own funds to pay a litigation expense or personal expense
  is not a contribution if it has not been deposited into the bank
  account referred to in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} subsection 476.65(1), in the case of a nomination
    contestant;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subsection 477.46(1), in the case of a candidate;
    or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subsection 478.72(1), in the case of a leadership
    contestant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion for goods and services ---
  registered parties, registered associations and candidates

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A provision of goods or services is permitted and is
  not a contribution for the purposes of this Act if it is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} from a registered party to an electoral district
    association of the party or a candidate endorsed by the party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} from a registered association to the registered
    party with which it is affiliated, another registered association of
    the party or a candidate endorsed by the party;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} from a registered party or registered association
    to a nomination contestant or a leadership contestant in compliance
    with subsection 365(1);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} from a candidate endorsed by a registered party to
    the party or a registered association of the party;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} from a candidate to themselves in their capacity as
    a nomination contestant in respect of the same election; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case where a writ is deemed to be withdrawn
    under subsection 31(3) of the [Parliament of Canada
    Act](/eng/acts/P-1), from a candidate in an election that is
    cancelled to themselves in their capacity as a candidate in respect
    of the general election resulting from the dissolution of
    Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion for funds --- registered
  parties, registered associations and candidates

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A transfer of funds is permitted and is not a
  contribution for the purposes of this Act if it is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} from a registered party to an electoral district
    association of the party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} from a registered association to the registered
    party with which it is affiliated or another registered association
    of the party;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} from a candidate endorsed by a registered party to
    the party or a registered association of the party;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} from a candidate to themselves in their capacity as
    a nomination contestant in respect of the same election; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case where a writ is deemed to be withdrawn
    under subsection 31(3) of the [Parliament of Canada
    Act](/eng/acts/P-1), from a candidate in an election that is
    cancelled to themselves in their capacity as a candidate in respect
    of the general election resulting from the dissolution of
    Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion for funds other than trust
  funds --- registered parties and registered associations

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A transfer of funds, other than trust funds, is
  permitted and is not a contribution for the purposes of this Act if it
  is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} from a registered party to a candidate endorsed by
    the party; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} from a registered association to a candidate
    endorsed by the registered party with which the association is
    affiliated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion for funds --- nomination
  contestants, leadership contestants and registered parties

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A transfer of funds is permitted and is not a
  contribution for the purposes of this Act if it is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} from a nomination contestant of a registered party
    to the party, the registered association of the party that held the
    nomination contest or the official agent of the candidate endorsed
    by the party in the electoral district in which the nomination
    contest was held;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} from a leadership contestant of a registered party
    to the party or a registered association of the party; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} from a registered party to a leadership contestant
    out of funds from a directed contribution referred to in subsection
    365(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- paid leave of absence

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The provision by an employer of a paid leave of
  absence to an employee for the purpose of allowing the employee to be
  a nomination contestant or candidate is not a contribution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- membership fees

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The payment by an individual during a year of fees of
  not more than \$25 per year for a period of not more than five years
  for membership in a registered party is not a contribution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, the payment by or on behalf of
  an individual of fees to attend an annual or biennial convention or
  leadership convention of a particular registered party is a
  contribution to that party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity other than an individual who is a
  Canadian citizen or a [[permanent resident]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as
  defined in subsection 2(1) of the [Immigration and Refugee Protection
  Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5) shall pay fees to attend an annual or biennial
  convention or leadership convention of a particular registered party,
  or pay fees on behalf of another individual for them to attend such a
  convention.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 364
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 239](#1042905-1133211){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042905-1133211.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-364-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 364"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certain transfers prohibited

- **[[365]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-365 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  registered party and no electoral district association of a registered
  party shall provide goods or services or transfer funds to a
  nomination contestant or a leadership contestant, unless the goods or
  services are offered equally to all contestants.

- Definition of [[directed contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[directed
  contribution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an amount that is all or part
  of a contribution made to a registered party and that the contributor
  requests in writing be transferred to a particular leadership
  contestant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to a directed
  contribution that is transferred by the registered party to the
  leadership contestant mentioned in the request if the party provides,
  with the amount transferred, a statement in the prescribed form
  setting out the name and address of the contributor, the amount and
  date of the contribution, the amount of the directed contribution, the
  amount that the party is transferring and the date of the transfer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Presumption

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The amount of a directed contribution that is to be
  transferred to a leadership contestant is deemed to be a contribution
  made by the contributor to the contestant.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 365
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-365-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 365"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issuance of receipts

- **[[366]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-366 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  person who is authorized to accept contributions on behalf of a
  registered party, a registered association, a nomination contestant, a
  candidate or a leadership contestant shall issue a receipt --- of
  which the person shall keep a copy --- for each contribution of more
  than \$20 that they accept.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Record keeping

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If anonymous contributions of \$20 or less per person
  are collected in response to a general solicitation at a meeting or
  fundraising event related to the affairs of a registered party, a
  registered association, a nomination contestant, a candidate or a
  leadership contestant, the person authorized to accept those
  contributions shall record the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a description of the function at which the
    contributions were collected;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date of the function;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the approximate number of people at the function;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the total amount of the anonymous contributions
    received.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 366
- 2004, c. 24, s. 3
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-366-20040514.html "Link to previous version of section 366"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution limits

- **[[367]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-367
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 373(4), no
  individual shall make contributions that exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} \$1,500 in total in any calendar year to a
    particular registered party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} \$1,500 in total in any calendar year to the
    registered associations, nomination contestants and candidates of a
    particular registered party;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} \$1,500 in total to a candidate for a particular
    election who is not the candidate of a registered party; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} \$1,500 in total in any calendar year to the
    leadership contestants in a particular leadership contest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Increase to contribution limits

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The contribution limits set out in subsection (1)
  increase by \$25 on January 1 in each year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Testamentary dispositions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A contribution may be made by way of a testamentary
  disposition if the contribution is made only in one calendar year and
  does not cause the contributor to exceed the relevant limit under
  subsection (1), taking into account any contributions that the
  contributor made before their death.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-conforming testamentary
  dispositions read down

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A testamentary disposition that provides for a
  contribution that would cause the contributor to exceed the relevant
  limit under subsection (1) shall be read as if the contribution is for
  the highest amount that would not cause the contributor to exceed that
  limit, and a testamentary disposition that provides for a contribution
  to be made in more than one calendar year after the year in which this
  subsection comes into force shall be read as if the contribution is to
  be made only in the first of those calendar years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attribution of certain contributions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), a contribution to
  a person who presents themselves as seeking the endorsement of a
  particular registered party is to be treated as a contribution
  referred to in paragraph (1)(b) to a candidate of that party and a
  contribution to a person who presents themselves as seeking to be a
  candidate not endorsed by any registered party is to be treated as a
  contribution referred to in paragraph (1)(c).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- nomination contestant's
  contributions to own campaign

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Contributions that do not exceed \$1,000 in total by
  a nomination contestant out of their own funds to their own campaign
  as a nomination contestant do not count towards the nomination
  contestant's contributions for the purposes of paragraph (1)(b).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributions --- candidates and
  leadership contestants

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (7), no candidate in a
  particular election and no leadership contestant in a particular
  leadership contest shall make a contribution out of their own funds to
  their own campaign.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- certain contributions to
  own campaign

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The following contributions are permitted:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} contributions that do not exceed \$5,000 in total
    by a candidate for a particular election out of their own funds to
    their own campaign; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contributions that do not exceed \$25,000 in total
    by a leadership contestant in a particular leadership contest out of
    their own funds to their own campaign.

  For greater certainty, contributions made by a candidate under
  subsection (1) to a registered party or a registered association that
  later transfers funds to the candidate for the purpose of their
  campaign do not have the effect of reducing the amount that the
  candidate may contribute under this subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributions under subsection (1) not
  affected

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Contributions made under subsection (7) do not have
  the effect of reducing the amounts that the candidate or leadership
  contestant, as the case may be, may contribute under subsection (1) to
  other candidates or to other leadership contestants, as the case may
  be.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 367
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 86, 87
- [2018, c. 31, s. 240](#1042912-1133213){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042912-1133213.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-367-20160101.html "Link to previous version of section 367"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- circumventing limits

- **[[368]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-368 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person or entity shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} circumvent, or attempt to circumvent, the
    prohibition under subsection 363(1) or 367(6) or a limit set out in
    subsection 367(1) or (7) or section 371; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} act in collusion with another person or entity for
    that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- concealing source of
  contribution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} conceal, or attempt to conceal, the identity of the
    source of a contribution governed by this Act; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} act in collusion with another person or entity for
    that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- accepting excessive
  contributions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person who is permitted to accept contributions
  under this Act shall accept a contribution that exceeds a limit under
  this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibited agreements

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity shall enter into an agreement for
  the provision for payment of goods or services, directly or
  indirectly, to a registered party or a candidate that includes a term
  that any individual will make a contribution, directly or indirectly,
  to a registered party, a registered association, a nomination
  contestant, a candidate or a leadership contestant.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 368
- 2004, c. 24, s. 4
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 241](#1042916-1133216){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042916-1133216.html"}
:::

:::

**[[368.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-368.1 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2014,
c. 12, s. 86\]]{.Repealed}

Version](section-368.1-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 368.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- soliciting or accepting
contribution

- **[[369]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-369 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person or entity shall solicit or accept a contribution on behalf of a
  registered party, a registered association or a candidate if the
  person or entity makes a representation to the contributor or
  potential contributor that part or all of the contribution would be
  transferred to a person or entity other than the registered party or a
  candidate, a leadership contestant or an electoral district
  association.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- collusion

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity shall act in collusion with
  another person or entity for the purpose of circumventing the
  prohibition under subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 369
- 2004, c. 24, s. 5
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-369-20040514.html "Link to previous version of section 369"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- making indirect
contributions

- **[[370]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-370 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  individual shall make a contribution to a registered party, a
  registered association, a nomination contestant, a candidate or a
  leadership contestant that comes from money, property or the services
  of any person or entity that was provided to that individual for that
  purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- candidates and leadership
  contestants

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a candidate or a leadership
  contestant may make a contribution under subsection 367(7) that comes
  from money provided by way of a loan to the candidate or leadership
  contestant made in writing by a financial institution as defined in
  section 2 of the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01) at a fair market rate of
  interest, as long as no security is given for the loan except property
  of the candidate or leadership contestant, as the case may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 370
- 2004, c. 24, s. 5
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on cash contributions

**[[371]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-371 .sectionLabel}** No individual shall, in
respect of each contribution made under this Division, contribute cash
in an amount that exceeds \$20.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 371
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-371-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 371"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return of contributions

**[[372]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-372 .sectionLabel}** If a registered party,
a registered association, a nomination contestant, a candidate or a
leadership contestant receives a contribution made in contravention of
subsection 367(1) or (6) or 368(4) or section 370 or 371, the chief
agent of the registered party, the financial agent of the registered
association, the official agent of the candidate or the financial agent
of the nomination contestant or leadership contestant, as the case may
be, shall, within 30 days after becoming aware of the contravention,
return the contribution unused to the contributor or, if that is not
possible, pay the amount of it --- or, in the case of a non-monetary
contribution, an amount of money equal to its commercial value --- to
the Chief Electoral Officer, who shall forward that amount to the
Receiver General.

- 2000, c. 9, s. 372

:::

#### [Loans, Guarantees and Suretyships]{.HTitleText3} {#h-207065 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligible lenders and guarantors

- **[[373]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-373
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as permitted under this
  section, no person or entity shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} make a loan to a registered party or a registered
    association;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make a loan to a nomination contestant, a candidate
    or a leadership contestant in relation to the contestant's or
    candidate's campaign; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} guarantee a loan referred to in paragraph (a) or
    (b).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligible borrowers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except if the loan is permitted under this section,
  no registered agent of a registered party and no financial agent of a
  registered association shall borrow money on behalf of the party or
  association, and no official agent of a candidate and no financial
  agent of a nomination contestant or of a leadership contestant shall
  borrow money for the purposes of the candidate's or contestant's
  campaign.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- financial institutions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A financial institution as defined in section 2 of
  the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01) may in writing make a loan referred
  to in subsection (1) at a fair market rate of interest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- individuals

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An individual who is a Canadian citizen or is a
  permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the [Immigration
  and Refugee Protection Act](/eng/acts/I-2.5) may in writing make a
  loan referred to in subsection (1) or guarantee such a loan. However,
  the total of the following amounts shall not at any time exceed the
  individual's relevant contribution limit set out in paragraphs
  367(1)(a) to (d), subsection 367(5) and paragraphs 367(7)(a) and (b):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amounts of the individual's contributions,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the amounts of the individual's loans made in the
    relevant contribution period, not including any amount that has been
    repaid in the calendar year in which the loan was made, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amounts guaranteed by the individual in the
    relevant contribution period, not including any amount for which the
    individual has ceased to be liable in the calendar year in which the
    guarantee was given.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- certain loans

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A loan may be made in writing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by a registered party to a registered association
    of the party or a candidate endorsed by the party; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by a registered association to the registered party
    with which it is affiliated, another registered association of the
    party or a candidate endorsed by the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- certain guarantees and
  suretyships

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A registered party or registered association may in
  writing guarantee a loan made in writing to a party, association or
  candidate to which it itself is permitted to make a loan under
  subsection (5).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 373
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-373-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 373"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- making indirect loans

**[[374]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-374 .sectionLabel}** No individual shall
make a loan to a registered party, a registered association, a
nomination contestant, a candidate or a leadership contestant that is
made possible by money, property or the services of any person or entity
that was provided to that individual for that purpose.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 374
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-374-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 374"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Expenses]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1133237 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nomination campaign expenses

- **[[374.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-374.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A nomination campaign expense of a
  nomination contestant is an expense reasonably incurred as an
  incidence of the nomination contest, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a nomination contest expense;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a litigation expense;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} travel and living expenses;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a personal expense; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any fees of an auditor appointed under subsection
    476.77(1) that have not been reimbursed by the Receiver General.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusions --- administrative monetary
  penalties, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, none of the following is a
  nomination campaign expense:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount of any administrative monetary penalty
    imposed under Part 19;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any amount that is required to be paid under a
    compliance agreement entered into under Part 19 solely as a result
    of that compliance agreement; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any amount that is required to be paid under an
    undertaking provided under Part 19 solely as a result of that
    undertaking.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2004, c. 24, s. 7; 2014, c. 12, s. 86](#1042924-1133234){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042924-1133234.html"}
- [2018, c. 31, s. 243](#1042924-1133235){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042924-1133235.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-374.1-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 374.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nomination contest expenses

- **[[374.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-374.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A nomination contest expense is any
  of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any cost incurred, or non-monetary contribution
    received, by a nomination contestant, to the extent that the
    property or service that the cost was incurred for or that was
    received as a non-monetary contribution is used to directly promote
    or oppose a nomination contestant during a nomination contest; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any acceptance by a nomination contestant of a
    provision of goods or services that is permitted under paragraph
    364(2)(c), to the extent that the goods or services are used to
    directly promote or oppose a nomination contestant during a
    nomination contest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- fundraising

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Expenses for a fundraising activity, other than
  expenses referred to in paragraphs (3)(a) and (b) that are related to
  that activity, are not nomination contest expenses under subsection
  (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inclusions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A nomination contest expense includes a cost incurred
  for, a non-monetary contribution in relation to, or a provision of
  goods and services in relation to,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the production of advertising or promotional
    material;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distribution, broadcast or publication of such
    material in any media or by any other means during the nomination
    contest, including by the use of a capital asset;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the payment of remuneration and expenses to or on
    behalf of a person for their services as a financial agent or in any
    other capacity;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} securing a meeting space or the supply of light
    refreshments at meetings;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any product or service provided by a government, a
    Crown corporation or any other public agency; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the conduct of surveys or research during a
    nomination contest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[cost
  incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[cost
  incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an expense that is incurred by a
  nomination contestant, whether it is paid or unpaid.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 243](#1042924-1133256){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042924-1133256.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Litigation expenses --- nomination
contestants

**[[374.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-374.3 .sectionLabel}** A litigation
expense of a nomination contestant is an expense of the contestant
related to an application to a judge made under this Part, including an
expense related to any appeal or judicial review arising from the
application.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 243](#1042924-1133260){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042924-1133260.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Personal expenses --- nomination
contestants

- **[[374.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-374.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A nomination contestant's personal
  expenses include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} childcare expenses;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} expenses relating to the provision of care for a
    person with a physical or mental incapacity for whom the contestant
    normally provides such care; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a contestant who has a disability,
    additional expenses that are related to the disability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusions --- travel and living
  expenses, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Neither litigation expenses nor travel and living
  expenses are personal expenses of a nomination contestant.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 243](#1042924-1133270){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042924-1133270.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electoral campaign expenses

- **[[375]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-375 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  electoral campaign expense of a candidate is an expense reasonably
  incurred as an incidence of the election, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an election expense;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} a litigation expense;

  - [(a.2)]{.lawlabel} travel and living expenses;

  - [(a.3)]{.lawlabel} an accessibility expense;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a personal expense; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any fees of an auditor appointed under subsection
    477.1(2) that have not been reimbursed by the Receiver General.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusions --- administrative monetary
  penalties, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, none of the following is an
  electoral campaign expense:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount of any administrative monetary penalty
    imposed under Part 19;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any amount that is required to be paid under a
    compliance agreement entered into under Part 19 solely as a result
    of that compliance agreement; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any amount that is required to be paid under an
    undertaking provided under Part 19 solely as a result of that
    undertaking.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 375
- 2003, c. 19, s. 9
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 244](#1042935-1133288){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042935-1133288.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-375-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 375"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election expenses

- **[[376]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-376 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  election expense is any of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any cost incurred, or non-monetary contribution
    received, by a registered party or a candidate, to the extent that
    the property or service that the cost was incurred for or that was
    received as a non-monetary contribution is used to directly promote
    or oppose a registered party, its leader or a candidate during an
    election period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any acceptance by a registered party or a candidate
    of a provision of goods or services that is permitted under
    subsection 364(2), to the extent that the goods or services are used
    to directly promote or oppose a registered party, its leader or a
    candidate during an election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusions --- certain fundraising and
  nominations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Expenses for a fundraising activity and expenses to
  directly promote the nomination of a person as a candidate or the
  selection of a person as leader of a registered party, other than
  expenses referred to in paragraphs (3)(a) and (b) that are related to
  such fundraising and promotional activities, are not election expenses
  under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inclusions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An election expense referred to in subsection (1)
  includes a cost incurred for, a non-monetary contribution in relation
  to, or a provision of goods and services in relation to,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the production of advertising or promotional
    material;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distribution, broadcast or publication of such
    material in any media or by any other means during the election
    period, including by the use of a capital asset;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the payment of remuneration and expenses to or on
    behalf of a person for their services as an official agent or
    registered agent or in any other capacity;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} securing a meeting space or the supply of light
    refreshments at meetings;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any product or service provided by a government, a
    Crown corporation or any other public agency; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the conduct of election surveys or other surveys or
    research during an election period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- accessibility expenses

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} An accessibility expense of a registered party or a
  candidate, as the case may be, is not an election expense of that
  party or candidate.

- Definition of [[cost incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (1), [[cost
  incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an expense that is incurred by a
  registered party or a candidate, whether it is paid or unpaid.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 376
- 2003, c. 19, s. 10
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 245](#1042944-1133291){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042944-1133291.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-376-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 376"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Partisan advertising expenses

**[[376.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-376.1 .sectionLabel}** A partisan
advertising expense of a registered party or an electoral district
association of a registered party, as the case may be, includes any of
the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} any non-monetary contribution received by the party
  or association, to the extent that the property or service that was
  received as a non-monetary contribution is used in relation to the
  production of a partisan advertising message or the transmission of a
  partisan advertising message to the public; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any acceptance by the party or association of a
  provision of goods or services that is permitted under subsection
  364(2), to the extent that the goods or services are used in relation
  to the production of a partisan advertising message or the
  transmission of a partisan advertising message to the public.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 246](#1042946-1133297){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042946-1133297.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributions for ticketed fundraising
functions

- **[[377]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-377 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  fundraising activity is held for the primary purpose of soliciting a
  monetary contribution for a registered party, a registered
  association, a nomination contestant, a candidate or a leadership
  contestant by way of selling a ticket, the amount of the monetary
  contribution received is the difference between the price of the
  ticket and the fair market value of what the ticket entitles the
  bearer to obtain.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calculation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), in calculating
  what a ticket bearer is entitled to obtain, to be included in the
  calculation is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the cost of any goods or services received by the
    ticket bearer personally, such as meals and promotional products;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} their share of any general expenses incurred by the
    registered party, registered association, nomination contestant,
    candidate or leadership contestant, as the case may be, in holding
    the activity, such as expenses incurred for the rental of a meeting
    space or for any audiovisual equipment used.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 377
- 2003, c. 19, s. 11
- 2004, c. 24, s. 8
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 247](#1042948-1133305){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042948-1133305.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-377-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 377"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Litigation expenses --- candidates

**[[377.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-377.1 .sectionLabel}** A litigation
expense of a candidate is an expense of the candidate related to any of
the following requests or applications, including an expense related to
any appeal or judicial review arising from the request or the
application:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a request or an application made under Part 14;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an application to a judge made under this Part; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an application to contest the election in the
  candidate's electoral district.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 248](#1042950-1133312){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042950-1133312.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Accessibility expenses

- **[[377.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-377.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An accessibility expense of a
  registered party or a candidate, as the case may be, is any of the
  following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount of any cost incurred, or non-monetary
    contribution received, by the party or candidate, to the extent that
    the property or service that the cost was incurred for --- or that
    was received as a non-monetary contribution --- is used solely to
    make accessible, to persons with a disability, materials used or
    activities held during an election period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the difference between the amounts referred to in
    subparagraphs (i) and (ii), to the extent that the amount referred
    to in subparagraph (i) is greater than the amount referred to in
    subparagraph (ii):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the amount of any cost incurred, or non-monetary
      contribution received, by the party or candidate, to the extent
      that the property or service that the cost was incurred for --- or
      that was received as a non-monetary contribution --- is used for
      materials used or activities held during an election period and
      those materials or activities are accessible to persons with a
      disability, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the amount equal to the value of the property or
      service if the materials or activities had not been accessible to
      persons with a disability;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amount equal to the value of goods or services
    referred to in subsection 364(2) that are accepted by the party or
    candidate, to the extent that the goods or services are used solely
    to make accessible, to persons with a disability, materials used or
    activities held during an election period; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the difference between the amounts referred to in
    subparagraphs (i) and (ii), to the extent that the amount referred
    to in subparagraph (i) is greater than the amount referred to in
    subparagraph (ii):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the amount equal to the value of goods or
      services referred to in subsection 364(2) that are accepted by the
      party or candidate, to the extent that the goods or services are
      used for materials used or activities held during an election
      period and those materials or activities are accessible to persons
      with a disability, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the amount equal to the value of the goods or
      services if the materials or activities had not been accessible to
      persons with a disability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- fundraising, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An amount referred to in subsection (1) that is
  related to a fundraising activity, to the nomination of a person as a
  candidate or to the selection of a person as leader of a registered
  party is not an accessibility expense.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[cost
  incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (1), [[cost
  incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an expense that is incurred by a
  registered party or a candidate, whether it is paid or unpaid.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Personal expenses --- candidate

- **[[378]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-378 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  candidate's personal expenses include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 249\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} childcare expenses;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} expenses relating to the provision of care for a

    normally provides such care; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a candidate who has a disability,

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusions --- travel and living

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Neither litigation expenses nor travel and living

maximums

**[[378.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-378.1 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may establish, in respect of candidates, categories of personal
expenses and of travel and living expenses and may fix maximum amounts
of expenses that may be incurred in each category.

representatives

**[[379]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-379 .sectionLabel}** Any expenses of a
candidate that are incurred to remunerate the candidate's
representatives referred to in subsection 136(1) or 237.1(2) are deemed
to be personal expenses of the candidate.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Leadership campaign expenses

- **[[379.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-379.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A leadership campaign expense of a
  leadership contestant is an expense reasonably incurred as an
  incidence of the leadership contest, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a leadership contest expense;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a litigation expense;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} travel and living expenses;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a personal expense; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any fees of an auditor appointed under Division 6
    of Part 18 that have not been reimbursed by the Receiver General.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusions --- administrative monetary
  penalties, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, none of the following is a
  leadership campaign expense:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount of any administrative monetary penalty
    imposed under Part 19;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any amount that is required to be paid under a
    compliance agreement entered into under Part 19 solely as a result
    of that compliance agreement; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any amount that is required to be paid under an
    undertaking provided under Part 19 solely as a result of that
    undertaking.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 251](#1042970-1133356){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042970-1133356.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Leadership contest expenses

- **[[379.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-379.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A leadership contest expense is any
  of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any cost incurred, or non-monetary contribution
    received, by a leadership contestant, to the extent that the
    property or service that the cost was incurred for or that was
    received as a non-monetary contribution is used to directly promote
    or oppose a leadership contestant during a leadership contest; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any acceptance by a leadership contestant of a
    provision of goods or services that is permitted under paragraph
    364(2)(c), to the extent that the goods or services are used to
    directly promote or oppose a leadership contestant during a
    leadership contest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- fundraising

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Expenses for a fundraising activity, other than
  expenses referred to in paragraphs (3)(a) and (b) that are related to
  that activity, are not leadership contest expenses under subsection
  (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inclusions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A leadership contest expense includes a cost incurred
  for, a non-monetary contribution in relation to, or a provision of
  goods and services in relation to,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the production of advertising or promotional
    material;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distribution, broadcast or publication of such
    material in any media or by any other means during the leadership
    contest, including by the use of a capital asset;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the payment of remuneration and expenses to or on
    behalf of a person for their services as a financial agent or in any
    other capacity;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} securing a meeting space or the supply of light
    refreshments at meetings;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any product or service provided by a government, a
    Crown corporation or any other public agency; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the conduct of surveys or research during a
    leadership contest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[cost
  incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[cost
  incurred]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an expense that is incurred by a
  leadership contestant, whether it is paid or unpaid.

::: HistoricalNote

related to an application to a judge made under this Part, including an

application.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence of payment --- \$50 or more

- **[[380]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-380 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an expense of \$50 or more was incurred under this Act by or on behalf
  of a registered party, a registered association, a nomination

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an expense of less than \$50 was incurred and paid

  was paid.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Petty expenses

- **[[381]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-381 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person may pay a petty expense incurred for office supplies, postage,
  courier services and other incidental expenses under the written
  authorization of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a registered agent of a registered party, as an
    expense incurred on behalf of the registered party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an electoral district agent of a registered
    association, as an expense incurred on behalf of the association;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the financial agent of a nomination contestant, as
    a nomination campaign expense;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the official agent of a candidate, as an electoral

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a leadership campaign agent of a leadership
    contestant, as a leadership campaign expense.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorized maximum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The written authorization referred to in

  expenses that the person is authorized to pay.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement and evidence of payment

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who is authorized to pay a petty expense
  shall provide the agent who authorized it with a statement of payments
  that the person made and the documentation referred to in section 380
  within three months after

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a petty expense incurred on behalf
    of a registered party, the day on which it is incurred;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a petty expense incurred on behalf

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person who is authorized to pay petty expenses

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of electoral campaign returns
and election expenses returns

- **[[382]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-382 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall, in the manner that he or she considers
  appropriate, publish the original election expenses returns of
  registered parties and electoral campaign returns of candidates and
  any corrected or revised versions of those returns

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an original return, within one year
    after the issue of a writ for an election;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a corrected or revised version of a
    return, as soon as feasible after he or she receives it; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a document referred to in subsection
    477.59(10), (11), (12) or (15), or a corrected or revised version of
    such a document, as soon as feasible after he or she receives it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of financial transactions
  returns

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall publish the
  following, as soon as feasible after receiving them, in the manner
  that he or she considers appropriate:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the financial transactions returns of registered
    parties and registered associations, and any corrected or revised
    versions of those returns;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the nomination campaign returns of nomination
    contestants, any document referred to in subsection 476.75(10),
    (11), (12) or (15), and any corrected or revised versions of those
    returns or documents; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the leadership campaign returns of leadership
    contestants, any document referred to in subsection 478.8(10),
    (11), (12) or (15), any corrected or revised versions of those
    returns or documents, the returns in respect of contributions
    required under section 478.81, and any statements containing
    information with respect to contributions referred to in paragraph
    478.3(2)(d).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Summary of return on candidates'
  election expenses

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} As soon as feasible after receiving an electoral
  campaign return, any document referred to in subsection 477.59(10),
  (11), (12) or (15) or any corrected or revised version of those
  returns or documents for each candidate in an electoral district, the
  Chief Electoral Officer shall, in the manner that he or she considers
  appropriate, publish a summary report that includes the maximum
  election expenses allowed for the electoral district and, for each
  candidate,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the total election expenses;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} the total litigation expenses;

  - [(a.2)]{.lawlabel} the total travel and living expenses that are
    related to travel and sojourns during the election period;

  - [(a.3)]{.lawlabel} the total accessibility expenses;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the total personal expenses;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number of contributors and the total amount of
    contributions received;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name of the official agent;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the name of the auditor; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, an indication that the auditor's
    report on a return was qualified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of return of deregistered
  parties

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} As soon as feasible after receiving a financial
  transactions return under subparagraph 420(a)(i) from a deregistered
  political party, the Chief Electoral Officer shall publish it in the
  manner that he or she considers appropriate.

#### [Inflation Adjustment Factor]{.HTitleText3} {#h-207202 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inflation adjustment factor

**[[384]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384 .sectionLabel}** Before April 1 in each
year, the Chief Electoral Officer shall cause to be published in the
[Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) an inflation adjustment
factor that is in effect for a period of one year beginning on that
date. It shall be a fraction with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a numerator that is the annual average Consumer Price
  Index, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the
  [Statistics Act](/eng/acts/S-19), for the calendar year immediately
  before that date, calculated on the basis of 1992 being equal to 100;
  and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a denominator that is 108.6, which is the annual
  average Consumer Price Index, as published by Statistics Canada under
  the authority of the [Statistics Act](/eng/acts/S-19), for 1998,
  calculated on the basis of 1992 being equal to 100.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 384
- 2004, c. 24, s. 15
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::
