### [DIVISION 1.1]{.HLabel2}[Regulated Fundraising Events]{.HTitleText2} {#h-207209 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-207210 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[regulated fundraising
event]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

- **[[384.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this Division, [[regulated
  fundraising event]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an event

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that is organized for the financial benefit of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a registered party that is represented in the
      House of Commons on the day the event occurs or, if Parliament is
      dissolved, on the date of dissolution, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a registered association, nomination contestant,
      candidate or leadership contestant of a registered party described
      in subparagraph (i); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is attended by

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a leader, interim leader or leadership contestant
      of the registered party for whose financial benefit the event is
      organized or the registered party described in subparagraph
      (a)(ii), or a minister of the Crown or minister of state who is a
      member of the registered party for whose financial benefit the
      event is organized or the registered party described in that
      subparagraph, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} at least one person who, in order to attend it,
      is required

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} to have made a contribution or contributions of
        a total amount of more than \$200 to the registered party or any
        of its registered associations, nomination contestants,
        candidates or leadership contestants, or to any combination of
        them, or to be the guest of a person who has made such a
        contribution or contributions, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} to have paid more than \$200, the amount
        including a contribution to the registered party or any of its
        registered associations, nomination contestants, candidates or
        leadership contestants, or to any combination of them, or to be
        the guest of a person who has made such a payment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- conventions and
  leadership contestant debates

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a regulated fundraising event
  does not include a convention, including a leadership convention, of a
  registered party referred to in subparagraph (1)(a)(i), or a
  leadership contestants' debate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inclusion --- fundraising events that
  are part of conventions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), a regulated fundraising event
  includes an event that is part of a convention referred to in that
  subsection if the event is attended by at least one person who, in
  order to attend it, is required

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to make a contribution or contributions --- in
    addition to any amount that they were required to pay to attend the
    convention --- of a total amount of more than \$200 to the
    registered party or any of its registered associations, nomination
    contestants, candidates or leadership contestants, or to any
    combination of them, or to be the guest of a person who has made
    such a contribution or contributions; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to pay more than \$200 --- in addition to any
    amount that they were required to pay to attend the convention ---
    to attend the event, the amount including a contribution to the
    registered party or any of its registered associations, nomination
    contestants, candidates or leadership contestants, or to any
    combination of them, or to be the guest of a person who has made
    such a payment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion --- contributor appreciation
  events

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (3), a regulated fundraising event
  does not include any event that is part of a convention referred to in
  subsection (2) and that is organized to express appreciation for
  persons who have made a contribution to the registered party or any of
  its registered associations, nomination contestants, candidates or
  leadership contestants.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2004, c. 24, s. 16
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-384.1-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 384.1"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Publication and Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-207232 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulated fundraising event organized by
registered party

- **[[384.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a registered party organizes all
  or part of a regulated fundraising event for its own financial benefit
  or for the financial benefit of one of its registered associations,
  nomination contestants, candidates or leadership contestants, the
  registered party shall publish the information set out in
  subsection (2) in a prominent location on its Internet site for the
  period beginning five days before the day the regulated fundraising
  event takes place and ending at the time the event starts.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The information to be published under subsection (1)
  and provided under subsection (3) is the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date, time and location of the regulated
    fundraising event;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of each entity or person referred to in
    paragraph 384.1(1)(a) for whose financial benefit the event is
    organized;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name of each person referred to in subparagraph
    384.1(1)(b)(i) who will be attending the event;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the total amount of contributions that a person
    will be required to have made, or the amount that they will be
    required to have paid, in order to attend the event; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the contact information of an individual who may be
    contacted and from whom further information about the event may be
    obtained.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulated fundraising event not
  organized by registered party

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a regulated fundraising event is organized
  entirely by one or more persons or entities other than the registered
  party for whose financial benefit the event is organized, or for the
  financial benefit of whose registered association, nomination
  contestant, candidate or leadership contestant the event is organized,
  each person or entity that organizes the event or any part of it shall
  provide the information set out in subsection (2) to the registered
  party in time for the registered party to be able to publish the
  information as required under subsection (4).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered party to publish information

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If at least one person or entity referred to in
  subsection (3) complies with the obligation under that subsection ---
  to provide information to the registered party in time for the
  registered party to be able to publish it --- the registered party
  shall publish that information in a prominent location on its Internet
  site for the period beginning five days before the day the regulated
  fundraising event takes place and ending at the time the event starts.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered party to notify Chief
  Electoral Officer

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} If a registered party is required to publish
  information under subsection (1) or (4), it shall also notify the
  Chief Electoral Officer of the regulated fundraising event no later
  than five days before the day the event takes place.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Updating published information

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a registered party referred to in subsection (1)
  or (4) becomes aware, after publishing information under this section,
  of any change to that information, the registered party shall replace
  the old information on its Internet site with the new information as
  soon as feasible after becoming aware of the change.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Updating information provided

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a person or entity referred to in subsection (3)
  becomes aware, after providing information to a registered party under
  this section, of any change to that information, the person or entity
  shall provide the new information to the registered party as soon as
  feasible after becoming aware of the change.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Updating published information

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If new information is provided to a registered party
  under subsection (6), the registered party shall replace the old
  information on its Internet site with the new information as soon as
  feasible after being provided with it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- election period

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1) to (7) do not apply in respect of a
  regulated fundraising event that takes place during the election
  period of a general election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report on regulated fundraising event
organized by registered party

- **[[384.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a registered party organizes all
  or part of a regulated fundraising event for its own financial benefit
  or for the financial benefit of one of its registered associations,
  nomination contestants, candidates or leadership contestants, the
  registered party's chief agent shall provide the Chief Electoral
  Officer with a report, in the prescribed form, on the regulated
  fundraising event.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of report

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), the report referred to in
  subsection (1) shall set out the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date, time and location of the regulated
    fundraising event;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of each entity or person referred to in
    paragraph 384.1(1)(a) for whose financial benefit the event was
    organized;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name of each person referred to in subparagraph
    384.1(1)(b)(i) who attended the event;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name of each person --- other than any person
    referred to in paragraph (c) --- who attended the event, along with
    the name of their municipality or its equivalent, their province and
    their postal code;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the total amount of contributions that a person was
    required to have made, or the amount that they were required to have
    paid, in order to attend the event; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the name of each person or entity that organized
    the event or any part of it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information not to be included in
  report

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The registered party's chief agent shall not include
  in the report referred to in subsection (1) the name of any of the
  following persons who attended the regulated fundraising event, nor
  the name of their municipality or its equivalent, their province or
  their postal code:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any person who was under 18 years of age on the day
    on which the event took place;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} any person who attended the event solely to
    assist a person with a disability;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any person who attended the event solely because
    they were employed in the organization of the event;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any of the following persons who attended the event
    solely in the course of their employment:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an employee or other representative of any media
      organization, as well as any freelance journalist, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a member of the support staff, including
      security staff, of any person referred to in subparagraph
      384.1(1)(b)(i) who attended the event; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any person who attended the event solely in order
    to provide volunteer labour.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulated fundraising event not
  organized by registered party

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a regulated fundraising event is organized
  entirely by one or more persons or entities other than the registered
  party for whose financial benefit the event is organized, or for the
  financial benefit of whose registered association, nomination
  contestant, candidate or leadership contestant the event is organized,
  each person or entity that organizes the event or any part of it
  shall, subject to subsection (5), provide the information set out in
  subsection (2) to the registered party in time for the registered
  party's chief agent to be able to provide the Chief Electoral Officer
  with a report on the event as required under subsection (6).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Updating information provided

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} If a person or entity referred to in subsection (4)
  becomes aware, after providing information to a registered party under
  that subsection or this subsection, of any change to that information,
  the person or entity shall provide the new information to the
  registered party as soon as feasible after becoming aware of the
  change.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information not to be provided

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity referred to in subsection (4) or
  (4.1) shall include in the information provided to the registered
  party under that subsection the name of any person referred to in
  paragraphs (3)(a) to (d) who attended the regulated fundraising event,
  nor the name of their municipality or its equivalent, their province
  or their postal code.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report on regulated fundraising event

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If at least one person or entity referred to in
  subsection (4) complies with the obligation under that subsection ---
  to provide information to the registered party in time for the
  registered party's chief agent to be able to provide the Chief
  Electoral Officer with the report --- that chief agent shall provide
  the Chief Electoral Officer with a report, in the prescribed form, on
  the regulated fundraising event setting out that information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Period for providing report

  [(6.1)]{.lawlabel} The registered party's chief agent shall provide
  the Chief Electoral Officer with the reports referred to in
  subsections (1) and (6) within 30 days after the day the regulated
  fundraising event takes place.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- election period

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1) to (6.1) do not apply in respect of a
  regulated fundraising event that takes place during the election
  period of a general election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election period

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} A registered party's chief agent shall provide the
  Chief Electoral Officer with a single report, in the prescribed form,
  on all the regulated fundraising events that were held during the
  election period for a general election and

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all or part of which were organized by the
    registered party for its own financial benefit or for the financial
    benefit of one of its registered associations, nomination
    contestants, candidates or leadership contestants; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in respect of which at least one person or entity
    that organized the event or any part of it complied with the
    obligation under subsection (9).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Period for providing report

  [(8.1)]{.lawlabel} The registered party's chief agent shall provide
  the Chief Electoral Officer with the report referred to in
  subsection (8) within 60 days after polling day at the general
  election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulated fundraising event not
  organized by registered party

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} If a regulated fundraising event that was held during
  the election period for a general election was organized entirely by
  one or more persons or entities other than the registered party for
  whose financial benefit the event was organized, or for the financial
  benefit of whose registered association, nomination contestant,
  candidate or leadership contestant the event was organized, each
  person or entity that organized the event or any part of it shall,
  subject to subsection (10), provide the information set out in
  subsection (2) to the registered party in time for the registered
  party's chief agent to be able to provide the Chief Electoral Officer
  with the report as required under subsection (8).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Updating information provided

  [(9.1)]{.lawlabel} If a person or entity referred to in subsection (9)
  becomes aware, after providing information to a registered party under
  that subsection or this subsection, of any change to that information,
  the person or entity shall provide the new information to the
  registered party as soon as feasible after becoming aware of the
  change.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information not to be provided

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} No person or entity referred to in subsection (9) or
  (9.1) shall include in the information provided to the registered
  party under that subsection the name of any person referred to in
  paragraphs (3)(a) to (d) who attended the regulated fundraising event,
  nor the name of their municipality or its equivalent, their province
  or their postal code.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of report

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (12), the report referred to
  in subsection (8) shall set out the information referred to in
  subsection (2) for each regulated fundraising event referred to in
  subsection (8).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information not to be included in
  report

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} The registered party's chief agent shall not include
  in the report referred to in subsection (8), in respect of a given
  regulated fundraising event, the name of any person referred to in
  paragraphs (3)(a) to (d) who attended that event, nor the name of
  their municipality or its equivalent, their province or their postal
  code.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of reports

  [(13)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall publish reports
  provided under subsections (1), (6) and (8), and any corrected or
  revised versions of those reports, as soon as feasible after receiving
  them, in the manner that he or she considers appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

#### [Contributions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-207311 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return of contributions

**[[384.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.4 .sectionLabel}** If a registered
party, a registered association, a nomination contestant, a candidate or
a leadership contestant receives a contribution in respect of a
regulated fundraising event in respect of which section 384.2 or 384.3
is not complied with, the chief agent of the registered party, the
financial agent of the registered association, the official agent of the
candidate or the financial agent of the nomination contestant or
leadership contestant, as the case may be, shall, within 30 days after
becoming aware of the non-compliance, return the contribution unused to
the contributor or, if that is not possible, pay the amount of it ---
or, in the case of a non-monetary contribution, an amount of money equal
to its commercial value --- to the Chief Electoral Officer, who shall
forward that amount to the Receiver General.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

#### [Corrections, Revisions and Extended Reporting Periods]{.HTitleText3} {#h-207316 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minor corrections --- Chief Electoral
Officer

**[[384.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.5 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may correct a report referred to in subsection 384.3(1), (6) or
(8) if the correction does not materially affect its substance.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extensions --- Chief Electoral Officer

- **[[384.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.6
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the
  written application of a registered party's chief agent or, if the
  chief agent is absent or unable to perform their duties, its leader,
  shall authorize the extension of the period referred to in subsection
  384.3(6.1) or (8.1) unless he or she is satisfied that the chief
  agent's failure to provide the report was deliberate or was the result
  of the chief agent's failure to exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application may be made within the period
  referred to in subsection 384.3(6.1) or (8.1) or within two weeks
  after the end of that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corrections or revisions --- Chief
Electoral Officer

- **[[384.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.7
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the
  written application of a registered party's chief agent or, if the
  chief agent is absent or unable to perform their duties, its leader,
  shall authorize the correction or revision of a report referred to in
  subsection 384.3(1), (6) or (8) if he or she is satisfied by the
  evidence submitted by the applicant that the correction or revision is
  necessary in order for the requirements of this Act to be complied
  with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application made without delay

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall be made immediately after the
  applicant becomes aware of the need for correction or revision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline for corrections or revisions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The applicant shall provide the Chief Electoral
  Officer with the corrected or revised version of the report within 30
  days after the day on which the correction or revision is authorized
  or within any extension of that period authorized under subsection (4)
  or (5).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New deadline

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written
  application of the applicant made within two weeks after the end of
  the 30-day period referred to in subsection (3), shall authorize the
  extension of that period, unless he or she is satisfied that the
  applicant's failure to provide the corrected or revised version of the
  report was deliberate or was the result of the applicant's failure to
  exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension of new deadline

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written
  application of the applicant made within two weeks after the end of an
  extension authorized under subsection (4) or under this subsection,
  shall authorize the further extension of that period, unless he or she
  is satisfied that the applicant's failure to provide the corrected or
  revised version of the report was deliberate or was the result of the
  applicant's failure to exercise due diligence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extensions, corrections or revisions ---
judge

- **[[384.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-384.8
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The chief agent of a registered
  party or, if the chief agent is absent or unable to perform their
  duties, its leader, may apply to a judge for an order

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} authorizing an extension referred to in subsection
    384.6(1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} authorizing a correction or revision referred to in
    subsection 384.7(1).

  The applicant shall notify the Chief Electoral Officer that the
  application has been made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application may be made

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (1)(a), within two weeks after, as
    the case may be,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if an application for an extension is not made to
      the Chief Electoral Officer within the period referred to in
      subsection 384.6(2), the end of the two-week period referred to in
      that subsection,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the rejection of an application for an extension
      made in accordance with section 384.6, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the end of the extended period referred to in
      subsection 384.6(1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (1)(b), within two weeks after the
    rejection of an application for a correction or revision made in
    accordance with section 384.7.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Grounds --- extension

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall grant an order authorizing an
  extension unless the judge is satisfied that the chief agent's failure
  to provide the required report was deliberate or was the result of the
  chief agent's failure to exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Grounds --- corrections or revisions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall grant an order authorizing a
  correction or revision if the judge is satisfied by the evidence
  submitted by the applicant that the correction or revision is
  necessary in order for the requirements of this Act to be complied
  with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of order

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The order may require that the applicant satisfy any
  condition that the judge considers necessary for carrying out the
  purposes of this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 20, s. 2
:::

### [DIVISION 2]{.HLabel2}[Political Parties]{.HTitleText2} {#h-207362 .Subheading}

#### [SUBDIVISION A]{.HLabel3}[Registration of Political Parties]{.HTitleText3} {#h-207363 .Subheading}

##### [Application for Registration]{.HTitleText4} {#h-207364 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for registration

- **[[385]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-385 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  leader of a political party may apply to the Chief Electoral Officer
  for the political party to become a registered party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application for registration shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the political party's full name;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the party's short-form name, or its abbreviation,
    if any, that is to be shown in election documents;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the party's logo, if any;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the party's leader and a
    copy of the party's resolution to appoint the leader, certified by
    the leader and another officer of the party;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the address of the party's office where records are
    maintained and to which communications may be addressed;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the names and addresses of the party's officers and
    their signed consent to act in that capacity;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the party's auditor and
    their signed consent to act in that capacity;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the party's chief agent and
    their signed consent to act in that capacity;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the names and addresses of 250 electors and their
    declarations in the prescribed form that they are members of the
    party and support the party's application for registration;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the leader's declaration in the prescribed form
    that, having considered all of the factors --- including those
    described in subsection 521.1(5) --- relevant to determining the
    party's purposes, one of the party's fundamental purposes is to
    participate in public affairs by endorsing one or more of its
    members as candidates and supporting their election;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the party's policy for the protection of personal
    information, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a statement indicating the types of personal
      information that the party collects and how it collects that
      information,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a statement indicating how the party protects
      personal information under its control,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a statement indicating how the party uses
      personal information under its control and under what
      circumstances that personal information may be sold to any person
      or entity,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a statement indicating the training concerning
      the collection and use of personal information to be given to any
      employee of the party who could have access to personal
      information under the party's control,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a statement indicating the party's practices
      concerning

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the collection and use of personal information
        created from online activity, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} its use of cookies, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of a person to
      whom concerns regarding the party's policy for the protection of
      personal information can be addressed; and

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the address of the page --- accessible to the
    public --- on the party's Internet site where its policy for the
    protection of personal information is published under subsection
    (4).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Short-form name

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may establish a maximum
  length for a political party's short-form name that is to be shown in
  election documents.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} To confirm that the purpose referred to in paragraph
  (2)(j) is one of the party's fundamental purposes, the Chief Electoral
  Officer may ask the party's leader to provide any relevant
  information, including information about the factors described in
  subsection 521.1(5).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of policy for the
  protection of personal information

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A political party shall publish on its Internet site
  its policy for the protection of personal information referred to in
  paragraph (2)(k) before its leader applies under this section for the
  party to become a registered party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 385
- 2003, c. 19, s. 13
- 2004, c. 24, s. 16
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 254](#1042984-1121049){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042984-1121049.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-385-20190401.html "Link to previous version of section 385"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policy for the protection of personal
information --- parties already registered, etc.

- **[[385.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-385.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Within three months after the day on
  which this section comes into force, the leader of a political party
  shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with the party's policy for
  the protection of personal information referred to in paragraph
  385(2)(k) and the Internet address referred to in paragraph 385(2)(l),
  if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} before the day on which this section comes into
    force, the leader of the party has applied under section 385 for the
    party to become a registered party but, as of that day, the Chief
    Electoral Officer has not yet informed the leader under subsection
    389(1) whether or not the party is eligible for registration under
    section 387; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on the day on which this section comes into force,
    the party is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an eligible party, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a registered party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to comply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the leader of the political party does not comply
  with subsection (1), then

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a party referred to in paragraph
    (1)(a), the party is not eligible for registration under section
    387;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a party referred to in subparagraph
    (1)(b)(i), the party may not become a registered party under section
    390; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a party referred to in subparagraph
    (1)(b)(ii), the Chief Electoral Officer shall implement the
    procedure for non-voluntary deregistration set out in sections 415,
    416 and 418.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed inclusion in application for
  registration

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the leader of a political party provides the Chief
  Electoral Officer with the policy and the address referred to in
  subsection (1) in compliance with that subsection, or in compliance
  with section 415, then the policy and the address are deemed, as of
  the day on which they are provided, to be included in the application
  for registration referred to in subsection 385(2) in respect of the
  party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2004, c. 24, s. 16
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 255](#1042991-1121066){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042991-1121066.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-385.1-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 385.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of [[personal
information]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}

- **[[385.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-385.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite the definition [[personal
  information]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in subsection 2(1), for the
  purposes of this section, [[personal information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
  means information about an identifiable individual.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Collection, use, disclosure, retention
  and disposal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In order to participate in public affairs by
  endorsing one or more of its members as candidates and supporting
  their election, any registered party or eligible party, as well as any
  person or organization acting on the party's behalf, including the
  party's candidates, electoral district associations, officers, agents,
  employees, volunteers and representatives, may, subject to this Act
  and any other applicable federal Act, collect, use, disclose, retain
  and dispose of personal information in accordance with the party's
  privacy policy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Purpose

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The purpose of this section is to provide for a
  national, uniform, exclusive and complete regime applicable to
  registered parties and eligible parties respecting their collection,
  use, disclosure, retention and disposal of personal information.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2004, c. 24, s. 16
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2023, c. 26, s. 680](#1411426-1415564){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1411426-1415564.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-385.2-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 385.2"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Withdrawal of application

**[[386]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-386 .sectionLabel}** A leader who has made
an application under subsection 385(1) may withdraw it at any time
before registration by sending a signed request to that effect to the
Chief Electoral Officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 386
- 2003, c. 19, s. 14
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-386-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 386"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligibility for registration

**[[387]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-387 .sectionLabel}** A political party whose
leader has made an application under subsection 385(1) becomes eligible
for registration if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} its name, short-form name, abbreviation or logo does
  not

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} so resemble the name, short-form name, abbreviation
    or logo of a registered party or an eligible party that it would, in
    the Chief Electoral Officer's opinion, likely be confused with it,
    or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} include the word "independent" or a word that so
    resembles "independent" that it would, in the Chief Electoral
    Officer's opinion, likely be confused with it;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the party has at least three officers in addition to
  its leader and has appointed a chief agent and an auditor; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the Chief Electoral Officer is satisfied that the
  party has provided the information required under subsection 385(2)
  and that the information is accurate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 387
- 2003, c. 19, s. 15
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-387-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 387"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Preservation of name

**[[388]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-388 .sectionLabel}** In the period of 30
days after the deregistration of a political party,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} no application for another political party to become
  a registered party shall be accepted --- and no report under section
  405 is effective --- if the application or report would permit another
  political party to use a name, short-form name, abbreviation or logo
  that would, in the Chief Electoral Officer's opinion, likely be
  confused with that of the deregistered party; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if a new application is made for the registration of
  the deregistered party under the name, short-form name, abbreviation
  or logo that it had at the time of its deregistration, the Chief
  Electoral Officer shall not refuse the application on the ground that
  it does not comply with subparagraph 387(a)(i).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 388
- 2003, c. 19, s. 16
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-388-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 388"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of eligibility

- **[[389]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-389 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall, as soon as feasible after the day on
  which the application is received, inform the leader of a political
  party who has applied for the party to become registered whether or
  not the party is eligible for registration under section 387. If the
  party is not eligible, the Chief Electoral Officer shall also indicate
  which of that section's requirements have not been met.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loss of eligibility

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A political party whose leader has been informed
  under subsection (1) that it is eligible loses its eligibility if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it contravenes any of section 391, subsection
    395(1), sections 399 to 402, subsections 405(1), (3) and (4) and
    406(1) and section 407;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} one of its officers is not eligible under
    subsection 395(2) and the party has not complied with subsections
    395(3) and (4);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} its chief agent is not eligible under section 397
    and the party has not complied with section 400; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} its auditor is not eligible under section 398 and
    the party has not complied with section 400.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 389
- 2003, c. 19, s. 17
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

Version](section-389-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 389"){.PITLink}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration

- **[[390]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-390 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  eligible party becomes a registered party if it has at least one
  candidate whose nomination has been confirmed for an election and its
  application to become registered was made at least 60 days before the
  issue of the writ or writs and has not been withdrawn.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Late application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An eligible party whose application was made after
  the 60 days referred to in subsection (1) becomes a registered party
  for the next general election --- or any by-election that precedes it
  --- if it satisfies the requirements of that subsection for that
  election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, as soon as
  feasible after the end of the 48-hour period following the close of
  nominations,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} inform the leader of an eligible party that meets
    the requirements of subsection (1) that the party has been
    registered; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a general election, inform the
    leader of an eligible party that does not meet the requirements of
    subsection (1) that the party has not been registered.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loss of eligibility

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An eligible party, other than one referred to in
  subsection (2), loses its eligibility on being informed under
  paragraph (3)(b) that it has not been registered.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligible party deemed registered

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of sections 363, 367, 376, 430, 437
  and 444, an eligible party that becomes a registered party under
  subsection (1) is deemed to have been registered from the day of the
  issue of the writ or writs.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligible party deemed registered

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of section 429.1 and --- despite
  subsection (5) --- sections 363 and 367, an eligible party that
  becomes a registered party under subsection (1) is deemed to have been
  registered from the first day of the pre-election period --- if any
  --- before the election period of the election referred to in that
  subsection.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 390
- 2003, c. 19, s. 19
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 256](#1042993-1133399){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042993-1133399.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-390-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 390"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report on agents of eligible parties

**[[391]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-391 .sectionLabel}** An eligible party
shall, within 30 days after being informed under subsection 389(1) that
it is eligible, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a written
report, certified by its leader or chief agent, containing the name and
address of any person appointed as its registered agent and any terms
and conditions to which the appointment is subject. The Chief Electoral
Officer shall, on the registration of the eligible party, register that
information in the registry of political parties.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 391
- 2003, c. 19, s. 19
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-391-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 391"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of assets and liabilities

**[[392]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-392 .sectionLabel}** Within six months after
becoming a registered party, the registered party shall provide the
Chief Electoral Officer with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a statement, prepared in accordance with generally
  accepted accounting principles, of its assets and liabilities,
  including any surplus or deficit, as of the day before the effective
  date of the registration;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report on that statement made by the registered
  party's auditor to its chief agent that contains the auditor's opinion
  as to whether that statement presents fairly and in accordance with
  generally accepted accounting principles the information on which it
  is based; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a declaration in the prescribed form by the
  registered party's chief agent that the statement is complete and
  accurate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 392
- 2003, c. 19, s. 20
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-392-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 392"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Annual fiscal period

- **[[393]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-393 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  fiscal period of a registered party is the calendar year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjustment of fiscal period

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without delay after becoming registered, a political
  party shall, if necessary, adjust its fiscal period so that it ends at
  the end of the calendar year. The adjusted fiscal period shall not be
  less than six months or more than 18 months.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 393
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-393-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 393"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registry of political parties

**[[394]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-394 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall maintain a registry of political parties that contains the
information referred to in paragraphs 385(2)(a) to (h), (k) and (l) and
subsections 396(2) and 418(2).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 394
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 257](#1042995-1121069){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1042995-1121069.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-394-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 394"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Officers, Registered Agents, Auditors and Members]{.HTitleText4} {#h-207455 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum number of officers

- **[[395]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-395
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), a
  registered party and an eligible party shall have at least three
  officers in addition to the leader of the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligibility --- officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Only a person who is an elector and whose ordinary
  residence is in Canada is eligible to be an officer of a registered
  party or an eligible party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of replacement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the event of the death, incapacity, resignation or
  ineligibility of an officer of a registered party or eligible party,
  or the revocation of the appointment of one, the party shall, if the
  remaining number of officers is less than four, appoint a replacement
  within 30 days.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of appointment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Within 30 days after the day on which the replacement
  is appointed, the registered party or eligible party shall inform the
  Chief Electoral Officer of the appointment by providing a report under
  subsection 405(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 395
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-395-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 395"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered agents

- **[[396]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-396 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  registered party may appoint persons to act as its registered agents,
  subject to any terms and conditions that the appointment specifies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of appointment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Within 30 days after the day on which a registered
  agent is appointed, the registered party shall provide the Chief
  Electoral Officer with a written report, certified by its leader or
  chief agent, that includes the registered agent's name and address and
  any terms and conditions to which the appointment is subject. The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall register that information in the
  registry of political parties.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 396
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-396-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 396"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Agents --- corporations

- **[[397]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-397 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  corporation incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province is
  eligible to be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a chief agent or a registered agent of a registered
    party; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a chief agent or an agent of an eligible party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Agents --- ineligibility

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following persons are ineligible to be a chief
  agent, a registered agent or an agent:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an election officer or a member of the staff of a
    returning officer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a candidate;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an auditor appointed as required by this Act;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (1), a person who is not an
    elector;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an undischarged bankrupt; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who does not have full capacity to enter
    into contracts in the province in which the person ordinarily
    resides.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 397
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-397-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 397"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor --- eligibility

- **[[398]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-398 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Only
  the following are eligible to be an auditor for a registered party or
  an eligible party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person who is a member in good standing of a
    corporation, association or institute of professional accountants;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a partnership of which every partner is a member in
    good standing of a corporation, association or institute of
    professional accountants.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor --- ineligibility

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following persons are ineligible to be an
  auditor:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an election officer or a member of the staff of a
    returning officer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a candidate or their official agent;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an officer of a registered party or an eligible
    party;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a chief agent of a registered party or an eligible
    party;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a registered agent of a registered party;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} an electoral district agent of a registered
    association;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a nomination contestant or their financial agent;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a leadership contestant or their leadership
    campaign agent; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a financial agent of a registered third party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 398
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-398-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 398"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consent

**[[399]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-399 .sectionLabel}** A registered party and
an eligible party shall obtain from its officers, chief agent and
auditor, on appointment, their signed consent to act in that capacity.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 399
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-399-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 399"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Replacement of chief agent or auditor

- **[[400]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-400 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  the event of the death, incapacity, resignation or ineligibility of
  its chief agent or auditor, or the revocation of the appointment of
  one, a registered party or eligible party shall without delay appoint
  a replacement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of appointment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Within 30 days after the day on which the replacement
  is appointed, the registered party or eligible party shall inform the
  Chief Electoral Officer of the appointment by providing a report under
  subsection 405(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 400
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-400-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 400"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Only one chief agent and auditor

**[[401]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-401 .sectionLabel}** A registered party or
eligible party shall have no more than one chief agent and one auditor
at a time.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 401
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-401-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 401"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum number of members

**[[402]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-402 .sectionLabel}** A registered party and
an eligible party shall have at least 250 members who are electors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 402
- 2003, c. 19, s. 22
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-402-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 402"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- officer

- **[[403]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-403 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person who is ineligible to be an officer of a registered party or an
  eligible party shall act in that capacity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- agent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person who is ineligible to be a chief agent or
  registered agent of a registered party or an eligible party shall act
  in that capacity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- auditor

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person who is ineligible to be an auditor of a
  registered party or an eligible party shall act in that capacity.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 403
- 2001, c. 21, s. 21
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-403-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 403"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- fundamental purpose

- **[[404]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-404
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall act or continue to act as an officer of a registered party or an
  eligible party if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} they know that the party does not have as one of
    its fundamental purposes participating in public affairs by
    endorsing one or more of its members as candidates and supporting
    their election; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the party has not made an application for
    deregistration under section 414.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person referred to in subsection (1) may sign an
  application for deregistration under section 414.

::: HistoricalNote

##### [Changes in Information Concerning Parties]{.HTitleText4} {#h-207591 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Changes in information

- **[[405]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-405
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Within 30 days after the day on
  which there is a change in the information in respect of a registered
  party or an eligible party in the registry of political parties, the
  party shall report the change to the Chief Electoral Officer in
  writing. The report shall be certified by the leader of the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New name, abbreviation or logo

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The report of a change in the information referred to
  in paragraphs 385(2)(a) to (c) shall include a copy of the resolution
  of the party to make the change. If the changed information complies
  with subparagraph 387(a)(i) or (ii), the change is deemed to be
  effective as of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the day after polling day, in the case of a report
    made during an election period; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the day on which the report was made, in any other
    case.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New leader

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The report of a change of leader for a party shall
  include a copy of the resolution of the party to appoint the new
  leader, certified by the new leader and another officer of the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New officer, chief agent or auditor

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the report involves the replacement of an officer,
  the chief agent or the auditor, it shall include a copy of the signed
  consent referred to in section 399.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration of change

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall enter any change in
  the information referred to in this section in the registry of
  political parties.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entry in registry of electoral district
  associations

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall enter any change in
  the information referred to in subsection (2) in the registry of
  electoral district associations.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 405
- 2003, c. 19, s. 25
- 2006, c. 9, s. 46
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 80, 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-405-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 405"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of changes to policy for the
protection of personal information

**[[405.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-405.1 .sectionLabel}** As soon as feasible
after reporting a change in its policy for the protection of personal
information to the Chief Electoral Officer in writing under subsection
405(1), a registered party or an eligible party shall publish on its
Internet site the updated version of the policy, incorporating the
change set out in the report.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2003, c. 19, s. 25; 2006, c. 9, s. 47; 2014, c. 12, ss. 81,
  86](#1042999-1122675){.wb-lbx ajax-after="1042999-1122675.html"}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confirmation of information at general
election

- **[[406]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-406 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  registered party and an eligible party shall, not later than 10 days
  after the issue of the writs for a general election, provide the Chief
  Electoral Officer with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a statement certified by its leader confirming the
    validity of the information concerning the party in the registry of
    political parties; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if there is a change in that information, the
    report of the change made under subsection 405(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Endorsement of candidates

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A registered party and an eligible party shall
  include with the statement or report referred to in subsection (1) a
  statement certified by its chief agent that sets out the names of the
  person or persons who are authorized by the party to endorse
  prospective candidates at a general election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 406
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- 2015, c. 37, s. 6
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-406-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 406"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confirmation of registration yearly

- **[[407]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-407 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  or before June 30 of every year, a registered party and an eligible
  party shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a statement certified by its leader confirming the
    validity of the information concerning the party in the registry of
    political parties; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if there is a change in that information, the
    report of the change made under subsection 405(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confirmation of members

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On or before June 30 of every third year, beginning
  in 2016, a registered party and an eligible party shall provide the
  Chief Electoral Officer with the names and addresses of 250 electors
  and their declarations in the prescribed form that they are members of
  the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration of leader

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On or before June 30 of every year, a registered
  party and an eligible party shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer
  with a declaration in the prescribed form by the leader that, having
  considered all of the factors relevant to determining the party's
  purposes --- including those described in subsection 521.1(5) --- one
  of the party's fundamental purposes is as described in paragraph
  385(2)(j).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 407
- 2003, c. 19, s. 26
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-407-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 407"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- false or misleading
information (leader)

- **[[408]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-408 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  leader of a political party shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer
  with information under section 385 that the leader knows is false or
  misleading.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- false or misleading
  information (party)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No registered party and no eligible party shall
  provide the Chief Electoral Officer with information under any of
  sections 405 to 407 that it knows is false or misleading.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- certification by leader

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No leader of a registered party or of an eligible
  party shall certify, under any of sections 405 to 407, a report or
  statement that they know contains false or misleading information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- leader's declaration

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No leader of a political party shall make a
  declaration referred to in section 385, 405 or 407 that they know is
  false or misleading.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- false or misleading
  declaration

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person shall make a declaration referred to in
  paragraph 385(2)(i) or subsection 407(2) that they know is false or
  misleading.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 408
- 2003, c. 19, s. 27
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 259](#1043001-1133402){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043001-1133402.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-408-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 408"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Deregistration of Registered Parties]{.HTitleText4} {#h-207648 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration --- no candidates

**[[409]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-409 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall, effective on the expiry in a general election of the
period for the confirmation of nominations under subsection 71(1),
deregister a registered party that, at that time, has not endorsed a
candidate in that general election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 409
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-409-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 409"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[409.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-409.1 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2014,
c. 12, s. 86\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-409.1-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 409.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration --- officers or members

- **[[410]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-410 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Chief Electoral Officer is not satisfied that a registered party
  is in compliance with subsection 395(1) or section 402, he or she
  shall, in writing, notify the party that it is required to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} show its compliance with subsection 395(1) within
    60 days after the day on which the party receives the notice; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} show its compliance with section 402 within 90 days
    after the day on which the party receives the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Chief Electoral Officer is satisfied that the
  party has made reasonable efforts to comply with subsection 395(1) or
  section 402 within the time set out in the notice, he or she may, in
  writing, notify the party that it has another period of up to 60 or 90
  days, as the case may be, in which to comply.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall deregister a
  registered party if it fails to comply with a notice under
  subsection (1) or (2), as the case may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 410
- 2003, c. 19, s. 28
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-410-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 410"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of deregistration

**[[411]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-411 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer shall give notice of a deregistration under section 409 or 410
to the registered party and its chief agent and of the resulting
deregistration under section 417 to the registered associations and
their financial agents.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 411
- 2003, c. 19, s. 29
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-411-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 411"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration --- failure to provide
documents

- **[[412]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-412 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer may deregister a registered party if the party
  fails to provide

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any of the documents referred to in section 392;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report under subsection 396(2) concerning the
    appointment of a registered agent;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any of the documents referred to in subsection
    400(2) or 405(1) or (4) with respect to a replacement of its auditor
    or chief agent;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} either of the documents referred to in subsections
    405(1) and (3) with respect to a change of its leader;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a report in accordance with subsection 405(2) of a
    change in the registered information on its name, short-form name,
    abbreviation or logo mentioned in paragraphs 385(2)(a) to (c);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a report under subsection 405(1) concerning a
    change in any other registered information;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} confirmation under subsection 406(1) or section 407
    of the validity of the registered information;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a report that is required to be filed under
    subsection 476.1(1) by the registered party; or

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a statement that is required under subsection
    478.1(1) or (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration --- failure to publish
  updated policy for the protection of personal information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may deregister a
  registered party if the party fails to publish an updated version of
  its policy for the protection of personal information on its Internet
  site in accordance with section 405.1.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration --- failure to continue
  to have policy for the protection of personal information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may deregister a
  registered party if the party fails to continue to have a policy for
  the protection of personal information referred to in paragraph
  385(2)(k).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 412
- 2003, c. 19, s. 30
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 260](#1043005-1121100){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043005-1121100.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-412-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 412"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration --- failure to file return
and auditor's report

**[[413]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-413 .sectionLabel}** The Chief Electoral
Officer may deregister a registered party if its chief agent fails

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} to provide him or her with a document for a fiscal
  year in accordance with subsection 432(1); or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to provide him or her with a document for a general
  election in accordance with subsection 437(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 413
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-413-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 413"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voluntary deregistration

**[[414]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-414 .sectionLabel}** On application, other
than during the election period of a general election, by a registered
party to become deregistered, signed by the leader and any two officers
of the party, the Chief Electoral Officer may deregister the party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 414
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-414-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 414"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure for non-voluntary
deregistration

- **[[415]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-415 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Chief Electoral Officer believes on reasonable grounds that a
  registered party, its leader, its chief agent or one of its other
  officers has omitted to perform any obligation referred to in section
  412 or 413, the Chief Electoral Officer shall, in writing, notify the
  party and any of its officers who are named in the registry of
  political parties that the party or officer must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} rectify the omission by the discharge of that
    obligation,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} within 5 days after receipt of the notice, in the
      case of a failure to comply with subsection 406(1), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} within 30 days after receipt of the notice, in
      any other case; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} satisfy the Chief Electoral Officer that the
    omission was not the result of negligence or a lack of good faith.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension or exemption

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If paragraph (1)(b) applies, the Chief Electoral
  Officer may amend the notice by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} exempting, in whole or in part, the recipients of
    the notice from complying with the obligations referred to in
    section 412 or 413; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} specifying a period for compliance with the
    obligations referred to in subparagraph (1)(a)(i) or (ii), as the
    case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistration

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may deregister a
  registered party if its leader, its chief agent or one of its officers
  fails to comply with a notice referred to in subsection (1) or with a
  notice amended under subsection (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 415
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-415-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 415"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of deregistration

- **[[416]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-416 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Chief Electoral Officer proposes to deregister a registered party
  under section 414 or subsection 415(3), he or she shall, in writing,
  so notify the party and its registered associations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Date of deregistration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The notice shall specify the effective date of the
  deregistration, which shall be at least 15 days after the day on which
  the notice is sent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of service

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The notice shall be sent by registered mail or by a
  method of courier service that provides proof of mailing, a record
  while in transit and a record of delivery.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 416
- 2003, c. 19, s. 31
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-416-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 416"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of deregistration of registered
party

**[[417]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-417 .sectionLabel}** If a registered party
is deregistered, its registered associations are also deregistered.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 417
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-417-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 417"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of deregistration

- **[[418]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-418 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall without delay cause a notice of the
  deregistration of a registered party and of its registered
  associations to be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entry of deregistration in registry of
  political parties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall indicate the
  deregistration of the party in the registry of political parties.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 418
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-418-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 418"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuation of registered status for
limited purpose

**[[419]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-419 .sectionLabel}** A registered party that
is deregistered continues to have the obligations of a registered party
for the purpose of section 420.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 419
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-419-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 419"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Fiscal period and returns

**[[420]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-420 .sectionLabel}** The chief agent of a
deregistered political party shall, within six months after the day of
its deregistration, provide the Chief Electoral Officer with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the documents referred to in subsection 432(1) for

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the portion of its current fiscal period ending on
    the day of its deregistration, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any earlier fiscal period for which those
    documents have not already been provided under that subsection; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the documents referred to in subsection 437(1), for
  any general election for which those documents have not already been
  provided under that subsection.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 420
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-420-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 420"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Merger of Registered Parties]{.HTitleText4} {#h-207739 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for merger

- **[[421]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-421 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Two
  or more registered parties may, at any time other than during the
  period beginning 30 days before the issue of a writ for an election
  and ending on polling day, apply to the Chief Electoral Officer to
  become a merged registered party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An application to merge two or more registered
  parties shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be certified by the leaders of the merging parties;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} be accompanied by a resolution from each of the
    merging parties approving the proposed merger; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} contain the information required from a political
    party to become a registered party, except for the information
    referred to in paragraph 385(2)(i).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 421
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-421-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 421"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration for eligible merged parties

- **[[422]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-422 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Chief Electoral Officer shall amend the registry of political parties
  by replacing the names of the merging parties with the name of the
  merged party if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the application for the merger was not made in the
    period referred to in subsection 421(1); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} he or she is satisfied that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the merged party is eligible for registration
      under this Act, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the merging parties have discharged their
      obligations under this Act, including their obligations to report
      on their financial transactions and their election expenses and to
      maintain valid and up-to-date information concerning their
      registration.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall notify the officers
  of the merging parties in writing whether the registry of political
  parties is to be amended under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice in [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Chief Electoral Officer amends the registry of
  political parties, he or she shall cause to be published in the
  [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) a notice that the names of
  the merging parties have been replaced in the registry with the name
  of the merged party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 422
- 2003, c. 19, s. 32
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-422-20040101.html "Link to previous version of section 422"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of merger

- **[[423]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-423 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  merger of registered parties takes effect on the day on which the
  Chief Electoral Officer amends the registry of political parties under
  subsection 422(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consequences of merger

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the merger of two or more registered parties,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the merged party is the successor of each merging
    party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the merged party becomes a registered party;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the assets of each merging party are transferred to
    the merged party;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the merged party is responsible for the liabilities
    of each merging party;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the merged party is responsible for the obligations
    of each merging party to report on its financial transactions and
    election expenses for any period before the merger took effect;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the merged party replaces a merging party in any
    proceedings, whether civil, penal or administrative, by or against
    the merging party; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} any decision of a judicial or quasi-judicial nature
    involving a merging party may be enforced by or against the merged
    party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of merger on registered
  associations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On the merger of registered parties, any registered
  association of a merging party is deregistered and, despite paragraph
  447(c), may transfer goods or funds to the merged party or a
  registered association of the merged party in the six months
  immediately after the merger. Any such transfer is not a contribution
  for the purposes of this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 423
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

Version](section-423-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 423"){.PITLink}

c. 12, s. 86\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Returns

**[[424]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-424 .sectionLabel}** Within six months after
a merger

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} each of the merging parties shall provide the Chief
  Electoral Officer with the documents referred to in subsection 432(1)
  for

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the portion of its current fiscal period that ends
    on the day before the day on which the merger takes effect, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any earlier fiscal period for which those
    documents have not been provided; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the merged party shall provide the Chief Electoral
  Officer with

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a statement, prepared in accordance with generally
    accepted accounting principles, of its assets and liabilities,
    including any surplus or deficit, at the date of the merger,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a report on that statement made by the merged
    party's auditor to its chief agent that contains the auditor's
    opinion as to whether that statement presents fairly and in
    accordance with generally accepted accounting principles the
    information on which it was based, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a declaration in the prescribed form by the chief
    agent of the merged party that the statement is complete and
    accurate.

::: HistoricalNote

- 2003, c. 19, s. 34
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
