##### [Surplus of Electoral Funds]{.HTitleText4} {#h-209377 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Surplus of electoral funds

- **[[477.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.8
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The surplus amount of electoral
  funds that a candidate receives for an election is the amount by which
  the candidate's electoral revenues referred to in subsection (3) are
  more than the total of the candidate's electoral campaign expenses
  paid from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1) and the
  transfers referred to in subsection (4).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer or sale of capital assets

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before the surplus amount of electoral funds is
  disposed of in accordance with sections 477.81 and 477.82, a
  candidate's official agent shall either transfer any capital assets
  whose acquisition constitutes an electoral campaign expense within the
  meaning of subsection 375(1) to the registered party that has endorsed
  the candidate --- or to the registered association of that party in
  the candidate's electoral district --- or sell them at their fair
  market value.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electoral revenues

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The electoral revenues of a candidate include any
  amount that represents

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a monetary contribution made to the candidate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any of the following for which the candidate was
    reimbursed under this Act:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an election expense,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} travel and living expenses,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an accessibility expense,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a personal expense paid from the bank account
      referred to in subsection 477.46(1), and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a cost incurred in respect of a request or an
      application made under Part 14, if the cost was paid from the bank
      account referred to in subsection 477.46(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 305\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the resale value of the capital assets referred to
    in subsection (2); and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other amount that was received by the candidate
    for their electoral campaign and that is not repayable.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (3), for the purposes of this
  Act, none of the following is electoral revenue:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any amount used to pay for a candidate's litigation
    expenses that was not deposited into the bank account referred to in
    subsection 477.46(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any amount used to pay for a candidate's personal
    expenses that was not deposited into the bank account referred to in
    subsection 477.46(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any amount paid to the candidate under this Act as
    a reimbursement of personal expenses that were paid other than from
    the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1); and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any amount paid to the candidate under this Act as
    a reimbursement of a cost incurred in respect of a request or an
    application made under Part 14, if that cost was paid other than
    from the bank account referred to in subsection 477.46(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfers

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A transfer made by a candidate is a transfer of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any funds that the candidate transfers, during the
    election period, to a registered party or a registered association;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any amount of a reimbursement referred to in
    paragraph (3)(b) that the candidate transfers to that registered
    party; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any funds transferred by the candidate under
    paragraph 364(3)(d).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 305](#1043338-1133724){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043338-1133724.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-477.8-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 477.8"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of estimated surplus

- **[[477.81]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.81
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Chief Electoral Officer
  estimates that a candidate has a surplus of electoral funds, the Chief
  Electoral Officer shall issue a notice of the estimated amount of the
  surplus to the candidate's official agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposal of surplus funds

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The candidate's official agent shall dispose of a
  surplus of electoral funds within 60 days after the day on which they
  receive the notice of estimated surplus.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposal without notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a candidate has a surplus of electoral funds but
  their official agent has not received a notice of estimated surplus,
  the official agent shall dispose of the surplus within 60 days after,
  as the case may be,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the day on which they receive the final instalment
    of the reimbursement of the candidate's expenses; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the day on which the Chief Electoral Officer is
    provided with the candidate's electoral campaign return, if the
    candidate did not receive the reimbursement mentioned in paragraph
    (a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 306](#1043353-1133727){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043353-1133727.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-477.81-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 477.81"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Method of disposal of surplus

**[[477.82]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.82 .sectionLabel}** A candidate's
official agent shall dispose of surplus electoral funds by transferring
them

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a candidate who was endorsed by a
  registered party, to that party or to the registered association of
  that party in the candidate's electoral district; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, to the Receiver General.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of disposal of surplus

- **[[477.83]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.83
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A candidate's official agent shall,
  within seven days after disposing of a candidate's surplus electoral
  funds, give the Chief Electoral Officer a notice in the prescribed
  form of the amount and date of the disposal and to whom the surplus
  was transferred.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} As soon as feasible after the disposal of a
  candidate's surplus electoral funds, the Chief Electoral Officer shall
  publish the notice in any manner that he or she considers appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requisition for repayment

- **[[477.84]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.84
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An official agent who has disposed
  of a candidate's surplus electoral funds under paragraph 477.82(b) and
  must subsequently pay an electoral campaign expense of the candidate
  may apply to the Chief Electoral Officer for repayment in an amount
  that is not more than the lesser of the amount of the subsequent
  payment and the amount of the surplus electoral funds.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Repayment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of a request for payment from the Chief
  Electoral Officer in relation to an application, the Receiver General
  shall pay the amount specified in the application to the official
  agent out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Persons to whom this section applies

- **[[477.841]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.841
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies to any person
  who was a candidate at an election but who was not endorsed by a
  registered party and whose official agent disposed of the candidate's
  surplus electoral funds under paragraph 477.82(b).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for repayment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The official agent of a candidate who is a person
  referred to in subsection (1) may, for the purpose of the candidate's
  electoral campaign, apply to the Chief Electoral Officer for repayment
  of the amount of the surplus electoral funds referred to in that
  subsection if that candidate

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a candidate at the general election next
    following the election to which the funds relate but is not endorsed
    by a registered party and was not a candidate at any intervening
    by-election;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a candidate at one, and only one, intervening
    by-election and at that by-election is not endorsed by a registered
    party; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is a candidate at more than one intervening
    by-election and, at the first intervening by-election at which they
    are a candidate, is not endorsed by a registered party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of a request for payment from the Chief
  Electoral Officer in relation to an application, the Receiver General
  shall pay the amount specified in the application to the candidate's
  official agent out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 307](#1043357-1133739){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043357-1133739.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- transfer of contributions

**[[477.85]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.85 .sectionLabel}** No registered
agent of a registered party, no financial agent of a registered
association and no financial agent of a nomination contestant shall
transfer funds to a candidate after polling day except to pay claims
related to the candidate's electoral campaign.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

##### [Supply and Use of Forms]{.HTitleText4} {#h-209434 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prescribed forms --- [Income Tax
Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3)

**[[477.86]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.86 .sectionLabel}** A candidate and
their official agent shall use the prescribed forms for official
receipts to contributors for the purpose of subsection 127(3) of the
[Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of forms to returning officers

**[[477.87]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.87 .sectionLabel}** The Chief
Electoral Officer shall provide each returning officer with copies of
prescribed forms.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of forms to candidates

- **[[477.88]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.88
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A returning officer shall provide
  each candidate in their electoral district with a reasonable number of
  copies of each prescribed form requested by the candidate or by their
  official agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Return of unused forms

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A candidate and their official agent shall return any
  unused forms referred to in section 477.86 within a month after
  polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designated forms

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer may, from among forms
  that are to be provided under subsection (1), designate those that may
  be provided only to the official agent of a candidate whose nomination
  has been confirmed under subsection 71(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

#### [SUBDIVISION C]{.HLabel3}[Gifts and Other Advantages]{.HTitleText3} {#h-209452 .Subheading}

Definition of [[candidate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[477.89]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.89 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of sections 477.9 to 477.95, a candidate is deemed to have become a
candidate on the earlier of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the day on which they are selected at a nomination
  contest, and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the day on which the writ is issued for the election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

- **[[477.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.9
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No candidate shall accept any gift
  or other advantage that might reasonably be seen to have been given to
  influence them in the performance of their duties and functions as a
  member of the House of Commons if the candidate were to be elected,
  during the period that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} begins on the day on which they are deemed to have
    become a candidate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ends on

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the day on which they withdraw, if they withdraw
      in accordance with subsection 74(1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the day on which they become a member of the
      House of Commons, if they are elected, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} polling day, in any other case.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a candidate may accept a gift
  or other advantage that is given by a relative or as a normal
  expression of courtesy or protocol.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of candidate

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The candidate shall provide the Chief Electoral
  Officer with a statement in the prescribed form that discloses, in
  respect of all gifts or other advantages that the candidate accepted
  during the period referred to in subsection (1) whose benefit to the
  candidate exceeds \$500 or, if accepted from the same person or entity
  in that period, exceeds a total of \$500, other than gifts or other
  advantages given by relatives or made by way of an unconditional,
  non-discretionary testamentary disposition,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the nature of each gift or other advantage, its
    commercial value and the cost, if any, to the candidate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the person or entity giving
    the gift or other advantage; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the circumstances under which the gift or other
    advantage was given.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Clarification

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (3), the benefit to a
  candidate of a gift or other advantage that is a service or property,
  or the use of property or money, is the difference between the
  commercial value of the service or property or the use of the property
  or money and the cost, if any, to the candidate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Period for providing statement

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The candidate shall provide the statement to the
  Chief Electoral Officer within four months after polling day.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The following definitions apply in this section.

  [[common-law partnership]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[common-law partnership]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      relationship between two persons who are cohabiting in a conjugal
      relationship, having so cohabited for a period of at least one
      year. ([union de fait]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[gift or other advantage]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[gift or other advantage]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an amount of money if there is no obligation to
        repay it; and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a service or property, or the use of property
        or money, that is provided without charge or at less than its
        commercial value.

      It does not include a contribution made by an eligible individual
      under Division 1 of this Part to the official agent of a candidate
      that does not exceed the limits set out in that Division, or a
      provision of goods or services or a transfer of funds under
      section 364. ([cadeau ou autre avantage]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[relative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[relative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a candidate, means
      a person related to the candidate by marriage, common-law
      partnership, birth, adoption or
      affinity. ([parent]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
- [2018, c. 31, s. 308](#1043359-1133742){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043359-1133742.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-477.9-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 477.9"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extensions --- Chief Electoral Officer

- **[[477.91]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.91
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the
  written application of a candidate, shall authorize the extension of
  the period referred to in subsection 477.9(5), unless he or she is
  satisfied that the candidate's failure to make the statement was
  deliberate or was the result of the candidate's failure to exercise
  due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application may be made within the period
  referred to in subsection 477.9(5) or within two weeks after the end
  of that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corrections or revisions --- Chief
Electoral Officer

- **[[477.92]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.92
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the
  written application of a candidate, shall authorize the correction or
  revision of the statement if he or she is satisfied by the evidence
  submitted by the candidate that the correction or revision is
  necessary in order for the requirements of this subdivision to be
  complied with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application made without delay

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall be made immediately after the
  candidate becomes aware of the need for correction or revision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline for corrections or revisions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The candidate shall provide the Chief Electoral
  Officer with the corrected or revised version of the statement within
  30 days after the day on which the correction or revision is
  authorized or within any extension of that period authorized under
  subsection (4) or (5).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New deadline

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written
  application of the candidate made within two weeks after the end of
  the 30-day period referred to in subsection (3), shall authorize the
  extension of that period, unless he or she is satisfied that the
  candidate's failure to provide the corrected or revised version of the
  statement was deliberate or was the result of the candidate's failure
  to exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension of new deadline

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer, on the written
  application of the candidate made within two weeks after the end of an
  extension authorized under subsection (4) or under this subsection,
  shall authorize the further extension of that period, unless he or she
  is satisfied that the candidate's failure to provide the corrected or
  revised version of the statement was deliberate or was the result of
  the candidate's failure to exercise due diligence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extensions, corrections or revisions ---
judge

- **[[477.93]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.93
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A candidate may apply to a judge for
  an order

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} authorizing an extension referred to in subsection
    477.91(1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} authorizing a correction or revision referred to in
    subsection 477.92(1).

  The candidate shall notify the Chief Electoral Officer that the
  application has been made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deadline

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application may be made

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (1)(a), within two weeks after, as
    the case may be,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if an application for an extension is not made to
      the Chief Electoral Officer within the period referred to in
      subsection 477.91(2), the end of the two-week period referred to
      in that subsection,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the rejection of an application for an extension
      made in accordance with section 477.91, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the end of the extended period referred to in
      subsection 477.91(1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (1)(b), within two weeks after the
    rejection of an application for a correction or revision made in
    accordance with section 477.92.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Grounds --- extension

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall grant an order authorizing an
  extension unless the judge is satisfied that the candidate's failure
  to provide the required statement was deliberate or was the result of
  their failure to exercise due diligence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Grounds --- corrections or revisions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The judge shall grant an order authorizing a
  correction or revision if the judge is satisfied by the evidence
  submitted by the candidate that the correction or revision is
  necessary in order for the requirements of this subdivision to be
  complied with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of order

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} An order under subsection (1) may require that the
  candidate satisfy any condition that the judge considers necessary for
  carrying out the purposes of this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief Electoral Officer to retain
statements

- **[[477.94]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.94
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall
  retain in its possession the statements referred to in subsection
  477.9(3) for at least one year after the return of the writ for the
  election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be kept confidential

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall keep the statements
  provided under subsection 477.9(3) confidential.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not prohibit the Commissioner
  from inspecting the statements referred to in that subsection, and any
  of those statements may be provided to the Director of Public
  Prosecutions and produced by the Director for the purpose of a
  prosecution for an offence under this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- false, misleading or
incomplete statement

**[[477.95]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-477.95 .sectionLabel}** No candidate
shall provide the Chief Electoral Officer with a statement referred to
in subsection 477.9(3) that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the candidate knows or ought reasonably to know
  contains a material statement that is false or misleading; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} does not substantially set out the information
  required under that subsection.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

#### [SUBDIVISION A]{.HLabel3}[Registration of Leadership Contestants]{.HTitleText3} {#h-209565 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of leadership contest

- **[[478.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-478.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a registered party proposes to
  hold a leadership contest, the party's chief agent shall file with the
  Chief Electoral Officer a statement setting out the dates on which the
  leadership contest is to begin and end.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Variation and cancellation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A registered party that proposes to vary the
  leadership contest period or to cancel a leadership contest shall file
  with the Chief Electoral Officer a statement setting out, as the case
  may be, the amended beginning date or ending date or the fact of its
  cancellation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall, in the manner that
  he or she considers appropriate, publish a notice containing the
  information referred to in subsections (1) and (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2003, c. 19, s. 57
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to register

- **[[478.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-478.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who accepts
  contributions for, or incurs leadership campaign expenses in relation
  to, their campaign for the leadership of a registered party shall
  apply to the Chief Electoral Officer for registration as a leadership
  contestant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of Division 1 of this Part and this
  Division, a leadership contestant is deemed to have been a leadership
  contestant from the time they accept a contribution, incur a
  leadership campaign expense or borrow money under section 373.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of application

- **[[478.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-478.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An application for registration as a
  leadership contestant shall include the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the leadership contestant;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the address of the place where the records of the
    leadership contestant are maintained and to which communications may
    be addressed;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the leadership contestant's
    auditor; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the leadership contestant's
    financial agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Accompanying documents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall be accompanied by the
  following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the signed consent of the financial agent to act in
    that capacity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the signed consent of the auditor to act in that
    capacity;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a declaration signed by the chief agent of the
    registered party holding the leadership contest certifying that the
    party accepts the applicant as a leadership contestant; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a statement containing the information referred to
    in paragraphs 478.8(2)(d) to (g) with respect to contributions
    received and loans incurred before the first day of the leadership
    contest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of application

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Chief Electoral Officer shall register a
  leadership contestant who meets the requirements set out in
  subsections (1) and (2). In the case of a refusal to register, the
  Chief Electoral Officer shall indicate which of those requirements
  have not been met.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2003, c. 19, s. 57
- 2004, c. 24, s. 20
- 2014, c. 12, s. 86
:::
