##### [Offences under Division 6 of Part 18 (Leadership Contestants)]{.HTitleText4} {#h-210495 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Strict liability offences --- summary
conviction

- **[[497.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-497.5
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence
  who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} being a registered party, contravenes subsection
    478.1(1) or (2) (failure to inform of leadership contest or related
    changes);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} being a person, contravenes subsection 478.2(1)
    (failure to register for a leadership contest);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, contravenes
    subsection 478.5(2) or section 478.62, 478.63 or 478.64 (failure to
    comply with requirements re: appointment of leadership campaign
    agent, financial agent or auditor);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, contravenes
    subsection 478.66(1) or (2) (failure to report changes to leadership
    contestant information);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, contravenes section
    478.67 (failure to file statement of withdrawal);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} being a registered party, contravenes section
    478.68 (failure to file statement of withdrawal of acceptance);

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes section 478.72 (failure to satisfy bank
    account requirements);

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant or the financial
    agent of one, contravenes subsection 478.75(1) or (2) (failure to
    pay recoverable claim within three years or paying without
    authorization);

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes subsection 478.8(1), (2), (5) or (7)
    (failure to provide leadership campaign return or related
    documents);

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, fails to comply with a requirement of the Chief
    Electoral Officer under subsection 478.8(4);

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, contravenes
    subsection 478.8(8) (failure to send declaration re: leadership
    campaign return to financial agent) or subsection 478.84(1) (failure
    to provide Chief Electoral Officer with declaration re: leadership
    campaign return);

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes subsection 478.8(10) or (15) (failure to
    provide report on payment of claim);

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes subsection 478.8(11) or (12) (failure to
    provide updated version of statement of unpaid claims);

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, fails to comply with a requirement of the Chief
    Electoral Officer under subsection 478.8(14);

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes any of subsections 478.81(1) to (3) (failure
    to provide return on contributions or related documents);

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes section 478.82 (failure to forward certain
    contributions);

  - [(p.1)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, contravenes
    subsection 478.85(1) or (3) (failure to send written statement or
    advise financial agent);

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes subsection 478.86(3) (failure to provide
    corrected or revised document within specified period);

  - [(r)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant or the financial
    agent of one, contravenes subsection 478.88(3) (failure to provide
    corrected or revised document within 30-day period or any extension
    of that period);

  - [(s)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes paragraph 478.93(b) (providing document that
    is substantially incomplete); or

  - [(t)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes subsection 478.95(2) or (3) or section
    478.96 (failure to dispose of surplus leadership campaign funds).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offences requiring intent --- dual
  procedure

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} being a registered party, knowingly contravenes
    subsection 478.1(1) or (2) (failure to inform of leadership contest
    or related changes);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} being a person, knowingly contravenes subsection
    478.2(1) (failure to register for a leadership contest);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} being a person, knowingly contravenes subsection
    478.65(1) or (2) (acting as financial agent, leadership campaign
    agent or auditor when ineligible to do so);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, knowingly
    contravenes section 478.67 (failure to file statement of
    withdrawal);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} being a registered party, knowingly contravenes
    section 478.68 (failure to file statement of withdrawal of
    acceptance);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} being a person or entity other than a leadership
    campaign agent, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.73(1)
    (acceptance of contribution while ineligible);

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} being a person or entity other than a leadership
    campaign agent of a leadership contestant, knowingly contravenes
    subsection 478.73(2) (while ineligible, accepting provision of goods
    or services or transfer of funds or transferring funds);

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership campaign agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.73(3) (accepting
    prohibited contribution);

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} being a person or entity, knowingly contravenes
    subsection 478.73(4) or (5) (paying or incurring expenses for
    specified purposes while ineligible);

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} being a person or entity, knowingly contravenes
    subsection 478.73(6) (paying certain expenses of leadership
    contestant while ineligible);

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.8(1), (2), (5)
    or (7) (failure to provide leadership campaign return or related
    documents);

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly fails to comply with a requirement of the
    Chief Electoral Officer under subsection 478.8(4);

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, knowingly
    contravenes subsection 478.8(8) (failure to send declaration re:
    leadership campaign return to financial agent) or subsection
    478.84(1) (failure to provide Chief Electoral Officer with
    declaration re: leadership campaign return);

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.8(10) or (15)
    (failure to provide report on payment of claim);

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.8(11) or (12)
    (failure to provide updated version of statement of unpaid claims);

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly fails to comply with a requirement of the
    Chief Electoral Officer under subsection 478.8(14);

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes any of subsections 478.81(1)
    to (3) (failure to provide return on contributions or related
    documents);

  - [(r)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes section 478.82 (failure to forward
    certain contributions);

  - [(r.1)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, knowingly
    contravenes subsection 478.85(1) or (3) (failure to send written
    statement or advise financial agent);

  - [(s)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.86(3) (failure to
    provide corrected or revised document within specified period);

  - [(t)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant or the financial
    agent of one, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.88(3) (failure to
    provide corrected or revised document within 30-day period or any
    extension of that period);

  - [(t.1)]{.lawlabel} being a leadership contestant, contravenes
    section 478.921 (sending false or misleading declaration);

  - [(u)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, contravenes paragraph 478.93(a) or knowingly contravenes
    paragraph 478.93(b) (providing document that contains false or
    misleading information or that is substantially incomplete); or

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} being the financial agent of a leadership
    contestant, knowingly contravenes subsection 478.95(2) or (3) or
    section 478.96 (failure to dispose of surplus leadership campaign
    funds).

#### [Offences under this Part (Enforcement)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-210545 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Strict liability offence --- summary
conviction

- **[[498]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-498
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every chief agent of a registered
  party is guilty of an offence who fails to comply with a requirement
  of the Commissioner under section 510.001.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offence requiring intent --- dual
  procedure

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} knowingly contravenes subsection 479(4) (refusal to
    obey order to leave office or place); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} being the chief agent of a registered party,
    knowingly fails to comply with a requirement of the Commissioner
    under section 510.001.

#### [Offences under Part 21 (General)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-210548 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Strict liability offence --- summary
conviction

- **[[499]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-499
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who contravenes
  subsection 548(1) (removal of posted election documents) is guilty of
  an offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offences requiring intent --- dual

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} knowingly contravenes subsection 549(3) (making
    false declaration in solemn declaration or affidavit) or 549(4)
    (compelling or inducing false declaration); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate, knowingly contravenes section
    550 (signing document that limits freedom of action in Parliament).

### [Punishment]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210556 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment --- strict liability offences

- **[[500]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-500
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an
  offence under any of subsections 484(1), 489(1), 491(1), 492(1),
  495(1), 495.1(1), 495.2(1), 495.21(1), 495.3(1), 496(1), 496.1(1),
  497(1), 497.1(1), 497.2(1), 497.3(1), 497.4(1), 497.5(1), 498(1) and
  499(1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than
  \$2,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three months,
  or to both.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment --- strict liability
  offences

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an offence under
  section 497.01 is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more
  than \$1,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment --- offences requiring
  intent (summary conviction)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an offence under any of
  subsections 484(2) and 486(2), paragraph 487(1)(a), subsections 488(1)
  and 489(2), sections 491.1 and 493 and subsections 495(2) and (3),
  497.1(2) and 497.2(2) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not
  more than \$5,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six
  months, or to both.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment --- offences requiring
  intent (summary conviction)

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an offence under
  subsection 485(1) or paragraph 487(1)(b) is liable on summary
  conviction to a fine of not more than \$10,000 or to imprisonment for
  a term of not more than one year, or to both.

- [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2014, c. 12, s. 100\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment --- offences requiring
  intent (summary conviction --- fine only)

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an offence under
  subsection 495(4) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not
  more than \$50,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment --- offences requiring
  intent (dual procedure)

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an offence under any of
  subsections 480(1) and (2), 480.1(1), 481(1) and 482(1), section
  482.1, subsections 484(3), 485(2), 486(3) and (4), 487(2), 488(2) and
  489(3), section 490, subsection 491(3), section 491.2, subsection
  492(2), section 494, subsections 495(5), 495.1(2), 495.2(2),
  495.21(2), 495.3(2), 496(2), 496.1(2), 497(2), 497.1(3), 497.2(3),
  497.3(2), 497.4(2), 497.5(2), 498(2) and 499(2) is liable

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than
    \$20,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or
    to both; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more
    than \$50,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five
    years, or to both.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional punishment --- third parties

  [(5.1)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is guilty of an offence
  under paragraph 495.21(1)(a) or (b) or subsection 495.21(2) is, in
  addition to the punishment provided under subsection (1) or (5),
  liable to a fine of up to five times the amount of the funds whose
  source was a foreign entity that were used, or the amount of the funds
  that were used to circumvent the prohibition on using funds whose
  source is a foreign entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional punishment --- third parties

  [(5.2)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is guilty of an offence
  under paragraph 495.3(1)(a) or (2)(a) is, in addition to the
  punishment provided under subsection (1) or (5), liable to a fine of
  up to five times the amount by which the third party exceeded the
  pre-election period expenses limit in question.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional punishment --- third parties

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Every third party that is guilty of an offence under
  paragraph 496(1)(a) or (2)(a) is, in addition to the punishment
  provided under subsection (1) or (5), liable to a fine of up to five
  times the amount by which the third party exceeded the election period
  expenses limit in question.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional penalties

- **[[501]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-501 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When
  a person has been convicted of an offence under this Act, the court
  may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances
  surrounding its commission, and in addition to any other punishment
  that may be imposed under this Act, by order direct the person to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} perform community service, subject to any
    reasonable conditions that may be specified in the order;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} if the offence results, directly or indirectly,
    in a financial benefit under this Act, or a contribution for which a
    receipt referred to in subsection 127(3) of the [Income Tax
    Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3) was issued, pay to the Receiver General an
    amount that is not more than the financial benefit or contribution,
    as the case may be;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} compensate any other person who has suffered
    damages as a result of the commission of the offence;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} perform any obligation the non-performance of which
    gave rise to the offence; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} take any other reasonable measure that the court
    considers appropriate to ensure compliance with this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional penalties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a registered party, its chief agent or registered
  agent or one of its officers has been convicted of an offence referred
  to in subsection (3), the court may, having regard to the nature of
  the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, and in
  addition to any other punishment that may be imposed under this Act,
  by order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} direct the Chief Electoral Officer to deregister
    the party;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if it directs deregistration under paragraph (a),
    direct the chief agent --- or another person specified by the court
    --- to liquidate the party's assets; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if it directs liquidation under paragraph (b),
    direct the financial agent of each registered association --- or
    another person specified by the court --- to liquidate the
    registered association's assets.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offences

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (2), the provisions
  are the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497(2)(h) (entering into prohibited
    agreement);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497(2)(i) (soliciting or accepting
    contribution);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497(2)(j) (collusion);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497.1(3)(d) (providing or certifying
    false or misleading information or making false or misleading
    declaration);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497.1(3)(e) (providing false or
    misleading information);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497.1(3)(k) (failure to provide financial
    transactions return or related documents);

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497.1(3)(n) (providing document that
    contains false or misleading information);

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497.1(3)(p) (providing document that
    contains false or misleading information); and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 497.2(3)(h) (failure to provide financial
    transactions return or related documents).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Documents to be provided to Chief
  Electoral Officer

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The chief agent or specified person shall, within six
  months after being directed to liquidate the party's assets under
  subsection (2), provide to the Chief Electoral Officer

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a statement --- prepared in accordance with
    generally accepted accounting principles --- of the fair market
    value of the party's assets and liabilities on the day of the order;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report by the party's auditor to the chief agent
    or specified person containing the auditor's opinion as to whether
    the statement presents, in accordance with generally accepted
    auditing standards, the fair market value of those assets and
    liabilities; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a declaration in the prescribed form by the chief
    agent or specified person concerning that statement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remittance to Receiver General

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Within three months after providing the documents
  referred to in subsection (4), the chief agent or specified person
  shall remit an amount equal to any net balance of the assets over
  liabilities, calculated on the basis of the statement mentioned in
  paragraph (4)(a), to the Chief Electoral Officer who shall forward
  that amount to the Receiver General.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liability of chief agent

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The chief agent or specified person is liable for the
  remittance of the amount referred to in subsection (5).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to registered associations

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (4) to (6) apply to the liquidation of a
  registered association's assets under subsection (2) and any reference
  in those subsections to "party" and "chief agent" shall be read as a
  reference to "registered association" and "financial agent",
  respectively.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 501
- 2004, c. 24, s. 22
- 2014, c. 12, s. 101
:::

### [Illegal Practices and Corrupt Practices]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210614 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Illegal practice

- **[[502]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-502
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence
  that is an illegal practice who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, contravenes section 92 (publication of false statement of
    withdrawal of candidate);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent, contravenes
    subsection 330(2) (foreign broadcasting);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} being an official agent, a candidate or a person
    authorized under paragraph 477.55(c), knowingly contravenes section
    477.52 (exceeding election expenses limit);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, commits an offence under subsection 480(1) (obstructing
    electoral process) or 480(2) (inciting, conspiring to act in
    disorderly manner);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate, contravenes subsection 549(3)
    (making false declaration in solemn declaration or affidavit) or
    549(4) (compelling or inducing false declaration); or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate, contravenes section 550 (signing
    of document that limits freedom of action in Parliament).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corrupt practice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every person is guilty of an offence that is a
  corrupt practice who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 347\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, contravenes paragraph 43(a) (obstruction of election
    officer);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, knowingly contravenes paragraph 43(b) (impersonation of
    election officer);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, contravenes paragraph 56(b) (making false statement to
    have person deleted from Register of Electors);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, contravenes paragraph 56(c) or (d) (forbidden acts re
    Register of Electors);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} contravenes section 89 (signing of nomination paper
    when ineligible);

  - [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2014, c. 12, s. 102\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} contravenes paragraph 111(a), (d) or (e) (forbidden
    acts re list of electors);

  - [(g.1)]{.lawlabel} contravenes section 281.5 (only one vote);

  - [(g.2)]{.lawlabel} contravenes paragraph 281.7(1)(a) (request or
    apply for a ballot or special ballot under false name);

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, commits an offence under subsection 282.7(1) (offering
    bribe);

  - [(h.01)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate, knowingly contravenes
    subsection 477.9(1) (accepting prohibited gift or other advantage);

  - [(h.1)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, commits an offence under subsection 480.1(1)
    (impersonation); or

  - [(h.2)]{.lawlabel} being a candidate or an official agent of a
    candidate, commits an offence under section 482.1 (obstruction).

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 347\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consequences of illegal, corrupt
  practices

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Any person who is convicted of having committed an
  offence that is an illegal practice or a corrupt practice under this
  Act shall, in addition to any other punishment for that offence
  prescribed by this Act, in the case of an illegal practice, during the
  next five years or, in the case of a corrupt practice, during the next
  seven years, after the date of their being so convicted, not be
  entitled to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be elected to or sit in the House of Commons; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} hold any office in the nomination of the Crown or
    of the Governor in Council.

::: HistoricalNote

- 2014, c. 12, s. 102
- [2018, c. 31, s. 347](#1043794-1134150){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043794-1134150.html"}
:::

### [Miscellaneous Provisions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210645 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistered parties

- **[[503]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-503 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  political party that is deregistered during a pre-election period does
  not commit an offence under paragraph 495.3(1)(a) or (2)(a) if, before
  the deregistration, its partisan activity expenses, partisan
  advertising expenses and election survey expenses exceeded any maximum
  amount set out in section 349.1.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prior expenses applied against spending
  limit

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If subsection (1) applies, then partisan activity
  expenses, partisan advertising expenses and election survey expenses
  incurred before the deregistration shall be applied against any
  maximum amount set out in section 349.1 and, if the limit is exceeded,
  the political party shall not incur any additional partisan activity
  expenses, partisan advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistered parties

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} A political party that is deregistered during an
  election period does not commit an offence under paragraph 496(1)(a)
  or (2)(a) if, before the deregistration, its partisan activity
  expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey expenses
  exceeded any maximum amount set out in section 350.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligible party

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An eligible party that does not become a registered
  party during the election period of a general election does not commit
  an offence under paragraph 496(1)(a) or (2)(a) if its partisan
  activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey
  expenses, as of the day that it is informed under subsection 390(4)
  that it has not been registered, exceed any maximum amount set out in
  section 350.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prior expenses applied against spending
  limit

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If subsection (1.2) or (2) applies, then partisan
  activity expenses, election advertising expenses and election survey
  expenses incurred before the deregistration or before the day referred
  to in subsection (2), as the case may be, shall be applied against any
  maximum amount set out in section 350 and, if the maximum amount is
  exceeded, the party shall not incur any additional partisan activity
  expenses, election advertising expenses or election survey expenses.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 503
- 2003, c. 19, s. 59
- 2014, c. 12, s. 103
- [2018, c. 31, s. 348](#1043807-1134162){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043807-1134162.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-503-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 503"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Judicial proceedings and compliance
agreements

**[[504]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-504 .sectionLabel}** In the case of judicial
proceedings or a compliance agreement involving an eligible party, a
registered party, a deregistered political party or an electoral
district association,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the party or association is deemed to be a person;
  and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any act or thing done or omitted to be done by an
  officer, a chief agent or other registered agent of the party, or by
  an officer, the financial agent or other electoral district agent of
  the association within the scope of their authority to act, is deemed
  to be an act or thing done or omitted to be done by the party or
  association, as the case may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 504
- 2001, c. 21, s. 24
- 2003, c. 19, s. 60
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-504-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 504"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prosecution of third parties --- groups

- **[[505]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-505 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  third party that is a group commits an offence under paragraph
  495(1)(a.2) or 495(5)(a.1) or section 495.21, 495.3, 496 or 496.1, the
  person who is responsible for the group or its financial agent commits
  the offence if the person or financial agent authorized, consented to
  or participated in the act or omission that constitutes the offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prosecution of third parties ---
  vicarious liability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of a prosecution brought against a
  third party under paragraph 495(1)(a.2) or 495(5)(a.1) or section
  495.21, 495.3, 496 or 496.1, the third party is deemed to be a person
  and any act or omission of the person who signed the application for
  registration in respect of the third party --- or, in the absence of
  an application, the person who would have signed it --- or the third
  party's financial agent, within the scope of that person's or
  financial agent's authority, is deemed to be an act or omission of the
  third party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prosecution of third parties --- groups
  or corporations (\$50,000)

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a third party that is a group or corporation
  commits an offence under paragraph 495.3(1)(d) or 496(1)(c), the third
  party is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than \$50,000
  instead of the punishment set out in subsection 500(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prosecution of third parties --- groups
  or corporations (\$100,000)

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a third party that is a group or corporation
  commits an offence under paragraph 495.3(2)(e) or 496(2)(e), the third
  party is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than \$100,000
  instead of the punishment set out in subsection 500(5).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 505
- 2014, c. 12, s. 104
- [2018, c. 31, s. 349](#1043811-1134172){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043811-1134172.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-505-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 505"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming --- calling service providers

**[[505.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-505.1 .sectionLabel}** For the purpose of
a prosecution brought under subsection 495.1(1) or (2) against a calling
service provider that is a group or for the purpose of entering into a
compliance agreement with the calling service provider,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the calling service provider is deemed to be a
  person; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any act or thing done or omitted to be done by a
  member of the calling service provider within the scope of their
  authority to act is deemed to be an act or thing done or omitted to be
  done by the calling service provider.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 105
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming --- third parties that are groups

- **[[505.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-505.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of a prosecution
  brought under subsection 495.2(1) or (2) against a third party that is
  a group or for the purpose of entering into a compliance agreement
  with the third party, the third party is deemed to be a person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Official representatives

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a third party that is a group commits an offence
  under subsection 495.2(1) or (2), its official representative commits
  the offence if he or she authorized, consented to or participated in
  the act or omission that constitutes the offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 105
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prosecution of third parties ---
vicarious liability

**[[505.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-505.3 .sectionLabel}** For the purpose of
a prosecution brought under subsection 495.2(1) or (2) against a third
party, any act or omission of its official representative is deemed to
be an act or omission of the third party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 105
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interpretation

**[[505.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-505.4 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes of
sections 505.1 to 505.3, [[calling service
provider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, [[group]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm},
[[official representative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and [[third
party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} have the same meaning as in section 348.01.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 105
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistered party --- strict liability

- **[[506]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-506 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  deregistered political party whose chief agent commits an offence
  under paragraph 497.1(1)(e) is guilty of an offence and liable on
  summary conviction to a fine of not more than \$50,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deregistered party --- offence
  requiring intent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A deregistered political party whose chief agent
  commits an offence under paragraph 497.1(3)(g) is guilty of an offence
  and liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than \$100,000.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 506
- 2003, c. 19, s. 61
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 106, 107
:::

[Previous
Version](section-506-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 506"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered party --- strict liability

- **[[507]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  registered party whose chief agent commits an offence under any of
  paragraphs 497.1(1)(h), (i), (k), (l), (m) and (n) is guilty of an
  offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than
  \$50,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered party --- offences requiring
  intent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A registered party whose chief agent commits an
  offence under any of paragraphs 497.1(3)(i), (k), (m), (o) and (p) is
  guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine of not
  more than \$100,000.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 507
- 2003, c. 19, s. 61
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 106, 107
:::

Version](section-507-20140619.html "Link to previous version of section 507"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

**[[508]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-508 .sectionLabel}** In a prosecution for an
offence under this Act, the written statement of the returning officer
is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, sufficient evidence of
the holding of the election and of any person named in the certificate
having been a candidate.

### [Violations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1134173 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Violation

**[[508.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-508.1 .sectionLabel}** Every person or
entity that contravenes section 281.3, 281.4 or 281.5 or a provision of
any of Parts 16, 17 and 18 -- or that fails to comply with a requirement
of the Chief Electoral Officer under any of those Parts, with a
provision of a compliance agreement or with a provision of an
undertaking that has been accepted by the Commissioner --- commits a
violation and is liable to an administrative monetary penalty in an
amount established in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 350](#1043815-1134177){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043815-1134177.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuing violation

**[[508.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-508.2 .sectionLabel}** A violation that is
committed or continued on more than one day constitutes a separate
violation in respect of each day on which it is committed or continued.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 350](#1043815-1134181){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043815-1134181.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}How act or omission may be proceeded with

**[[508.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-508.3 .sectionLabel}** If an act or
omission may be proceeded with as a violation or as an offence under
this Act, proceeding in one manner precludes proceeding in the other.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 350](#1043815-1134185){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043815-1134185.html"}
:::

### [Administrative Monetary Penalties]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1134186 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Purpose of penalty

**[[508.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-508.4 .sectionLabel}** The purpose of an
administrative monetary penalty is to promote compliance with this Act,
and not to punish.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 350](#1043815-1134190){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043815-1134190.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum amount of penalty

- **[[508.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-508.5
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the
  maximum administrative monetary penalty for a violation is \$1,500, in
  the case of an individual, and \$5,000, in the case of a corporation
  or an entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maximum --- sections 363 and 367

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The maximum administrative monetary penalty for a
  violation arising from the contravention of section 363 or 367 is an
  amount equal to twice the amount that was contributed in contravention
  of that section, plus

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} \$1,500, in the case of an individual who
    contravenes section 363 or 367; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} \$5,000, in the case of a corporation or an entity
    that contravenes section 363.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 350](#1043815-1134199){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043815-1134199.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Criteria for penalty

- **[[508.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-508.6
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The amount of an administrative
  monetary penalty is to be determined taking into account

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the degree of intention or negligence on the part
    of the person or entity that committed the violation;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the harm done by the violation;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} whether the person or entity derived any advantage
    from the violation;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} whether the person or entity made reasonable
    efforts to mitigate or reverse the violation's effects;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} whether the person or entity has taken steps to
    avoid committing the violation in the future;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} whether the person or entity has provided all
    reasonable assistance to the Commissioner with respect to the
    violation, including reporting it and providing any relevant
    information;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the person's or entity's history of compliance with
    the provisions of this Act;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the person's or entity's ability to pay the
    penalty;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any aggravating and mitigating circumstances; and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} any other factor that, in the opinion of the
    Commissioner, is relevant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner may take into account a factor under
  paragraph (1)(j) only if a notice that sets out the factor has been
  published on his or her Internet site.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consultations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Before publishing the notice, the Commissioner shall
  consult with the Chief Electoral Officer and then

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} consult with the Advisory Committee of Political
    Parties established by subsection 21.1(1); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} publish on his or her Internet site, for the
    purpose of public consultation, a notice that sets out the proposed
    factor for at least 30 days.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 350](#1043815-1134220){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043815-1134220.html"}
:::

### [Commissioner of Canada Elections]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210709 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Commissioner of Canada Elections

- **[[509]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Commissioner of Canada Elections shall be appointed by the Chief
  Electoral Officer, after consultation with the Director of Public
  Prosecutions, to hold office during good behaviour for a non-renewable
  term of 10 years and may be removed by the Chief Electoral Officer for
  cause.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remuneration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner shall be paid the remuneration that
  is fixed by the Chief Electoral Officer, after consultation with the
  Director of Public Prosecutions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligibility

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person is not eligible to be appointed as
  Commissioner if the person is or has been

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a candidate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an employee of a registered party or a person whose
    services have been engaged by the registered party to support its
    electoral or political financing activities; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a member of the staff referred to in any of
    paragraphs 4(2)(a) to (f) of the [Parliamentary Employment and Staff
    Relations Act](/eng/acts/P-1.3) or a person referred to in paragraph
    4(2)(g) of that Act.

  - [(d) and (e)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s.
    351\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No re-appointment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person who has served as Commissioner is not
  eligible for re-appointment to that office.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 509
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 108, 154
- 2018, c. 31, s. 351
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-509-20141219.html "Link to previous version of section 509"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Position within Office of Chief Electoral
Officer

- **[[509.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The position of Commissioner of
  Canada Elections is within the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deputy head --- [Financial
  Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of sections 11 to 13 of the
  [Financial Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11), the Commissioner is
  the deputy head in relation to the portions of the federal public
  administration in the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer in which
  the employees referred to in section 509.3 occupy their positions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deputy head --- [Public Service
  Employment Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01)

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of the [Public Service Employment
  Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01), the Commissioner is the deputy head in
  relation to the portions of the federal public administration in the
  Office of the Chief Electoral Officer in which the employees referred
  to in section 509.3 occupy their positions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 108
- [2018, c. 31, s. 352](#1043817-1121117){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043817-1121117.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty

**[[509.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.2 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner's
duty is to ensure that this Act, other than Division 1.1 of Part 16.1,
is complied with and enforced by taking any measure that is provided for
in this Act, including by

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} conducting investigations;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} instituting prosecutions for offences under this Act;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} entering into compliance agreements;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} issuing notices of violation that set out an
  administrative monetary penalty; or

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} accepting undertakings.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, ss. 108, 157
- [2018, c. 31, s. 352](#1043817-1121125){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043817-1121125.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-509.2-20190401.html "Link to previous version of section 509.2"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Independence

- **[[509.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} All decisions made and actions taken
  by the Commissioner under any provision of Part 19 are to be made or
  taken independently of the Chief Electoral Officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Clarification

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) precludes the Commissioner
  from consulting with the Chief Electoral Officer in respect of any
  matter if the Commissioner considers it appropriate to do so.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 352](#1043817-1121132){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043817-1121132.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to take measures

**[[509.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.22 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner,
if he or she considers it to be in the public interest, may take any
measures, including incurring any expenses, when exercising or
performing any of his or her powers, duties and functions under this
Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 352](#1043817-1121136){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043817-1121136.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation

**[[509.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.23 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner
may delegate to any member of his or her staff, subject to any
restrictions or limitations that he or she may specify, any of his or
her powers, duties or functions that relate to the issuance of notices
of violation or the acceptance of undertakings under this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 352](#1043817-1134226){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043817-1134226.html"}
:::

### [Staff]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210738 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Employees

- **[[509.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The employees necessary for the
  Commissioner to exercise or perform his or her powers, duties and
  functions under this Act are to be appointed in accordance with the
  [Public Service Employment Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Casual employees, etc.

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any additional employees that the Commissioner
  considers necessary for the exercise or performance of his or her
  powers, duties and functions under this Act may be appointed for a
  specified term or on a casual basis in accordance with the [Public
  Service Employment Act](/eng/acts/P-33.01).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 108
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Technical assistance

**[[509.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.4 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner
may engage on a temporary basis investigators or persons having
technical or specialized knowledge to advise and assist him or her in
the exercise or performance of his or her powers, duties and functions
under this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 108
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authorization to assist

**[[509.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.5 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner
may authorize a person employed in the Office of the Chief Electoral
Officer to assist the Commissioner in the exercise or performance of any
of his or her powers, duties and functions arising from subsections
509.1(2) and (3) and in the exercise of his or her power under section
509.4, subject to the terms and conditions that the Commissioner sets.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 108
- [2018, c. 31, s. 353](#1043821-1121149){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043821-1121149.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-509.5-20141001.html "Link to previous version of section 509.5"){.PITLink}

### [Payments out of Consolidated Revenue Fund]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210754 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amounts to be paid out of C.R.F.

**[[509.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.6 .sectionLabel}** The following shall
be paid out of unappropriated moneys forming part of the Consolidated
Revenue Fund on the certificate of the Chief Electoral Officer:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the remuneration paid to the Commissioner or to a
  person employed under subsection 509.3(2) and any additional
  remuneration paid to employees referred to in subsection 509.3(1) for
  overtime work to enable the Commissioner to exercise or perform his or
  her powers, duties and functions under this Act; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any expenses incurred by, on behalf of or in relation
  to the Commissioner under any other provision of this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 108
- [2018, c. 31, s. 354](#1043825-1121151){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043825-1121151.html"}
:::

### [Investigations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210761 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Investigation by Commissioner

- **[[510]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-510 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Commissioner, on his or her own initiative or in response to a
  complaint, may conduct an investigation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} As soon as feasible after beginning an investigation,
  the Commissioner shall give written notice of the investigation to the
  person whose conduct is being investigated. The notice is not to be
  given if, in the Commissioner's opinion, to do so might compromise or
  hinder the investigation or any other investigation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Public officer --- [Criminal
  Code](/eng/acts/C-46)

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of Part XV of the [Criminal
  Code](/eng/acts/C-46), any person who is charged by the Commissioner
  with duties relating to the administration or enforcement of this Act
  is deemed to be a public officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 510
- 2014, c. 12, s. 108
- [2018, c. 31, s. 356](#1043833-1111397){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043833-1111397.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-510-20141001.html "Link to previous version of section 510"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election expenses return --- supporting
documents

**[[510.001]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-510.001 .sectionLabel}** In the course
of conducting an investigation under section 510 in response to a
complaint, the Commissioner may require the chief agent of a registered
party to provide by a specified date documents evidencing any expense
set out in the party's election expenses return, including bank
statements, deposit slips and cancelled cheques.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 357](#1043837-1134230){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043837-1134230.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order requiring testimony or written
return

- **[[510.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-510.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, on application of the
  Commissioner or his or her authorized representative, a judge is
  satisfied by information on oath that there are reasonable grounds to
  believe that this Act has been contravened or is about to be
  contravened and that an individual has or is likely to have
  information that will provide evidence of the contravention, the judge
  may order the individual to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} attend as specified in the order and be examined on
    oath by the Commissioner or the authorized representative on any
    matter that is relevant to the contravention before an individual,
    in sections 510.02 to 510.04 referred to as a "presiding officer",
    designated in the order; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make and deliver to the Commissioner or the
    authorized representative, within the time specified in the order, a
    written return under oath showing in detail the information that is
    required by the order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Date for hearing and notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of the application, the judge shall fix a
  date for the hearing of the application and direct that notice of the
  hearing be given, in the manner that the judge may specify, to the
  individual against whom the order is sought.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No order may be made under subsection (1) against an
  individual who is alleged to have committed, or who is about to
  commit, the contravention to which the application relates.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When hearing may proceed ex parte

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A judge may proceed [ex parte]{.otherLang lang="la"}
  to hear and determine the application in the absence of the individual
  against whom the order is sought if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Commissioner or the authorized representative
    establishes to the satisfaction of the judge that the disclosure of
    any information set out in the application would

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} compromise the identity of a confidential
      informant,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} compromise the nature and extent of an ongoing
      investigation,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} endanger an individual engaged in particular
      intelligence-gathering techniques and thereby prejudice future
      investigations in which similar techniques would be used, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} prejudice the interests of an innocent
      individual; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the judge is satisfied for any reason that the ends
    of justice would be subverted by the disclosure of the information
    set out in the application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sealing packet of documents

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If an order made under subsection (1) is issued [ex
  parte]{.otherLang lang="la"}, all documents relating to the
  application shall, subject to any terms and conditions that the judge
  considers desirable in the circumstances, including any term or
  condition concerning the duration of the prohibition, partial
  disclosure of a document, deletion of any information or the
  occurrence of a condition, be placed in a packet and sealed by the
  judge immediately on determination of the application, and that packet
  shall be kept in the custody of the court in a place to which the
  public has no access or in any other place that the judge may
  authorize and shall not be dealt with except in accordance with the
  terms and conditions specified in the order or as varied under
  subsection (7).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order prohibiting disclosure

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If the order made under subsection (1) is issued [ex
  parte]{.otherLang lang="la"}, the judge shall make an order
  prohibiting a person or entity from disclosing, during the period set
  out in the order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the existence of the application;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the existence of the order made under subsection
    (1); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the content of any testimony given or of any
    written return made under the order made under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for variance of order

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} An application to terminate an order made under
  subsection (6) or to vary any of its terms and conditions may be made
  to the judge who made the order or a judge of the same court.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of order

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} An order made under this section has effect anywhere
  in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 357](#1043837-1111427){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043837-1111427.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Witness competent and compellable

- **[[510.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-510.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An individual who is the subject of
  an order under paragraph 510.01(1)(a) is competent and may be
  compelled to give evidence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No individual excused from complying
  with order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No individual shall be excused from complying with an
  order that is made under subsection 510.01(1) on the ground that the
  testimony or written return required of the individual may tend to
  incriminate the individual or subject them to any proceeding or
  penalty.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance of individual whose conduct
  is being investigated

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An individual whose conduct is being investigated
  during an examination conducted under an order under paragraph
  510.01(1)(a), and their counsel, may attend the examination unless the
  Commissioner or the authorized representative, or the individual being
  examined, establishes to the satisfaction of the presiding officer
  that the presence of the individual whose conduct is being
  investigated would be prejudicial to the effective conduct of the
  examination or the investigation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (3) does not apply in respect of an
  examination conducted under an order that was issued [ex
  parte]{.otherLang lang="la"}.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Testimony, evidence and return not
  receivable

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (6), no testimony given by an
  individual under an order made under paragraph 510.01(1)(a), or
  written return made by an individual under an order made under
  paragraph 510.01(1)(b), and no evidence derived from the testimony or
  written return, shall be used or received against that individual in
  any civil or criminal proceedings instituted against them, other than
  a prosecution for an offence under section 482.1 of this Act or
  section 132 or 136 of the [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Part XV of the Criminal Code

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Information contained in the testimony or written
  return referred to in subsection (5) and information derived from such
  information may be used in an application under Part XV of the
  [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Fees

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} An individual who is the subject of an order made
  under paragraph 510.01(1)(a) is entitled to the fees and allowances
  for so doing as if they were summoned to attend before a superior
  court of the province in which the individual is summoned to attend.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representation by counsel

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} A presiding officer shall permit an individual who is
  being examined under an order made under paragraph 510.01(1)(a) to be
  represented by counsel.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 357](#1043837-1111446){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043837-1111446.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Presiding officer

- **[[510.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-510.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any individual who is a barrister or
  advocate of at least ten years standing at the bar of a province, or
  who has been a barrister or advocate at the bar of a province for at
  least ten years, may be designated as a presiding officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remuneration and expenses

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A presiding officer is to be paid the remuneration
  fixed in the order designating them as such, and is entitled to be
  paid the travel and living expenses, incurred in the performance of
  their duties under this Act, in accordance with Treasury Board
  directives.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 357](#1043837-1111453){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043837-1111453.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Administration of oaths

- **[[510.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-510.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The presiding officer may administer
  oaths for the purpose of examinations conducted under an order made
  under paragraph 510.01(1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Orders of presiding officer

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A presiding officer may make any order that they
  consider to be proper for the conduct of an examination under an order
  made under paragraph 510.01(1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination to be in private

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The examination before the presiding officer shall be
  conducted in private.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to judge

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A judge may, on application by a presiding officer,
  order any individual to comply with an order made by the presiding
  officer under subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No order may be made under subsection (4) unless the
  presiding officer has given the individual in respect of whom the
  order is sought and the Commissioner 24 hours' notice of the hearing
  of the application for the order, or any shorter notice that the judge
  to whom the application is made considers reasonable.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2018, c. 31, s. 357](#1043837-1111466){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043837-1111466.html"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confidentiality

- **[[510.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-510.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), neither
  the Commissioner nor any person acting under his or her direction
  shall disclose any information relating to an investigation that comes
  to their knowledge in the exercise of their powers or the performance
  of their duties and functions under this Act, including information
  that reveals or from which may be inferred the name of the
  complainant, if any, the person whose conduct is being investigated or
  any witness.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure authorized

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner may disclose or may authorize any
  person acting under his or her direction to disclose

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with the consent of the person in question, the
    name of any of the following: the complainant, if any, the person
    whose conduct is being investigated and any witness;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} information that, in the Commissioner's opinion, is
    necessary to carry out an investigation;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when a prosecution has been instituted under
    subsection 511(1), information that the Director of Public
    Prosecutions requires;

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} when a review by the Chief Electoral Officer is
    requested under section 521.14, information that the Chief Elector
    Officer requires;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} information that is required to be disclosed in the
    course of a prosecution for an offence under this Act;

  - [(d.1)]{.lawlabel} information that is required to be disclosed in
    the course of an application for judicial review in respect of a
    decision taken under this Act;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} information that is required to be disclosed under
    any other Act of Parliament;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} information that, in the Commissioner's opinion, is
    necessary in order to enter into or renegotiate a compliance
    agreement;

  - [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} information that, in the Commissioner's opinion,
    is necessary in order for a person or entity to provide an
    undertaking; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} information whose disclosure is, in the
    Commissioner's opinion, in the public interest.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Public interest

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraph (2)(g), the
  Commissioner shall take into consideration the effects of disclosure
  on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the privacy rights of any person who is the subject
    of the disclosure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the right of the person under investigation to be
    presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} public confidence in the fairness of the electoral
    process.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2014, c. 12, s. 108
- [2018, c. 31, s. 358](#1043839-1121154){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043839-1121154.html"}
:::

### [Prosecutions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1121155 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Commissioner may institute a prosecution

- **[[511]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-511 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Commissioner believes on reasonable grounds that an offence under
  this Act has been committed, the Commissioner may institute a
  prosecution or cause one to be instituted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A prosecution for an offence under this Act is
  instituted by the laying of an information in writing and under oath
  before a justice, as defined in section 2 of the [Criminal
  Code](/eng/acts/C-46).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 511
- 2003, c. 19, s. 62
- 2006, c. 9, s. 130
- [2018, c. 31, s. 360](#1043859-1121161){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043859-1121161.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-511-20061212.html "Link to previous version of section 511"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director's consent required

- **[[512]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-512 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  prosecution for an offence under this Act may be instituted by a
  person, other than the Commissioner or a person acting under his or
  her direction, without the prior written consent of the Director of
  Public Prosecutions provided after consultation with the Commissioner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to an offence in
  relation to which an election officer has taken measures under
  subsection 479(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of consent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every document purporting to be the Director's
  consent under subsection (1) is deemed to be that consent unless it is
  called into question by the Director or by someone acting for the
  Director or for Her Majesty.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 512
- 2006, c. 9, s. 131
- [2018, c. 31, s. 361](#1043863-1121163){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043863-1121163.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-512-20061212.html "Link to previous version of section 512"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[513]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-513 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2018, c.
31, s. 362\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-513-20061212.html "Link to previous version of section 513"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation period

- **[[514]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-514
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Proceedings in respect of an offence
  under a provision set out in subsection 500(1) may be commenced at any
  time within, but not later than, six years after the day on which the
  subject-matter of the proceedings arose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), if a prosecution cannot be
  instituted because the offender has left the jurisdiction of the
  court, the prosecution may be instituted within one year after the
  offender's return.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No limitation period

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Proceedings in respect of an offence under a
  provision set out in any of subsections 500(2) to (5) may be commenced
  at any time.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 514
- 2003, c. 19, s. 63
- 2006, c. 9, s. 59
- 2014, c. 12, s. 109
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-514-20061212.html "Link to previous version of section 514"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Allowance of costs

- **[[515]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-515 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  court of criminal jurisdiction before which a private prosecution is
  instituted for an offence against this Act may order payment by the
  defendant to the prosecutor of such costs and expenses as appear to
  the court to have been reasonably incurred in and about the conduct of
  the prosecution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prior recognizance required

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A court shall not make an order under subsection (1)
  unless the prosecutor, before or on the laying of the information,
  enters into a recognizance with two sufficient sureties, in the amount
  of \$500, and to the satisfaction of the court, to conduct the
  prosecution with effect and to pay the defendant's costs in case of
  acquittal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Costs of defendant

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In case of an information by a private prosecutor for
  an offence against this Act, if judgment is given for the defendant,
  the defendant is entitled to recover from the prosecutor the costs
  incurred by the defendant by reason of the proceedings, which costs
  shall be taxed by the proper officer of the court in which the
  judgment is given.

### [Injunctions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210828 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for injunction

- **[[516]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-516 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Commissioner has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has
  committed, is about to commit or is likely to commit an act or
  omission that is contrary to this Act, the Commissioner may, during an
  election period, after taking into account the nature and seriousness
  of the act or omission, the need to ensure fairness of the electoral
  process and the public interest, apply to a competent court described
  in subsection 525(1) for an injunction described in subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Injunction

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the court, on application by the Commissioner
  under subsection (1), is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds
  to believe that a person has committed, is about to commit or is
  likely to commit an act or omission that is contrary to this Act, and
  that the nature and seriousness of the act or omission, the need to
  ensure fairness of the electoral process and the public interest
  justify the issuing of an injunction, the court may issue an
  injunction ordering any person named in the application to do one or
  both of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} refrain from committing any act that it appears to
    the court is contrary to this Act; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} do any act that it appears to the court is required
    by this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No injunction may be issued under subsection (2)
  unless at least 48 hours notice is given to each person named in the
  application or the urgency of the situation is such that service of
  notice would not be in the public interest.

### [Compliance Agreements]{.HTitleText2} {#h-210838 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to enter into compliance agreement

- **[[517]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-517
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (7), if the
  Commissioner believes on reasonable grounds that a person or entity
  has committed, is about to commit or is likely to commit an act or
  omission that could constitute an offence under this Act, the
  Commissioner may enter into a compliance agreement, aimed at ensuring
  compliance with this Act, with the person or entity (in this section
  and sections 518 to 521 called the "contracting party").

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms and conditions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A compliance agreement may contain any terms and
  conditions that the Commissioner considers necessary, including a
  requirement that the contracting party pay a specified amount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligations of Commissioner

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Before entering into a compliance agreement, the
  Commissioner shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} advise the prospective contracting party of the
    right to be represented by counsel and give it an opportunity to
    obtain counsel; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} obtain the consent of the prospective contracting
    party to the publication of the agreement under section 521.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Admission of responsibility

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A compliance agreement may include a statement by the
  contracting party in which it admits responsibility for the act or
  omission that constitutes the offence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inadmissible in evidence

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The fact that a compliance agreement was entered
  into, and any statement referred to in subsection (4), is not
  admissible in evidence against the contracting party in any civil or
  criminal proceedings.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2018, c. 31, s. 363\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remittal of matter despite institution
  of prosecution

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If a prosecution has been instituted, the Director of
  Public Prosecutions may --- if, after consultation with the
  Commissioner, the Director considers that a compliance agreement would
  better serve the public interest --- suspend the prosecution and remit
  the matter back to the Commissioner so that it may be dealt with in
  that way.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of compliance agreement

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} When a compliance agreement is entered into,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} no prosecution may be instituted against the
    contracting party for an act or omission that led to the agreement
    unless there is non-compliance with it; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any prosecution of the contracting party instituted
    before the agreement was entered into for an act or omission that
    led to the agreement is suspended unless there is non-compliance
    with the agreement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Renegotiation

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner and the contracting party may
  renegotiate the terms of the compliance agreement at the request of
  the Commissioner or contracting party at any time before it is fully
  executed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner shall provide the contracting party
  with a copy of the compliance agreement, without delay after it is
  entered into or renegotiated under subsection (9). The Commissioner
  shall also provide a copy of the compliance agreement to the Director
  of Public Prosecutions if a prosecution of the contracting party had
  been instituted before the agreement was entered into.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 517
- 2001, c. 21, s. 25(E)
- 2006, c. 9, s. 133
- [2018, c. 31, s. 363](#1043887-1121181){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043887-1121181.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-517-20061212.html "Link to previous version of section 517"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}If agreement complied with

- **[[518]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-518 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Commissioner is of the opinion that the compliance agreement has
  been complied with, the Commissioner shall cause a notice to that
  effect to be served on the contracting party. The Commissioner shall
  also provide a copy of the notice to the Director of Public
  Prosecutions if a prosecution of the contracting party for an act or
  omission that led to the agreement had been instituted before the
  agreement was entered into.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of service

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Service of the notice terminates any prosecution of
  the contracting party that is based on the act or omission in question
  and prevents the institution of any prosecution of the contracting
  party for the act or omission.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 518
- 2006, c. 9, s. 134
- [2018, c. 31, s. 364](#1043904-1121187){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043904-1121187.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-518-20061212.html "Link to previous version of section 518"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}If agreement not complied with

- **[[519]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-519 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Commissioner is of the opinion that a contracting party has not
  complied with a provision of a compliance agreement, the Commissioner
  shall cause a notice of default to be served on the contracting party,
  informing it that, as the case may be,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a notice of violation may be served on the
    contracting party as a result of the failure to comply with the
    provision of the compliance agreement;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a prosecution may be instituted against the
    contracting party in respect of any act or omission that led to the
    agreement; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if a prosecution in respect of any act or omission
    that led to the agreement was suspended by virtue of subsection
    517(8), it may be resumed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy to Director of Public Prosecutions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner shall also provide a copy of the
  notice to the Director of Public Prosecutions if a prosecution in
  respect of any act or omission that led to the agreement had been
  instituted before the agreement was entered into.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 519
- 2006, c. 9, s. 134
- [2018, c. 31, s. 364](#1043904-1121196){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043904-1121196.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-519-20190401.html "Link to previous version of section 519"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dismissal of proceedings

**[[520]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-520 .sectionLabel}** The court shall dismiss
proceedings against a contracting party if it is satisfied on a balance
of probabilities that the contracting party has totally complied with
the compliance agreement or, in the case of partial compliance and
taking into account the contracting party's performance with respect to
the agreement, is of the opinion that the proceedings would be unfair.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 520
- [2018, c. 31, s. 364](#1043904-1121201){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1043904-1121201.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-520-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 520"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

**[[521]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner shall
publish, in the manner and form that he or she considers appropriate, a
notice that sets out the contracting party's name, the act or omission
in question and the text of the compliance agreement, other than the
signatures of the individuals who signed it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2000, c. 9, s. 521
- 2014, c. 12, s. 110
- [2018, c. 31, s. 364](#1043904-1121204){.wb-lbx
